title: Joint Time Delay and Frequency Offset Estimation in vMIMO-Beamforming Relays with Population-Based Techniques and Importance Sampling.
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of joint time delay (TD) and carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation in virtual multiple-input multiple-output (vMIMO) decode-andforward relay systems. A data-aided (DA) maximum likelihood (ML) estimation framework is developed by combining population-based metaheuristic optimization methods with importance sampling (IS). Three optimization algorithms are considered: particle swarm optimization (PSO), grey wolf optimization (GWO), and differential evolution (DE). While these methods provide global search capabilities, their performance may be limited by convergence speed and estimation accuracy in high-dimensional parameter spaces. To address this issue, IS is incorporated into each algorithm to guide the generation of candidate solutions. The resulting hybrid estimators, namely IS-PSO, IS-GWO (or GWOEIS), and IS-DE, leverage pseudoprobability density functions to improve the exploration of the parameter space. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed estimators achieve improved TD and CFO estimation performance compared to their original counterparts and conventional expectation-maximization-based techniques.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low-PAPR Channel Estimation for MIMO-OTFS Systems via Embedded Pilot Codes.
abstract: This paper proposes a delay-Doppler (DD) domain channel estimation scheme for Orthogonal Time-Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation that utilizes embedded pilot codes to overcome the limitations of traditional single-symbol methods. By embedding a sequence with low autocorrelation sidelobes, such as a Barker code, into the transmit grid, the transmitter spreads pilot energy across multiple bins. At the receiver, the DD channel transfer function is estimated through cross-correlation, leveraging the code's ideal autocorrelation properties to achieve high precision. This approach significantly improves the Peak-to-Average-Power Ratio (PAPR) by avoiding the high-power spikes of single-symbol pilots while maintaining robust performance and bit error rate convergence even in low-SNR environments. We further extend this to MIMO-OTFS systems by employing a set of pilot codes with low mutual crosscorrelation, allowing for simultaneous multi-antenna channel estimation with minimal guard band overhead and maintained power efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Secure Rate-Distortion-Perception Trade-Off with Side Information.
abstract: Secure rate-distortion-perception (RDP) trade-offs are relevant for applications such as semantic compression, where the perceptual quality needs to be maximized. We study a framework for secure RDP over an ideal public communication channel in the presence of an eavesdropper, where the legitimate parties also have access to side information correlated with the source. The exact rate region for the secure RDP tradeoff is established when both the encoder and the decoder have access to the side information. We then characterize an inner bound when only the decoder has access to the side information and establish the exact region for a special case. Moreover, we provide an RDP example to illustrate remarkable gains in communication rate due to common randomness, which is not possible to obtain for rate-distortion trade-offs. Our results show that binning-based schemes can achieve high perceptual quality, low distortion, and strong secrecy simultaneously, establishing the information-theoretic limits for next-generation trustworthy semantic compression systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Decentralized Learning Framework for Anomaly Detection in Integrated UAV and CAV Ecosystems.
abstract: The simultaneous operation of multiple autonomous vehicles, including Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), is transforming intelligent transportation systems by enhancing communication, collaborative assessment, and decision-making across both aerial and ground platforms. However, this interconnectivity also introduces new challenges for anomaly detection, as attacks or cyber intrusions in a single vehicle can propagate through the system, increasing vulnerability. Existing intrusion detection approaches typically focus on CAVs or UAVs in isolation, leaving integrated CAV–UAV systems largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose a machine learning-based methodology for anomaly detection in combined UAV–CAV environments. The framework is architecture-agnostic and data-driven, enabling adaptation to diverse operational scenarios and vehicle types. The proposal incorporates temporal, spatial, and feature-level anomaly detection through attention mechanisms and a dynamic ensemble scheme, enhancing robustness and accuracy. By leveraging vehicle-level decentralized computation, the proposed method supports scalable detection across interconnected aerial and ground vehicles. The proposed approach provides an adaptive, scalable, and cooperative platform for resilient anomaly detection in next-generation integrated UAV–CAV ecosystems, achieving improvements of up to 50%, 40%, and 12% in computational cost, detection delay, and accuracy, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: PR-EML: Physics-Respecting and Explainable Machine Learning for Proactive Multi-Band Adaptation in UAV-V2X Networks.
abstract: Adaptive resource allocation across the multi-tier Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN) in Sixth Generation (6 G) systems presents growing complexity due to diverse physical environments and mobility dynamics. In particular, aerial base stations exhibit distinct propagation behaviors that are often overlooked in conventional models. This paper proposes a Physics-Respecting and Explainable Machine Learning (PR-EML) framework for proactive multi-band selection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks. Mobility-induced channel variations, intermittent blockages, and band-dependent interference render reactive, thresholdbased switching unreliable. To address this, the proposed PR-EML integrates ($i$) a monotonic gradient-boosted classifier that enforces propagation-consistent decision boundaries, and (ii) a stacked ensemble regressor that forecasts per-band throughput over short look-ahead horizons. Thus, the feature set captures geometry, path loss, SINR (Signal-to-Interference Noise Ratio) dynamics, and temporal memory. Evaluations on a realistic UAV-V2X dataset demonstrate high accuracy, near-perfect top- 2 reliability, and physically interpretable SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)based explanations. The modular design supports integration with a reactive constraint-enforcement layer, enabling a complete twostep multi-band control strategy for agile and reliable 6G-SAGIN communication.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: FLeXHO: A Federated Learning Based Inter-Cell Handover Optimisation for Open 6G RAN.
abstract: High-speed mobility poses significant challenges to meeting Quality of Service (QoS) requirements of next-generation networks, as traditional handover mechanisms based on static thresholds often underperform in dynamic environments, resulting in higher handover failures, ping-pong effects, and persistent cell load imbalances. To this end, we propose a mobility-aware federated learning (FL)-based handover optimisation framework for open radio access network (O-RAN) compliant networks. The proposed architecture includes three xApps within the near-RT RAN Intelligent Controller (near-RT RIC): a metrics collector extended application (xApp) that obtains real-time radio and mobility measurements, an FL-based load predictor xApp that forecasts load imbalance using distributed LSTM models, and a handover handler xApp that performs proactive AI-driven mobility management. Implemented on an OpenAirInterface (OAI) based end-to-end testbed with 3GPP protocol stack support, the proposed system achieves notable performance gains: a 94.5% handover success rate, a 95% reduction in load imbalance, and a 73% decrease in packet loss. By maintaining a near-RT RIC decision pipeline latency on the order of 10 ms, this work demonstrates the practical feasibility of federated, xApp-driven mobility optimisation in O-RAN.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Explainability Boosted Anomaly Detection Framework for O-RAN Based NextG Networks.
abstract: The wireless networks have historically faced significant security vulnerabilities, necessitating advanced anomaly detection mechanisms, especially as networks evolve towards 6G and beyond. This study introduces an advanced anomaly detection framework that leverages explainable artificial intelligence to enhance the security of next-generation (NextG) cellular networks. By implementing and evaluating a variety of artificial intelligence models, the framework demonstrates high accuracy and efficient runtime performance in identifying malicious traffic within a realistic Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) testbed. A key innovation of this work is the integration of post-hoc explainability methods to identify the most critical key performance metrics (KPMs), which enables a significant 80% reduction in dataset complexity without compromising detection accuracy. Additionally, explainability analyses identify several critical attack traffic characteristics, such as protocol type, bandwidth, interval, and duration, to prevent upcoming network attacks. The resulting framework effectively balances computational efficiency, accuracy, and explainability, underscoring its practical applicability for enhancing security in next-generation cellular networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Improved Data Detection Scheme for Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) serves as a cornerstone technology for beyond fifth-generation$(5 \mathrm{G})$wireless networks, delivering significant improvements in both spectral and energy efficiency. However, one of the key challenges lies in designing signal detection algorithms that achieve high performance while maintaining low computational complexity. Iterative detection techniques have gained significant attention, where they progressively improve the accuracy of detection through a series of successive updates or iterations. In this work, we propose two novel hybrid massive MIMO detectors: the improved Newton method (INI) combined with Gauss-Seidel (GS) and the INI combined with successive overrelaxation (SOR). The motivation behind this work is to combine low-complexity iterative methods with the adaptive and recursive estimation power of INI, resulting in a more efficient and accurate detection process. By first applying a lightweight INI-based initialization and then refining the estimate using efficient iterative updates, the proposed detectors can accelerate convergence with significantly reduced complexity. Simulation results demonstrate superior performance, outperforming existing up-to-date detectors, making them well-suited for practical deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive Federated Control: An Event-Driven MARL Framework for Fair and Efficient Traffic Management.
abstract: Next-generation networks require distributed traffic management to handle dynamic loads, but frequent interagent coordination consumes scarce bandwidth. We propose an adaptive federated multi-agent reinforcement learning (Fed-MARL) framework that triggers model synchronization only when congestion is near. Our congestion index combines queue occupancy, latency, and utilization to detect network stress. When the threshold is exceeded, federated learning aggregates distributed agent models using FedAdam. For fairness, we introduce empathy-weighted reward shaping, where agents balance individual rewards with peer performance, aligning selfish routing with system-wide welfare. DDPG agents deployed at edge switches make routing and load balancing decisions. Evaluated on Fat-Tree K=4 topology, Fed-MARL achieves 93% latency reduction vs. RL-MR (7.77 vs 105 ms), 57% vs. DRAMA (18.15 ms), 192.6 Mbps throughput, and perfect delivery with minimal communication overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: CRAFT: A Co-Adaptive Freeze and Train Strategy for Dynamic Neural Networks.
abstract: Dynamic Neural Networks (DyNNs) can adapt their structure or parameters dynamically, making them suitable for wireless communication systems with varying modulation schemes and channel conditions. A key challenge, however, is the large memory overhead of storing separate parameter sets for each modulation order. To address this issue, we present three main contributions. 1) A DyNN-based demodulator that computes log-likelihood ratios for multiple modulation schemes, where higher-order constellations reuse parameters from lowerorder ones via a Co-adaptive Freeze and Train (CRAFT) strategy. 2) A link-level evaluation on a 5G-NR SIMO CDL-C channel, demonstrating a minimal SNR loss (1 dB) for lowerorder modulations, with comparable or improved performance for higher-order constellations relative to a fully flexible DyNN and consistent gains over approximate ML-MAP demodulation. 3) A parameter count and memory analysis in GF$22-\text{nm}$FDSOI CMOS technology, demonstrating a 24% reduction in parameters and up to 28% reduction in area and total power using an 8k SRAM macro compared to a fully flexible DyNN.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Resource-Aware Semantic Communication with Adaptive Vision Transformers for Digital Twins.
abstract: In the Metaverse, real-time digital twin (DT) updates enable immersive, interactive environments by reflecting real world states. Metaverse can engage its users to share data in order to ensure the completeness of the DT. However, the limitations and heterogeneity in IoT devices' computation and transmission resources are critical challenges to synchronizing the vast volume of real-world objects with their digital replicas. In this work, we propose a novel adaptive Vision Transformer (ViT)- based semantic communication (SemCom) system to extract semantic information from raw data collected by IoT devices. The system dynamically adjusts the model size and computational complexity according to the resource constraints of individual IoT devices, enables broader participation of heterogeneous devices, enhances feature extraction capabilities, and ensures completeness and efficient DT representation. We formulate our problem as an utility-maximization optimization to manage ViT complexity under resource constraints, allowing the Metaverse Services Provider (MSP) to select high-performing IoT devices. To guide the optimization, we profile ViT models with varying architectural complexities and conduct an empirical analysis to capture the relationship between model scale and performance. To address the scalability and privacy limitations of the optimization, we propose a decentralized solution where each IoT device independently optimizes its own utility under local constraints. The MSP, in turn, selects among these devices to ensure quality and maximize its overall utility. We show that our distributed solution achieves near-optimal performance and significantly outperforms other approaches in terms of MSP utility, semantic data quality, and overall IoT utility. © 2026 IEEE.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Sparse OFDM Design for Interference and Ambiguity Mitigation in Multi-Static ISAC.
abstract: The sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks promises the integration of radar-like sensing capabilities into communication infrastructure. In this paper, we investigate a multi-static sensing framework where half-duplex base stations (BSs) are assigned as either transmitter or sensing receiver nodes. We propose a randomized sparse resource allocation scheme based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform design tailored for the multi-static scenario to simultaneously mitigate inter-BS interference (IBI) and sensing ambiguities. The waveform design also ensures robustness against inter-symbol interference (ISI) and intercarrier interference (ICI) via a judicious choice of subcarrier spacing according to the deployment of BSs. The potential ambiguity caused by sparse signaling is addressed through controlled irregularity in both time and frequency domains, with a negligible noise floor elevation. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and resilience of the proposed design in the presence of multiple targets and clutter.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Challenger-Based Combinatorial Bandits for Subcarrier Selection in Ofdm Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates the identification of the top-m user-scheduling sets in multi-user MIMO downlink, which is cast as a combinatorial pure-exploration problem in stochastic linear bandits. Because the action space grows exponentially, exhaustive search is infeasible. We therefore adopt a linear utility model to enable efficient exploration and reliable selection of promising user subsets. We introduce a gap-index framework that maintains a shortlist of current estimates of champion arms (top-m sets) and a rotating shortlist of challenger arms that pose the greatest threat to the champions. This design focuses on measurements that yield the most informative gap-index-based comparisons, resulting in significant reductions in runtime and computation compared to state-of-the-art linear bandit methods, with high identification accuracy. The method also exposes a tunable trade-off between speed and accuracy. Simulations on a realistic OFDM downlink show that shortlist-driven pure exploration makes online, measurement-efficient subcarrier selection practical for AI-enabled communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Performance Evaluation for Deep Learning-Based Signal Detection in Underwater Visible Light Communication.
abstract: Underwater visible light communication (UVLC) has sparked wide research interest for its potential of providing high data-rate services in underwater scenarios. However, UVLC faces significant challenges due to the complicated and unpredictable underwater channel conditions caused by absorption and scattering that vary with different water types. These phenomena make acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) and reliable signal detection particularly difficult. In this paper, we propose a deep learning (DL)-based approach that combines the channel estimation (CE) and signal detection (SD) processes using long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network. By leveraging the underwater channel characteristics learned through offline training, our DL-based method treats the channel as a black-box and jointly performs CE and SD. Simulation results demonstrate that without prior channel knowledge, the proposed method significantly outperforms the conventional CE approach, i.e., minimum mean square error (MMSE) in terms of bit-error-rate (BER) across varying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and closely matches with the optimal maximum likelihood (ML) detection that typically requires perfect CSI. This highlights the potential of LSTM in learning the complex underwater environment, and providing robust UVLC signal detection compared to traditional CE technique.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: GAN-Augmented and LLM-Enhanced Intrusion Detection for Intelligent Vehicles.
abstract: The rapid growth of connected and autonomous vehicles has greatly expanded the cyberattack surface of invehicle networks, especially those based on the Controller Area Network (CAN) bus, which lacks built-in authentication and encryption. This paper presents a lightweight, semi-supervised intrusion detection system (IDS) that integrates generative adversarial networks (GANs) and large language models (LLMs) to deliver high accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability. CAN traffic is transformed into image-like representations that combine identifiers, data length codes, and payload bytes to capture both structural and semantic features. A binarized GAN discriminator generates compact, discriminative embeddings that are classified by a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) under limited supervision. To improve robustness, GAN-based data augmentation enhances detection stability when trained with as little as 10% of attack data. Experiments on the Car-Hacking and Survival benchmark datasets achieve over 99% detection accuracy, outperforming existing baselines while maintaining a total footprint under 10 MB and inference latency below 2 ms. Also, an LLM-driven interpreter produces concise, human-readable explanations for IDS alerts, increasing operator trust and transparency. The results demonstrate the feasibility of a scalable, explainable, and real-time IDS for next-generation intelligent vehicles.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Transformer-Based Web Attack Detection for 6G MEC-Enabled SDN Architectures.
abstract: Future 6G networks will rely heavily on multi-access edge computing (MEC) and software-defined networking (SDN) to support ultra-low latency services, large-scale automation, and AI-native operation. This increased softwarization, however, expands the attack surface of controllers and edge services, particularly at the application layer where web-based threats continue to grow in sophistication. Existing SDN security mechanisms often depend on signature-based techniques or centralized detection, making them unsuitable for the distributed and realtime requirements of 6 G environments. In this paper, we propose an AI-Native, Zero-Trust (ZT) security framework for 6G MEC-enabled SDN architectures. We leverage the lightweight nature of DistilBERT to enable ultralow latency, multi-class web attack detection. Deployed as a microservice at the MEC layer, the model inspects and classifies HTTP requests across seven CAPEC-defined attack types in real time. Our primary contribution is demonstrating that this decentralized approach achieves microsecond-scale inference; end-toend latency is at millisecond-scale due to controller/API overhead. Experimental results in an SDN testbed confirm high accuracy (< 99%) and minimal overhead, validating the model's suitability for AI-Native and resource-constrained edge environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Spectrum Sensing Under Random Beam Geometry.
abstract: Directional wireless systems employing phased arrays or massive-antenna beams are inherently influenced by geometric uncertainty arising from beam jitter, pointing errors, and user mobility. This paper develops a unified likelihood-ratio framework for directional spectrum sensing with random beam geometry, where boundary erosion and receiver location jointly govern the illumination state of a secondary user (SU). Beam jitter can intermittently place primary receivers in the dark while the primary transmitter remains active, creating transient spectrum opportunities that conventional models cannot exploit. By marginalizing the random geometry within a Bayesian formulation, likelihood-ratio tests are derived for the PU-centric, SU-centric, and geometry-blind cases. For flat-top beams under truncated Gaussian boundary jitter and uniform-area receiver geometry, the LRTs reduce to closed-form scalar energy tests with explicit Bayesian thresholds. Monte Carlo results confirm that the PU-centric detector achieves the minimum total error and reveal a critical jitter level beyond which all detectors converge in performance. The framework quantifies how geometric uncertainty degrades link reliability and enables spatial spectrum reuse, providing a theoretical basis for probabilistic sensing.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Variational Bayesian Detection for Quantized AFDM Systems.
abstract: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM) provides strong robustness in high-mobility channels, but its practical deployment is limited by the nonlinear distortion introduced by low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). This paper proposes a Variational Bayesian (VB) detection framework that explicitly incorporates quantization constraints while exploiting the sparse delay-Doppler structure of AFDM channels. By modeling interference-plus-noise as Gaussian and employing a mean-field approximation, we derive closed-form iterative updates that reduce the original high-dimensional inference problem to efficient evaluations of truncated-Gaussian likelihoods. The resulting algorithm features linear computational complexity with respect to the frame length and constellation size, making it scalable to wideband systems. Simulation results demonstrate significant gains over Bussgang-based linear receivers and message-passing detectors, especially under fractional Doppler spreads and 3-4 bit ADCs where nonlinear quantization effects dominate. The proposed approach achieves near-unquantized performance at moderate resolutions and delivers substantial normalized mean squared-error (NMSE) and bit error rate (BER) improvements at low resolutions, establishing VB inference as a principled and practical solution for quantized AFDM systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low-Complexity VAMP Detector for Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing Systems.
abstract: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM) has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility wireless communications, achieving full delay-Doppler diversity through the discrete affine Fourier transform. This paper presents a computationally efficient detector for AFDM systems using a low-complexity Vector Approximate Message Passing (VAMP) algorithm that employs the conjugate gradient method to solve the linear estimation problem iteratively, eliminating the need for expensive singular value decomposition operations required by standard VAMP algorithms. The proposed approach employs diagonal preconditioning and simultaneous trace estimation to maintain detection accuracy while significantly reducing computational complexity from cubic to quadratic scaling in the number of subcarriers. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed detector achieves bit error rate performance comparable to standard VAMP across multiple modulation schemes while reducing computational burden by factors ranging from five to ten for practical system dimensions, making it highly suitable for real-time implementation in resource-constrained high-mobility communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Reference Signal Received Power Prediction for Measurement Gap Reduction.
abstract: Traditionally, User Equipment (UE) relies on Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) measurements from serving and neighboring cells for essential mobility management tasks, such as cell selection and handover, while navigating through cellular networks. These tasks ensure seamless connectivity and high quality of service (QoS) for emerging services like eXtended reality (XR). A significant challenge arises from the need for UEs to enter measurement gaps (MGs) for inter-frequency measurements, during which communication with their serving cell is temporarily disrupted. Excessive or untimely RSRP measurements lead to inefficient power consumption and wasted radio resources that could otherwise boost system throughput. To address these issues, we propose a novel Machine Learning (ML)-based intelligent mobility management framework that predicts future RSRP values across various scenarios, including reduced number of RSRP measurements. We compare different MG reduction techniques using XGBoost and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and demonstrate through simulations that our ML-based approach effectively predicts RSRP with less than a$\mathbf{2 ~ d B}$threshold, while achieving close to$\mathbf{1 5 \%}$more throughput by reallocating resources.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Jamming Attacks on the Random Access Channel in 5G and B5G Networks.
abstract: Random Access Channel (RACH) jamming poses a critical security threat to 5G and beyond (B5G) networks. This paper presents an analytical model for predicting the impact of Msg1 jamming attacks on RACH performance. We use the OpenAirInterface (OAI) open-source user equipment (UE) to implement a Msg1 jamming attacker. Over-the-air experiments validate the accuracy of the proposed analytical model. The results show that low-power and stealthy Msg1 jamming can effectively block legitimate UE access in 5G/B5G systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel 3D Non-Stationary GBSM for Underground Parking Lot Scenarios.
abstract: As typical underground pillar structure scenarios, underground parking lots play an essential role in the urbanization process. In this paper, a novel three-dimensional (3D) geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM) is proposed for underground parking lot scenarios, based on sixth generation pervasive channel model (6GPCM). Dense multipath components (DMCs) are incorporated into the proposed model, enabling a more accurate description of diffuse scattering caused by complex structures and small objects in the environment. The model focuses on the unique physical features of underground parking lots, considering vehicle density and the corner effect caused by significant pillar-induced corner losses. Based on the proposed model, the statistical properties of the channel are derived and simulated, such as the temporal auto-correlation function (TACF), spatial cross-correlation function (SCCF), angular power spectral density (angular PSD), delay spread, and channel capacity. The results indicate that the variations in vehicle density and the number of corners can significantly affect signal propagation, making them indispensable in channel modeling. Incorporating the effects of unique physical features and the presence of DMCs enables the channel model to reflect the actual signal propagation mechanisms, leading to improve its practical accuracy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MIMO-Zak-OTFS with Superimposed Spread Pilots.
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of spread pilot design and effective channel estimation in multiple-input multiple-output Zak-OTFS (MIMO-Zak-OTFS) with superimposed spread pilots, where data and spread pilot signals are superimposed in the same frame. To achieve good estimation performance in a MIMO setting, the spread pilots at different transmit antennas need to be effectively separated at the receiver. Towards this, we propose a spread pilot design that separates the pilot sequences in the cross-ambiguity domain and enables the estimation of the effective channel taps by a simple read-off operation. To further alleviate the effect of pilot-data interference on performance, we carry out turbo iterations between channel estimation and detection. Simulation results for $2\times 2$ and $3\times 3$ MIMO-Zak-OTFS with Gaussian-sinc pulse shaping filter for vehicular-A channel model show that the proposed pilot design and estimation scheme with three turbo iterations can achieve very good estimation/detection performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: GENIAL: A Genetic and Intelligent Adaptive Link Orchestrator for Mobile TSCH Networks.
abstract: Reliable, low-latency wireless networking is critical for mobile robot swarms operating in dynamic environments. The IEEE 802.15.4e Time Slotted Channel Hopping (TSCH) standard offers predictable MAC-layer performance, but existing scheduling algorithms are not designed for scenarios in which nodes are continuously moving. This paper presents GENIAL, a centralized cross-layer orchestrator for mobile robot swarms that jointly optimizes topology formation, routing, and TSCH slot allocation using a genetic algorithm. Running at the gateway, GENIAL leverages real-time queue and link quality metrics to dynamically adapt parent-child relationships and resource allocation. Compared to the state-of-the-art OST scheduler, GENIAL delivers up to 67.2% more packets, reduces latency by 58.4%, and improves fairness under mobility, making it well suited for large mobile networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Atmospheric Ducts in Wireless Propagation: Analytical and Data-Driven Range Extension Models.
abstract: Tropospheric ducts extend radio links beyond the geometric horizon, significantly impacting terrestrial backhaul and maritime connectivity; however, accurately modeling this phenomenon remains challenging. Widely used approaches, such as parabolic-equation (PE) solvers and ITU-R P.452, are either computationally intensive or rely on limited-fidelity climatological surrogates. We develop a vertical-profile-driven, closed-form model for ducted path loss and range. First, vertical refractivity gradient and duct thickness are mapped to a confinement index that governs an effective spreading model and a bounce-tokilometer attenuation slope combining gas/rain absorption with reflection/leakage. Second, a single analytic loss model is inverted in closed form via the Lambert-$W$function to yield ducted distance, range extension, and duct gain directly from link-budget inputs. Calibration against ITU-R P. 452 via a confinement-to-time-percentage mapping shows monotone scaling, cross-band coherence, and close agreement: RMSE$=14.7 ~\text{km}$and MAE = 13.6 km for ducted-range medians and path-loss curves at 7 GHz track within 1-2 dB across weak/medium/strong ducts. Reliability curves and gain-confinement plots show that ducts provide over 100 km of additional reach, depending on band and confinement.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Physical Layer Security for RIS-Aided Hardware-Impaired Cell-Free Massive MIMO.
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of dynamicresolution analog-to-digital converter (ADC)/digital-to-analog converter (DAC) and radio frequency (RF) impairments on the secrecy performance of a spatially correlated multi-reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output system. We obtain the linear minimum meansquare error estimation to acquire the channel estimate and derive a closed-form expression for the achievable secrecy sum rate (SSR) under the impact of imperfect channel state information and practical hardware impairments. Each access point injects an artificial noise (AN) signal during the downlink data transmission phase to enhance the secrecy performance. Numerical results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate that the presence of RF impairments and low-resolution ADCs/DACs results in a notable degradation of the achievable SSR. Furthermore, maintaining the secrecy performance under both mixedresolution and low-resolution ADCs/DACs necessitates more AN power. Additionally, different architectures of dynamic-resolution ADCs/DACs play a crucial role in achieving an optimal SSR.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: GRAPE: Gossip-Based Representation Alignment Using Prototypical Embeddings for Heterogeneous IoT Devices.
abstract: Gossip learning (GL) introduces a fully decentralized framework for training machine learning models across large-scale networks of heterogeneous IoT devices, leveraging peer-to-peer communication to enable collaborative learning without centralized coordination or raw data exchange. However, in real-world IoT environments, devices commonly operate under non-IID data distributions and often contains different model architectures, computational power, and storage capacity which leads to model heterogeneity. In such settings, conventional GL fails to converge reliably, as weight averaging is incompatible with heterogeneous architectures, while existing alternatives still rely on centralized coordination. To address these challenges, we introduce GRAPE, a fully decentralized, prototype-based GL framework that tackles both data and model heterogeneity. Instead of exchanging full model parameters, participating devices communicate compact class prototypes that serve as semantic summaries of local knowledge. We propose a contrastive prototype alignment objective that enables devices to refine their learned representations by attracting semantically consistent prototypes while repelling inconsistent ones during peer-to-peer exchanges. This approach enforces consistent representations across heterogeneous models within a unified embedding space. Extensive experiments show that GRAPE outperforms standard GL baselines, achieving higher accuracy, improved robustness to heterogeneity, and lower communication costs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Machine Learning-Based Transceivers: Two-Stage Training for Digital Modulation.
abstract: Recent advances in machine learning have inspired the redesign of fundamental building blocks of wireless communication systems. In this paper, we investigate an end-to-end learning framework for digital modulation using neural networks. We introduce a machine learning (ML)-based transceiver that we name in short “smart transceiver”. For this, we propose a two-stage training process: (i) supervised demodulation training with pilot symbols transmitted by a conventional system, and (ii) modulation training via communication between a learned demodulator and a neural modulator, under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) conditions. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are employed to learn robust symbol constellations and decoding strategies without relying on explicit channel models. We systematically analyze the impact of training parameters, including the number of training bits, on the learning outcome. Performance is evaluated in terms of bit error rate (BER) and compared against conventional transceivers. Our results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance with a loss of less than 0.5 dB while adapting to channel conditions, highlighting the potential of ML for future communication systems beyond manually engineered constellations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Learning Codes and Decoders Simultaneously: A Cross-Attention Transformer Approach.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Performance Analysis of RIS-Assisted ISAC-NOMA Uplink System Under Imperfect SIC.
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system comprising two communication users and one target. An RIS partitioning strategy is used, wherein separate RIS zones are allocated to support communication users and radar echo reflection simultaneously. The practical effect of inter-zone interference among RIS partitions is considered and the probability density function of the effective channel power gain from communication users to the base station considering reflections from all RIS zones are provided. Under the imperfect successive interference cancellation scenario, closedform expressions for the outage probability of communication users and sensing target are derived. We also obtain analytical expression of average sensing information rate that characterizes long-term sensing throughput. Numerical results reveal that our proposed scheme substantially outperforms orthogonal multiple access scheme and bring out the efficacy of deploying RIS and partitioning coefficient configurations for reliable communication and sensing in ISAC-NOMA system.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enabling Green Hybrid Networks with Plasmodesmata-Inspired Molecular Links.
abstract: Molecular communication via diffusion (MCvD) is a bio-inspired paradigm for nanonetworks and sustainable communication systems, enabling nanoscale information transfer where electromagnetic methods are limited. MCvD occurs naturally in biological systems and can take place in both unbounded and bounded environments, often relying on specialized structures that mediate selective transport, such as plasmodesmata (PDs) in plants. Here, we focus on PDs, whose structural simplicity makes them suitable as models for communication frameworks. To address scalability issues of particle-based models in complex tissues, a voxel-based framework for PD-mediated MCvD is introduced, enabling efficient simulations through spatial discretization. Incorporating plasmodesmata-inspired molecular links allows MCvD to integrate into broader network architectures as controllable nanoscale channels bridging molecular, optical, and wireless modalities. This approach supports dense IoT sensing and hybrid networks with wireless systems, while laying the foundation for the Internet of Plants, with applications in crop monitoring, precision agriculture, and bio-hybrid networks for energy-efficient communication inspired by natural intercellular processes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Timing Recovery and Sequence Detection for Integrate-and-Fire Time Encoding Receivers.
abstract: Recent advances in neuromorphic signal processing have introduced time encoding machines as a promising alternative to conventional uniform sampling for low-power communication receivers. In this paradigm, analog signals are converted into event timings by an integrate-and-fire circuit, allowing information to be represented through spike times rather than amplitude samples. While event-driven sampling eliminates the need for a fixed-rate clock, receivers equipped with integrate-and-fire time encoding machines, called time encoding receivers, often assume perfect symbol synchronization, leaving the problem of symbol timing recovery unresolved. This paper presents a joint timing recovery and data detection framework for integrate-and-fire time encoding receivers. The log-likelihood function is derived to capture the dependence between firing times, symbol timing offset, and transmitted sequence, leading to a maximum likelihood formulation for joint timing estimation and sequence detection. A practical two-stage receiver is developed, consisting of a timing recovery algorithm followed by a zero-forcing detector. Simulation results demonstrate accurate symbol timing offset estimation and improved symbol error rate performance compared to existing time encoding receivers.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Modal Data Driven Virtual Base Station Construction for Massive MIMO Beam Alignment.
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is a key enabler for the high data rates required by the sixth-generation networks, yet its performance hinges on effective beam management with low training overhead. This paper proposes an interpretable framework to tackle beam alignment in mixed line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation environments. Our approach utilizes multi-modal data to construct virtual base stations (VBSs), which are geometrically defined as mirror images of the base station across reflecting surfaces reconstructed from 3D LiDAR points. These VBSs provide a sparse and spatial representation of the dominant features of the wireless environment. Based on the constructed VBSs, we develop a VBS-assisted beam alignment scheme comprising coarse channel reconstruction followed by partial beam training. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves near-optimal performance in terms of spectral efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Integrate and Fire Counting Spike Detection for Spiking Communications.
abstract: We focus on low-power spike-based sensor node communication where runlength-limited (RLL) encoding is applied to map the information to the timing of the spikes. In this type of sensor communication, often rare events need to be communicated such that spikes are transmitted rarely, and the detection of those spikes has to be performed in an energyefficient way. Generally, standard analog-to-digital converter (ADC) based detectors are employed at the receiver, which are always active even if there is no spike being transmitted, resulting in unnecessary power consumption. To mitigate this issue, this paper studies an integrate-and-fire (IF) circuit followed by a counter and pre-processor as an energy-efficient spike detector. It counts the number of fires in each symbol interval, which is further used by the pre-processing unit to map the fire count within each symbol interval into transmitted RLL symbols' loglikelihood ratios. We evaluate a lower bound on the mutual information (MI) rate and the bit error rate of the communication system using this spike detector. Numerical results indicate that the proposed spike detection enables to receive RLL encoded spike sequences at a significantly lower energy per communicated bit Eb than traditional ADC based spike detection and alternative low-power IF time encoding machine (IF-TEM) based detection methods. Moreover, the required Eb decreases when increasing the minimum runlength constraint jointly with the signaling rate. Furthermore, a comparative discussion on the power consumption between the IF circuit based analog-todigital conversions and standard ADCs is presented.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RIS-Assisted Localization: Cascaded vs Physics-Compliant Model from a CRB Perspective.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) are increasingly being explored for enhancing localization in wireless systems due to their ability to finely tune the propagation channel. This paper addresses localization in a SISO system with a binary RIS, comparing a physics-compliant model to the conventional affine cascaded model via the Cramér-Rao bound and highlighting the impact of reverberation on position estimation accuracy. The channel is reformulated as a sum of matrices representing paths of specific bounce orders, and position parameters are estimated via the Cramér-Rao bound, with optional truncation. The results indicate that the linear cascaded model performs well only in low-reverberation scenarios, while it underestimates localization errors in highly reverberant environments, potentially leading to misleading RIS configurations. In contrast, the PhysFad model provides physically consistent bounds across all reverberation levels, and reverberation is found to enhance localization accuracy, confirming prior experimental findings and highlighting the importance of multipath and bounce-based modeling.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: LOREN: Low-Rank-Based Code-Rate Adaptation in Neural Receivers.
abstract: Neural network based receivers have recently demonstrated superior system-level performance compared to traditional receivers. However, their practicality is limited by high memory and power requirements, as separate weight sets must be stored for each code rate. To address this challenge, we propose LOREN, a Low Rank-Based Code-Rate Adaptation Neural Receiver that achieves adaptability with minimal overhead. LOREN integrates lightweight low rank adaptation adapters (LOREN adapters) into convolutional layers, freezing a shared base network while training only small adapters per code rate. An end-to-end training framework over 3GPP CDL channels ensures robustness across realistic wireless environments. LOREN achieves comparable or superior performance relative to fully retrained base neural receivers. The hardware implementation of LOREN in 22nm technology shows more than 65% savings in silicon area and up to 15% power reduction when supporting three code rates.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Secure Isac Waveform Design Framework Via Random Frequency and Pri Agility.
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for enhancing the security, data rate, and sensing performance of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems. We employ a random frequency and pulse repetition interval (PRI) agility (RFPA) method for the waveform design, where the necessary random sequences are governed by shared secrets. These secrets, which can be pre-shared or generated via channel reciprocity, obfuscate critical radar parameters like Doppler frequency and pulse start times, thereby significantly impeding the ability to perform reconnaissance from a passive adversary without the secret key. To further introduce enhanced data throughput, we also introduce a hybrid information embedding scheme that integrates amplitude shift keying (ASK), phase shift keying (PSK), index modulation (IM), and spatial modulation (SM), for which a low-complexity sparse-matched filter receiver is proposed for accurate decoding with practical complexity. Finally, the excellent range-velocity resolution and clutter suppression of the proposed waveform are analyzed via the ambiguity function (AF).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive Multi-Receiver-Oriented Semantic Communication in Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Semantic Communication (SC) enhances communication efficiency by transmitting meaning rather than raw data, improving the efficiency of communication, especially in vehicular networks. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for vehicular networks that embeds rich semantic content across multiple dimensions while preserving the key advantages of SC, namely data size reduction and communication efficiency. Our approach extracts semantics from car-view videos across multiple dimensions (10 in our implementation) and leverages user feedback to identify the most relevant dimensions for each receiver. This enables the transmitter to refine its understanding of the receivers' Knowledge Bases (KBs), enhancing the relevance and efficiency of communication. This adaptive learning improves communication relevance and efficiency, particularly in varied KB scenarios. Our simulations demonstrate that the Receiver Satisfaction (RS) score, a metric evaluating how relevant the received semantics for the receivers, can be improved by over 20% compared to when the receivers' feedback is not accounted for. This highlights the potential of the receiveroriented multidimensional SC to improve message transmission in both the receivers' satisfaction and communication efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Distributed Asynchronous Server Selection in Cloud Gaming with Delayed Load Information.
abstract: Cloud gaming allows resource-constrained players to offload computation-intensive tasks to edge and cloud servers. Delay-sensitive gaming benefits from edge computing, but limited server capacity can degrade QoE, and centralized assignment is impractical at scale. We propose DASS, a distributed asynchronous server selection framework where players autonomously choose servers to optimize the delay-QoE tradeoff, even with potentially stale load information. Unlike synchronous approaches, DASS accounts for realistic propagation delays and asynchronous decisions. Simulations show that under server overload, DASS converges to stable assignments resembling a Nash equilibrium and can achieve higher QoE than an ideal synchronous scenario. However, this gain comes at the cost of less balanced load distribution, highlighting the trade-off between efficiency and fairness in decentralized, asynchronous resource selection.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Salxo: Semantic Augmentation Via Latent-Space Exploration.
abstract: Recent advances in wireless networks have spurred interest in using Wi-Fi signals for human-centric mobile sensing tasks, such as gesture recognition and activity detection. To address the scarcity of labeled data in these applications, researchers increasingly turn to self-supervised learning (SSL) techniques for representation learning. In parallel, deep generative models, e.g., generative adversarial networks (GANs) and diffusion models, have been used to expand wireless sensing datasets via synthetic data generation. However, these efforts often treat generative models as black-box data expanders, with limited attention to semantic context or augmentation quality. In this paper, we propose a novel augmentation method termed the semantic augmentation via latent-space exploration (SALxO), which leverages the latent space of a variational auto-encoder (VAE) to generate semantically consistent views for contrastive learning. SALxO uses a latent chaining algorithm that traverses structured regions of the latent manifold, producing meaningful positive pairs without labels or handcrafted perturbations. Integrated into fixed SimCLR and AutoFi backbones, SALxO improves few-shot accuracy by up to 13 % and accelerates convergence, without requiring architecture changes. These results highlight SALxO's promise for scalable and label-efficient SSL-enabled wireless sensing.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Chance-Constrained Optimization Framework for Reliable Aerial Networking.
abstract: Aerial edge computing can enable reliable Internet of things (IoT) services in sixth-generation (6 G) networks, particularly for connecting isolated regions with limited or no communication infrastructure. In this context, we propose a trust-aware framework that integrates uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) and high-altitude platforms (HAPs) to support efficient task offloading and adaptive resource allocation. The framework optimizes UAV positions to maximize coverage and integrates a hybrid trustworthiness model that considers both dependent and independent performance metrics. The dependent metrics capacity, energy, and task interact to determine a UAV's reliability, while the independent metrics connectivity and security contribute independently to reinforce overall trust. We embed this trustworthiness model in a chance-constrained, multi-criteria optimization problem. The formulation ensures that the total energy consumption of IoT devices stays within acceptable limits with high probability, while balancing trust, deployment cost, latency, and IoT-UAV connectivity. We further propose a penalty-guided optimization (PGO) algorithm to solve this problem and evaluate its performance against baseline relaxation, greedy, and benchmark algorithms. Simulation results show that the PGO algorithm achieves near-optimal performance with significantly lower computational complexity. These findings highlight the framework's potential to enable trustworthy and low-latency aerial edge computing in 6 G networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Doppler-DCNet: A Low Sampling Rate CSI Reconstruction Algorithm for Traffic-Driven WiFi Sensing.
abstract: Traffic-driven WiFi sensing suffers from a low CSI sampling rate and non-uniform, bursty sampling, leading to severe Doppler aliasing and feature distortion. To address this challenge, we formulate CSI recovery from irregular observations as a physics-constrained inverse problem and propose Doppler-DCNet, a model-driven cascaded network. Doppler-DCNet explicitly alternates a learnable time-Doppler prior with a hard data-consistency (DC) projection, ensuring fidelity to physical observations while effectively suppressing aliasing artifacts. Experiments on the Widar3.0 dataset show that DopplerDCNet outperforms existing baselines in both reconstruction quality and recognition accuracy, demonstrating superior robustness under sparse and bursty traffic conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy Efficiency Optimization for ISAC-Enabled Terrestrial-Satellite Networks.
abstract: The growing demand for wireless connectivity, coupled with the need for robust sensing capabilities, poses significant challenges for future communication systems, particularly in terms of spectrum scarcity and energy efficiency. A promising approach combines integrated terrestrial-satellite networks (ITSNs) with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) and rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA), creating a unified framework capable of supporting communication and sensing simultaneously while effectively managing interference. In this work, we investigate an underlay cognitive LEO satellite coexisting with a terrestrial cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) network to perform simultaneous sensing and communication using RSMA. We formulate a non-convex energy efficiency (EE) optimization problem that jointly designs RSMA precoders and rate variables under constraints on minimum user rates, satellite power budget, sensing beampattern, and interference limits. A solution framework combining quadratic transformation and successive convex approximation-based method is proposed. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme satisfies sensing, data rates and coexistence constraints while achieving superior EE performance compared to conventional approaches without RSMA.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Nonparametric Variational Bayesian Learning for Channel Estimation with OTFS Modulation.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation has demonstrated significant advantages in high-mobility scenarios in future 6 G networks. However, existing channel estimation methods often overlook the structured sparsity and clustering characteristics inherent in realistic clustered delay line (CDL) channels, leading to degraded performance in practical systems. To address this issue, we propose a novel nonparametric Bayesian learning (NPBL) framework for OTFS channel estimation. Specifically, a stick-breaking process is introduced to automatically infer the number of multipath components and assign each path to its corresponding cluster. The channel coefficients within each cluster are modeled by a Gaussian mixture distribution to capture complex fading statistics. Furthermore, an effective pruning criterion is designed to eliminate spurious multipath components, thereby enhancing estimation accuracy and reducing computational complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in terms of normalized mean squared error compared to existing methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Transmission of Binary Sequences Over Gaussian Channels Under Privacy Constraints.
abstract: We focus on encoding of dependent bits that are sent to a receiver employing an optimal Bayes detector. While some of the bits denote the common information to be sent to the receiver as accurately as possible, the remaining bits carry private information. The transmitter aims to hide the private information by encoding the bits into suitable signal levels. On the other hand, the receiver wishes to detect all the bits with the highest accuracy. Considering the bit error probabilities related to the common and private bits as the performance metrics, we propose an optimal encoding approach at the transmitter. Due to the complexity of the original problem, we first perform an asymptotic analysis for single common and private bits by considering a noiseless channel between the transmitter and the receiver, and provide theoretical results related to the structure of the optimal encoding at the transmitter. Then, for the generic case with multiple common and private bits, we develop a machine learning approach for encoding of bits at the transmitter. We provide numerical examples to illustrate the results, which also show that the asymptotic results are attainable through gradientbased optimization using machine learning.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DRS-TD3 for Joint Freshness and Energy Optimization in UAV-Assisted Energy-Harvesting Sensor Networks.
abstract: In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) enabled communication is considered a promising technology for real-time remote data collection. This paper studies a UAV-assisted data collection system where stochastic energyharvesting sensors generate data packets probabilistically in each time slot. We aim to jointly minimize the global average Age of Synchronization (AoS) and the UAV's energy consumption. The inherent uncertainty of AoS prior to UAV's visits renders conventional Age of Information (AoI) oriented optimization methods inapplicable. To tackle this issue, we formulate a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and introduce the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework incorporated with a novel Delayed Reward Shaping mechanism (DRS-TD3). The proposed algorithm demonstrates strong performance in addressing the sparse reward issue for UAV trajectory optimization. Experimental results validate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior performance and enhances robustness compared to baseline methods, significantly reducing the weighted sum of the average AoS and UAV energy consumption.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: High-Resolution Multipath Delay Estimation for ISAC-Based Terminal Proximity Sensing.
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced scheme for the subspace-based high-resolution multipath delay estimation algorithm, targeting at full-duplex (FD) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) based proximity sensing applications at terminal devices. First, we propose to calibrate, in an online manner, the imperfect phase alignment among different frequency bands using the self-interference (SI) signal, which should be considered when aggregating non-contiguous multiband communication signals for proximity sensing. Second, we introduce a DFT-like transformation operation to transform the frequency-domain (FDom) covariance-like measurement matrix (CMM) into a truncated delay domain (DDom) before performing the subspace-based estimation, leveraging the fact that proximity sensing operates only within a limited range. Finally, a subspace-based de-ambiguity method is developed to eliminate ghost targets, addressing the target ambiguity caused by the non-contiguous frequency allocation of the sensing signals. Simulation results show that the proposed methods can achieve centimeter-level ranging accuracy using Fifth Generation (5 G) New Radio (NR) compliant communication signals.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Reasoning Meets Adaptation: Bridging Global LLM Planning and Distributed UAV Control.
abstract: Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs) provide rapid and flexible communication infrastructures in mission-critical scenarios such as disaster response and emergency connectivity. However, establishing a connected FANET in dynamic environments is challenging due to the NP-hard nature of jointly addressing trajectory planning, obstacle avoidance, and connectivity maintenance. In this paper, we propose a Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted hierarchical framework that combines global reasoning from an LLM with distributed local execution by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The LLM generates global coordination points by solving a relaxed placement problem, whereas UAVs locally refine their trajectories using a lightweight local policy to ensure obstacle avoidance and connectivity. Through UAVNetSim-based simulations, we evaluate five LLMs under realistic mobility, channel, and obstacle settings. The simulation results show that the proposed framework achieves a packet delivery ratio above 95 % across all models, reduces execution time by up to an order of magnitude compared to obstacle-aware global planning and A* baselines, and sustains low end-to-end delay and high throughput even in complex environments. These findings highlight the potential of integrating LLM-based reasoning with distributed UAV control for scalable and adaptive FANET formation in real-world deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Comparative Analysis of Differential and Collision Entropy for Finite-Regime QKD in Hybrid Quantum Noisy Channels.
abstract: In this work, a comparative study between three fundamental entropic measures, differential entropy, quantum Rényi entropy, and quantum collision entropy for a hybrid quantum channel (HQC) was investigated, where hybrid quantum noise (HQN) is characterized by both discrete and continuous variables (CV) noise components. Using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) to statistically model the HQN, we construct as well as visualize the corresponding pointwise entropic functions in a given 3D probabilistic landscape. When integrated over the relevant state space, these entropic surfaces yield values of the respective global entropy. Through analytical and numerical evaluation, it is demonstrated that the differential entropy approaches the quantum collision entropy under certain mixing conditions, which aligns with the Rényi entropy for order$\alpha=2$. Within the HQC framework, the results establish a theoretical and computational equivalence between these measures. This provides a unified perspective on quantifying uncertainty in hybrid quantum communication systems. Extending the analysis to the operational domain of finite-key QKD, we demonstrated that the same 10 % approximation threshold corresponds to an order-of-magnitude change in Eve's success probability and a measurable reduction in the secure key rate.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel On-Policy Deep Actor-Critic Framework for NOMA-Enabled RIS-Aided Cell-Free mMIMO.
abstract: This paper investigates a non-orthogonal multiple access enabled reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) aided cellfree massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) system by designing optimal RIS beamforming to maximize the achievable throughput, while considering imperfect channel state information and spatial correlation. Most existing studies primarily focus on off-policy deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based RIS phase shifts designing in conventional RIS-assisted cellular systems. However, there is a lack of research in applying on-policy DRL methods for designing optimal RIS phase shifts in a more complex scenario of RISaided CF-mMIMO systems. To address the formulated nonconvex throughput maximization problem, a novel on-policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed within a Markov decision process framework, namely Enhanced Advantage Actor-Critic (E-A2C). E-A2C offers improved exploration efficiency through its advantage function and multi-worker agent learning structure. Numerical results validate the stability, convergence, and optimality of the proposed E-A2C algorithm. Furthermore, the proposed E-A2C algorithm demonstrates superior throughput performance compared to the baseline schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Quantum-Neuromorphic Hybrid Architecture for Energy-Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination in Distributed Healthcare Networks.
abstract: This study introduces a hybrid quantum-neuromorphic computing architecture for multi-agent wireless healthcare networks that must meet strict energy, latency, and reliability requirements. My approach separates global optimization from real-time execution by combining Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) for system-wide coordination with Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) running on neuromorphic hardware for ultra-low-power local decision making. To reduce communication overhead, I propose a Quantum-inspired Spike-Timing Protocol (QSTP), which converts a quantum-derived correlation structure into spike-timing patterns that enable event-driven coordination with minimal beaconing. I implemented a VQC-based multi-agent resource allocation method (QC-MARA) and deployed policy execution using STDP-enabled spiking agents. Across a 12-agent Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) under interference and mobility, the proposed system achieves a 78% energy reduction compared with classical deep reinforcement learning while maintaining sub-50 ms end-toend latency and$99.9 {\%}+$packet delivery reliability, supporting safety-critical medical monitoring and long-term operation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dynamic Edge-User Scheduling and Hybrid Precoding for Cell-Free mmWave MIMO Networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Design of an Integrated Sensing and Communication System Based on IM-OCDM.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) has emerged as a key enabling technology for next-generation wireless networks. However, conventional ISAC systems based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) suffer performance degradation and limited sensing resolution under multipath propagation. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an ISAC framework built on orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM), whose waveform structure provides enhanced robustness against multi-path interference. Furthermore, index modulation (IM) is incorporated into the OCDM-ISAC design to implicitly convey additional information bits through activated subcarrier indices, thereby improving spectral efficiency. At the receiver, a joint equalization and lowcomplexity log-likelihood ratio (LLR)-based detection scheme is employed for communication symbols, whereas a highaccuracy cyclic cross-correlation (CCC)-based algorithm is adopted for target parameter estimation in radar sensing. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed IM-OCDM-ISAC system outperforms the conventional OFDM-ISAC, providing more reliable communication performance in multipath channels and achieving higher sensing resolution.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Graph Neural Network-Based End-to-End Learning for Multi-User MIMO Systems.
abstract: End-to-end (E2E) learning has recently been proposed to jointly design the modulator and symbol detector by using deep neural networks (DNNs). However, existing schemes lack sufficient capability to cancel multi-user interference (MUI) in uplink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. In this paper, we propose a graph neural network (GNN)-based E2E learning scheme that employs a GNN-based modulator to generate learned constellation points, and a GNN-based detector to cancel MUI. They are jointly optimized to minimize the symbol error rate (SER) performance loss. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed E2E outperforms existing schemes with a predefined modulator. Specifically, it achieves an approximate 2 dB gain in a high MUI environment and surpasses even the maximum-likelihood (ML) detector in a low MUI condition.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Effective Rate Analysis and Optimization of THz-NOMA System Using Fox's H-Function with ME and THI.
abstract: Unlike conventional wireless systems tolerating higher transmission delays, emerging delay-sensitive and mission-critical applications demand ultra-low latency and high reliability. In such scenarios, impairment like misalignment errors (ME) and transceiver hardware impairments (THI) critically affect system performance and compromise quality of service (QoS). Thus, this work analyzes the effective rate of a THz-based NOMA system considering ME and THI effects. Closed-form probability density function (PDF) and cumulative density function (CDF) are derived using Fox's Hfunction to characterize the channel behavior under various THz fading conditions accurately. Interestingly, although the PDF of the instantaneous signal-to-noise ratio appears relatively simple in form, its application in analyzing wireless system performance metrics becomes mathematically intricate. Hence, for the effective rate analysis, we adopt the same methodological framework as presented in [1]. Both fixed and adaptive antennaarray configuration are evaluated, demonstrating that adaptive optimization significantly enhances the effective rate. Finally, the presented analytical results are thoroughly validated through extensive simulation, where their accuracy is confirmed by close assessment with the corresponding Monte-Carlo simulation results.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Emergency UAV Networks for 5G and Beyond: DRQN-Based Task Allocation and NTN-Aware Uplink Optimization.
abstract: This paper introduces an intelligent framework for emergency drone networks that harness the capabilities of 5G and beyond, integrating deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to enable autonomous task allocation and uplink channel optimization. At the heart of the system is a Deep Recurrent Q-Network (DRQN), which consistently outperforms traditional approaches in disaster response scenarios. The proposed architecture incorporates realistic uplink channel modeling, accounting for disaster-induced impairments such as path attenuation and multipath fading. Simulation results demonstrate that DRQN achieves a mission success rate of 94.63 % with an average response time of 9.92 seconds, surpassing Deep Q-Learning (DQL), which records 89.74 % success and 12.70 seconds response time. Beyond emergency applications, the framework is scalable to largescale drone fleets and adaptable to urban delivery systems, where autonomous coordination and communication reliability are equally critical. This work lays a foundation for nextgeneration aerial systems that combine artificial intelligence with advanced wireless technologies to deliver resilient, sustainable, efficient, and intelligent operations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: PPO-Optimized RIS for Reliable 5G and Beyond Subterranean Tunnel Communications.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6 G) wireless networks are expected to extend connectivity into challenging environments such as underwater systems, subterranean tunnels, and deep mining operations. Underground tunnels pose severe communication challenges due to high path loss, multipath fading, and limited line-of-sight. While 5 G millimeter-wave (mmWave) systems at 28 GHz offer high throughput and low latency, their performance underground remains constrained. To address this, we propose a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted architecture enhanced by Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), employing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for real-time adaptive control. The PPO-based framework dynamically tunes RIS parameters under uncertain channel conditions, improving coverage and reliability. Simulation results show gains of 209.7% in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), 177.1% in channel capacity, and 74.3% in coverage compared to baseline systems. The proposed RIS-PPO framework provides a robust foundation for scalable wireless deployment in mining and tunnel operations, supporting 5G and beyond.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: GrCLR: Gradient Contrastive Learning for Human Motion Recognition Using Gradient Radar Combination Map.
abstract: Millimeter-wave FMCW radar offers privacypreserving, contact-free human-motion sensing, yet indoor deployments suffer from angular ambiguity and multipath reflections. The proposed GrCLR radar-camera fusion framework mitigates these issues by converting each radar frame into Range-Doppler, Range-Azimuth, and Range-Elevation maps, weighting them by recency, and merging them into a single Gradient-Radar Combination Map embedded in the RGB channels. Dedicated radar and camera encoders are then trained with temporally weighted cross-modal contrastive learning, bring positive samples closer and push negative samples apart. This strategy lifts radar-only recognition accuracy by 9 % over a gradient-free baseline and 4 % over a time-weight-free baseline, while retaining robust indoor performance and seamless extensibility to integrated sensing-communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive Topology Snapshot Updating in LEO Satellite Networks Using Deep Q-Networks.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations provide global network coverage but face challenges arising from highly dynamic and rapidly changing topologies. Fully dynamic routing introduces excessive computational and signaling overhead, while traditional snapshot-based topology management struggles to balance update frequency and accuracy. This paper proposes a dynamic snapshot update mechanism based on a Deep Q-Network (DQN), which learns to determine when a new topology snapshot is necessary under varying network conditions. By adaptively controlling snapshot updates, the proposed method reduces long-term computational overhead while maintaining accurate routing decisions. Simulation results show that the DQN-based strategy achieves lower packet loss, higher throughput, and significantly fewer snapshot updates compared with conventional approaches.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: CKM Beyond Channel Gain: Spatial Correlation Map Construction with Deep Learning.
abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) is a promising technique to achieve environment-aware wireless communication and sensing. Constructing the complete CKM based on channel knowledge observations at sparse locations is a fundamental problem for CKM-enabled wireless networks. However, most existing works on CKM construction only consider the special type of CKM, i.e., the channel gain map (CGM), which only records the channel gain value for each location. In this paper, we consider the channel spatial correlation map (SCM) construction, which signifies the location-specific spatial correlation matrix for multi-antenna systems. Unlike CGM construction, constructing SCM poses significant challenges due to its extremely highdimensional structure. To address this issue, we first decompose the high-dimensional SCM into lower-dimensional path gain map (PGM) and path angle map (PAM).
