Then we propose a deep learning model termed E-SRResNet for constructing high-quality SCM from sparse samples, which incorporates multi-head attention (MHA) mechanisms and multi-scale feature fusion (MSFF) to accurately model both local and global spatial relationships of channel parameters and complex nonlinear mappings. Furthermore, we preprocess the dataset to provide priors including line-of-sight (LoS) map, binary building map and base station (BS) map for the model to reconstruct SCM more accurately. Simulations conducted on the CKMImageNet dataset demonstrate that the proposed E-SRResNet achieves significant performance improvements over baseline methods. Moreover, the cosine similarity between the constructed SCM and the ground truth exceeds 0.8 in most regions, validating the effectiveness of the proposed construction method.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Average Age of Synchronization in Status Update System with Periodic Updating.
abstract: In this paper, we consider a status update system with periodic updating scheme, where multiple sensors monitor their respective target sources that undergo random state changes and transmit the sensing information to the server. The server aims to perform timely and synchronized monitoring of the source with respect to the Age of synchronization (AoS). By incorporating the periodic updating scheme and transmission deadline, we derive closed-form expressions for the status synchronization probability and the average AoS. Based on the analysis, the impact of sampling interval and transmission deadline on the average AoS is investigated. Moreover, under low update frequency constraints, we further develop a squareroot approximation and an alternating optimization algorithm to minimize the average weighted AoS by jointly optimizing the sampling frequencies and transmission deadlines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Model Splitting and Computing Resource Allocation for Collaborative Edge-Device LLM Inference: A Transformer-Enhanced DRL Approach.
abstract: The edge-device collaborative computing paradigm enables low-latency AI inference while preserving privacy, particularly for deep neural networks (DNNs). However, existing model splitting approaches, primarily designed for DNNs, fail to account for the distinct computational characteristics between the prefill and decoding phases in large language model (LLM) inference, often resulting in excessive latency. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel collaborative edge-device LLM inference framework that decouples the prefill and decoding stages and strategically partitions the model between the edge server and the end device, balancing latency and privacy. We further formulate a joint optimization problem for split point selection and resource allocation to minimize inference latency. To solve this problem, a transformer-enhanced actor-critic (A2C) algorithm is developed. By incorporating a transformer encoder, the algorithm captures global system states and inter-user dependencies, thereby supporting effective multi-user decision-making in dynamic environments, such as fluctuating channel conditions, varying numbers of users, and diverse user attributes, without retraining. Comprehensive simulations validate that our framework significantly outperforms existing baselines across key performance metrics, including latency and energy consumption.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low-Complexity Sniffer-Based Port Selection for Fluid Antenna OTFS Systems Under Time-Varying Channels.
abstract: A fluid antenna system (FAS) enables dynamic port switching and spatial diversity, but faces challenges in rapidly varying channels due to the high switching overhead. We first propose a novel orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) system integrated with a double-droplet FAS architecture, where two independently controlled droplets support rapid port switching in response to channel changes. This allows the OTFS receiver to dynamically adapt to the time-varying environment. Based on this, we further propose a low-complexity “sniffer” port switching method for the first time. In each frame, one port is used for decoding while the other “sniffs” nearby ports to gather additional channel information. The proposed approach achieves improved diversity gains and significantly reduced switching overhead compared to conventional single-droplet baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Design and Experimental Validation of a Low-Jitter and High-Reliability VLC System for Industrial Internet-of-Things.
abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end visible light communication (VLC) system for Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications. The system employs a laser diode (LD) transmitter and photomultiplier tube (PMT) receiver, with Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based low-density paritycheck (LDPC) coding and custom signal conditioning circuits. A timestamp-embedded frame structure is designed to isolate network interface-induced latency, enabling accurate jitter measurement. Experiments under mobility and industrial smoke are conducted using a sliding rail and fog generator. Experimental results show that within the effective communication area, the system achieves a delay jitter less than$2 \mu$s with zero packet error and loss rates when network interface effects are excluded. The system demonstrates strong robustness in dynamic and harsh environments, offering a promising solution for reliable human-machine and machine-to-machine communication in IIoT scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Unified Trellis Design for Realizing Pilot-Symbol-Less Wireless Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a unified trellis-based estimation and detection approach for realizing Pilot-SymbolLess (PSL) wireless communications. We incorporate the prior knowledge to the data symbols and make them become a special art of Reference Signal (RS), i.e. PSL symbols, which is the key design philosophy of PSL communication. PSL communication does not assign dedicated wireless resource for the conventional pilots purpose, and is thus free of the pilot overhead. In order to approach the PSL effect, we can exploit either differential coding to integrate the prior knowledge through Differential Phase Shift Keying (DPSK) based PSL symbols or standard compliant Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) based PSL symbols. The unified trellis structure will facilitate the joint channel estimation, channel tracking and data detection. Furthermore, we extend the trellis design to support the Multiple-Input MultipleOutput (MIMO) and massive MIMO (mMIMO) systems without introducing exponential increasing of the state nodes in the trellis, which leads to acceptable implementation complexity. Numerical simulations exhibit that mMIMO systems will be benefited from PSL philosophy due to rich spatial diversity, even preferably for medium and high mobility scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Learning Doppler-Resilient Keys via CNN-Based Channel Mapping for UAV Communications.
abstract: Physical layer key generation (PLKG) offers a lightweight and scalable approach to securing wireless communications by exploiting the reciprocity and randomness of the channel. However, in high-mobility scenarios such as unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications, rapid channel variations and reduced coherence time undermine channel reciprocity, significantly degrading the reliability of PLKG. In this work, we propose a Doppler-resilient PLKG framework to improve key generation performance in dynamic wireless environments. We develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model that learns to map the channel frequency response (CFR) observed at the ground control station (GCS) to the corresponding CFR at the UAV. By integrating Doppler frequency and CFR through a feature fusion layer, the framework adapts to varying mobility conditions and enables stable key generation across different Doppler scenarios. A unified model is trained on aggregated datasets to support robust performance without requiring Doppler-specific tuning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior key consistency and adaptability, significantly reducing the key disagreement rate (KDR) compared with existing deep learning-based approaches across a wide range of Doppler frequencies.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Real-Time Pollution Detection for IIoT: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Offloading Framework for Multi-Tier Satellite Networks.
abstract: Continuous and real-time pollution detection in industrial environments within the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is crucial for maintaining ecological balance and ensuring the safe operation of industrial facilities. However, traditional pollution detection methods suffer from limitations in coverage and data timeliness. In recent years, the rapid development of satellite remote sensing technology has provided new opportunities to address these challenges. To this end, we propose an edge computing framework integrating satellite remote sensing with IIoT. This approach deploys deep learning models for pollution detection directly on satellites, enabling real-time on-orbit analysis and processing of captured images and downlinking only key detection results (e.g., pollution location, type, and extent), thereby significantly enhancing response speed. We first outline the architecture and processing workflow of this edge computing system, followed by the development of a hybrid Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) and Decision Transformer (DT) reinforcement learning algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method dynamically optimizes the trade-off between processing accuracy and latency in pollution detection tasks under strict delay constraints, thus meeting the urgent demands for high timeliness and wide coverage in IIoT scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Detection Model for Ultrasonic Pulse-Based Intra-Body Communications.
abstract: Intra-body communication (IBC) technology can enable revolutionary medical applications. To achieve safe and reliable IBCs, ultrasonic pulse signals can effectively mitigate multipath effects and heating issues, benefiting from their high resolution and low duty cycle. However, the detection of ultrasonic pulses faces challenges, including transient waveform distortion and strong temporal correlation caused by multipath propagation. To achieve high reliability, this paper proposes a hybrid convolutional neural network and long-short term memory (CNN-LSTM) detection model for detecting ultrasonic pulse signals. The CNN module is used to automatically extract local spatial features from the received signal, and these features are then used as input to the LSTM module that utilizes the temporal dependencies of the input. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations are conducted to compare the bit-error rate (BER) performance of deep learning-based models, including LSTM and CNN-LSTM models, with traditional matched filter (MF) receivers and energy detection (ED) receivers. Simulation results show that the CNNLSTM model can achieve a significantly lower BER than the LSTM model and the MF and ED receivers, demonstrating the superiority of the proposed CNN-LSTM detection model for reliable ultrasonic IBCs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A MAML-TCN-Based Approach to LEO Satellite Network Traffic Forecasting.
abstract: Traffic prediction plays a crucial role in routing decisions, resource allocation, and load balancing for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, serving as a key approach to improving network Quality of Service (QoS). However, the high dynamics of LEO networks and the limited onboard resources pose great challenges to traffic prediction algorithms. In addition to achieving high accuracy, the algorithms must also ensure high sensitivity and low resource consumption. To address these challenges, we propose a novel LEO satellite network traffic forecasting model named CMT-TF, which achieves high prediction accuracy while maintaining strong sensitivity and low resource overhead. Specifically, CMT-TF employs the Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) framework to optimize the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN)'s parameter initialization across multiple tasks, enabling rapid adaptation and outstanding performance in new scenarios. Furthermore, we introduce a Cumulative Step Loss (CSL) mechanism during the MAML training process to fully exploit losses from all inner-loop steps, thereby accelerating convergence and enhancing prediction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with baseline models, CMT-TF improves prediction accuracy by 18.3 %-48.7 %, reduces memory usage by 35.7 %, and shortens training time by 42.4 %, showcasing its accuracy, sensitivity and efficiency for LEO satellite traffic forecasting.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Ultra-Low-Complexity Multigroup Multicast Beamforming in Frame-Based Geo Satellite Communication.
abstract: Multicast transmission have been widely adopted in geosynchronous satellites for resource efficiency. This paper proposes an ultra-low-complexity multigroup multicast beamforming algorithm using nonlinear eigenvalue problem (NEPv) formulation and Lagrange dual decomposition (LDD). Specifically, we formulate a sum rate maximization (SRM) problem under power and quality of service (QoS) constraints. By decoupling the problem, we optimize beam directions via NEPv while reallocating power by LDD to satisfy the constraints. Unlike conventional successive convex approximation (SCA) methods, our approach addresses first-order optimality directly to obtain semi-closedform solutions. Simulations show that the proposed NEPv-LDD performs near-identically to existing SCA-based algorithms while reducing computation time to$0.6 \%-2 \%$.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On-Demand Delivery Scheduling for UAVs with Heterogeneous Orders: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: While unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) exhibit enormous potential in last-mile delivery service, challenges arise for efficient UAV delivery scheduling. In reality, delivery orders dynamically emerge in an on-demand pattern that traditional optimization struggles to adapt to. Meanwhile, existing works neglect the presence of heterogeneous delivery orders, which exhibit distinct priorities and implicit characteristics. In response, this paper proposes an efficient UAV delivery scheduling approach, termed HGA-DRL (Hierarchical Gated Attention-based DRL), that jointly tackles delivery task assignment and energy replenishment under on-demand order-heterogeneous conditions. Specifically, a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) is modeled to enhance long-horizon decision dependencies that traditional RL-based approaches struggle to capture. In addition, HGA-DRL integrates a GRU-based temporal module and a cross-attention mechanism to learn implicit representations of delivery status, enhancing the adaptability to dynamic delivery environments. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach develops an energy-aware and order-specific strategy, effectively improving delivery throughput and reducing delay.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Toward Multi-Service Atomic Receivers: Co-Referenced, Co-Located Detection of Sub-MHz and Microwave Signals.
abstract: Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks (SAGINs) require sensing infrastructures covering sub-MHz to microwave frequencies. While Rydberg sensors offer ultra-wideband capabilities, a unified framework for concurrent detection remains unexplored. This paper proposes a unified atomic receiver simultaneously recovering microwave waveforms via LO-assisted mixing and sub-MHz fields via bias-assisted Stark modulation. We develop a linearized equivalent baseband model that transforms stiff time-domain dynamics into a rapid frequency-domain solution. Our analysis reveals a fundamental trade-off: the strong LO field required for microwave mixing induces Autler-Townes broadening, suppressing the spectral slope essential for lowfrequency detection. Consequently, we formulate a systematic strategy to reconfigure the receiver for microwave-priority, low-frequency-priority, or balanced sensing. By unifying disparate modalities within a single quantum aperture, this work offers a vital solution to reduce hardware complexity for size-constrained integrated sensing and communications platforms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Version Age of Information Oriented Risk-Sensitive Scheduling with Distributional Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Timely delivery of fresh information is critical in real-time wireless systems, where outdated updates can compromise performance or safety. The recently proposed Version Age of Information (VAoI) extends the classical Age of Information (AoI) by measuring the version gap between transmitted and received updates, capturing freshness in version-asynchronous environments. Existing works primarily optimize average AoI or VAoI, overlooking rare but catastrophic staleness events. To address this gap, we study a risk-sensitive VAoI scheduling problem in multiuser wireless networks under resource constraints, formulated as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). Unlike conventional reinforcement learning, which estimates only expected returns, our approach leverages distributional DRL (C51, QR-DQN, IQN) to model the full return distribution, enabling optimization of the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR), a principled risk measure that quantifies extreme VAoI realizations beyond the mean. We design a scheduling framework that minimizes CVaR of VAoI while respecting resource budgets. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method not only maintains competitive average VAoI but also significantly reduces the CVaR of VAoI in IQN-based implementations, providing a flexible trade-off between average performance and tail-risk mitigation. These results highlight the essential role of distributional learning for robust, low-risk status update scheduling in wireless systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Resource Allocation of SIM-Aided Integrated Communication and Computation in 6G Networks.
abstract: To alleviate the multi-service conflicts in sixthgeneration (6G) networks, this paper investigates an integrated communication and computation (ICC) system aided by a stacked intelligent metasurface (SIM). The 6G ICC system is desired to support coexisting over-the-air computation (AirComp) tasks with high-precision data aggregation, and traditional communication tasks with high-quality data transmission under the same radio resource. To this end, we design a joint resource allocation framework for SIM-aided ICC with the goal of minimizing the total computation mean squared error (MSE) while meeting the communication quality of service (QoS) constraints. An efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed to solve the formulated joint resource allocation problem. Simulation results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves rapid convergence and significantly outperforms benchmark schemes, highlighting SIM's potential for enabling efficient and harmonious 6G ICC system.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Large Language Model-Based Decision Transformer Approach for UAV Data Collection.
abstract: The deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for data collection from spatially distributed devices holds great promise in supporting diverse Internet of Things (IoT) applications. While reinforcement learning (RL) has been extensively explored for UAV trajectory optimization, its interactive nature entails high costs and risks in real-world environments. To address these challenges, we propose a large language model (LLM)-empowered critic-regularized decision transformer (DT) framework, termed LLM-CRDT, to learn effective UAV control policies. In LLM-CRDT, we incorporate critic networks to regularize the DT model training, thereby integrating the sequence modeling capabilities of DT with critic-based value guidance to enable learning effective policies from suboptimal datasets. Furthermore, we employ a pre-trained LLM as the transformer backbone of the DT model and adopt a parameter-efficient finetuning strategy, i.e., LoRA, enabling rapid adaptation to UAV control tasks with small-scale dataset and low computational overhead. Simulations demonstrate that LLM-CRDT outperforms benchmark online and offline RL methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Communication-Control Co-Design in Industrial IoT: A Hybrid Soft Actor Dual-Critic Algorithm.
abstract: In wireless Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems, constrained communication resources have become a critical bottleneck that affects control performance. Issues such as limited bandwidth and transmission delays significantly hinder system stability and response efficiency. To address this challenge, we propose a communication-control co-design framework that leverages reinforcement learning to jointly optimize dynamic bandwidth allocation and control commands. Specifically, a Hybrid Soft Actor Dual-Critic (HSADC) algorithm is developed, where two critic networks are designed to evaluate system stability and task-oriented rewards, respectively. An actor network then integrates these evaluations to jointly generate control commands and bandwidth allocation decisions, while an action projection mechanism is introduced to ensure compliance with bandwidth constraints. In addition, to improve sampling efficiency in high-dimensional action spaces, a hybrid control command is constructed. Simulation experiments on a dualarm robotic manipulation task demonstrate that the proposed HSADC algorithm outperforms traditional methods in terms of convergence speed, control stability, and robustness, validating its effectiveness in bandwidth-constrained industrial environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dual-Function Waveform Design for ISAC Systems with Equalized Constructive Interference.
abstract: This paper presents a joint optimization framework for the dual-functional transmit waveform and the communication equalization coefficients in a MIMO integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. To provide more degrees of design freedom, the concept of equalized constructive interference (ECI) is proposed, extending conventional constructive interference (CI) to the equalized communication symbols. An adaptive relaxation factor is further introduced to the ECI in the case of QAM, to flexibly balance interference exploitation and demodulation reliability. The optimization maximizes radar SINR under ECI and power constraints, and is efficiently solved using successive convex approximation (SCA). Simulation results verify that the proposed ECI scheme achieves improved sensing performance under guaranteed communication quality, compared with conventional CI-based schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Intent-Driven Network Optimization Copilot with a Dual-Check Cognitive Agent.
abstract: Traditional network optimization requires a severalmonth life-cycle to develop a solution for a specific task. This is inefficient for continuously evolving wireless network infrastructure and technologies, leading to the need for constantly developing new solutions for new tasks and re-developing solutions for existing ones. While Large Language Models (LLMs) show potential for autonomous solution development, they are still significantly limited by hallucination, amnesia, and limited context windows issues, hindering their wider application in critical wireless network infrastructure. This paper proposes an Intent-Driven Network Optimization Copilot (NO-Copilot), designed to automate the entire network optimization life-cycle based on a newly-devised cognitive agent. This agent remarkably enhances LLM reliability by synergistically integrating a cognitive kernel for reasoning, structured memory for learning, a high-fidelity network environment for experimentation, and an adversarial challenger for validation. Our extensive experiments on a complex, cross-layer 3D reconstruction optimization task demonstrate the superior performance and reliability of NOCopilot.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning-Aided Joint Design of Beam Hopping and Robust Precoding for LEO Satellite Communication Systems.
abstract: In this paper, a deep learning (DL) aided joint intelligent optimization framework of beam hopping and robust precoding is proposed for low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems to mitigate severe inter-beam interference and match dynamic ground traffic demands. Specifically, a robust precoding network is designed in the context of imperfect channel state information (CSI), leveraging unsupervised deep learning (DL) that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and attention mechanisms. Building upon the precoding network, an adaptive beam scheduling strategy is further incorporated into the joint framework and optimized via the advantage actorcritic (A2C) reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm to enhance system throughput and reduce average delay. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves system throughput by up to 23.85 % and reduces average delay by up to 29.36 % compared with the baseline algorithms under heavy traffic load.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: INTo6: In-Band Network Telemetry Over IPv6.
abstract: As a representative of network telemetry, In-band Network Telemetry (INT) has become a popular solution for network measurement. INT enables network devices to collect real-time state information based on telemetry instructions and embed the telemetry data into the INT header of forwarding packets, thereby addressing the “black box” limitation inherent in traditional end-to-end measurement methods. Nevertheless, the current INT standard exhibits poor adaptability to IPv6 and presents three major challenges. First, its modification of key packet header fields may interfere with standard packet processing and introduce security vulnerabilities. Second, its scenario-specific header formats increase complexity for network management and device implementation. Third, its deployment is hindered by the lack of INT support in most legacy network devices, necessitating a solution for transparent transmission in hybrid networks. This paper proposes INTo6 (INT over IPv6), which designs an INT option in the IPv6 hop-by-hop extension header, seamlessly integrating network telemetry and data forwarding. The prototype system and the physical testbed have verified the integrity, correctness, and measurement performance of INTo6. Experimental results demonstrate that INTo6 ensures smooth packet forwarding and efficient programmable node processing. Moreover, INTo6 is capable of measuring nanosecond-level latency, monitoring queue status, locating network congestion, and evaluating congestion control algorithms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dynamic Carbon-Aware Hybrid Task Offloading for Collaborative Edge-Cloud Computing.
abstract: Collaborative edge-cloud computing is an emerging paradigm that balances processing efficiency and user experience by offloading edge workloads to the cloud (i.e., vertical offloading). Adding the option of horizontal offloading (i.e., edge-to-edge offloading) can further enhance the flexibility of this architecture. However, prior work ignored temporal and spatial variations in carbon emissions when making offloading decisions. Our study aims to jointly optimize the carbon footprint and the balance of edge servers' workloads, which is challenged by dynamic workload arrivals to edge servers and time-and-location-varying carbon intensity (CI). We propose an online algorithm Lyapunov optimization framework to configure offloading workload and transmission power for mixed vertical and horizontal offloading. Simulations based on historical CI data reveal that the proposed algorithm can efficiently reduce carbon footprint while balancing queue backlogs among edge and cloud servers.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for Adaptive Resource Allocation of UAV-enabled ISAC Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive resource allocation scheme for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, in which communication and sensing resources, including radio frequency (RF) chains and transmit power, are dynamically allocated to meet the varying task requirements in complex environments. Specifically, we first propose an adaptive scheduling mechanism that judiciously determines the ratio of resources allocated for communication. Accordingly, a hybrid beamforming scheme is introduced, where RF resources are allocated by the resource ratio to achieve dynamic communication and sensing resource distribution. Finally, an alternating optimization framework is developed to jointly optimize the UAV trajectory, resource allocation, and beamforming for maximizing the system's communication and sensing performance performance. Simulations validate that the proposed scheme can adaptively adjust the resource allocation strategy to better satisfy communication and sensing performance requirements due to complex environments and dynamic task demands, compared to various benchmarks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: GRLP-Based Resource Allocation for Multimodal Semantics and Bit Coexistence Communication in Heterogeneous Vehicle Networks.
abstract: Semantic communications are widely regarded as a key enabling technology for future sixth-generation (6 G) networks. The fundamental idea is to leverage deep neural networks to extract and compress task-relevant semantic information over end-to-end links, thereby significantly enhancing communication efficiency and intelligence. In future vehicular networks, connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HDVs) are expected to coexist for a long period: the former can be equipped with semantic transceivers, while the latter continue to operate with conventional transceivers. To meet the stringent communication requirements of vehicles during critical maneuvers (e.g., lane changes), we proposes a joint resource optimization approach tailored for heterogeneous vehicular networks. Specifically, we jointly optimize the beamforming matrix, power allocation, and the number of semantic symbols to maximize the weighted semantic rate of CAVs and the bit rate of HDVs. Meanwhile, lane-change probabilities are embedded into the objective function to enable resource prioritization for vehicles with potential lane-changing intentions. To this end, we design a framework based graph neural network (GNN) with deep reinforcement learning (DRL), while integrating lane-change prediction(GRLP). In this framework, vehicles are modeled as graph nodes, where a graph aggregation mechanism captures inter-vehicle correlations, and the resulting representations are fed into a reinforcement learning agent to derive optimal resource allocation strategies. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can adaptively configure resource for lane-changing vehicles, while preserving the communication performance of other vehicles, thereby significantly improving link reliability and system throughput.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Agent Path Planning for Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Control Systems.
abstract: To address the challenges of limited sensing range, high computational overhead, and insufficient real-time performance in path planning for automated guided vehicles (AGV) systems in dynamic industrial scenarios, this paper proposes a perception-driven conflict-based search (P-CBS) algorithm. This method constructs a sensing cost mapping model within an integrated sensing, communication, and control (ISCC) framework, which integrates sensing, communication, and control functions into wireless networks to achieve reciprocal enhancement. This allows the system to adaptively balance sensing update frequency against communication load during path control. Specifically, it converts visual detection information such as position, speed, and confidence into a confidence-weighted spatiotemporal Gaussian cost field. Soft constraints are introduced in the$\mathrm{A}^{*}$search algorithm to achieve continuous obstacle avoidance. Furthermore, an event-triggered replanning mechanism based on cost growth rate prediction is designed, initiating global planning only when high risks accumulate, reducing computational load. Finally, a communication-adaptive threshold adjustment strategy is introduced to maintain system stability and consistency in bandwidth-constrained environments. Simulation results show that compared with traditional CBS and global dynamic CBS algorithms, the proposed algorithm can reduce the frequency of global replanning by at least 83 % and improve system throughput by at least 12.5 %, verifying its efficiency and robustness in dynamic industrial scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Smartphone-Based Cooperative Perception.
abstract: We propose a lightweight cooperative perception architecture that leverages smartphones to enhance the situational awareness of non-autonomous vehicles in urban environments. Unlike most existing approaches requiring expensive sensors and dedicated communication modules, our system relies solely on standard smartphone capabilities-namely, the RGB camera and GPS-to detect surrounding vehicles and share their locations with a nearby edge server. The server performs spatio-temporal fusion of the received data and sends back a contextualized, augmented view of the environment to each user. Implemented and evaluated in the CARLA simulation platform, our solution achieves near real-time performance with an average end-to-end latency of 96 ms per frame and minimal communication overhead (0.35 KB for uplink, 0.15 KB for downlink). Experimental results show a significant increase in perception coverage and recall, especially for occluded vehicles. This work demonstrates the feasibility of smartphone-based cooperative sensing as a cost-effective alternative to V2X-based systems, with promising prospects for large-scale, infrastructureagnostic deployment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Delay- and Mobility-Aware Parallelized SFC Deployment in Space-Ground Integrated Networks.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) networks aim to deliver seamless global connectivity with ultra-low latency; however, meeting such requirements in remote and mobility-driven scenarios remains challenging. Space-Ground Integrated Networks (SGIN) combine satellite constellations and terrestrial infrastructures to provide ubiquitous coverage, while Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) enables flexible and dynamic service provisioning through software-based Virtual Network Functions (VNFs). Many emerging services rely on sequential Service Function Chains (SFCs), where cumulative VNF processing delays limit end-to-end performance. Parallelized SFCs (PSFCs) address this by enabling concurrent execution of independent VNFs, yet their realization in SGIN remains largely unexplored due to satellite mobility and heterogeneous resource distribution between space and ground segments. This paper presents one of the first studies on PSFC deployment in SGIN. We mathematically formulate the PSFC deployment problem and, given its NP-hard nature, propose DMPSFC—a Delay- and Mobility-aware Parallelized SFC deployment heuristic. DMPSFC predicts satellite availability, clusters ground nodes efficiently, and co-locates parallelizable VNFs to reduce packet duplication overhead. Simulation results demonstrate that proposed approach show$\text{1 9}-\text{2 3} \%$delay reduction,$\text{1 0} - \text{1 5 \%}$higher acceptance ratio, and$\text{1 0} - \text{2 8 \%}$better resource utilization compared to the state-of-the-art approaches.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: UAV-Enabled Movable Antenna Array Designs for Wireless Communications.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with movable antennas demonstrate significant potential for enhancing communication system performance, leveraging their platform mobility and antenna spatial degrees of freedom. To this end, this work proposes a joint optimization framework that aims to maximize the uplink communication rate by cooperatively optimizing the receive beamforming vector, user transmit power, and antenna positioning. Due to the highly coupled and non-convex nature of the problem, an iterative algorithm is developed to efficiently solve it. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves notable performance improvement compared to the conventional schemes with fixedposition antennas.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Tier Split Federated Learning for Multi-Level Personalization.
abstract: Achieving multi-level personalization in federated learning (FL) is increasingly important in multi-tier computing networks, where client preferences are influenced not only by individual data but also by regional environments. However, existing personalized FL approaches focus primarily on userspecific data and fail to capture this hierarchical structure. We propose Multi-Tier Split Federated Learning (MT-SFL), an efficient FL framework that enables multi-level personalization by integrating split learning with a multi-exit model architecture. MT-SFL performs both training and inference across different network tiers, reflecting heterogeneous computing capabilities and significantly reducing client-side computation, communication overhead, and inference latency. Simulation results demonstrate that MT-SFL effectively personalizes models to clientpreferred tasks while capturing broader regional and global preferences, providing a scalable and resource-adaptive solution for hierarchical FL systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multiuser Semi-Full-Duplexing With User Paring and Power Allocation.
abstract: While bands in the 7–24 GHz range are being considered for sixth-generation (6 G) beyond current FR1, and below FR2 (24.25-52.6 GHz), maximizing spectral efficiency remains critical. Full-duplex (FD) communication, enabled by advances in self-interference cancellation, offers a promising solution. This paper investigates a generalization of FD, namely semi-full-duplex (SFD), in a multiuser system to minimize total transmit power under an open radio access network scenario. Using time division multiple access, we formulate a power minimization problem divided into user pairing and resource allocation sub-problems. Simulations show that SFD provides greater flexibility and lower power consumption than pure FD while meeting target rates.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Physical-Sensing-Enhanced Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning for Multi-UAV Relaying in Low-Altitude Environments.
abstract: In low-altitude environments, a major challenge for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications is wireless link degradation caused by random terrain obstacles. However, the UAV's purely reactive avoidance system means it mechanically swerves around anything in its trajectory, consuming a significant amount of energy while failing to improve communication quality. To address this issue, we propose a Physical-Sensing-enhanced Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning (PS-GAIL) framework for multi-UAV relaying. The PS-GAIL mechanism enables relay UAVs to minimize energy consumption and avoid obstacles while maintaining high link quality, by leveraging data from onboard visual and radio sensors. Equipped with this mechanism, a relay UAV is capable of real-time trajectory planning and establishing an optimal-rate communication corridor, even in the absence of a prior environmental map. The simulation results demonstrate that, when compared to typical schemes such as Behavioral Cloning (BC) and Q-Mixing network (QMIX), the proposed PS-GAIL mechanism exhibits a superior capability in maintaining a consistently high average transmission rate while consuming minimal energy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Federated Multi-RIC Threat Intelligence for Secure and Scalable Open 6G Radio Access Networks.
abstract: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RANs) are a key component of future 6G systems. They rely on distributed intelligence and programmable control to support large-scale and heterogeneous services. However, this decentralization also introduces new security challenges. In particular, attacks may be distributed across multiple RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), while privacy and operational constraints limit centralized monitoring.In this paper, we propose a federated multi-RIC threat intelligence framework for Open 6G RANs. Each RIC locally learns threat patterns from its own telemetry and control data. A federated learning mechanism enables collaboration between RICs without sharing raw data. The proposed approach preserves privacy, scales to large deployments, and improves the detection of coordinated and stealthy attacks. We also present some insights on how the system tries to mitigate and respond to the threat. Results show that the proposed framework significantly outperforms local-only detection and closely approaches centralized intrusion detection while maintaining low communication and energy overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Semantic-Aware Learning-Based NOMA User Grouping for Programmable 6G RANs.
abstract: As wireless systems evolve toward task-oriented and semantic-aware communications, RAN control decisions must account not only for channel conditions but also for the semantic relevance of transmitted content. This paper treats dynamic user grouping in Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) as a programmable RAN control function, enabling flexible and policy-driven cluster formation beyond static channel-based designs. Building on this perspective, we propose a semanticaware NOMA user grouping framework in which grouping decisions incorporate semantic utility alongside channel conditions, enabling context-aware and service-driven clustering. Under this model, we benchmark brute-force grouping, classical heuristics, and a semantic greedy baseline (SG-NOMA), revealing the inherent limitations of myopic grouping strategies. To address these limitations, we introduce Semantic Q-learning NOMA (SQ-NOMA), a learning-driven grouping framework that allows grouping policies to improve through experience by maximizing long-term semantic utility. Simulation results show that SQNOMA consistently approaches the performance of optimal grouping while maintaining significantly lower computational complexity, demonstrating the effectiveness of learning-based programmability for intelligent 6G RAN control.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Vehicle Target Detection Based on ISAC-Vision System.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a vehicle target detection scheme based on integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) plus Vision system in urban scenarios. Specifically, we apply clutter suppression and Capon spectral estimation to obtain the range-angle (RA) spectrum. Then we design the CaponFormer network to detect and cluster vehicle targets from the RA spectrum. Meanwhile, we use YOLO11 and MiDaS to process the camera images and generate cropped RGB and depth images. Then a VisionFormer network is designed to extract deep visual features from the cropped images. Next, we design a fusion network to fuse the CaponFormer and VisionFormer features, which is followed by a decision-level fusion to simultaneously detect multiple vehicle targets. Experimental results demonstrate the higher F1-Score of the proposed scheme compared to single-modal schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Distributed Tokenization-Based Model for Multi-TRP Localization.
abstract: Location awareness is crucial for emerging applications and resource optimization in next-generation networks. In this context, multi-transmission reception point (TRP) systems specified in 3GPP 5G New Radio standards play a pivotal role by providing the rich spatial diversity required for high-precision localization. This paper proposes a localization technique for large-scale multi-TRP systems based on distributed tokenization, which reinterprets classical localization within a modern deep learning framework. To align with the procedures of classical localization, a transformer encoder distributed to each TRP extracts the tokens (i.e., latent representation of channel features) from the measurement and positional information of a set of selected TRPs. Then, a multi-head attention pooling layer at the central unit merges these tokens and produces the final position estimate. This procedure allows efficient model design in macro and micro urban areas with numerous TRPs, as well as improving localization accuracy. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm improves the localization accuracy by 40 percent compared to existing convolutional neural network and transformer-based methods, in the 40,000 square meter urban area.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: QTCAJOSA: Low-Complexity Joint Offloading and Subchannel Allocation for NTN-Enabled IoT.
abstract: In this work, we consider the resource allocation problem for task offloading from Internet of Things (IoT) devices, to a non-terrestrial network.The architecture considers clusters of IoT devices that offload their tasks to a dedicated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) serving as a multi-access edge computing (MEC) server, which can compute the task or further offload it to an available high-altitude platform station (HAPS) or to a lowearth orbit (LEO) satellite for remote computing.We formulate a problem that has as objective the minimization of the weighted sum delay of the tasks.Given the non-convex nature of the problem, and acknowledging that the complexity of the optimization algorithms impact their performance, we derive a lowcomplexity joint subchannel allocation and offloading decision algorithm with dynamic computing resource initialization, developed as a greedy heuristic based on convex optimization criteria.Simulations show the reduced delay obtained by including the different non-terrestrial nodes against architectures without them and state of the art benchmarks.Index Terms-multi-access edge
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Topology Semantic Routing in Multi-Layer Satellite Networks.
abstract: Mega-constellations introduce frequent and predictable topological changes due to orbital motion, link dynamics, and weather-affected feeder availability. Classical routing approaches relying on global re-signaling are unable to maintain stable connectivity under such dynamics, leading to increased overhead, delayed convergence, and degraded delivery. In this article, we introduce the topology semantic routing concept that enables space nodes to adapt their forwarding behavior based on local and momentary topology interpretation. Routing protocol signaling is deferred or avoided for transient or expected changes, and path selection is adjusted using time-aligned information or localized failure detection. The mechanism integrates with distributed and centralized frameworks and is suited for homomorphic and cyclic topologies, frequently occurring in mega-constellations. Furthermore, the results of a simulation-based evaluation under orbital shifts, feeder handovers, and link degradation show that time- and event-driven redirect strategies maintain delivery performance and reduce signaling overhead, confirming applicability in dynamic non-terrestrial infrastructures.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Beyond Link-Level Enhancements: System-Level Optimizations in AI-Native 6G RANs.
abstract: The increasing complexity of dense 6G RAN environments necessitates a paradigm shift from conventional linklevel optimization toward system-level control mechanisms that ensure intelligent coordination of radio resources, mobility, and device management across multiple coexisting RANs. Traditional optimization techniques, including advanced beamforming, modulation schemes, and interference mitigation, operate within isolated link boundaries, lacking the global awareness necessary for dense deployments. In contrast, system-wide AI-driven control frameworks enable holistic optimization, dynamically adjusting network parameters to adapt to fluctuating demand, user mobility patterns, and energy efficiency constraints. This paper proposes an AI-native system-level RAN control architecture, which redistributes core network functionalities to the edge and introduces a flexible deployment model: as part of C-RAN, as an independent edge core, or within the centralized network infrastructure. The proposed approach enhances power and frequency management, optimizes paging and mobility execution at the edge, and reduces core signaling overhead by executing localized resource coordination and interference control. AI plays a fundamental role in this transition, enabling real-time adaptive decision-making tailored to localized network conditions. By shifting from isolated, link-level improvements to a coordinated, AI-driven system-level optimization paradigm, the proposed framework enables efficient, scalable, and resilient dense RAN deployments. Future work will focus on prototype development and real-world validation, assessing the impact of AI-based RAN management and local mobility execution while ensuring seamless integration with existing 6G network architectures.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Multi-UAV Platform with 5G and NTN Backhaul for PPDR Scenarios.
abstract: As Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) become more widespread and accessible, their rapid deployment and flexibility make them valuable assets in Public Protection and Disaster Relief (PPDR) operations. However, when operated individually, UAVs are limited by their coverage range of action and are constrained to ground-based infrastructures. To mitigate these issues, this work proposes a fleet of UAVs designed to assist rescue teams in such catastrophe scenarios. The proposed approach considers a mesh of UAVs, building a mobile 5 G Base Station (BS) backhauled by mobile Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN). The UAVs, equipped with video and depth cameras, gather footage and distance metrics to capture live real-time feed of the scenes, and allow autonomous detection and tracking to follow relevant targets. To ensure seamless connectivity, a Wi-Fi mesh network connects the UAVs with dynamic routing to enable communication between nodes, as well as adapt the network to changes in topology. The proposed platform is tested in real scenarios, with an operational UAV mesh that supports the communication and mission requirements. The results show a successful connection to the Internet by the users in the ground, along with low latency of video streaming and object detection.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Analysis of a Frequency- and Phase-Keying Waveform for Joint Radar and Communication.
abstract: This paper considers a frequency- and phase-keying (FPK) waveform for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). Compared to FSK-based ISAC waveforms in the literature, the proposed waveform shows superior performance both in terms of data rates and radar global accuracy, while maintaining a constant modulus that is attractive in both communications and sensing. Also, while the proposed waveform has lower data rates than the state-of-the-art OFDM waveform, it shows similar radar performance while achieving low and constant PAPR. The ambiguity function (AF) is used as a tool to evaluate the radar performance of the FPK waveform. We show that incorporating phase modulation into the FSK waveform to produce the FPK waveform generally reduces the values of sidelobe levels (SLs) in the AF. To achieve this, we first derive an expression for the AF SLs of the FPK waveform. Since the AF SLs vary depending on the data embedded into the waveform, we analyze the distribution of the AF SLs. Furthermore, we provide two approximations of the distribution of the AF SL based on a random walk model and a Rayleigh model. While the Rayleigh approximation is easier to compute, numerical results show that the random walk approximation is more accurate, especially for waveforms with fewer subpulses and higher FSK modulation orders. Numerical examples illustrate the accuracy of our approximations and show the performance improvements of the FPK waveform compared to traditional FSK waveforms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Falcon: Random Network Distillation Enhanced Energy-Efficient Scheduling in Heterogeneous UAV-Enabled Edge Computing.
abstract: UAV-enabled edge computing offers dynamic service provisioning in scenarios where terrestrial infrastructure is overloaded or inaccessible. However, efficient workload scheduling in such hybrid systems is challenged by resource heterogeneity and stringent UAV energy constraints. To address these issues, we propose Falcon, a reinforcement learning-based scheduling framework that integrates Random Network Distillation (RND) with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to enhance exploration in sparse-reward environments. The scheduling problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with a composite reward function balancing resource utilization, load balancing, and energy efficiency. Intrinsic rewards from RND accelerate convergence by encouraging exploration of under-explored states, which reduce convergence time by 9.5%. Experiments on realworld workload traces from the Alibaba Cluster Trace Dataset demonstrate that Falcon outperforms k8s scheduling methods in resource utilization by 6.7% and energy consumption by 14.8%.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: UAV Path Planning for Joint Localization and Communications.
abstract: This paper studies the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for joint localization and communication. The UAV collects data from ground users over multiple rounds of the mission. We assume that users are located in given regions of uncertainty, and their exact positions are unknown. In each round, the UAV estimates users' positions using collected signals, thereby reducing location errors and facilitating data collection in subsequent rounds. We aim to minimize the UAV's total travel distance by optimizing its flight paths. The formulated problem is challenging to solve because the signals to be collected in future rounds are unavailable. A penalty-based approach is proposed to decompose the multiple-round problem into multiple per-round problems, which can be solved efficiently. The simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in comparison with several baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hierarchical Deep Learning for Joint Turbulence and PE Estimation in Multi-Aperture FSO Systems.
abstract: Accurate characterization of free-space optical (FSO) channels requires joint estimation of transmitter pointing errors, receiver angle-of-arrival (AoA) fluctuations, and turbulence-induced fading. However, existing literature addresses these impairments in isolation, since their multiplicative coupling in the received signal severely limits conventional estimators and prevents simultaneous recovery. In this paper, we introduce a novel multi-aperture FSO receiver architecture that leverages spatial diversity across a lens array to decouple these intertwined effects. Building on this hardware design, we propose a hierarchical deep learning framework that sequentially estimates AoA, transmitter pointing error, and turbulence coefficients. This decomposition significantly reduces learning complexity and enables robust inference even under strong atmospheric fading. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves near-MAP accuracy with orders-of-magnitude lower computational cost, and substantially outperforms end-to-end learning baselines in terms of estimation accuracy and generalization. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to demonstrate practical joint estimation of these three key parameters, paving the way for reliable, turbulence-resilient multi-aperture FSO systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-User ISAC Beamforming Considering Hardware Impairments of Linear Power Amplifiers.
abstract: This paper investigates the beamforming design for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with hardware imperfections in linear power amplifiers. The Cram'er Rao Bound (CRB) minimization problem is formulated by constraining the power of communication devices and the signalto-noise ratio threshold. Specifically, we first reformulate the CRB using the Schur complement theorem, and then employ semidefinite relaxation to equivalently reconstruct the nonconvex constraints. Subsequently, we obtained the optimal solution using the Gaussian randomization algorithm. Simulation results confirm that the proposed transmission waveform design is more robust when accounting for hardware impairments of linear power amplifiers.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Distributed Federated Generative-AI Field Learning for Synthetic Sensing in 6G Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Autonomous vehicular systems are increasingly dependent on collaborative perception over 6G networks, where sensing reliability and communication efficiency are jointly constrained by mobility and bandwidth variability. The existing federated learning (FL) frameworks struggle to provide robust perception when sensor data are degraded and communication resources are limited. In this paper, we propose Distributed Federated Generative-AI field learning for Synthetic sensing in 6 G (DFG6G) Vehicular Networks framework that enables vehicles to locally reconstruct degraded sensor observations while collaboratively training a shared perception model through tier-aware aggregation across vehicles, roadside units, and the core cloud. The design explicitly couples generative sensing, communication cost, and aggregation latency within a 6G aware architecture. In all evaluations, DFG6G consistently achieves better accuracy with low training delay and reduced communication overhead relative to the compared federated learning baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Machine-Learning-Based BPSK Decoding Under Fading Channels: A Comparative Study with Maximum Likelihood Detection.
abstract: Machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly being explored as alternatives to classical detection methods in wireless communication systems, particularly in scenarios involving complex or unknown channel conditions. This paper presents a detailed comparative analysis of several supervised ML classifiers for detecting binary phase shift keying (BPSK) symbols transmitted through representative small scale fading channels, namely Rayleigh, Rician, and Nakagami-m. Five commonly used classifiers like Decision Tree,$k$Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gaussian Naive Bayes and Random Forest are evaluated and compared against the optimal single input single output (SISO) maximum likelihood detector (MLD). Monte Carlo simulations are conducted on a wide range of signal to noise ratio (SNR) values from 0 to 20 dB, using instantaneous channel state information (CSI) for both MLD based detection and feature generation for classifier training. The results show that while the SISO MLD continues to provide the theoretical lower bound on the bit error rate (BER), several ML classifiers approach ML performance at moderate to high SNR levels, with Random Forest and SVM demonstrating the strongest consistency across fading environments. The analysis highlights the potential of low complexity ML-based detectors in practical systems and provides insights into classifier robustness, cross channel generalization behavior, and computational trade offs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Resource Slicing for eMBB and URLLC in O-RAN.
abstract: Open radio access networks (O-RAN) enable flexible orchestration of heterogeneous services such as enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC), but jointly satisfying their conflicting throughput and latency requirements leads to a highly combinatorial resource allocation problem. In this paper, we propose a hybrid quantum-classical optimization framework for dynamic O-RAN resource slicing, leveraging the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to jointly optimize radio resource block assignment, punctured scheduling, and power allocation in multi-O-RU networks. The proposed framework integrates orthogonal and shared slicing through a quantumenabled puncturing mechanism that allows URLLC traffic to preempt eMBB transmissions while maintaining overall system efficiency. An adaptive weight normalization strategy driven by real-time queue dynamics balances eMBB throughput maximization and URLLC latency minimization. The resulting constrained optimization problem is mapped to a quantum-executable Hamiltonian and solved using a hybrid QAOA-classical refinement loop compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. Simulation results show that the proposed approach outperforms classical optimization baselines, achieving up to 25% higher eMBB throughput, faster convergence, and consistently lower URLLC latency across different power budgets and network densities.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fairness-Aware Throughput Optimization for Dynamic Traffic in 5G Networks.
abstract: In 5G networks, diverse services and applications are supported through network slicing. Resource optimization of limited physical resource blocks (PRBs) is required given heterogeneous user SNR conditions and dynamic arrivals. When earlier users with poor channel conditions consume excessive resources, fewer remain for the other users, especially later arrivals, raising long-term fairness concerns. Furthermore, the base station does not have information on future arrivals, which complicates long-term resource allocation. In this paper, we present FP-Alloc, a Lyapunov-based dynamic and fair resource allocation framework, which allocates PRBs to users in an online manner as users arrive. Our algorithm admits a control parameter that balances optimizing the gap between desired and achieved throughput (a metric of efficiency) for individual users and throughput fairness across the dynamic users, over time, i.e. balancing between serving the needs of earlier users, and also reserving resources for later user requests. We derive upper bounds of the long-term user-averaged virtual queue length under FP-Alloc, as well as the upper bounds of the long-term user-averaged throughput-gap. Simulation results illustrate the performance of FP-Alloc and verify its improved effectiveness over existing methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: ReClub: $\underline{\text{Re}}$al-Time $\underline{\text{Clu}}$ster-Formation for Uav-Assisted Scala$\underline{\mathrm{b}}$le Data-Collection.
abstract: Dividing a network into clusters is a well-established strategy to address scalability challenges in data collection. With the advent of multi-access edge computing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly being deployed to collect data from these clusters. For efficient and scalable UAVassisted data collection, the cluster formation, beyond being energy efficient, must also satisfy several critical properties, such as maintaining uniformity in cluster shape and size, ensuring appropriate placement of cluster heads, and forming compact, multi-hop structures. When nodes are mobile, clustering also needs to be fast enough to remain consistent despite topology dynamics. Existing approaches struggle to balance these diverse requirements effectively. We propose ReClub, a novel Concurrent-Transmission (CT)-based clustering framework that enables ultra-fast, energy-efficient, and topology-aware cluster formation for UAV-assisted data collection. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that ReClub is up to 92% faster than state-of-theart approaches, while sustaining reliable data collection under mobility. Moreover, ReClub-based data aggregation supports up to 7 × higher information refresh rates, making it highly suitable for next-generation mobile and large-scale edge-assisted IoT applications where 'age of information' is critical.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Perceptual-Quality Based AMC for Enhanced mmWave Spectral Efficiency: Concept and Experiment.
abstract: For high-throughput applications such as ultra-high-definition video streaming and immersive extended-reality, perceptual quality rather than bit-level accuracy defines the primary performance criterion and provides a more informative and spectrally efficient objective than strict bitwise reconstruction. This is particularly relevant in millimeter-wave (mmWave) and sub-Terahertz (sub-THz) systems, where path loss, short channel coherence times and phase noise introduce severe fluctuations that degrade link spectral efficiency. We propose an extension to conventional Adaptive Modulation and Coding (AMC) framework that incorporates perceptual quality awareness into link adaptation. In this framework, the decision metric is a Perceptual Quality Indicator (PQI) derived from the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM). The receiver employs a Denoising Convolutional Neural Network (DnCNN) denoiser to enhance post-decoding image quality before feedback estimation. The resulting perceptual metric replaces the standard Channel Quality Indicator (CQI) in the AMC loop, enabling adaptation to maximize spectral efficiency while satisfying a perceptual-fidelity constraint. Experiments on a 5 G -compliant mmWave testbed demonstrate up to a twofold gain in spectral efficiency while maintaining perceptual fidelity, underscoring the potential of perception-optimized link adaptation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Split Channel Based CSI Auto-Encoder for Resource Limited Devices.
abstract: Optimal wireless communication performance relies on aligning transmitted data with the actual channel with the help of precoding matrix, necessitating accurate downlink (DL) channel state information (CSI) at the network (NW). Existing solutions either use codebook-based techniques by exploiting sparsity in spatial or temporal domains, or AI/ML models to compress CSI feedback, but these suffer from high complexity for relatively low-end user equipment (UE) and require multiple models to support several Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) configurations. To address this, we propose a single neural network (NN) based auto-encoder (AE) framework compatible with all MIMO setups through a novel pre/post-processing technique. By training the model on individual 1 × 1 subchannels, we achieve lower complexity, while eliminating the need for configuration-specific models thus reducing UE storage demands significantly. Through mathematical modelling and extensive simulations, we show that with proposed method of using split channel matrix in comparison to full channel matrix as input for NN model, memory requirement for storing model for 4 × 4 MIMO configuration at UE and NW is reduced by 93.58%, with improvement in model performance on high correlation test data by 5.76 dB is observed.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Performance Characterization of Pinching-Antenna System with Movable Waveguides.
abstract: This paper proposes a movable waveguide (MW)-enabled pinching-antenna system (PASS), in which each waveguide is connected via a flexible cable and can be linearly moved by drivers. By simultaneously moving the MWs and the pinching antennas (PAs) on them, MW-enabled PASS can effectively track user locations and form flexible array geometries for efficient beamforming. We consider a multi-user downlink communication scenario and derive an upper bound on the minimum rate among all users. To maximize their minimum rate, we propose a low-complexity two-scale optimization algorithm, where the large-scale global search coarsely determines the MW and PA positions, followed by a small-scale local search to finely tune them. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves performance close to the derived bound and can flexibly adapt to different user distributions compared with the conventional PASS employing dense or sparse fixed-position waveguides (FPWs).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Open5GFusion: Synergizing Open-Source 5G Platforms for Enhanced Network Flexibility and Research.
abstract: The deployment of 5G networks using open-source software platforms on commodity hardware and software defined radios (SDRs) has become increasingly important for both research and prototyping. Most work is constrained to a single platform such as OpenAirInterface (OAI), inhibiting the potential for cross-platform trade-offs. This paper presents Open5GFusion, a heterogeneous 5G Standalone (SA) testbed that combines OAI, srsRAN, and Open5GS to enable flexible experimentation with different core network (CN) and radio access network (RAN) alternatives and to exploit the strengths of each. A graphical user interface (GUI) simplifies deployment management and monitoring across different CN/RAN combinations. The testbed leverages commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware with USRP B210 and N310 SDRs, allowing real-time evaluation of throughput, latency, modulation schemes, network slicing, and other capabilities. Experimental results show that OAI RAN achieves higher throughput while srsRAN provides lower latency and greater configuration flexibility. We demonstrate the practical applicability of the platform through use cases, demonstrating network slicing, low-latency performance, and cell broadcast support.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: PreAlzNet: Smartwatch-Based Attention-LSTM for Early-Stage Alzheimer's Prediction.
abstract: Early Prediction of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is vital for timely intervention, yet existing diagnostic methods remain invasive, costly, and unsuitable for continuous use. To overcome these barriers, we have presented Pre-Alzheimer's Network (PreAlzNet), a modified attention enhanced Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework optimized for wearables actigraphy based early Alzheimer's prediction. Within an edge-cloud collaborative framework, PreAlzNet performs on-device signal preprocessing, temporal embedding, and uncertainty guided compression, followed by selective uplink transmission for cloud-level refinement. It is deployed on an ARM Cortex-A53 edge prototype, PreAlzNet achieves 96.1 % classification accuracy, while reducing inference latency to 18.3 mili seconds (ms) and uplink bandwidth by 41.6 %, compared to lightweight 1 -direction convolutional neural network (1D-CNN-LSTM) baselines. Moreover, the adaptive offload strategy improves overall accuracy by$+3.7\%$while lowering energy consumption by 29.3 % under mobile constraints. These results highlight a robust balance between accuracy, latency, and communication efficiency, establishing PreAlzNet as a privacy-preserving, energy-aware medical health (mHealth) framework for real-time cognitive screening via commodity smartwatches.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: SafeCOMM: A Study on Safety Degradation in Fine-Tuned Telecom Large Language Models.
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on telecom datasets is a common practice to adapt general-purpose models to the telecom domain. However, little attention has been paid to how this process may compromise model safety. Recent research has shown that even benign fine-tuning can degrade the safety alignment of LLMs, causing them to respond to harmful or unethical user queries. In this paper, we investigate this issue by fine-tuning LLMs on three representative telecom datasets and show that safety degrades even for light telecom domain adaptation. To this end, we introduce TeleHarm, the first telecom-specific red-teaming benchmark, which we use alongside established DirectHarm and HexPhi datasets to systematically assess harmful behavior. We further extend our analysis to publicly available TeleLLMs that were continually pre-trained on large telecom corpora, revealing that safety alignment is severely lacking, primarily due to the omission of safety-focused instruction tuning. To address these issues, we evaluate three realignment defenses: SafeInstruct, SafeLoRA, SafeMERGE. We show that, across all settings, the proposed defenses can effectively restore safety without compromising telecom task performance, leading to Safe teleCOMMunication (SafeCOMM) models. Our work serves as both a diagnostic study and practical guide for safety realignment in telecom-tuned LLMs, underscoring the need for safety-aware instruction and fine-tuning in the telecom domain.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MeshPay: Resilient Offline Payment with Wireless Mesh Network.
abstract: Mobile payment systems have become an essential part of modern digital services, supporting applications such as money transfer, mobile banking, and digital wallets. Despite their widespread adoption, these systems rely heavily on stable Internet connectivity, which remains unavailable or unreliable in many parts of the world. To address these challenges, we propose MeshPay, a decentralized offline payment framework that integrates wireless mesh networking with a blockchain-based settlement layer, enabling secure, real-time transaction settlement without Internet access. Blockchain technology provides a transparent and tamper-resistant ledger, reduces transaction costs and long process of validity by eliminating intermediaries. The proposed system is implemented and evaluated using MininetWiFi, demonstrating its ability to achieve up to 5000 transactions per second and keep latencies below 800 milliseconds with 20 authority nodes under ideal conditions. These results highlight the feasibility of mesh-based offline payment systems as a robust alternative for connectivity-constrained environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Uplink Performance Analysis of CF-mMIMO Networks with Unknown Interference.
abstract: In 5G dense urban deployments, a considerable fraction of indoor traffic is served by outdoor access points (APs). Co-channel interference is a key challenge in cellfree massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) networks, primarily attributed to the dense time-frequency reuse across geographically overlapping areas. In practice, only the interference from user equipments (UEs) associated with the same AP cluster can be determined in real-time and suppressed via precoding or combining schemes. Consequently, the residual unknown interference complicates rate adaptation and leads to link outages. This paper proposes an enhanced framework for modeling unknown interference in CF-mMIMO networks with both indoor and outdoor UEs. Analytical results validate that the proposed model accurately characterizes the distribution of the unknown interference power. By leveraging the proposed interference model, we evaluate the uplink performance of indoor UEs, revealing a fundamental trade-off: increasing indoor UE density reduces per-user spectral efficiency (SE) due to intensified interference, but this is compensated by a substantial gain in the achievable outage rate, owing to more stable indoor channels and optimized resource allocation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Uplink Performance and Trade-Offs in Integrated Space-Air-Ground Networks: A Stochastic Geometry Analysis with Shadowed-Rician Fading.
abstract: With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, various aerial applications have emerged, which require robust connectivity and high-quality link performance. However, due to the limitations of onboard resources, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have difficulty providing robust services for diverse applications, requiring the assistance of satellites or terrestrial base stations (TBSs). In this paper, we propose an integrated space-air-ground network (ISAGN), in which low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites and TBSs collaboratively provide communication coverage for UAVs. We derive the analytical expressions of connectivity and network capacity, and evaluate the impact of UAV density, satellite height, and number of satellites on connectivity and capacity for air-to-ground and air-to-satellite links. Through numerical results, we validate the analytical expressions of connectivity and capacity, and demonstrate that there exists a trade-off between connectivity and capacity, in which capacity can be significantly enhanced by judiciously designing the number of LEO satellites.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Vision-Based Framework for Intelligent gNodeB Mobility Control.
