abstract: This paper proposes a vision-based framework for the intelligent control of mobile Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) base stations (gNBs) operating in dynamic wireless environments. The framework comprises three innovative components. The first is the introduction of novel Service Models (SMs) within a vision-enabled O-RAN architecture, termed VisionRAN. These SMs extend state-of-the-art O-RAN-based architectures by enabling the transmission of vision-based sensing data and gNB positioning control messages. The second is an O-RAN xApp, VisionApp, which fuses vision and radio data, and uses this information to control the position of a mobile gNB, using a Deep Q-Network (DQN). The third is a digital twin environment, VisionTwin, which incorporates vision data and can emulate realistic wireless scenarios; this digital twin was used to train the DQN running in VisionApp and validate the overall system. Experimental results, obtained using real vision data and an emulated radio, demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces the duration of Line-of-Sight (LoS) blockages by up to 75 % compared to a static gNB. These findings confirm the viability of integrating multimodal perception and learning-based control within RANs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy-Efficient Distributed Access in Wireless Control Networks Via Hypergraph Potential Games.
abstract: Dense wireless control networks, such as those in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), face significant challenges from co-channel interference due to massive device access. Traditional resource allocation models, often based on simple graphs, fail to accurately capture the complex multi-user conflicts, while centralized control mechanisms struggle with scalability and latency. To address these issues, we propose a novel distributed access mechanism to maximize network energy efficiency. Our approach innovatively models the multi-user resource competition as a hypergraph, which precisely represents cumulative interference. We then formulate the user association problem as a non-cooperative game on this hypergraph and prove it is an Exact Potential Game, thus guaranteeing convergence to a stable Nash equilibrium. Based on this theoretical foundation, we design an iterative algorithm that jointly optimizes user association and power allocation using the game-theoretic framework and fractional programming techniques. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed mechanism significantly outperforms a conventional greedy baseline method, achieving substantial improvements in system energy efficiency, particularly in dense network scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DRL-Based Multi-AUVs Cooperative Path Planning Under Acoustic Field Constraint.
abstract: Employing autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) for ocean observation and data collection holds great promise for building large-scale underwater monitoring networks. Path planning is a key technique for improving multi-AUVs cooperative efficiency; however, it faces significant challenges from unknown obstacles and highly heterogeneous underwater acoustic fields. In this article, we consider AUVs coordinating environmental sensing during travel to designated target locations. This approach maximizes platform utilization. In particular, we use ray-tracing to construct a three-dimensional acoustic transmission model. We propose a cooperative path planning scheme integrating acoustic field alignment (AFA) and collision-avoidance constraints. The scheme shortens trajectory length and enhances network throughput. Furthermore, to address this challenging dynamic planning problem, we design an energy- and acoustic-aware dueling deep$Q$network (EA-DuelingDQN) that incorporates a recurrent neural network (RNN) module to capture the temporal characteristics of sensing data. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior collision-avoidance capability and network throughput, with the task completion rate improving by 40% compared to conventional DQN-based approaches.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Waveform Design for ISAC System: A Consensus ADMM Approach.
abstract: We study joint transmit-waveform and receive-filter design for a multi-user downlink integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system under practical constant-modulus and similarity constraints. We cast the design as a unified multi-objective program that balances communication sum rate and sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). To address this, we introduce an efficient algorithm that use consensus alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) framework to alternately update the transmit waveform and radar filter. The proposed method effectively handles the non-convex fractional sensing's SINR formulation and ensures fast convergence. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves better trade-offs between communication sum rate and sensing's SINR compared to existing benchmark schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Resource Allocation for Multiple Aircomp Systems: A Polynomial-Time Optimal Framework.
abstract: Over-the-air computation has emerged as a promising technique for fast and efficient aggregation of distributed data in wireless networks. While prior studies have mainly focused on transceiver design for a single AirComp system-optimizing transmit power and receiver denoising factors-the coexistence of multiple AirComp systems in the same network has received limited attention. In practical large-scale deployments, however, wireless networks must often support multiple AirComp systems simultaneously, each corresponding to a distinct sensing or learning task. This necessitates frequency allocation at the system level, where all devices in a system share a common frequency for in-air aggregation, and different systems use orthogonal frequencies to avoid interference. We formulate, for the first time, a joint optimization problem for multi-AirComp systems that integrates frequency allocation, power control, and receiver denoising. The resulting mixed-integer nonlinear program is challenging due to the coupling between discrete and continuous variables. By exploiting problem structure, we derive closedform transceiver solutions under fixed frequency assignments and show that the remaining frequency allocation reduces to a classical assignment problem solvable optimally in polynomial time using the Hungarian method. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves substantial reductions in computation mean-square error compared with baselines that optimize only transceiver parameters.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Semantic-Aware Transmission Via Small Object Detection Over Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: Drone-based small-object detection faces a dual bottleneck of task accuracy and transmission energy efficiency. To improve detection performance in drone scenarios, this paper proposes an efficient detection model. Its core components include: expert decoder branches dedicated to persistently low-accuracy classes to enhance the representational capability of specific weak classes; and a wavelet-domain feature enhancement module for integrating high-resolution details. Experiments on the VisDrone dataset show that, compared to the baseline method, the proposed model achieves improvements of 1.3% in AP and 1.6% in AP50. To enable high-efficiency transmission of detection results, we propose a semantic-aware transmission strategy: adaptively compressing the background region while leaving the object region uncompressed, thereby significantly reducing communication overhead. Building on this, we formulate a total energy optimization problem under bandwidth, latency, and compression ratio constraints, which is solved through an alternating iterative algorithm, achieving low-energy, low-latency, and reliable transmission of detection results. Simulation experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hexa-Steiner Space Modulation: A Combinatorial Design Approach for Enhanced MIMO Spectral Efficiency.
abstract: A novel indexing scheme, termed hexa-Steiner system (Hexa-SS), is proposed to enhance the spectral efficiency of the recently introduced Steiner space shift keying (Steiner-SSK) technique for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The design leverages the combinatorial structure of the Steiner triple system (STS) by merging two distinct STS triples to form a six-dimensional activation vector (Hexa-vector) that defines the unique configuration of six simultaneously active antennas. In the proposed scheme, three antennas transmit the inphase component of an unmodulated carrier, while the remaining three convey the quadrature component, achieving efficient joint spatial and signal representation. Analytical expressions for the average bit error rate (ABER) and computational complexity are derived, and their accuracy is verified through extensive Monte Carlo simulations. Comparative analysis with Generalized SSK (GSSK) and Steiner-SSK demonstrates that Hexa-SS achieves superior performance over GSSK at equivalent spectral efficiency with only a moderate increase in complexity, whereas SteinerSSK retains its performance edge at the expense of higher computational cost. The results highlight Hexa-SS as a promising tradeoff between performance and complexity for next-generation index modulation schemes in large-scale MIMO systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Pilot Distortion Design for ToA Obfuscation in Uplink OFDM Communication.
abstract: We study uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) pilot distortion to deliberately obfuscate time-of-arrival (ToA) estimation at a single base station while preserving communication performance. We design a complex persubcarrier distortion vector that increases sidelobes of the mismatched ambiguity function (MAF) relative to its mainlobe, using two objectives: the sidelobe-to-peak level ratio and the integrated sidelobe level. The design is subject to a transmit-power budget and a proximity (dissimilarity) constraint around the communication-optimal pilot. Communication impact is quantified by a capacity-motivated lower bound obtained from the linear minimum mean-squared error error covariance with a mismatched channel estimate. The resulting generalized fractional program is solved with Dinkelbach's transform and a difference-of-convex update that yields a closed-form Karush-Kuhn-Tucker step. Simulations on a single-input single-output OFDM link show that the optimized distortions raise MAF sidelobes and degrade delay estimation, as validated by a mismatched maximumlikelihood ToA estimator, while incurring only marginal capacity loss over a broad signal-to-noise ratio range. The method requires no protocol changes or artificial path injection and provides a signal-level mechanism to control ToA observability under communication constraints.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Q-Sentinel: Towards Adversarial Robustness for Quantum-Classical xApps in Intelligent O-RAN.
abstract: As Open radio access networks(O-RAN) shifts toward microservice-based disaggregation, learning-enabled xApps now shoulder near-real-time tasks such as interference classification that must react within tens of milliseconds. Hybrid quantum-classical models are a potential fit for that workload because expressive quantum feature maps can be paired with lightweight classical heads to deliver low-latency, energy-efficient inference as the hardware matures. Yet the same variational circuits remain vulnerable to RF adversaries: input perturbations collapses the quantum decision boundary, while parameter-space attacks silently corrupt circuit weights. We present$Q$-Sentinel, a quantum-fidelity aware robust stack that unifies (i) quantum state transformation guided by trusted manifolds, (ii) fidelity-based decision-boundary reinforcement, and (iii) sentinel snapshots that monitor cosine drift and trigger auto-repair of the variational (fusion-inclusive) parameters. We also build a quantum-aware adversarial training (QAT) baseline that applies QC-FGSM/PGD to both spectrogram inputs and quantum encodings. Evaluating with the public dataset SOI-vs-CWI, Q-Sentinel sustains 98.2 % clean accuracy, raises worst-case QC-FGSM/QC-PGD accuracy to 84.7 % / 73.6 % at$\epsilon=0.1$, and retains 70.8 % accuracy under QCPoison while capping mean parameter drift at$1.8 \times 10^{-2}$less than half that of the undefended model. These results indicate that future quantum-assisted O-RAN deployments will require defenses that preserve quantum-state geometry on Hilbert manifolds and continuously repair compromised circuits, extending beyond input-only adversarial training.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Orientation-Aware Adaptive Kalman Filtering for Robust UWB Indoor Localization on Smartphones.
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) indoor localization on smartphones, an emerging form of wireless sensing, is influenced by device orientation and human motion, which affect antenna directionality and ranging stability. This paper presents a feature-guided segmented adaptive Kalman filtering method that dynamically estimates the process and measurement noise parameters from data-driven features. Experiments were conducted using three DWM3001CDK anchors and two smartphones (iPhone 13 Pro and iPhone 16) under two anchor orientations-horizontal (H) and vertical (V)-combined with multiple smartphone orientation and motion states. Compared with the raw trilateration and an Adaptive KF (covariance-matching / normalized innovation squared), the proposed method achieved an average RMSE reduction of approximately$\mathbf{1 0 - 1 2 \%}$, and up to 18 % improvement relative to the fixed-parameter Kalman filter. Under the horizontal (H) orientation, two of the three smartphone orientations exhibited smaller root-mean-square error (RMSE) under shaking conditions than under stable conditions, suggesting a complex interaction between antenna orientation and motion dynamics.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Heterogeneous Multi-Computing-Units Based LT Coded Computation in Wireless Networks.
abstract: When confronted with distributed computing architectures in wireless networks that interconnect heterogeneous multi-computing-units (multi-CUs), the existing coded computation schemes are unable to efficiently execute computational tasks. This inefficiency is attributed to several challenges, including the presence of heterogeneous computing architectures, double straggling phenomena, and complex transmission cases. In this paper, we propose the wireless Luby transform (LT) coded computation based on two-layer block division. The master performs sub-block division at the workers' level, and the workers perform micro-block division at the CUs' level, which improves their computational efficiency. Then, in order to describe the computation and transmission performance of task execution in the whole network clearly, the computing power relationship between workers and their CUs is constructed. Finally, we design the optimal sub-block size and micro-block size to achieve the minimized total latency. The simulation results also indicate that the proposed scheme can recognize the straggling workers and straggling CUs, thereby improving the latency performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Grover's Search-Inspired Quantum Reinforcement Learning for Massive MIMO User Scheduling.
abstract: The efficient user scheduling policy in the massive Multiple Input Multiple Output (mMIMO) system remains a significant challenge in the field of 5 G and Beyond 5 G (B5G) due to its high computational complexity, scalability, and Channel State Information (CSI) overhead. This paper proposes a novel Grover's search-inspired Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) framework for mMIMO user scheduling. The QRL agent can explore the exponentially large scheduling space effectively by applying Grover's search to the reinforcement learning process. The model is implemented using our designed quantum-gate-based circuit, which imitates the layered architecture of reinforcement learning, where quantum operations act as policy updates and decision-making units. Moreover, the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves proper convergence and significantly outperforms classical Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Quantum Deep Learning (QDL) benchmarks by 51 % and 43 %, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Duality-Based Fixed Point Iteration Algorithm for Beamforming Design in ISAC Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the beamforming design problem in an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where a multi-antenna base station simultaneously serves multiple communication users while performing radar sensing. We formulate the problem as the minimization of the total transmit power, subject to signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints for communication users and mean-squarederror (MSE) constraints for radar sensing. The core challenge arises from the complex coupling between communication SINR requirements and sensing performance metrics. To efficiently address this challenge, we first establish the equivalence between the original ISAC beamforming problem and its semidefinite relaxation (SDR), derive its Lagrangian dual formulation, and further reformulate it as a generalized downlink beamforming (GDB) problem with potentially indefinite weighting matrices. Compared to the classical DB problem, the presence of indefinite weighting matrices in the GDB problem introduces substantial analytical and computational challenges. Our key technical contributions include (i) a necessary and sufficient condition for the boundedness of the GDB problem, and (ii) a tailored efficient fixed point iteration (FPI) algorithm with a provable convergence guarantee for solving the GDB problem. Building upon these results, we develop a duality-based fixed point iteration (Dual-FPI) algorithm, which integrates an outer subgradient ascent loop with an inner FPI loop. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed Dual-FPI algorithm achieves globally optimal solutions while significantly reducing computational complexity compared with existing baseline approaches.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: NetDiT: A Diffusion-Transformer Framework for Synthetic Network Packet Generation.
abstract: With the rapid growth of modern networks, synthetic network traffic has become vital for secure testing and evaluation. Traditional rule-based methods often produce unrealistic data, while privacy concerns limit the sharing of real traffic. Current generative models like VAEs and GANs frequently struggle with mode collapse and complex patterns. To address this, we propose NetDiT, a novel framework based on Diffusion Transformers that operates directly on discrete hexadecimal tokens. By injecting protocol-specific inductive biases through network-aware attention and embedding mechanisms, NetDiT captures both structural rules and statistical dependencies. Experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves 99.98 % structural correctness and closely mirrors real-world traffic diversity, significantly outperforming standard DiT and deep baselines in both accuracy and computational efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Intelligent Trajectory Design for Free-Space Optical Assisted UAVs Relay Communications in Low-Altitude Airspace.
abstract: With the booming development of low-altitude intelligent networking (LAIN), free-space optical (FSO) based unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) communication offers a promising scheme to effectively address the challenge of the intense spectrum scarcity. However, due to the characteristics of FSO propagation, its performance is severely affected by the lowaltitude atmospheric conditions and complex airspace environment. To address these challenges, this work constructs an FSO assisted UAVs multi-hop relay system, where a multiagent double deep Q-network with prioritized experience replay (MADDQN-PER) approach is proposed for trajectory design, under the complex environment of low-altitude airspace such as the low-altitude obstacles and atmospheric visibility. To expound, the proposed scheme is expected to enhance the relay system capacity by intelligently adjusting UAVs' trajectories in the low-altitude airspace to maintain the multi-hop link stability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can effectively avoid time-varying low-altitude threat of varying severity while attaining about 10 % higher capacity when scaling from three to four UAVs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Uniair: A Unified AI Framework for Multi-Task Joint Optimization Over the Air Interface.
abstract: In recent years, AI has become a key enabler for air interface task optimization. While encouraging performance gains have been observed in many studies, the prevailing One Model for One Task paradigm is inefficient and unsustainable in the long run due to heavy resource redundancy, poor task scalability, and neglect of inter-task correlations. To address this challenge, UniAir, a unified AI framework for multi-task joint optimization over the air interface is proposed in this paper. In UniAir, task-agnostic features are extracted from a unified encoder at UE and the two-stage training decouples new task adaptation to the gNB side only, reducing device-side resource consumption and ensuring scalability across diverse tasks. A prototype testbed is established with four representative air interface tasks to validate the effectiveness of UniAir in the emulated real-world environment. Experimental results show that UniAir achieves comparable performance compared with the task-specific baselines with significantly fewer model parameters, validating its efficiency and scalability for future wireless system.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A KAN-Enhanced Position Correction Network for Reference Signal Received Power Prediction.
abstract: In high-mobility scenarios, the rapid variation of channel characteristics poses significant challenges for reference signal receiving power (RSRP) prediction. However, traditional methods, including univariate time series models, often perform poorly in this task. While some studies integrate user trajectories, they typically treat position and RSRP prediction as separate tasks, without refining RSRP prediction through user positions. To address this gap, we propose a position correction network enhanced by Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), which applies multiple KAN modules to directly map the predicted positions to a correction term for RSRP refinement. Experimental results show that our network outperforms baseline methods, such as sequence-to-sequence long short-term memory, Transformer, multi-task learning models and multilayer perceptron in both single-step and multi-step prediction, achieving average reductions of 10.34% in mean absolute error and 8.20% in root mean square error, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Dynamic Occupancy Matrix Approach for VANET Routing Using Optimized TD-ISAC.
abstract: The dynamic topologies and high mobility in Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) lead to significant delays and substantial routing overhead, critically undermining safety by restricting real-time message exchange. Autonomous vehicles equipped with advanced sensors (e.g., LiDAR, radar) capture detailed environmental data, yet this capability remains underutilized for network-level optimization. This paper proposes a segmentation-based routing framework that leverages sensorderived vehicle positions to create a dynamic occupancy matrix, a shared topology representation disseminated via a Time Division Integrated Sensing and Communication (TD-ISAC) frame structure inspired by 5G Sidelink. We optimize sensing and communication slots allocation using a hybrid Lagrangian Relaxation and Branch-and-Bound approach to balance topological freshness with communication throughput. The protocol's robustness is further enhanced by a reserve relay mechanism. Simulation results using the Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) demonstrate that our framework outperforms the Zone Routing Protocol (ZRP) and the Ad-hoc On-demand Distance Vector (AODV) protocol, achieving up to 60 % reduction in end-to-end delay and 5 % reduction in routing overhead in multi-hop scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy-Efficient Federated Learning for UAV Communications.
abstract: This paper proposes a unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted federated learning (FL) framework that minimizes total system energy consumption through the joint optimization of UAV trajectory, user participation, power control, and data volume allocation. By incorporating the convergence behavior of the FL model under multiple local updates, the framework accounts for the impact of user participation and data volume on learning performance. The formulated joint optimization problem is inherently non-convex. To tackle this challenge, we adopt an alternating optimization (AO) approach combined with successive convex approximation (SCA) to handle non-convex constraints, leading to the development of an iterative energy consumption optimization (ECO) algorithm. Simulation results show that ECO consistently achieves superior performance compared to existing methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Learning Redundancy-Aware Representations for Robust Multi-Modal Task-Oriented Communications.
abstract: Task-oriented communications for multi-modal data aim to transmit task-relevant information efficiently over noisy and bandwidth-limited channels. A key challenge is to simultaneously address inter-modal redundancy and the degradation of semantic integrity under channel distortion. In this paper, we propose a robust and efficient multi-modal semantic communication framework that integrates a two-stage variational bottleneck with adversarial mutual information (MI) minimization. In the first stage, uni-modal variational bottlenecks compress each modality, i.e., text, audio, and video, while preserving task-specific features. To enhance efficiency, an adversarial MI minimization module then suppresses cross-modal dependencies, ensuring complementary rather than redundant representations. In the second stage, a multi-modal bottleneck further compresses the fused representation to enhance robustness against channel impairments. Experimental results on multi-modal regression task benchmarks show that the proposed framework significantly outperforms existing baselines in accuracy and resilience, particularly under low signal-to-noise ratio regimes. For instance, on the MOSI dataset over a Rayleigh channel at -12 dB, our model achieves a Top-2 Accuracy of 73.59 % and an F1 score of 0.7371, outperforming the baseline by 10.32 % and 10.40 %, respectively. This demonstrates that the proposed design not only improves task-oriented communication transmission accuracy but also enhances resilience under challenging wireless conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Single-RF Based XL-MIMO Empowered by Stacked Intelligent Metasurface.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel single-radio-frequency (single-RF)-based extremely large-scale (XL)-MIMO architecture relying on a stacked intelligent metasurface (SIM). In this architecture, only a single RF chain is deployed at the transmitter and then the joint multi-user signal modulation and precoding are performed by controlling the multi-layer unit cells of the SIM, where each unit cell could impose a controllable phase shift on the incident signal. To optimize the SIM phase shifts, we formulate a problem that minimizes the mean square error between the actual output signal and the desired signal. An alternating optimization algorithm is then proposed to solve this problem. Furthermore, a low-complexity SIM design scheme is developed to reduce the computational complexity for modulating phase-shift keying (PSK) signals. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves the target accuracy in wave-domain signal modulation and precoding, while offering substantial performance gains over single-layer reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in multi-user scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Pinching Antenna System (PASS) Assisted Wireless Power Transfer (WPT).
abstract: A novel pinching antenna system (PASS)-assisted wireless power transfer (WPT) framework is proposed, where an energy harvesting receiver (EHR) and an information decoding receiver (IDR) coexist. By activating pinching antennas (PAs) in the vicinity of both receivers and flexibly adjusting the PAs' power radiation ratios, the proposed framework is able to simultaneously enhance the energy harvesting efficiency and the communication quality. To tackle the strong coupling among variables, a bilevel optimization problem is formulated. Specifically, the upper level maximizes the power conversion efficiency (PCE) by jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming, PA positions, and the feasible interval of the power radiation ratio under the IDR's rate requirement, while the lower level refines the power radiation ratio within the obtained interval to maximize the achievable sum rate. Efficient solution methods are developed for the two-user case by leveraging alternating optimization (AO) and weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) techniques, yielding stationary solutions for the coupled design variables. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed PASS-WPT scheme substantially outperforms conventional MIMO and the conventional PASS with fixed power radiation in terms of both PCE and sum rate.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Peak Structure Analysis Based Phase-Optimized Precoding for PAPR Reduction in OTFS Systems.
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation offers superior performance for high-speed mobility wireless communications but suffers from high Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR), degrading power amplifier efficiency. While PAPR reduction techniques exist for OFDM systems, their application to OTFS remains challenging. This paper proposes a novel PAPR suppression method based on peak structure analysis in the time-frequency domain. By precisely locating time-domain peak structures and establishing an analytical framework for energy concentration regions, our approach guides phase optimization in precoding matrices. The method employs gradient-based finetuning with derived upper bound conditions for phase adjustment parameters and Hadamard multiplication precoding to avoid nonlinear distortion. Simulation results demonstrate over 7.6dB PAPR reduction for 16QAM/64*64 OTFS configurations while maintaining stable bit error rate performance, validating the method's effectiveness for practical high-performance communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: AgentWiFi: An Agentic-AI-Enabled Framework for Wi-Fi Cross Layer Optimization.
abstract: Agentic AI systems, supporting complex goal decomposition and effective collaboration among a large number of specialized AI agents, are promising to facilitate the management and performance enhancement of wireless communication networking systems. In this paper, we investigate the potential of agentic AI in future Wi-Fi networks, exploiting its capabilities to address key challenges in current Wi-Fi optimization, including the large-scale parameter configuration across physical and medium access control layers in the IEEE 802.11 standard family, personalized quality-of-experience requirements, and dynamic and diversified physical environments. We propose AgentWiFi, a novel semantic-aware agentic-AI-enabled architecture for crosslayer Wi-Fi network optimization. AgentWiFi can infer users' semantic goals, automatically decompose them into several subtasks, and invoke specialized agents associated with physical, medium access control, and application layers of the Wi-Fi network to fulfill the target goal. Furthermore, we develop a hardware prototype, where open-source large language modelbased agents are implemented and interacted with different layers, and conduct case studies in two representative scenarios of high-data-rate demanding ultra high definition live streaming and low-latency demanding online interactive gaming. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of AgentWiFi in improving Wi-Fi network performance via autonomous cross-layer parameter adjustments. Future directions for agentic AI for Wi-Fi are also discussed.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Time-Frequency Feature-Based MultiSensor Collaborative Topology Inference for Non-Cooperative Environments.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a Multisensor Time-Frequency Hawkes Topology Inference (MSTF-HTI) framework and a Hierarchical Mobile-Aware Subnetwork Traversal (H-MAST) algorithm for lightweight topology inference in dynamic, non-cooperative cognitive radio networks and unlicensed spectrum environments. The MSTF-HTI framework integrates collaborative multi-sensor spectrum sensing and time-frequency analysis with Hawkes process-based dynamic modeling to achieve accurate inference of primary/secondary user distribution and spectrum occupancy. The H-MAST algorithm employs a center-of-mass progressive expansion mechanism and mobile sensing path optimization for subnetwork partitioning, which enhances distributed spectrum access efficiency and improves inference accuracy with low complexity. The integrated system establishes a scalable and efficient framework that enables seamless local-to-global topology reconstruction while maintaining temporal consistency of network dynamics through adaptive parameter tuning, thereby supporting robust spectrum sharing and interference avoidance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior inference efficiency and accuracy compared to existing methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Feature-Domain Waveform Design for Multi-User Channel Acquisition in Massive MIMO with Decentralized Baseband Processing.
abstract: Traditional channel acquisition in massive multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) systems often relies on a centralized baseband processing (CBP) architecture, where signals from all antennas are processed at a central unit. However, as the antenna array scale grows, CBP suffers from prohibitive computational complexity and heavy fronthaul communication loads. To address these challenges, a decentralized baseband processing (DBP) architecture has emerged, partitioning the antenna array into multiple clusters, each managed by a local baseband unit (BBU). This paper proposes a distributed featuredomain channel acquisition (DFDCA) scheme tailored for the DBP framework. Each BBU exploits local channel statistics to construct a low-dimensional feature domain by approximating its channels as linear combinations of orthogonal basis vectors, thereby reducing the number of parameters to be estimated. To suppress inter-user interference, we develop a distributed iterative algorithm based on the minimum mean square error (MMSE) criterion for joint transceiver waveform design. This algorithm strategically distributes the optimization tasks: the central unit (CU) updates the global transmit precoding waveforms for all users, while each distributed unit (DU) computes local receive filter waveforms. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DFDCA scheme not only balances the computational and communication overhead, but also significantly improves channel acquisition accuracy in heavily loaded scenarios, validating its suitability for DBP-based massive MIMO systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Semantic Knowledge Base-Enhanced Joint Source-Channel Coding Framework for Robust Semantic Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a semantic knowledge base (SKB)-enhanced joint source-channel coding (JSCC) framework, named SKB-JSCC. This framework splits semantic features into two transmission branches with dynamically configurable split ratio, a JSCC-based branch that provides superior performance at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and an SKB-based branch that strengthens robustness at low SNR. Additionally, we introduce a bidirectional gated mutual errorcorrection (BGMEC) module at the receiver and provide theoretical analysis supporting its soundness and effectiveness. The BGMEC module uses cross attention to learn semantic associations between the two branches of streams and treats one stream as conditional information for the other to realize mutual correction and feature fusion. Experimental results illustrate that the BGMEC module provides performance gains for SKB-JSCC over the entire SNR range. Compared with a JSCC-based baseline, SKB-JSCC achieves a 14.3% improvement in transmission performance at low SNR and effectively mitigates the “cliff effect” relative to traditional separation-based schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Minimizing the Total Energy Consumption in the HAPS-Aided MEC with UAV Eavesdropper.
abstract: Although the high altitude platform station-aided mobile edge computing (HAPS-aided MEC) provides a promising framework to offloading tasks and further reduce the task completion time/energy, the possible existence of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based eavesdropper may disclose the privacy of the task-input data, which may further damage the user's identity privacy. However, the most existing works about the task offloading scheme in the HAPS-aided MEC have not considered the requirement from the privacy preserving. In this paper, we formulate the total energy minimization problem for the HAPS-aided MEC, where the secure transmission rate with the eavesdropper is considered as a constraint. Then we decompose the original problem into two subproblems via block coordinate descent (BCD) method. Based on the convex optimization theory and the sequential quadratic programming (SQP), we propose the whole optimization scheme to optimize the task offloading, the resource allocation and the user's movement. With the simulation results, we validate that the proposed scheme outperforms the benchmark schemes in terms of the energy consumption.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Spatiotemporal Differential Scheduling for Vehicle-to-Infrastructure Cooperative Perception.
abstract: This paper proposes a spatiotemporal differential scheduling (STDS) method for vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) cooperative perception. Leveraging collaborative perception with AI-enabled semantic processing, STDS mitigates bandwidth and latency bottlenecks. A long-term background model is built at the roadside unit (RSU), while vehicles transmit only differential foreground features to suppress static redundancies. We further design a two-stage uplink scheme with basic semantic upload and confidence-triggered feature patch refinement. To balance perception quality and communication cost, a joint sensing communication allocation model is formulated under strict latency and bandwidth constraints, and decomposed into macrolevel flow control and micro-level patch scheduling. The macro layer adapts semantic thresholds via proportional control, and the micro layer prioritizes patches by information gain density. Simulations show that STDS improves robustness over baselines in narrowband settings, achieving mAP above 0.75 at 20 MHz bandwidth while satisfying end-to-end latency limits.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dual-Polarized Wavenumber-Division Multiplexing in LoS Holographic MIMO Communications with Arbitrary Position and Orientation.
abstract: This paper studies the dual-polarized wavenumber-division multiplexing (WDM) in line-of-sight holographic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications with the receive surface located in arbitrary position and orientation. Specifically, the dual-polarized MIMO channel is first derived with arbitrary placement of the uniform planar surface at the receiver. Moreover, the radiation pattern of single-mode electric field, the co- and cross-polarization levels, and the channel capacity are analyzed, with emphasis on the impact of the azimuth and elevation angles of the receive surface. Finally, the superior performance of the dual-polarized WDM is verified in terms of the downlink sum-rate of several typical transceiver schemes, offering a viable solution for building future high-rate and flexibly-deployed wireless communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid Deep Learning Decoder for Satellite Communication Systems.
abstract: Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes have been adopted in 5G New Radio (NR) standards due to their strong error correction capabilities, making them a key enabler for reliable communications in satellite and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). However, conventional LDPC decoders can be computationally intensive, which poses a major challenge for power- and resource-constrained satellite terminals, onboard processors, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. To address these challenges, this paper presents a deep learning (DL)-assisted LDPC decoding framework designed for satellite communication systems. In particular, we utilize DL models, including recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory (LSTM), as auxiliary decoders to support LDPC decoding. The proposed architecture leverages DL inference followed by iterations of the LDPC decoder, reducing the number of required decoding iterations compared to standard implementations. Simulation results under satellite channel conditions demonstrate that the RNN-aided LDPC decoder overcomes the full-iteration belief propagation (BP) decoding in terms of bit error rate, block error rate, and throughput performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Ring Bayes Near-Field Channel Learning for mmWave Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Uniform Circular Array.
abstract: This work conceives a Ring-Bayes channel learning framework that unifies Bayesian learning with near-field channel estimation in millimeter-wave (mmWave) hybrid MIMO systems. We develop a near-field channel model with a uniform circular array (UCA) at the base station (BS) and a uniform linear array (ULA) at the user equipment (UE), explicitly accounting for spherical wavefront propagation. Exploiting the inherent sparsity of mmWave channels in the joint angular-distance domain, we construct a structured sparse representation and employ framewise processing to enhance the reliability of multi-antenna UE estimation. Furthermore, we design a concentric-ring codebook tailored to the UCA geometry, which efficiently captures nearfield channel features across both angular and distance domains. Leveraging this structure, the proposed Ring-Bayes framework achieves highly accurate recovery of UCA near-field channels. Extensive simulations demonstrate significant performance gains over existing approaches, establishing Ring-Bayes as a scalable and powerful solution for next-generation mmWave communications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid AI-Quantum Model with Attention-Guided Variational Circuits for MSSQL Attack Detection in Wireless Networks.
abstract: The increasing prevalence of application-layer attacks, such as MSSQL injection, presents serious security challenges for modern wireless networks. Traditional deep learning-based intrusion detection systems often exhibit high model complexity and limited ability to capture complex feature interactions under imbalanced traffic conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hybrid AI-quantum framework with attention-guided variational quantum circuits for MSSQL attack detection. Network traffic features from the CIC-DDoS2019 dataset are embedded and optimized using the Tunicate Swarm Algorithm, followed by convolutional learning to model local dependencies. A variational quantum circuit with learnable rotation and entanglement parameters captures higher-order feature interactions. Experimental results demonstrate an accuracy of 99.99%, with precision, recall, and F1-score all exceeding 99.99%. Ablation analysis further confirms improved parameter efficiency, highlighting the suitability of the proposed approach for secure and sustainable wireless systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: VoI-Driven Traffic Patch Transmission: A Synergistic Framework for Efficient SCC.
abstract: The evolution of the sixth-generation (6 G) Internet of Vehicles (IoV) necessitates a paradigm shift from raw data transmission to semantic communication. This paper proposes a distributed VoI-Driven Traffic Patch Transmission framework (VTPT) where roadside units (RSUs) and vehicles transmit Traffic Patches-time-sliced semantic blocks-to edge servers based on the value of information (VoI). By leveraging a SpatialTemporal Patch-based Self-Supervised Network (ST-PSSN), we implement a cloud-edge-end architecture. The experimental results show that the proposed framework can efficiently transmit the most valuable traffic information under resource-constrained conditions, thereby achieving more precise traffic control.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Session Aware Encrypted Traffic Classification with Contextual Position Selection.
abstract: Encrypted traffic classification has advanced, but several key gaps remain unsolved. Many models analyze only single packets, overlooking session context and missing broader patterns. Others rely on attention mechanisms with unstable scores and hard interpretation, posing risks in security-critical scenarios. In addition, high-performing models often demand excessive computation, limiting deployment. Therefore, we propose a model that addresses all three issues: it incorporates past packets to capture session context, replaces unstable attention weights with stable feature importance scores from tree-based models, and uses a lightweight queue-hash system to manage history efficiently. Our solution achieves a practical balance of accuracy, interpretability, and speed, making it suitable for real network environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Replacing ULCL with SRv6 in Multi-UPF 5G/6G Networks: An Open-Source Evaluation for Edge Computing.
abstract: Multi-User Plane Function (UPF) architectures in 5G core networks allow edge computing using the Uplink Classifier (ULCL) for traffic steering, but at the cost of additional complexity in the User Plane (UP) due to GPRS Tunneling Protocol for User Plane (GTP-U)-based traffic inspection and N9 tunneling. This poses a challenge for an open, affordable, and sustainable network intended for future 6 G systems, especially in private and resource-constrained scenarios. This paper presents an implementation where ULCLbased traffic steering is replaced by Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6)-based forwarding at Intermediate UPF (I-UPF) in the same overall multi-UPF architecture. This design removes additional GTP-U encapsulation on the N9 interface to steer traffic without modifying the access network or control plane. An evaluation using Vector Packet Processor (VPP)based User Plane Gateway (UPG-VPP), free5GC, and UERANSIM evaluation is conducted on a fully opensource testbed. Under identical topological and traffic conditions, a comparison is made for both approaches. Key performance metrics such as end-to-end latency, throughput, and CPU utilization are evaluated. The results show that SRv6 can practically replace ULCL in multi-UPF 5G/6G networks without requiring a full redesign of the UP architecture, while providing more flexible and programmable data-plane using open source technologies.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Semantic Communication: From Philosophical Conceptions Towards a Mathematical Framework.
abstract: Semantic communication has emerged as a promising paradigm to address the challenges of next-generation communication networks. While some progress has been made in its conceptualization, fundamental questions remain unresolved. In this paper, we propose a probabilistic model for semantic communication that, unlike prior works primarily rooted in intuitions from human language, is grounded in a rigorous philosophical conception of information and its relationship with data as Constraining Affordances, mediated by Levels of Abstraction (LoA). This foundation not only enables the modeling of linguistic semantic communication but also provides a domain-independent definition of semantic content, extending its applicability beyond linguistic contexts. As the semantic communication problem involves a complex interplay of various factors, making it difficult to tackle in its entirety, we propose to orthogonalize it by classifying it into simpler sub-problems and approach the general problem step by step. Notably, we show that Shannon's framework constitutes a special case of semantic communication, in which each message conveys a single, unambiguous meaning. Consequently, the capacity in Shannon's model-defined as the maximum rate of reliably transmissible messages-coincides with the semantic capacity under this constrained scenario. In this paper, we specifically focus on the sub-problem where semantic ambiguity arises solely from physical channel noise and derive a lower bound for its semantic capacity, which reduces to Shannon's capacity in the corresponding special case. We also demonstrate that the achievable rate of all transmissible messages for reliable semantic communication, exceeds Shannon's capacity by the added term H(X|S).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Sleep Mode Activation and Load Balancing with Dynamic Cell Load: A Combinatorial Bandit Approach.
abstract: We propose a combinatorial bandit formulation to opportunistically trigger sleep modes in gNode-B (gNB) small cells (SCs), followed by a cell range expansion (CRE)-based load balancing procedure. This is implemented by ensuring that the fifth generation$(5 \mathrm{G})$quality of service identifier (5QI)-requirements of user equipments (UEs) are maintained. The key challenge is the fact that while deactivating a given SC gNB reduces its own consumption, it may increase the load on neighboring gNBs and the macro gNB (coverage cell), impacting the overall energy efficiency. This phenomenon is accurately characterized by modeling the dynamic cell load that jointly takes into account the location of the UEs, their relative locations to all the SCs, and their data demands. We experimentally show that the proposed combinatorial upper confidence bound (CUCB) followed by the load balancer outperforms not only the naive strategies like arbitrarily keeping all the SCs on, but also other state-of-the-art reinforcement learning solutions. The proposed algorithm can be implemented as open-radio access network (O-RAN) near-real-time (NRT) RAN intelligent controller (RIC) xApps.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: VERGE-IDS: Variational Encoder-BiGRU Based Framework for Threat Detection in IoT Networks.
abstract: The growing deployment of resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices has significantly expanded the attack surface across critical sectors such as healthcare and manufacturing. Existing Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) solutions struggle to detect zero-day and evolving threats due to limited feature representation and reliance on static signatures. Moreover, many machine learning based IDS models are computationally intensive and prone to high false-alarm rates in dynamic IoT environments. This paper proposes VERGE-IDS, a lightweight, two-phase deep learning framework for accurate and efficient threat detection in IoT networks. In the first phase, a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) trained solely on benign traffic captures and learns the probabilistic distribution of normal behavior, with anomalies identified via an adaptive thresholding mechanism based on pro Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) and a lightweight latent-space classifier. In the second phase, a CNN-BiGRU model leverages spatio-temporal features to detect malicious traffic with high precision. Evaluations on two comprehensive datasets, Edge-IIoT and CICIoT2023, demonstrate detection accuracies of 98.89 % and 98.21 %, respectively, while maintaining a compact model size$(\approx 217 ~\text{KB})$. VERGE-IDS offers a scalable, low-overhead solution suitable for real-world, edge-level IoT deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Pareto Optimality Approach for Link Adaptation in DECT NR+.
abstract: DECT NR+ is a novel wireless IoT standard operating in the 1.9 GHz band, a band originally reserved for Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications (DECT). This technology is also announced as the first non-cellular 5G standard and theoretically offers wide flexibility in its application, ranging from Wireless Personal Area Network (WPAN) to Wide Area Network (WAN) scenarios. While this versatility is enabled by a wide range of configurable parameters, the practical application range is determined by the vendor's specific implementation. In this article, we investigate the impact of adjusting Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS), transmit power and packet length. We formulate objective functions for data rate, energy consumption, and Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), and analyze their dependence on the aforementioned parameters. To model specific relationships, we conduct practical experiments in two real-world testbeds using hardware from the Nordic nRF91 series. Finally, we present an approach for parameter selection based on the principle of Pareto optimality.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Channel Estimation Performance Analysis for RIS-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO with RF Impairments in Secure Communications.
abstract: In this article, we investigate the normalized mean square error (NMSE) performance of channel estimation in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems under radio frequency (RF) impairments and physical layer security constraints. Primarily, the entire channel estimation phase is formulated for both least squares (LS) and minimum mean square error (MMSE) methods, based on a practical cascaded channel model including RIS reflection and hardware distortion. To evaluate estimation accuracy, the NMSE metric is analyzed in closed-form. Specifically, its expectation is derived using largescale system analysis, revealing dependencies on the number of access point antennas$M$, the Ricean$K$-factor, and the pilot power. Then, asymptotic behavior of NMSE is characterized as$M$and$K$tend to infinity. It is shown that the estimation error decreases and then saturates as$M$increases, while it increases and then saturates as$K$becomes large. Furthermore, we explore the impact of pilot power allocation, and demonstrate that MMSE estimation allows for reduced pilot power without severe performance loss. Finally, all theoretical findings are verified through extensive simulations, confirming the effectiveness of our proposed analysis.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: FeDDRMoE: Dynamic Mixture-of-Experts with Attention Scheduling for Personalized Federated Learning.
abstract: As the deployment of federated learning expands across heterogeneous networks and devices, significant challenges arise from non-IID data distributions and constrained communication bandwidth, which critically impede convergence and training efficiency. It is vital to develop adaptive learning mechanisms that effectively tackle statistical heterogeneity and resource limitations across clients. To address the intertwined issues of data divergence and communication bottlenecks, we propose FedDRMoE, a federated learning framework that integrates a dynamic mixture-of-experts model with latent attentionbased client scheduling. Our approach introduces three core innovations built upon a LoRA-adapted backbone. First, we design an adaptive mixture-of-experts mechanism that dynamically routes inputs based on complexity to balance personalization and efficiency. Second, we introduce a periodic expert reconfiguration strategy, which evolves the expert pool by cloning high-utility experts and retiring underperforming ones. Third, we develop a multi-head latent attention scheduler that prioritizes diverse and high-impact clients in each training round. Experiments on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet under various non-IID settings demonstrate that our framework achieves substantial gains in accuracy while significantly reducing communication overhead compared to strong baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: SCHC Header Compression for GeoNetworking Protocol: Adaptation and Performance Evaluation.
abstract: The growing number of autonomous vehicles (AVs) significantly increases wireless network load, mainly due to the frequent exchange of safety messages such as Cooperative Awareness Messages (CAMs). A common strategy to mitigate this congestion is to compress application-layer data in these messages. However, a detailed analysis indicates that the GeoNetworking protocol, used for routing in ITS-G5 networks, represents a substantial part of the message overhead (about 40% of the size of an unsigned CAM). Therefore, we propose compressing this protocol using a generic header compression framework-Static Context Header Compression (SCHC). Our work adapts SCHC framework to the GeoNetworking protocol by defining two distinct compression rules. One of these rules is generic, provides lower compression, and can be pre-installed in all SCHCsupported vehicles. The second rule aggressively compresses the packet by leveraging the local conditions and can be optimised for a group of AVs, providing additional compression. In addition, we assess the effects of SCHC compression on an IEEE 802.11p based ITS-G5 network by estimating the Channel Busy Ratio (CBR) and Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) using analytical models and measuring the time on-air of SCHC compressed CAMs. Our findings indicate that by reducing time on-air by 13%, the compressed CAMs can decrease CBR by up to 19% and increase PDR by up to 6%. Moreover, they incur an additional overhead of approximately 5% for compression and 2% for decompression on the YoGoKo on-board unit.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RAG-LLM Driven Generative Semantic Communication for UAV-Assisted Emergency Response Systems in Adverse Channel Conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Turning Reliability into Shortest Path: Parameterized Probabilistic Routing for LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations enable global connectivity but suffer from highly dynamic topology and uncertain link quality, making reliable routing a key challenge. To address this, we propose Parameterized Probabilistic Routing (P2R), a lightweight optimization framework that reformulates reliability-aware routing into a standard shortest-path problem. P2R maps heterogeneous link indicators, such as signal-to-noise ratio, residual capacity, and visibility duration into additive edge weights through a tunable probabilistic fusion scheme. This transformation enables complex reliability objectives to be efficiently handled by classical routing solvers. Furthermore, we introduce a performance-guided tuning process that dynamically aligns these mappings with real system performance. Simulations on a Starlink constellation demonstrate that P2R reduces the flow drop rate by up to 52%, while also improving delay and throughput compared with strong feature fusion baselines, offering a robust and scalable solution for reliability-aware routing in large-scale LEO networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Robust UE-Assisted Sensing with Anchor Position Uncertainty for 6G ISAC.
abstract: This paper investigates a sensing system enabled by cellular networks, where a base station (BS) transmits orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals in the downlink and multiple user equipments (UEs) receive the echo signals reflected by multiple targets. The objective is to localize the targets using the BS and all UEs as anchors, employing the elliptic localization method based on the echo signals received at UEs. We address a practical yet challenging scenario in which part of the UEs have highly inaccurate position information. These inaccuracies can severely degrade overall localization performance. To overcome this issue, we propose a robust twophase localization protocol. Specifically, in Phase I, we estimate the bi-static ranges from the BS to each target to all UEs based on the received signals at UEs. In Phase II, we formulate a non-convex optimization problem to jointly estimate the target positions and refine the UE positions given the estimated ranges in Phase I. To solve it, we develop an iterative solution that relies solely on closed-form updates of target and UE positions per iteration by employing alternating optimization (AO) and majorization-minimization (MM) techniques. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach shows great robustness against anchor position uncertainty.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Neural Beam Field for Spatial Beam RSRP Prediction.
abstract: Accurately predicting beam-level reference signal received power (RSRP) is essential for beam management in dense multi-user wireless networks, yet challenging due to high measurement overhead and fast channel variations. This paper proposes Neural Beam Field (NBF), a hybrid neural-physical framework for efficient and interpretable spatial beam RSRP prediction. Central to our approach is the introduction of the Multi-path Conditional Power Profile (MCPP), a learnable physical intermediary representing the site-specific propagation environment. This approach decouples the environment from specific antenna/beam configurations, which helps the model learn site-specific multipath features and enhances its generalization capability. We adopt a decoupled ``blackbox-whitebox" design: a Transformer-based deep neural network (DNN) learns the MCPP from sparse user measurements and positions, while a physics-inspired module analytically infers beam RSRP statistics. To improve convergence and adaptivity, we further introduce a Pretrain-and-Calibrate (PaC) strategy that leverages ray-tracing priors for physics-grounded pretraining and then RSRP data for on-site calibration. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that NBF significantly outperforms conventional table-based channel knowledge maps (CKMs) and pure blackbox DNNs in prediction accuracy, training efficiency, and generalization, while maintaining a compact model size. The proposed framework offers a scalable and physically grounded solution for intelligent beam management in next-generation dense wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive Priority-Aware GTS Scheduling for OCC-Enabled Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Optical Camera Communication (OCC) is a promising enabler for Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) systems, leveraging existing vehicular cameras to provide high data rates and immunity to RF interference. However, its directional, line-of-sight (LoS) nature and dynamic vehicular topologies pose challenges for reliable medium access, especially for time-critical safety messages. This paper presents an adaptive Guaranteed Time Slot (GTS) scheduling framework that incorporates message priority, field-of-view (FoV) geometry, and interference awareness. A two-stage algorithm first performs priority-based slot allocation, followed by image-plane collision resolution using an optical projection model. The superframe structure is dynamically adjusted through payload-aware Superframe Order (SO) and Beacon Order (BO) tuning to reflect real-time traffic demands. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms IEEE 802.15.7, ESAD, and CSMA/CA baselines in terms of delay, throughput, and energy efficiency, making it a viable MAC-layer solution for dense, latencysensitive OCC-based V2V networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Prediction Model of Ionospheric foF2 and hmF2 for Multiple Stations for HF Skywave Communication.
abstract: Accurate prediction of the ionospheric F2-layer critical frequency (foF2) and peak height (hmF2) is crucial for global ionospheric modeling and the reliability of HighFrequency (HF) skywave communication systems. This paper proposes a prediction model of foF2 and hmF2 for multiple stations based on Informer. The model incorporates a spatial embedding layer to effectively capture the dependencies in ionospheric parameters across different geographical locations. Using data from Changping, Mohe, and Zuoling stations in China alongside geomagnetic indices and sunspot number (SSN), the model performs$\mathbf{2 4}$-hour predictions of$\mathbf{f o F 2}$and$\text{hmF2}$. Compared with the International Reference Ionosphere (IRI) model, and with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and standard Informer models using data from single stations, the proposed model reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) of foF2 by up to$43.9 \%, 26.4 \%$, and 25.2 %, respectively; for$\text{hmF2}$, the corresponding maximum RMSE reductions are$35.3 \%, 11.9 \%$, and 13.1 %. Furthermore, it exhibits enhanced robustness when handling noisy data. This study offers a more accurate solution for global ionospheric forecasting and HF skywave communication network planning.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Robust Beamforming for Digital Twin-Enabled RIS Systems: A Hierarchical Meta-Learning Approach.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless system performance, yet their deployment is constrained by the difficulty of acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI). Digital twin (DT) models provide useful prior information on channel characteristics, but the unavoidable sim-to-real gap caused by modeling inaccuracies and environmental mismatches can substantially degrade performance. To address this limitation, we propose an error-aware hierarchical learning framework, termed GMML-BO, which integrates a statistical channel error model with robust optimization. Distinguished from static uncertainty models, the physical channel realization is expressed as a DTderived estimate superimposed with a stochastic residual whose covariance is recursively updated to capture time-varying sim-to-real mismatches. This formulation enables an error-aware data augmentation scheme and yields a robust empirical risk minimization problem. The problem is solved through a hierarchical architecture: an inner gradient-based manifold metalearning (GMML) core leverages objective-function gradients for real-time adaptation, while an outer Bayesian Optimization (BO) controller autonomously tunes hyperparameters on a slower timescale, ensuring low-latency inference with robust generalization. Simulation results demonstrate that GMML-BO consistently outperforms conventional baselines, exhibits stable convergence, and approaches the performance bound under perfect CSI.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multiplicative Updates Beamforming Design for Hybrid Fully-Connected Millimeter-Wave MIMO Systems.
abstract: Achieving the optimal design of analog and digital beamformers, provided by a hybrid architecture using phase shifters (PSs), is crucial for ensuring the spectral efficiency (SE) of millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems. To tackle the challenge of finding optimal hybrid beamformers that directly maximize SE, several studies have adopted the matrix factorization problem as a viable solution in designing at each transceiver side. However, the unit constant modulus (UCM) constraints on analog beamformers resulting from PSs and the joint optimization of digital and analog parts render the hybrid beamforming design problem highly non-convex. In this paper, we develop a hybrid algorithm via the multiplicative update rules technique for solving the matrix factorization problem of finding optimal analog and digital beamformers by easily taking into account practical constraints. By removing the nonnegativity constraints, the proposed method achieves optimal analog and digital beamformers in the hybrid fully connected mmWave multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architecture through a simple implementation enabled by simultaneous updates offered from the closed-form of the multiplicative update rules. According to the numerical simulations, the proposed design is more effective than state-of-the-art design algorithms and is less complex.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Leveraging Kernel Symmetry for Joint Compression and Error Mitigation in Edge Model Transfer.
abstract: This paper investigates communication-efficient neural network transmission by exploiting structured symmetry constraints in convolutional kernels. Instead of transmitting all model parameters, we propose a degrees-of-freedom (DoF) based codec that sends only the unique coefficients implied by a chosen symmetry group, enabling deterministic reconstruction of the full weight tensor at the receiver. The proposed framework is evaluated under quantization and noisy channel conditions across multiple symmetry patterns, signal-to-noise ratios, and bit-widths. To improve robustness against transmission impairments, a projection step is further applied at the receiver to enforce consistency with the symmetry-invariant subspace, effectively denoising corrupted parameters. Experimental results on MNIST and CIFAR-10 using a DeepCNN architecture demonstrate that DoF-based transmission achieves substantial bandwidth reduction while preserving significantly higher accuracy than pruning-based baselines, which often suffer catastrophic degradation. Among the tested symmetries, central-skew symmetry consistently provides the best accuracy-compression tradeoff, confirming that structured redundancy can be leveraged for reliable and efficient neural model delivery over constrained links.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel HARQ Scheme for Semantic Communication Systems.
abstract: Semantic communication focuses on the transmission of semantic information and aims to improve communication efficiency. The combination of semantic communication and Hybrid Automatic Repeat reQuest (HARQ) schemes, which play a crucial role in ensuring reliability, is thus logically reasonable. However, traditional HARQ schemes use cyclic redundancy check (CRC) for error detection, which may lead to significant overhead since the CRC focuses on the bit-level errors and adds redundant bits, while semantic communication mainly focuses on the reliability of semantic information. To address this mismatch, a novel HARQ scheme is designed for semantic communication systems. Specifically, we propose a Semantic Quality Discriminator (SQD) network to assess the semantic quality score of the reconstructed information. Critically, a learnable re-transmission threshold is jointly optimized with the SQD network to enable re-transmission decision-making. The receiver combines the packets using the chase combining (CC) scheme to achieve a diversity gain. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly increases communication quality while reducing communication overhead by optimizing the threshold for the desired performance trade-off.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Pilot-Free End-to-End Communication System Using Complex Convolutional Encoder and Mixture-of-Experts Based Decoder.
abstract: Pilot-free end-to-end (E2E) communication is a promising approach to improve spectral efficiency by removing pilots while maintaining bit-error-rate (BER) performance. However, existing E2E solutions often entail substantial computational complexity to achieve reliable BER under challenging channel conditions, and a low-complexity design that attains low BER remains elusive. To fill in this gap, we propose a mixture-of-experts (MoE) based pilot-free E2E (MoE-E2E) communication framework in this paper. The proposed MoEE2E framework designs a complex convolutional neural network based encoder at the transmitter side instead of conventional real-valued encoder. For the decoder at the receiver side, an SENet-VoVUnit feature extractor is developed followed by a signal reconstruction module composed of delicately designed MoE-Transformer blocks. By leveraging an MoE layer, the MoETransformer blocks could activate only a small subset of experts for different inputs, which can support reliable signal reconstruction under complex channel environments without increasing complexity. Simulation results have shown that the proposed MoE-E2E framework achieves better BER performance with lower computational complexity compared with existing pilotfree E2E frameworks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Contextual Thompson Sampling for Airborne RIS in mmWave-Enabled Metaverse Networks.
abstract: Current millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless technology suffers from restricted coverage and inconsistent signal intensity due to tight line-of-sight (LoS) connectivity constraints. Hence, two cutting-edge technologies, aerials and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), overcome these limitations in mmWave-empowered Metaverse networks. We envision deploying an airborne RIS model to support the mmWave base station (mWBS) in highly dense traffic metaverse hotspots (MVHSs) where mWBS or Metaverse users (MVUs) experience complex propagation and non-LoS environment to deliver metaverse services. Yet commercial aerials suffer from limited battery lifetime. Therefore, the path planning of the airborne-RIS should be optimized to support multiple MVHSs simultaneously while accounting for its energy expenditure within mWBS coverage bounds. Hence, we convey this problem as a contextual multiarmed bandit (CMAB) and envision a contextual Thompson sampling (CTS) algorithm to address it effectively. We treat the airborne RIS as the bandit gamer. It serves different MVHSs (bandit arms) in its trajectory to optimize its achievable rate (i.e., the reward). The context vector includes the location of MVHSs, provided via a GPS service, and the payoff history of each MVHS. Extensive simulations confirm the superiority of our envisioned CTS scheme over baseline solutions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: OTFS-Enabled ISAC Scheduling for LEO Satellite with Reconfigurable Holographic Surfaces Using a Transformer Approach.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites with reconfigurable holographic surfaces (RHS) enable agile aperture control for joint communication and sensing. Fast orbital motion (i.e., 7.5 km/s) produces Doppler shifts exceeding ≈ 25 kHz at 20 GHz, which destabilize OFDM links and challenge real-time scheduling. We propose an orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS)based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that provides Doppler resilience and jointly optimizes beam power allocation, remote user (RU)-beam assignment, and sensing-communication resource sharing under regulatory constraints. Because the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) is highly non-convex and NP-hard, we design a transformer-based scheduler with feasibility-preserving projections and train it via imitation learning on small-scale instances. Simulations under realistic LEO conditions demonstrate (i) a controllable communication-sensing Pareto frontier, (ii) ITU-Rcompliant operation with PFD violations below 0.5% (vs. over 40% for baselines), and (iii) sub-millisecond inference latency (≈ 0.8 ms per epoch). These results confirm that our approach achieves up to 40% higher balanced feasible utility than baseline methods under ITU-R constraints, maintains ITU-R compliance with < 0.5% violation, and enables real-time deployment in nextgeneration LEO satellite systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Denoising-Enabled Semantic Communication for Robust Earth Observation in 6G Satellite Networks: A Swin Transformer Approach.
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) in 6G enable persistent Earth observation (EO), yet satellite downlinks remain bandwidth-limited and vulnerable to path loss, Doppler, and smallscale fading. We propose a semantic communication (SC) pipeline for satellite EO that deploys a lightweight Swin Transformer encoder onboard and a Swin-based decoder with an optional plug-and-play denoiser at the gateway. Training uses channeldiverse pairs of the same scene to promote channel-invariant representations, while inference operates on a single image for reliability and low latency. Across representative operating points, the gateway denoiser consistently improves reconstruction quality while keeping the transmitted feature budget unchanged. On average, it recovers about 60% of the gap in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and roughly 25% of the gap in multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM) relative to a higher-bit-rate baseline. These results show that relocating refinement to the gateway shifts the communication-computation balance toward lower downlink load at comparable quality.
