conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Large Reasoning Models for Optimal Resource Management in Next Generation Wireless Networks.
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks will increasingly rely on device-to-device (D2D) communication and nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) to meet stringent requirements on spectral efficiency (SE) and energy efficiency (EE). However, with growing network complexity and uncertainty, traditional optimization and even conventional large language model (LLM) approaches often struggle to adapt swiftly under changing channel conditions. In this paper, we propose a resource-allocation framework that leverages reasoning-oriented LLMs-referred to as large reasoning models (LRMs)-enhanced with chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting. By explicitly incorporating logical constraints and step-by-step inference, LRMs significantly outperform standard prompting and fine-tuning pipelines across both D2D and NOMA scenarios. Through empirical evaluation, we show that CoT-prompted LRMs achieve nearoptimal SE and EE in a D2D network scenario, while zeroshot prompting works best for a NOMA network scenario. Critically, this reduces the need for extensive retraining, making the approach highly flexible for dynamic network contexts. Our findings underscore the promise of reasoning-driven LLM architectures for next-generation wireless resource allocation, offering improved scalability, adaptability, and interpretability over traditional optimization methods and baseline LLM strategies.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Practical Beam Selection Algorithm Based on Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new practical, low-complex algorithm for Beam Selection (BS) based on Reinforcement Learning, namely the Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB). We analyze the performance of this algorithm in realistic scenarios of highly and moderately populated areas. The reward in the algorithm is defined to minimize the number of handovers, maximize the predefined goodput, minimize the outage probability, and ensure fairness. Moreover, a similar procedure of comparable complexity has been suggested based on heuristic optimization, serving as a benchmark for comparison. The performance of the proposed algorithms for BS has been verified through computer simulations. The results demonstrated the superiority of MAB over the related heuristic algorithm.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Visual-Aided Identification of RIS-Based Jammer via Angle-Aware Neural Modeling.
abstract: In open wireless environments, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) can launch jamming attacks by reflecting legitimate signals with preset phase shifts, causing the jamming and legitimate signals to be temporally simultaneous and spectrally overlapping. Existing countermeasures that rely on temporal or frequency differences between legitimate and jamming signals fail against such RIS-based attacks. This paper proposes a visual jammer identification method that encloses the jammer with a bounding box on the images captured at the base station, which contain both legitimate vehicles and the jamming vehicle equipped with a malicious RIS. We first apply a geometry-based blind source separation (BSS) algorithm to extract jamming signals, and then compute inter-antenna phase difference vectors which implicitly encode angle-of-arrival information, mitigating the impact of BSS-induced ambiguities. Since the angle information of wireless channels is determined by the location of the vehicle in the real environment, which directly corresponds to its position in each image, we propose a machine learning scheme to visually identify the jamming vehicle by enclosing it with a bounding box on the image. Simulation results demonstrate over 91% identification accuracy in common cases with a single base station and show that our method outperforms baseline schemes with multiple base stations by more than 20%.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Quantifying Geometry Effects on Low-Cost Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces.
abstract: Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) promise lowpower coverage extension, yet practical deployments must curb hardware complexity and control overhead. This paper quantifies the performance impact of two cost-saving measures, column-wise element grouping and 1-bit (binary) phase quantization, relative to the ideal fully-controlled, continuous-phase baseline. A single-input single-output link is simulated at 26 GHz (mmWave) across three deployment geometries that vary the relative heights of access point, IRS and user equipment. Results show that switching from continuous to binary phase control reduces median SNR gain by approximately 4 dB, while adopting column-wise grouping introduces a similar penalty; combining both constraints incurs approximately 8 dB loss under heightoffset deployments. When all nodes share the same height, the degradation from column-wise control becomes negligible, indicating deployment geometry can offset control-granularity limits. Despite the losses, a$32 \times 32$column-wise binary IRS still delivers double-digit SNR gains over the no-IRS baseline in most positions, confirming its viability for cost-constrained scenarios. The study provides quantitative guidelines on when simplified IRS architectures can meet link-budget targets and where full element-wise control remains justified.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Massive Digital AirComp with Vector Quantization and Bidirectional Links for FEEL.
abstract: In digital wireless networks, over-the-air computation (AirComp) for federated edge learning (FEEL) is constrained by discrete modulation and quantization, which hinder efficient model aggregation in massive-device scenarios. We propose a Massive Digital AirComp (MD-AC) framework that integrates vector quantization with shared codebooks and bidirectional uplink and downlink optimization in multi-antenna systems under Rician fading. An enhanced approximate message passing algorithm with direct aggregation (AMP-DA) is developed to recover superimposed signals without per-device decoding by exploiting sparsity and multi-antenna diversity. Furthermore, an normalized mean square error (NMSE)-based adaptive power control mechanism is introduced to adjust the uplink transmit power according to aggregation quality feedback, enabling efficient utilization of the total power budget and improved learning convergence. Simulation results on CIFAR-10 demonstrate that MD-AC achieves up to 85.36% test accuracy and accelerates convergence by up to 5.67%, while reducing aggregation NMSE by 23.8% under high-power settings. These results indicate the potential of the proposed framework for scalable and resource-constrained edge learning systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: From CSI to BFI: Calibration for Wi-Fi Sensing.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: SenSem: Integrated Sensing and Semantic Communications for Multi-Device Video Analytics.
abstract: Video analytics is essential for applications such as public safety and smart cities, but transmitting high-resolution video over wireless networks suffers from bandwidth and latency constraints. Existing semantic communication approaches mitigate communication overhead by discarding irrelevant content, yet they impose heavy computation on resource-limited devices. To overcome this challenge, we propose SenSem, a framework that integrates sensing and semantic communications by leveraging target-related information embedded in channel state information. Specifically, we design a location-assisted region-of-interest estimation method to crop video frames prior to transmission, followed by a lightweight semantic evaluator to assess block importance. Based on the reduced frames, we further develop a joint block selection and power control algorithm for multi-device uploading under latency constraints. Experiments on the WARP platform show that SenSem consistently outperforms existing baselines, reducing both transmission and computation overhead while delivering superior analytics performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Channel Knowledge Map-Enabled NLoS ISAC Localization.
abstract: Accurate localization in non-line-of-sight (NLoS) environments remains challenging even with both angle-ofarrival (AoA) and time-of-arrival (ToA) measurements. In complex urban scenarios, the absence of line-of-sight (LoS) paths and the lack of environment prior knowledge make geometric based localization methods inapplicable, while prior-based approach such as fingerprinting is sensitive to environmental perturbations. This paper proposes a novel environment-aware localization framework enabled by the emerging concept called channel knowledge map (CKM). In the offline stage, AoA-ToA path signatures are learned by the CKM, with each path mapped to one candidate scatterer, thereby forming geometric priors within the environment. In the online stage, observed paths are matched to the CKM to extract high-confidence scatterers. Nonlinear least squares (NLS) method is then applied to jointly estimate the user and dominant scatterer locations. Even with imperfect CSI matching, geometric feasibility consistent with CKM scatterer priors provides corrective information and suppresses ambiguity. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms fingerprinting and offers a robust and scalable solution to address the challenging NLoS localization for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Privacy and Security Challenges in Edge-Deployed Generative AI: Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Defense Mechanisms.
abstract: This survey examines the privacy and security challenges of deploying generative AI at the network edge. Unlike cloud-based systems, edge GenAI is susceptible to hardware-level exploits and training-data leakage due to physical accessibility and heterogeneous security boundaries. We present a comprehensive threat taxonomy and systematically evaluate documented attacks-such as power analysis and cache side-channel techniques-across mobile and industrial IoT platforms. We also analyze the efficacy of Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) and selective-protection schemes, highlighting a 3-21% CPU overhead associated with hardware isolation. The paper concludes by outlining open research directions for securing multimodal models and scaling enclaves for billion-parameter deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: An Intrusion Detection Mechanism for Smart Homes Using Channel-Based Lightweight Classification.
abstract: Smart home networks connect heterogeneous, resource limited devices over imperfect indoor wireless channels, making intrusion detection challenging unless communication effects and compute constraints are modeled jointly. We propose a security driven communication and compute framework that jointly accounts for communication impairments, computation limits, and queueing effects across edge, gateway, and cloud layers. The execution path selection problem is addressed with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) under a constraint-aware reward design that enforces cost and delay budgets while maximizing security performance. Experimental results show that the learned policy consistently prioritizes the edge-gateway-cloud (E-G-C) path, achieving a favorable balance between security, latency, and cost while remaining robust across varying traffic, payload, and channel conditions. For detection, we design a lightweight Neural Network (LNN) for near edge binary classification, which combines one dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (Conv1D) and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) to capture both traffic patterns and temporal dependencies. Across three real world datasets, the LNN consistently achieves over$\mathbf{9 2 \%}$accuracy and robustness with low model complexity and small model size. It is suitable for real time intrusion detection in smart homes. In conclusion, this framework provides a foundation for future dynamic Intrusion Detection System (IDS) placement and scalable deployment in modern smart homes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Cell-Satellite Association, Channel Assignment and Power Allocation in LEO Networks.
abstract: Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks have demonstrated advantages for efficiently and globally providing communication services across diverse environments, particularly in remote areas. However, reducing communication interference remains a critical issue. This paper studies a network of multiple LEO satellites that cover several ground cells with limited network resources. We aim to maximize the fair cell data rate by jointly considering cell-satellite association, channel assignment, and power allocation. The formulated problem appears to be a mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem, which is challenging to solve. To handle this, our optimization framework decomposes the problem into three subproblems, which are efficiently solved by the proposed algorithms and the successive convex approximation method. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed solution outperforms existing approaches in terms of the fair data rate for the served cells.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Communication-Efficient UAV-Mounted RIS for IoT: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) applications has highlighted the importance of reliable wireless connectivity in dense urban environments. Conventional terrestrial base stations often experience significant performance degradation due to building-induced blockages, leading to persistent non-line-of-sight (NLOS) transmissions. To address this challenge, this paper presents a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based framework that employs an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) integrated with a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS). The proposed approach enables adaptive optimization of data collection and communication processes, thereby improving connectivity in highly dynamic urban scenarios. Experimental evaluations conducted in NLOS-dominant environments show that all DRL-based strategies consistently outperform the random phase baseline. The results confirm the robustness and effectiveness of UAV-RIS systems and provide practical insights for their deployment in next-generation IoT-enabled communication networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dynamic Joint Localization and Data Collection for UAV-Assisted Networks with Location Uncertainty: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: UAV-assisted data collection faces significant challenges in scenarios where sensor locations are unknown or uncertain. Unlike traditional schemes that rely on ideal geometric information, this work models the dynamic reduction of position uncertainty through active sensing and formulates a joint optimization problem to minimize mission completion time. To tackle the inherent non-convexity and the Partial Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) nature of the system, a Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) framework is proposed. This framework intelligently decouples the decisionmaking process into macroscopic task scheduling (sensing vs. communication) and microscopic trajectory control. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms benchmark schemes, reducing the average system delay by up to 45.7%, thereby validating the robustness and efficiency of the proposed approach in dynamic environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Stgread: a Graph Diffusion-Based Approach for Satellite Network Traffic Prediction.
abstract: Satellite networks generate highly dynamic traffic due to frequent topology changes and diverse service demands, making long-horizon forecasting challenging. Existing spatiotemporal graph neural networks (STGNNs) rely on discrete diffusion layers that suffer from oversmoothing and accuracy degradation with depth. We propose STGREAD, a spatiotemporal model integrating reaction-diffusion dynamics with neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) solvers. Each block performs continuous-time propagation with adaptive reaction terms, preserving feature diversity and improving stability. Experiments on large-scale satellite traffic datasets show that STGREAD consistently outperforms baselines including STGCN, DCRNN, Graph WaveNet, and MTGNN. With only two blocks, it achieves a test MSE of 0.1718, reducing error by 9.6% vs. STGCN and 14.5% vs. DCRNN. Even under 200-s horizons, STGREAD maintains 0.187, while baselines exceed 0.19. Dirichlet energy analysis further shows that STGREAD preserves higher feature variance and robustness against oversmoothing, achieving strong accuracy with shallow architectures for dynamic, delay-sensitive satellite networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Securing LFM-Based Wireless Sensing Against Deception Jamming in 6G Networks.
abstract: In wireless sensing systems, Linear Frequency Modulation (LFM) signals are widely used due to their high resolution and Doppler robustness. However, their deterministic structure makes them vulnerable to deception jamming, where adversaries inject forged echoes to manipulate sensing outcomes. Existing waveform-agility-based countermeasures face critical trade-offs among detection robustness, security, and compatibility, as simple agility patterns can be rapidly spoofed while complex schemes degrade receiver synchronization. To address these limitations, we propose a Tag-embedded Deception Jamming Detection (TDJD) framework that superimposes low-power random tag signals onto LFM waveforms. These tags are preserved in genuine echoes but distorted during jamming operations, creating exploitable statistical asymmetries. A Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) detector is developed with thresholds derived from Generalized Gaussian Distribution (GGD) modeling. Simulation results demonstrate superior detection performance, enhanced security, and strong compatibility with legacy systems, particularly under low-SNR conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: AdaJSCCV: Adaptive Prompt-Tuning for Semantic Video Transmission.
abstract: DeepJSCC has shown potential in semantic video communication, yet existing methods face challenges in dynamically adapting to both channel conditions and content characteristics. Most approaches rely on static coding networks and computationally intensive entropy models, limiting their practical applicability. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces AdaJSCCV, an adaptive DeepJSCC framework for wireless video transmission that jointly optimizes channel robustness and content awareness. Our approach incorporates a prompt-tuning based dynamic channel adaptation module, which continuously adjusts both convolutional kernels and modulation coefficients in response to channel semantics-even under coarse or partial channel state information. Furthermore, we design a lightweight network-free entropy model that efficiently encodes video frames into variable-length codewords from a global temporal perspective, substantially reducing encoding complexity. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed AdaJSCCV consistently outperforms traditional separate video coding schemes as well as other DeepJSCC approaches, while adapting effectively to diverse channel variations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Iterative Compensation for Clipping Noise in Space-Time Line Coded OFDM Systems.
abstract: As a novel space-time code (STC) that achieves full spatial diversity, space-time line code (STLC) exploits channel state information (CSI) to encode symbols from two adjacent time slots. Owing to its special structure, the transmitted symbols can be retrieved at the receiver without full CSI, which becomes competitive in the implementation of industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) for the sixth-generation$(6 \mathrm{G})$networks. When combined with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), this STLC-OFDM scheme is capable of combating multipath fading in time-varying channels. However, the threat of high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) posed to the existing IIoT system can still not be overlooked. Considering clipping is an efficient technique to address high PAPR problem, this paper introduces an iterative hard-decision compensation method in order to mitigate the distortion caused by clipping noise. Specifically, the target symbols and clipping noise are first estimated based on a priori information, after which the received signal can be updated to a more accurate symbol model. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm delivers considerable bit error rate (BER) performance improvement compared to clipped STLC-OFDM systems without noise compensation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deviation-Aware Trajectory Embedding for Fine-Tuning Triggering in DRL-Based Wireless Network Resource Management.
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a viable solution for wireless network resource management, allowing agents to optimize long-term network performance through interaction with complex environments. However, DRL-based wireless resource management often requires expensive retraining or manual adjustments. To address this issue, we propose a trajectory-based triggering framework that enables DRL and meta-RL agents to perform deviation-aware fine-tuning only when a wireless environment drifts from its training distribution. By integrating offline trajectory modeling with real-time deviation detection, our method detects deviations using Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD). By forming fixed-length trajectories from state transitions and encoding them via a variational autoencoder (VAE), our approach detects trajectory deviation using JSD. Extensive experiments show that the proposed framework improves user satisfaction by up to 11 % and OOD detection accuracy by 16.7 % compared to the return-based IDAQ baseline, demonstrating efficient and reliable adaptation to dynamic wireless environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: GDL-Loc: GNSS-Based Deep Learning Localization for Large Underground Parking Lots.
abstract: With the rapid development of smart cities and intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) applications, demand for underground positioning is growing increasingly. However, traditional Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals fail to cover indoor areas due to obstructions, making indoor positioning impossible. This paper proposes a GNSS-Based Deep Learning Localization (GDL-Loc) system for practical applications in Large Underground Parking Lots (LUPLs). Specifically, a Variational Mode Decomposition-Wavelet (VW) processing algorithm is first proposed, which improves the temporal stability and learnability of features by performing modal decomposition and denoising on multidimensional observation time series. Secondly, a TimesNet-QTR localization model based on quality-aware trajectory regularization is proposed to ensure the continuity and stability of the trajectory in low-quality areas, thereby significantly improving localization accuracy. The experiment was deployed in a real$1028 \mathbf{m}^{2}$underground parking lot, using only one repeater connected to distributed antennas. Experimental results show that the GDL-Loc system achieves a dynamic positioning accuracy of 0.51 m, which is an overall improvement of 40 % in average error compared to the baseline model.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Sensing-Task-Oriented Generative Channel Model for 6G Integrated Sensing and Communications.
abstract: Accurate and efficient channel modeling is paramount for the performance evaluation of 6G integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. However, conventional methods face a critical trade-off among accuracy, generalization, and computational complexity, hindering large-scale system-level simulations. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel sensing-task-oriented generative channel model tailored for target localization, tracking, and identification. Our approach is founded on a transformer-based conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) that learns to generate realistic multiple scattering center (MSC) attributes from highfidelity full-wave electromagnetic simulation data of vehicle and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) targets. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a superior balance of these competing requirements. Notably, it reproduces channel characteristics with high fidelity while accelerating channel generation by a factor of one million compared to direct simulation. Furthermore, through task-oriented validation, our model shows significant performance advantages over traditional statistical models, particularly in collaborative sensing scenarios, which is a hallmark of future 6G ISAC. This work provides a foundational and computationally efficient tool for realistic performance evaluation of next-generation ISAC systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dynamic Beam-Hopping Design for Leo Satellite Networks with User Priority Awareness.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) multibeam satellites with beam-hopping (BH) enable flexible resource allocation, but spatio-temporally non-uniform traffic and heterogeneous service priorities pose significant challenges to beam coverage and scheduling design. This paper proposes a user-priority-driven BH scheme that embeds service priorities into both dynamic beam footprint construction and time-slot allocation, with the objective of maximizing the weighted number of satisfied users. A two-stage heuristic algorithm is developed, where beam footprints are first generated using a minimum disk-coverbased method, followed by a priority-aware BH scheduling strategy that jointly considers user priority and residual traffic demand. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly improves high-priority user satisfaction and achieves higher overall weighted satisfaction compared with fixed coverage and priority-agnostic schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Mixture-of-Generative-Experts Framework for Adaptive Security in Diverse Wireless Environments.
abstract: The future 6 G wireless networks are expected to provide reliable and secure service provisioning in diverse wireless environments, yet the existing studies are mostly based on the underlying assumption of single static wireless scenario. To fill this gap, this paper investigates the physical layer security issue aiming to cover over a variety of wireless scenarios. Specifically, we first establish a model to characterize a set of wireless scenarios and formulate the corresponding physical layer security beamforming problem. Then, we select a few representative scenarios and construct a dedicate generative diffusion model (GDM) for security beamformer output, over which a mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework is established with GDM-based experts. Within the MoE framework, a gating network is trained to recognize the properties of the scenario based on the feature engineering of the channel matrix. The top-rated experts matching the scenario are selected, where the output from the experts are combined as the security beamformer for the scenario. Simulation results show that the proposed MoE framework can accurately identify the scenario with matched experts, and combined experts provide effective security solution for unseen wireless scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Testbed for Digitally-Assisted RF Self-Interference Cancellation Based on Envelope Detectors.
abstract: Existing digitally-assisted radio frequency (RF) selfinterference (SI) cancellation methods often require high computational complexity and high-rate ADCs for the in-band full-duplex wireless system. Therefore, this paper proposes a digitally-assisted RF SI cancellation method based on envelope detectors (ED), requiring low computational complexity and lowrate ADCs. First, this paper models the RF SI cancellation system based on ED. Then, the SI cancellation ratio (SICR) expression is derived to evaluate the SI cancellation performance and to derive the closed-form expression for SICR accordingly. Next, this paper uses complex arithmetic operations (CAO) to compare the computational complexity of the proposed algorithm with that of existing algorithms. Finally, a testbed is designed and built to verify the feasibility of the proposed algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate that the CAO of the proposed RF SI cancellation algorithm is 76.9% and 95.2% lower than the adaptive dithered linear search (DLS) algorithm and the neural network (NN) algorithm, respectively, when the SICR reaches 35.8 dB. In addition, the proposed algorithm only requires the ADC rate of 40 MHz, while the DLS and the NN require the ADC rate of 1 GHz.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Joint Optimization for UAV-Mounted STAR-RIS Networks with Energy Harvesting.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) are increasingly recognized as an enabling component of sixthgeneration (6 G) wireless systems, as they allow controllable modification of the propagation environment to improve both sum-rate and energy efficiency. This work investigates a UAVmounted simultaneous transmitting and reflecting RIS (STARRIS) network, where an energy-harvesting-enabled aerial platform functions as a reconfigurable relay to support users located on both the reflection and transmission sides. A joint nonconvex optimization problem is formulated to optimize the UAV trajectory, base station beamforming, STAR-RIS reflection and transmission coefficients, and the energy harvesting powersplitting ratio. The objective is to maximize a weighted sum of energy efficiency and harvested energy while satisfying users' quality-of-service (QoS) requirements under practical mobility and transmit power constraints. To address this challenging control problem, deterministic policy-gradient-based deep reinforcement learning algorithms, namely deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) and twin delayed DDPG (TD3), are employed within a continuous-control environment that incorporates realistic Rician fading channels. Simulation results demonstrate that TD3 achieves more stable convergence behavior and superior energy efficiency compared to the baseline DDPG approach while effectively optimizing the weighted objective of energy efficiency and harvested energy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Soft Information Aided Diagonal Kalman Filter for Joint Channel Estimation and Detection in Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a soft-information-aided diagonal Kalman filter (SIA-DKF) for joint channel estimation and symbol detection (JED) in massive multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Specifically, building upon the Kalman filter (KF) framework for JED, the proposed SIA-DKF incorporates the symbol means and variances obtained from variational inference (VI) into the KF, improving its ability to track channels and mitigating mismatches in the update step. Furthermore, SIA-DKF not only exploits favorable propagation in massive MIMO to simplify the VI for symbol detection, but also employs a diagonal approximation of the covariance matrix at each channel update step, thereby significantly reducing the computational complexity. Simulations confirm that SIA-DKF improves the bit error rate (BER) with lower complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Age-Aware Scheduling for Joint Control-Communication Design in Cislunar Relay System.
abstract: Constructing the International Lunar Research Station (ILRS) represents a key objective of future lunar exploration, where heterogeneous distributed systems form a typical Relay Control-Communication System (RCCS). However, remote telemetry and telecommand operations in the RCCS face severe timeliness and effectiveness challenges due to limited relay satellite resources. To address this, we propose a Dynamic Programming-based Relay Scheduling Mechanism (DPRSM) for multi-loop Cislunar RCCS (CRCCS), introducing a novel Effective Value Loss (EVL) metric to jointly optimize communication and control for high timeliness and effectiveness. Simulation results demonstrate that DPRSM significantly outperforms existing Weighted Round Robin (WRR) and minimal Age of Information (AoI) schemes while ensuring system stability.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Robust Task-Oriented Semantic Communication with Visual-Brain Multimodal Learning.
abstract: Task-oriented semantic communication has gained popularity for its ability to reduce communication overhead without compromising task performance. Semantic-level perturbations pose a critical challenge to task-oriented communication by corrupting task-relevant information. We observe that electroencephalography (EEG) is inherently robust to this type of semantic perturbations, offering a promising avenue for model regularization. To address this problem, we introduce an EEGassisted visual-brain multimodal learning framework, leveraging EEG signals as a proxy for human semantic understanding in training to regularize the image encoder to perturbationrobust semantic representations. Specifically, our framework incorporates two key components: a dual-path learning strategy that balances robustness with task-specific accuracy, and a multipositive InfoNCE loss designed to capture deeper semantic associations between modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior robustness against varying levels of semantic perturbations while maintaining stable performance on clean data.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Safety-Constrained Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reliable Wireless Autonomy.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and reinforcement learning (RL) have shown significant promise in wireless systems, enabling dynamic spectrum allocation, traffic management, and large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) coordination. However, their deployment in mission-critical applications introduces the risk of unsafe emergent behaviors, such as UAV collisions, denial-ofservice events, or instability in vehicular networks. Existing safety mechanisms are predominantly reactive, relying on anomaly detection or fallback controllers that intervene only after unsafe actions occur, which cannot guarantee reliability in ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) settings. In this work, we propose a proactive safety-constrained RL framework that integrates proof-carrying control (PCC) with empowermentbudgeted (EB) enforcement. Each agent action is verified through lightweight mathematical certificates to ensure compliance with interference constraints, while empowerment budgets regulate the frequency of safety overrides to balance safety and autonomy. We implement this framework on a wireless uplink scheduling task using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PCC+EB controller eliminates unsafe transmissions while preserving system throughput and predictable autonomy. Compared with unconstrained and reactive baselines, our method achieves provable safety guarantees with minimal performance degradation. These results highlight the potential of proactive safety constrained RL to enable trustworthy wireless autonomy in future 6 G networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Synthetic Cellular Network Modeling via Public Data and AI-Enhanced KPI Modeling.
abstract: Cellular network design, optimization, and performance benchmarking have traditionally depended on proprietary datasets collected by mobile network operators (MNOs), constraining independent research and limiting replicability. This paper introduces an operator-agnostic modeling framework for synthetic cellular network planning and Key Performance Indicator (KPI) generation using openly accessible geospatial and demographic datasets. The framework integrates land use/land cover (LULC) data, population density grids, and publicly available LTE drive-test traces to characterize radio environments without operator intervention. A hybrid statistical-generative modeling pipeline is developed, combining geo-statistical clustering with deep generative AI models to synthesize realistic traffic loads, interference patterns, and KPI distributions across heterogeneous regions. Frequency, bandwidth, and deployment parameters are user-configurable, enabling scenario generalization and transferability across geographic domains. Furthermore, a domain-adaptive learning module enables the trained model to extrapolate KPI behavior in previously unseen environments, achieving operator-level fidelity in coverage, throughput, and quality-of-service metrics. The proposed approach establishes a data-independent methodology for cellular network emulation, promoting reproducibility, cost-efficiency, and open benchmarking. This work highlights how AI-driven surrogate modeling and open geospatial intelligence can democratize access to network performance analytics, accelerating innovation in wireless communication research, digital infrastructure planning, and policymaking.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Beamforming and RIS Phase Optimization for Secure HAPS Downlink Communications.
abstract: High altitude platform stations (HAPS) are envisioned as key non-terrestrial base stations in future sixthgeneration (6 G) networks, yet their broadcast links are inherently vulnerable to eavesdropping. This paper investigates the physical layer security (PLS) of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided HAPS downlink communication, where a multiantenna HAPS base station (BS) serves a single antenna ground user in the presence of a single antenna aerial eavesdropper. We formulate the joint design of the HAPS transmit beamformer and phase RIS matrix as a non-convex secrecy rate maximization problem under unit-norm and unit-modulus constraints. An alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed for (i) fixed RIS phases, where the secrecy ratio is cast as a generalized Rayleigh quotient, and the optimal beamformer is obtained from the dominant generalized eigenvector, and (ii) for fixed beamformer, RIS phases are refined via element-wise coordinate descent over a finite phase set. To rigorously validate the framework, a small discrete codebook is constructed, and the proposed algorithm is compared against true exhaustive and random optimization (RO). Monte Carlo simulations under realistic HAPS geometries show that the proposed scheme closely approaches exhaustive search while significantly outperforming RO, providing practical insights for secure RIS-aided HAPS deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Edge IoBNT Networks for Bioprocess Digital Twins: A Physics-Informed ML Approach.
abstract: Edge computing is becoming critical for real-time bioprocess monitoring and digital twin (DT) development, which enables low-latency data acquisition and localized intelligence. In biotechnology, wastewater treatment, pharmaceuticals, and healthcare, continuous monitoring of microbial growth requires near-sensor computation and reliable nano-scale communication. Conventional Internet of Things (IoT) frameworks and standard neural networks often lack the network efficiency and physics-awareness needed for precise, adaptive prediction. This paper proposes an Edge framework combining Monod kinetics, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and the Internet of Bio-Nano Things (IoBNT) to enhance DTs for bioprocess applications. The IoBNT layer enables real-time biochemical sensing through nano-sensors, while PINNs ensure accurate predictions under sparse measurements. Results show 68 % data reduction, latency improved from 24.7 ms to 8.4 ms, PDR increased from 93.5 % to 99.3 %, bandwidth reduced from 11.2 Mbps to 6.8 Mbps, and energy per node decreased from 13.7 mJ to 6.3 mJ, confirming the framework's high efficiency and precision.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Intelligent Multi-Agent Framework for RIS Optimization in 6G: A RAG-based Approach.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) are envisioned as key enablers for 6G wireless networks, enabling programmable propagation environments that enhance coverage, fairness, and energy efficiency. However, optimizing RIS configurations under time-varying and uncertain channel conditions remains challenging. Classical optimization approaches such as gradient descent (GD), manifold optimization (MO), and alternating optimization (AO) provide local optimality but lack adaptivity and incur high computational cost in dynamic scenarios. This paper proposes the Intelligent Multi-Agent Framework for RIS Optimization (MAFRO), which integrates a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based knowledge module with a cooperative multi-agent architecture. MAFRO comprises two interacting agents: a Coordinator Agent that retrieves and selects the most suitable optimization strategy (GD, AO, or MO) from a learned memory of prior scenarios, and an Evaluator Agent that assesses user Quality of Service (QoS) and fairness to guide the system's solver adaptation. Through this interaction, the framework first restores user QoS and then minimizes total transmit power under fairness-aware constraints. Simulation results under dynamic mmWave channel conditions show that MAFRO outperforms classical optimization methods by achieving up to$2 \times$higher rank-weighted satisfaction per watt and faster QoS recovery. These results highlight the potential of retrieval-based reasoning to improve adaptability, dependability, and energy efficiency in RIS-assisted 6G systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Design and Optimization of DGS-Based MIMO Antenna Using Machine Learning for Modern Wireless Communications.
abstract: This paper presents the design and machine learning (ML) optimization of a two-port MIMO antenna with a Defected Ground Structure (DGS) for modern wireless communications. The overall dimensions of the proposed MIMO antenna are 90$\text{mm} \times 40 ~\text{mm} \times 0.8 ~\text{mm}$on a Rogers RT duroid 5880 substrate. The results of the MIMO antenna give better isolation (20 dB) and a maximum gain of 2.65 dB with efficiency ($>90 \%$). DGS is used to achieve a resonance frequency of 2.57 GHz over a frequency range. The DGS functions work as a reflector, reducing unwanted radiation. As a result, good isolation in the resonant band is extended. The MIMO design's bandwidth ranges from 2.33 to 2.80 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 0.47 GHz, a center frequency of 2.565 GHz, and a fractional bandwidth of$\mathbf{1 8. 3 3 \%}$. MIMO diversity performance measures, including ECC ($<0.1$), DG ($>9.95 ~\text{dB}$), MEG (1), TARC ($<-10 ~\text{dB}$), and characteristic results such as S-parameters and radiation patterns, are satisfied and yield better diversity performance. A 2.57 GHz resonance frequency is used for various wireless communication applications, including LTE, Wi-Fi, WLAN, and WiMAX, wearable technology, IoT devices, and some other wireless devices operating in the sub- 6 GHz range. MIMO is optimized using KBNN, ANN, decision trees, and random forest ML methods. The ML optimization approach is used to determine the optimal design parameters for the MIMO. Random forest techniques outperform other ML algorithms in accurately predicting S-parameter S11 (99%).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Liski: a Lightweight Secret Key Generation Scheme for Resource-Constrained Iot Devices.
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has made secure and efficient communication increasingly critical. This paper introduces LISKI, a lightweight secret-key generation scheme designed for resource-constrained IoT environments. Built on the Internet Protocol (IP) framework, LISKI enables mutual authentication with integrity assurance through just two message exchanges, minimizing communication overhead and computational complexity. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on intensive computation and multiple message rounds, LISKI leverages steganography and lightweight cryptographic hashing to embed authentication data directly into payloads. By combining hidden data with randomly generated special-prime values using XOR operations, the scheme eliminates the need for a separate authentication phase. LISKI is implemented using standard cryptographic algorithms, including AES-256, RSA, DSA, ECC, and Diffie-Hellman. Performance evaluation shows that AES-256 significantly reduces key generation, encryption, and embedding time by up to 60 % compared to other algorithms. Moreover, LISKI outperforms conventional approaches by a factor of 2-5 in terms of efficiency and time complexity, making it a compelling solution for secure IoT communications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Transformer Based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Fine-Grained Network Throughput Prediction.
abstract: In the context of Edge Intelligence, network throughput exhibits significant non-stationarity and highly dynamic fluctuations. Traditional Transformer-based models, however, struggle to capture these dynamics, leading to insufficient prediction accuracy, which limits their application in realtime scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) Enhanced Transformer model. Unlike conventional architectures that rely solely on static activation functions, our model replaces the positionwise Feed-Forward Networks (FFNs) within the encoder with a KAN layer that utilizes learnable B-spline functions. This design is specifically tailored to capture the fine-grained dynamics of network throughput, where the local support property of B-splines enables adaptive, non-linear feature transformations at each depth in response to instantaneous input changes, without affecting the global approximation. As a result, the modified Transformer can more accurately reconstruct rapid micro-dynamics and sharp throughput peaks that are typically smoothed out by standard Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs), thereby maintaining high prediction fidelity amidst network instability. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach effectively mitigates peak detection lag and significantly improves throughput prediction accuracy at 100 ms granularity, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Model-Driven Aided Expectation Propagation Learning for AFDM Signal Detection in High-Mobility Communications.
abstract: In this paper, a deep learning-based Expectation Propagation (EP) algorithm model combined with a Graph Neural Network (GNN) detector (DeepEP-AFDM) is proposed for reliable symbol detection in affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) systems over doubly dispersive channels. The proposed method unfolds the iterative EP algorithm into a deep neural network, preserving the interpretable factor-graph structure while utilizing specialized neural modules to learn adaptive priors and layer-wise damping factors from data. This hybrid design effectively mitigates the severe inter-symbol interference and model mismatch inherent in dense effective AFDM channels, ensuring robust signal recovery in high-mobility scenarios. Simulation results demonstrate that DeepEP-AFDM achieves superior error rate performance compared to the classic EP benchmark, while maintaining a computational complexity order of$\mathcal{O}\left(L N^{2}\right)$comparable to standard EP.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Transmission Protocols for Uplink Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS)-Enhanced Sensing.
abstract: Two types of uplink sensing protocols for pinchingantenna systems (PASS)-assisted sensing are proposed in this paper: i) pinch switching (PS), which performs separate pinching beamforming for each time slot, and ii) pinch multiplexing (PM), which applies a single pinching beamforming for all time slots. Instead of using the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) as a sensing performance metric, Bayesian CRB (BCRB) is employed in this paper, which leverages the prior distributions of the sensing parameters, avoiding evaluation at a specific parameter realization. Based on these protocols, both the total power minimization problem subject to a BCRB threshold and the minmax BCRB problem subject to a total power constraint are formulated. By leveraging Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, these problems are equivalently converted into a search over pinching antenna (PA) positions and solved using an elementwise algorithm. Numerical results show the benefits of PASS over conventional benchmarks and heuristic PA-position-optimization methods for uplink sensing.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Dynamic Minimum-Hop-Region Ant Colony Optimization Routing Algorithm for LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: The deployment of large-scale Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations is poised to enable global networking with low latency and high bandwidth. Nevertheless, driven by the network's topological complexity alongside heterogeneous and dynamic user services, the ensuing traffic surge poses a significant challenge to the satellite Internet infrastructure. To reduce the end-to-end (E2E) delay, improve the inter-satellite data transfer efficiency and ensure the network quality of service, this paper proposes the Minimum-Hop-Region Ant Colony Optimization (MHACO) routing algorithm for large-scale LEO satellite networks. First, based on a coordinate graph (CG) model of Walker constellations, the algorithm computes a dynamic minimum-hop path region. It then employs an ant colony optimization procedure to generate routing tables. Subsequently, the lowest-delay feasible paths are iteratively selected. Simulation results show that the proposed MHACO routing algorithm not only reduces the route count, the hop count and the delay of E2E path, but also improves the file delivery ratio.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DGTS: Dependency-Aware GNN-Guided Proactive Task Scheduler for Cloud-Edge Systems.
abstract: The increasing number of latency-critical applications has shifted toward hybrid cloud-edge architectures, where scheduling interdependent tasks presents significant challenges. Existing approaches often manage dependencies reactively, leading to suboptimal resource utilization. Therefore, in this work, we propose DGTS (Dependency-aware GNN-guided Proactive Task Scheduling) Framework for Cloud-Edge systems. Our approach first trains a GNN offline to learn task priorities from dependency graph structures. When a new task set arrives, the pre-trained GNN model is used to proactively infer priorities online. This learned structural importance then guides a dynamic scheduling algorithm in making real-time, intelligent offloading and preemption decisions. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, achieving 22 % profit improvement over the strongest SOTA method. Moreover, DGTS strikes an effective balance between performance and efficiency. DGTS achieves profit levels nearly identical to a theoretical baseline while offering an$8 x$improvement in scheduling plan generation speed, making it a practical and powerful solution for large-scale cloud-edge systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RFF-BO: Efficient Antenna Position Optimization for Fluid Antenna-Aided MU-MISO Systems.
abstract: Fluid antennas (FAs) introduce a new degree of freedom in wireless systems by dynamically repositioning antenna elements to enhance link performance. However, identifying near-optimal antenna positions without channel state information (CSI) remains a major challenge. This paper proposes a Bayesian optimization (BO) framework that efficiently explores antenna locations and maximizes achievable sum rate without requiring explicit channel models. The framework adopts a random Fourier feature (RFF) surrogate with incremental ridgeregression updates, approximating Gaussian process learning at much reduced complexity. To accelerate exploration, a grid-based batch selection strategy combines variance-driven shortlisting, expected-improvement maximization, and spatialrepulsion constraints, ensuring diverse and information-rich sampling. Simulation results show that the proposed RFF-BO method achieves sum-rate performance comparable to particle swarm optimization (PSO) and exhaustive grid search, while greatly reducing pilot overhead and computational cost.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Step Traffic Forecasting with Future-Guided Learning and Multi-Teacher Distillation.
abstract: To address the challenges of error accumulation and long-horizon divergence in multi-step network forecasting for 5 G core and backbone transport networks, this paper proposes a method based on Future-Guided Learning (FGL) and Multi-Teacher Distillation. The proposed approach introduces a causally consistent framework that leverages futurewindow teachers and a history-window student model. More specifically, multiple heterogeneous teacher models generate predictive distributions based on short-horizon windows that are closer to the forecasting targets. Then time-shifted probabilistic distillation transfers the resulting future soft labels to the student model, which is trained solely on historical data. This method significantly improves the accuracy and stability of long-horizon predictions. It does not incorporate future data during inference. For the student model, we adopt iTransformer-Lite, a lightweight multivariate time-series architecture, which reduces model size while enhancing the efficiency of multivariate interaction modeling. Experiments on the real-world CESNET-TimeSeries24 dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves lower RMSE and higher R-squared values for long-horizon forecasting, while maintaining a lightweight inference process. This approach provides reliable forward-looking insights, supporting proactive operations, traffic engineering, and slice resource orchestration in 5G and beyond networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: One-Step Generative Channel Estimation via Average Velocity Field.
abstract: Generative models have shown immense potential for wireless communication by learning complex channel data distributions. However, the iterative denoising process associated with these models imposes a significant challenge in latency-sensitive wireless communication scenarios, particularly in channel estimation. To address this challenge, we propose a novel solution for one-step generative channel estimation. Our approach bypasses the time-consuming iterative steps of conventional models by directly learning the average velocity field. Through extensive simulations, we validate the effectiveness of our proposed method over existing state-of-the-art diffusion-based approach. Specifically, our scheme achieves a normalized mean squared error up to 2.65 dB lower than the diffusion method and reduces latency by around 90%, demonstrating the potential of our method to enhance channel estimation performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Euler: An Out-of-Order-Aware Load Balancing with Adaptive Granularity for AI Clusters.
abstract: Emerging artificial intelligence (AI) workloads pose new challenges on RoCE(RDMA over Converged Ethernet), due to their unique traffic patterns. In this paper, we first show that existing load balancing algorithms for RoCE fail to work well in AI scenarios, because of low-entropy AI traffic characteristics and the limited out-of-order recovery capability on hardware devices. Based on the insights, we propose Euler, a novel load balancing scheme for RoCE, which makes a trade-off between the network entropy and the degree of out-of-order packets by out-of-order-aware adaptive granularity switching. Euler also introduces a traffic isolation mechanism based on path weights to avoid the coexistence of traffic with different granularities on the same path. In this way, it can further reduce queueing delay and improve throughput. Euler is deployed on end-hosts, without any modifications on the switches. Thus, it can be easily deployed in practice. The experimental results of the NS3 simulations show that compared with the existing load balancing schemes, Euler achieves performance improvements of up to 17.2% and 37.5% respectively in the average Flow Completion Time (FCT) and 99 percent FCT, while simultaneously reducing the degree of network disorder by more than 6.8X.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Bit-Flip Fano Sequential Decoding of Polarization-Adjusted Convolutional (PAC) Codes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Efficient Beamforming for Discrete SIM-Aided Multiuser Systems Under Statistical CSI.
abstract: Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIM) have emerged as a revolutionary architecture for next-generation wireless communications, offering wave-domain signal processing capabilities with significantly reduced hardware complexity compared to conventional systems. However, most existing SIM research assumes continuous phase shifts and perfect instantaneous channel state information (CSI), which are impractical due to hardware discrete phase shift constraints and prohibitive pilot overhead. This paper presents a joint power allocation and discrete phase shift optimization framework for SIMaided multiuser multiple-input single-output(MISO) downlink systems under statistical CSI. We formulate the achievable sum rate maximization problem considering practical discrete phase constraints and derive a closed-form expression for the average achievable rate under statistical CSI. To tackle the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we decouple the problem by using the weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) algorithm and alternating optimization (AO). Subsequently, we utilize the Lagrangian multiplier method and alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to obtain closed-form iterative solutions. Our simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm reduces computational complexity by a factor of 50 compared to semi-definite relaxation (SDR) methods, while maintaining over 85 % of the continuous phase shift performance with only 1-bit quantization, highlighting its feasibility for low-cost hardware systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RIS-Assisted Physical Layer Group Key Generation: A MARL Perspective.
abstract: Physical-layer group key generation (PGKG) has been an attractive alternative for secure group communications in wireless networks. In this paper, we propose a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted PGKG scheme for the first time, which introduces RIS technology to enhance the key generation performance via a hybrid configuration of random and optimized phase shifts. To address the coordination challenge between the RIS and nodes under decentralized deployment, we propose an algorithm based on a fully cooperative multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL) mechanism that jointly configures the RIS phase shifts and the nodes' broadcasting coefficients. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms existing works, achieving a higher sum secret key rate (SKR) along with stronger robustness against eavesdropping.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Clover GAI-IoV: Enabling Secure, Efficient, and High-Quality Generative AI in Vehicular Networks.
abstract: The integration of Generative AI (GAI) into the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) holds great potential for improving user experience, but it also poses significant challenges in security, content quality, and system efficiency. GAI models require substantial computational resources, and frequent interactions between vehicles and roadside units (RSUs) risk privacy breaches. Further, resource-constrained vehicular edge networks complicate effective system optimization. To address these challenges, we propose Clover GAI-IoV, an end-edge-cloud system, to optimize security, content quality, and resource allocation. Specifically, Clover GAI-IoV incorporates a novel Decentralized Anti-Poisoning Privacy Enhancement (DAPE) strategy to enhance security. To overcome resource constraints, we formulate an optimization problem that balances privacy, accuracy, and efficiency. The problem is decomposed into per-RSU subproblems and efficiently solved by a Bayesian-guided metaheuristic approach. Experimental results show that Clover GAI-IoV achieves robust security, high-quality content generation, and efficient resource allocation in dynamic vehicular environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Towards Latency SLO Guaranteed Inference Serving in Dynamic Mobile Edge Computing Networks.
abstract: Serving accurate deep learning (DL) inference requests in time is critical for mobile edge computing (MEC) networks, and it is also challenging due to network dynamics. In this paper, we propose a novel edge DL inference scheme that provides soft latency service-level objective (SLO) guarantees. To handle the variability incurred by the uncontrollable wireless environment, deep neural network (DNN) model adaptation is exploited and aligned with the radio resource allocation. Followed by the optimization problem, we propose efficient algorithms to dynamically adapt DNN models and allocate radio resources in two time scales to strike a tradeoff between latency and inference accuracy. Focusing on DNN-based video analytics, we design and implement an experimental testbed that integrates a 5 G network, an MEC server, and a joint intelligent controller to support edge deep learning inference applications. Evaluation results obtained from this testbed demonstrate that the proposed scheme can effectively adapt to diverse latency SLO requirements, ensuring high-percentile performance while maintaining high inference accuracy in 5G scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Channel Estimation and Equalization for MU-MIMO-OFDM Uplink Based on Spatial-Temporal-Frequency GNN.
abstract: Multi-user multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MU-MIMO-OFDM) is a key technology for modern wireless communications, supporting high data rates and multi-user access. However, conventional approaches that perform channel estimation and equalization separately often suffer from error propagation, where inaccuracies in channel estimates adversely affect the subsequent multiuser detection and equalization process, leading to degraded overall performance. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a deep learning-based framework for joint channel estimation and equalization in MU-MIMO-OFDM uplink systems using a spatial-temporal-frequency graph neural network (STF-GNN). The proposed network architecture is designed to effectively exploit the inherent correlations in the spatial, temporal, and frequency domains, enabling more accurate and robust signal recovery. Experiment results demonstrate that the proposed joint method achieves a gain of 2-4 dB, which translates to a significant reduction in both the mean square error (MSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) of the recovered constellation symbols compared to traditional separated approaches.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Mitigating High-Frequency Component Degradation in Radio Map Generation: A Novel VAE-Enhanced Latent Diffusion Model.
abstract: Radio map (RM) serves as a fundamental tool to characterize the spatial distribution of wireless signals within geographical environments. Traditional RM reconstruction methods typically rely on high-density measurement data and complex physical models, which leads to high computational costs and limited generalizability. With the development of artificial intelligence generated content (AIGC), conditional diffusion model provides a novel solution for RM generation. However, the high training complexity hinders the application. Encoding the RM into low-dimensional latent space, variational autoencoder (VAE) becomes a promising component for reducing the training cost in mainstream diffusion models. Furthermore, high-frequency components can reflect subtle variations induced by scattering and reflection in the RM to accurately describe the spatial received signal strength (RSS) distribution. Hence, we propose a frequency-domain variational autoencoder (FDC-VAE) enhanced with discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and hybrid difference convolution (HDC). FDC-VAE employs explicit frequency decomposition and differentiated encoding mechanisms to enhance the extraction of high-frequency components and the representation capability of latent space. To evaluate the performance of FDC-VAE in the RM generation task, we utilize diffusion transformer (DiT) as conditional generation backbone model to generate fine-grained RM. Experimental results demonstrate that FDC-VAE outperforms baseline models in both PSNR and SSIM metrics.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On the Stabilizability and Scheduling of Wireless Control Network Design with RSMA.
abstract: Wireless control networks (WCNs) have been regarded as the key enablers of industrial Internet of Things (IoT) applications to provide intelligent and automatic services. This paper studies a multi-subsystem WCN in which a remote base station (BS) acquires plant states and delivers processed observations to the corresponding controllers over shared downlink channels. Given limited transmit power budgets and heterogeneous control requirements, we formulate a control scheduling and beamforming design problem based on rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) with finite blocklength (FBL). In particular, the system-level information, e.g., overall mission duration, is mapped into common messages that each subsystem needs to decode, while the corresponding observations are encoded as private data streams. The impact of communication performance on control stabilizability is analyzed. Subsequently, a computationally efficient iterative algorithm is proposed to address the resultant non-convex optimization problem. Extensive simulations have been conducted to validate the effectiveness of our proposed method and reveal the non-trivial tradeoff between wireless control stabilizability and scheduling.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Mitigating 6G Control-Plane Congestion via Group-Based Session Management Approach.
abstract: As a communication infrastructure connecting physical and cyber spaces, the Sixth-generation mobile communication system is expected to support trillions of IoT devices to facilitate the realization of various applications, e.g., smart cities, transportation, and healthcare. In this context, control plane (C-plane) congestion of mobile networks is emerging as a major issue. The standard specification of mobile networks requires tight coupling between the User Equipment (UE) and data communication session, known as the user plane (U-plane). This management structure generates significant C-plane signaling of Connection Management (CM) procedures, causing widespread communication disruption. This paper proposes a mobile network incorporating a novel U-plane management mechanism: Group-based Session Management (GSM). The GSM redesigns the structural coupling between the UE and U-Plane by enabling more flexible and scalable session management using abstract concepts. In evaluation, GSM performs significant suppression effects against CM signaling and demonstrates high scalability, reliability, and stability in a massive IoT device-connected environment. When one million Service Requests per second occur, the GSM improved connection establishment rate by 27 % compared with standard-compliant 5G.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: TRILLM: Triple-Based Semantic Communication with LLMS for Robust IIoT Communication.
abstract: This paper presents a triple-based large language model (LLM)-to-LLM (TRILLM) semantic communication framework for handling semantically impaired industrial internet of things (IIoT) text. We consider a system with N edge devices where each device uses a lightweight LLM to compress event-driven messages into triple representations before transmission to a central hub equipped with an LLMbased semantic decoder. To better evaluate reconstruction quality under semantic impairments, we introduce a semantic equivalence metric that combines cosine similarity with grammar fluency. We further analyze the rate and latency characteristics of the proposed framework. Simulation results show that TRILLM achieves up to 67% higher semantic equivalence than baseline knowledge graph (KG)-based schemes, demonstrating improved robustness in impaired IIoT text communication. Additionally, TRILLM offers adaptability and contextual reasoning advantages over KG approaches
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Terahertz Underlay D2D Using RIS Partitioning: Ergodic Rate Analysis and Optimization.
abstract: In this work, we investigate the use of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) partitioning and transmit power allocation for terahertz (THz) enabled spectrum-sharing underlay device-to-device (D2D) communication, assuming that instantaneous channel state information (CSI) for co-channel interference (CCI) links is unavailable. We first derive closed-form expressions for the ergodic rate (ER) based on statistical CSI using the moment matching technique and Gaussian–Chebyshev quadrature approximation, while accounting for generalized fading and pointing errors. We then develop a low-complexity particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm based solution to jointly partition the RIS and allocate transmit powers, aiming to maximize the ER of the D2D user. Analytical findings are validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations, which provide key system design insights and performance comparisons with both non-RIS systems and benchmark optimization schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Sequence-Based Deep Learning for Handover Optimization in Dense Urban Cellular Network.
abstract: Efficient handover management remains a critical challenge in dense urban cellular networks, where high cell density, user mobility, and diverse service demands increase the likelihood of unnecessary handovers and ping-pong effects. This paper leverages a real-world, multi-operator drive-test dataset of 30,925 labelled records collected within a 2 km area around Sunway City to investigate sequence-based deep learning approaches for handover detection and avoidance. We formulate handover prediction as a sequence problem and evaluate Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Transformer architectures under Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP)-only and all-feature settings. The integration of multi-dimensional features significantly enhanced handover performance in dense urban cellular networks. The proposed GRU-based model achieved a remarkable 98% reduction in ping-pong handovers, alongside a 46.25% decrease in unnecessary handovers, outperforming the baseline RSRP-only approach which yielded a 22.19% reduction. Furthermore, the model demonstrated a 46% improvement in Time of Stay (ToS), indicating more stable user connections. With an inference time of just 0.91 seconds, the solution proves highly efficient and well-suited for real-time edge deployment scenarios. Compared to the conventional 3GPP A3 algorithm, these improvements demonstrate significant gains in mobility robustness and user Quality of Experience (QoE) improvement. The dataset is released to foster reproducibility and further research in intelligent mobility management for 5G and beyond.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Optimizing NOMA-Assisted Backscatter Systems with Imperfect CSI and SIC: A DRL-Driven Approach.
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) combined with backscatter communication (BackCom) offers a promising framework for enabling low-power and spectrum-efficient Internet-of-things (IoT) networks. However, the performance of practical NOMA-assisted BackCom systems is strongly influenced by imperfections in both successive interference cancellation (SIC) and channel state information (CSI). This paper investigates the uplink performance optimization of a two-user NOMA-assisted BackCom system under realistic SIC and CSI imperfections. We consider a sum-rate maximization problem with quality-of-service and fairness constraints, where an adaptive power-allocation policy is learned via deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG). The proposed approach is evaluated against exhaustive search under both perfect and imperfect operating conditions. Simulation results show that while exhaustive search achieves near-optimal performance in ideal scenarios, parameters optimized under ideal assumptions exhibit noticeable degradation when directly reused under imperfect SIC and CSI. The DDPG-based solution maintains robust performance across impairment levels while incurring substantially lower computational complexity. These findings demonstrate the suitability of DRL-driven optimization for practical NOMA-assisted BackCom systems operating in dynamic and imperfect wireless environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Multiple UE Link Selection in 5G mm-wave Channels.
abstract: The use of High-frequency bands such as the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) are one of the key technologies for enabling high-speed wireless communication in future mobile networks. However, high-frequency bands are difficult to handle due to their high straightness and severe attenuation caused by blockage from obstacles, making communication stability a significant challenge. The instability of the high-frequency band becomes particularly prominent in wireless access links, as blockage by the user's own body occurs frequently. We have therefore been investigating multiple user equipment (UE) cooperation to stabilize the mm-wave access link among multiple mm-wave-capable UEs owned by a single user. Stable communication is achieved through selection diversity across different access links of UEs in the close vicinity of the user. In this paper, we propose a deep-Q-learning (DQL)-based proactive UE link selection method and perform experimental evaluation using commercial smartphones in an indoor 5 G area. Our proposal predicts the connection UE link to be used one second in advance, realizing proactive control that simultaneously stabilizes throughput and reduces power consumption. The results of experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can improve the$\mathbf{1 0} \boldsymbol{\%}$-ile throughput cumulative distribution function (CDF) by about$\mathbf{1 0} \boldsymbol{\%}$with$\mathbf{1 5} \boldsymbol{\%}$lower power consumption compared to the conventional reference signal received power (RSRP) based switching method.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Detecting Convolutional Codes via a Markovian Statistic.
abstract: Identifying the unknown channel code corresponding to the given intercepted data is an important problem in military surveillance and in wireless communication. In this paper, we focus on the situation when the given data corresponds to either of the two potential convolutional codes and the goal is to detect the correct code. While a variety of code detection algorithms are available in the literature, the key contribution of our work lies in the novel solution and the corresponding analysis. We decode the received data via Viterbi algorithm using either of the code and consider the corresponding sequence of Viterbi metric for code detection. We identify that the sequence of Viterbi metric follows a Markov chain (MC) and formulate the code detection problem as a hypothesis testing between two MCs. We provide a method to find the state-transition matrices for the two MCs and study the analytical asymptotic performance via the associated error exponent. We validate the performance of our method via a variety of simulations and also compare our performance with the method available in the literature.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Exact Minimum-Weight Codewords of Shortened Polar Codes and New Code Constructions.
abstract: This paper exploits algebraic structures of polar generator matrices to establish an exact expression of minimum Hamming-weight codewords$A_{d_{\min}}$and their corresponding information words of polar codes for any given information set, the set of polarized bit-channels allocated for data bits. The method, which can be effectively scaled with code lengths, serves as a foundation for constructing shortened polar code under a practical constraint of non-power-of-two block lengths. Specifically, we define a subcode derived from the polar generator matrix without imposing any constraint on the information set. The exact row combinations in the generator matrix that contribute to$A_{d_{\min}}$for each subcode are identified.
