Based on this, closed-form expressions of$A_{d_{\min}}$are developed through a deterministic method for any information set, applicable to both polar and shortened polar codes. Building on this, we further optimize the shortening pattern and information set to construct new shortened polar codes with enhanced weight spectra. Numerical results show that, at an ultra-reliable frame-error-rate (FER) level of 10−5or lower, the newly constructed shortened polar codes achieve significant coding gains of up to 1.5 dB over those adopted in 5 G -NR.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Polar Subcodes for MIMO Systems.
abstract: Polar-coded multiple-input multiple-output systems are investigated. An advanced receiver implementing joint list decoding of polar codes and QR- and MMSE-based detectors is proposed. The approximate and exact path metrics are derived for joint list decoder of polar codes. A construction of polar subcodes for MIMO systems with cross-antenna dynamic freezing constraints is proposed. The obtained polar subcodes provide significant performance gain compared to LDPC-coded MIMO systems with the same rate allocation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Design and Development of a Digital Twin Framework for V2I Channel Modeling.
abstract: Traditional vehicular network simulations rely on statistical channel models that often lack site-specific accuracy, failing to capture the unique radio propagation characteristics of complex urban environments. This paper presents the design and development of a Digital Twin (DT) framework for Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication, built on a co-simulation of the Unity game engine and the SUMO traffic simulator. The methodology integrates real-world 3D building and elevation data from OpenStreetMap (OSM) to create a to-scale virtual environment. A deterministic, geometry-aware channel model based on 3GPP standards, that uses real-time ray-casting to classify the communication link into Line-of-Sight (LOS), Non-Line-of-Sight blocked by vehicles (NLOSv), or Non-Line-of-Sight blocked by buildings (NLOSb). The framework's capability is demonstrated through a case study that generates detailed, site-specific path loss heatmaps, capturing the nuanced impact of the physical environment on wireless signals. This DT framework serves as a powerful and detailed tool for V2I network planning, analysis, and optimization.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for UAV-Aided Near-Field ISAC-System.
abstract: The integration of sensing and communication is a key enabler for next-generation wireless networks, where unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) play a crucial role due to their high mobility and flexible deployment. This paper investigates a UAV-assisted near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, in which a UAV-base station (UAV-BS) equipped with a uniform planar array (UPA) simultaneously serves multiple ground users and detects a sensing target. A joint optimization problem is formulated to minimize the Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) of target estimation while ensuring communication quality-of-service (QoS) and trajectory constraints of the UAV. To overcome the inherent complexity of this nonconvex problem, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) is proposed. The TD3-based approach effectively balances communication and sensing performance, and its superiority over conventional Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) is demonstrated in terms of convergence, estimation accuracy, and average sum-rate. Simulation results validate that the proposed solution achieves significant improvements in near-field ISAC performance, thereby providing new insights into the design of intelligent UAV-assisted wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Neural Network Approach for Real-Time Antenna Pattern Generation and Eirp Prediction.
abstract: In massive multiple-input, multiple-output (mMIMO) beamforming, antenna gain is increased in certain directions to adapt to instantaneous user distributions. Standardized methods, such as IEC62232 [1] use an actual maximum approach to assess human exposure to radio frequency (RF) electromagnetic fields (EMF). These methods monitor the actual EIRP (Effective Isotropic Radiated Power) and control it. During operation, this control ensures that the EIRP does not exceed the thresholds required for RF EMF exposure compliance within the related averaging time. This can be implemented either over the total cell or on cell segments. To meet these requirements, the EIRP of the gNB needs to be calculated dynamically, independently of the mMIMO beamforming algorithm. However, no current system provides highly accurate EIRP control for weight vectors computed dynamically. Additionally, in open radio access network (ORAN) standards, radio units may be owned by different vendors. Direct computation of the EIRP would require the exchange of proprietary information between the radio unit (O-RU) and the distributed unit (O-DU). We propose an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) framework for accurate computation of EIRP dynamically, without requiring any exchange of proprietary information between O-RU and O-DU vendors. This is a crucial requirement for future O-RAN products. We demonstrate that, using convolutional deep neural networks, the EIRP can be determined with high accuracy, achieving a tolerance of 0.1 dB for beam gain values within 5 dB from the peak and 1 dB for beam gains within 30 dB from the peak in our evaluation test cases.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Resource Effi cient Digital Predistortion Using the Orthogonal Matching Pursuit Algorithm.
abstract: Digital Predistortion (DPD) is a widely adopted technique for enhancing the efficiency and linearity of radio frequency (RF) power amplifiers (PAs), enabling them to operate in high-efficiency regions near saturation. A key challenge in DPD is the high computational complexity and poor numerical stability of conventional behavioral models such as the Memory Polynomial (MP) and Generalized Memory Polynomial (GMP). This work analyzes the MP and GMP models and proposes the use of the sparse recovery algorithm, Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP), for reducing the DPD model order. Unlike conventional preprocessing-based approaches such as PCA or PLS, OMP performs lightweight, offline feature selection, enabling stable coefficient estimation while reducing complexity and improving hardware compatibility. OMP reduces the coefficients from 66 to 30 (54% reduction) while maintaining NMSE within 1 dB of the full GMP. The proposed GMP model with OMP achieves a 50% reduction in coefficient bit usage compared to the full GMP model. This reduction in memory and computational resources is estimated to result in approximately 20–25% lower power consumption in Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) implementations, based on typical power profiles of Block Random Access Memory (BRAM) and Digital Signal Processor (DSP) blocks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Edge-Optimized ExmobileViT: A Lightweight Vision Transformer for Multi-Class Alzheimer's MRI Classification.
abstract: Early identification of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is critical for enabling timely clinical intervention and improving long-term patient outcomes. Although Vision Transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated exceptional representational capacity for medical imaging tasks, their substantial computational requirements limit deployment on resource-constrained platforms such as edge-enabled Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems. This work introduces ExMobileViT, a lightweight and hardwareefficient ViT enhanced with Ghost modules, explicitly designed for multi-class AD classification from structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The model emphasizes reduced latency and minimal memory footprint, providing an operational advantage for portable and real-time neurodiagnostic inference. Experimental evaluation against standard ViT and MobileViT baselines demonstrates that ExMobileViT achieves 95% accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.96, while operating with approximately 1.11 million parameters and 0.36 GFLOPs. These results verify that ExMobileViT sustains strong diagnostic performance with substantially lower computational cost. Although interpretability and clinician validation remain future objectives, the findings demonstrate the potential suitability of ExMobileViT for efficient and scalable transformer-based intelligence in resourceconstrained IoMT healthcare environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Pilot Assignment for Distributed Massive MIMO Based on Channel Estimation Error Minimization.
abstract: Pilot contamination remains a major bottleneck in realizing the full potential of distributed massive MIMO systems. We propose two dynamic and scalable pilot assignment schemes designed for practical deployment in such networks. First, we present a low-complexity centralized scheme that sequentially assigns pilots to user equipments (UEs) to minimize the global channel estimation errors across serving access points (APs). This improves the channel estimation quality and reduces interference among UEs, enhancing the spectral efficiency. Second, we develop a fully distributed scheme that uses a priority-based pilot selection approach. In this scheme, each selected AP minimizes the channel estimation error using only local information and offers candidate pilots to the UEs. Every UE then selects a suitable pilot based on its AP priority. This approach ensures consistency and minimizes interference while significantly reducing pilot contamination. The method requires no global coordination, maintains low signaling overhead, and adapts dynamically to the UE deployment. Numerical simulations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed schemes in terms of network throughput when compared to the existing state-of-the-art schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enhancing the Trustworthiness of Multi-Slice 6G Networks Through Hierarchical, Environment-Aware Resource Allocation.
abstract: The next generation of wireless networks (6G) seeks to ensure not only high throughput but also consistent trustworthiness and user satisfaction. This can be achieved by supporting diverse service demands through network slicing, a technique that partitions network resources into multiple virtual slices, each tailored to specific service requirements. This paper addresses the challenge of maximizing user satisfaction and enhancing communication trustworthiness, quantified through metrics related to reliability, availability, and fairness, via efficient resource allocation and scheduling. We formulate network slicing and user scheduling as a multi-objective, constrained optimization problem and propose a scalable, hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework to solve it. The framework integrates environment-aware knowledge, capturing line-of-sight or non-line-of-sight channel states and near-future predictions, combined with scheduling history. The proposed two-level RL architecture features an inter-slice agent that allocates resources fairly across slices to maximize the number of satisfied users, and intraslice agents that independently schedule users within slices to enhance trustworthiness. A novel per-user learning mechanism ensures that the solution scales linearly with the number of users, enabling efficient operation in dense network environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a trade-off between user satisfaction and trustworthiness (quantified through metrics of reliability, availability, and fairness), particularly in industrial environments with challenging channel conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Propagation Channel Modeling for LEO Satellite Missions Using Ray-Tracing Simulations.
abstract: This work presents a high-resolution, ray-tracing-based channel modeling for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite-to-ground links in a suburban environment at X-band. Using simulations conducted in Wireless InSite, we develop a parametric channel model that characterizes both large- and small-scale fading effects across different satellite elevation angles. Large-scale fading incorporates attenuation due to terrain-induced shadowing and dynamic environmental factors such as weather conditions, and is compared with 3GPP NTN channel model. Additionally, we quantify link degradation resulting from ground station (GS) antenna misalignment, considering both fixed single-element and electronically steerable phased-array antennas. Small-scale fading is modeled by fitting a shadowed and non-shadowed Rician distribution to the fading statistics at various satellite elevations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to propose a comprehensive elevation-aware channel model for satellite-to-ground propagation at X-band, integrating ray-traced environmental dynamics, elevation-dependent fading, and phased-array beam misalignment effects.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Uplink and Downlink Resource Allocation and Antenna Activation for Pinching Antenna Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we explore a novel joint uplink and downlink framework utilizing a pinching antenna system (PASS). We consider two waveguides, one dedicated to transmission and one to reception, and both of them are connected to a base station (BS). Each type of waveguide consists of several pinching antennas (PAs) in some preconfigured positions. In this framework, we assume the BS can serve downlink and uplink user equipments (UEs) at the same time using the same spectrum resources through the presented PASS. In this aspect, we formulate a sum rate optimization problem that jointly optimizes the antenna activation factor, the BS transmit power, and the UE's transmit power, subject to power budget constraints for the BS and the UEs, as well as minimum rate requirements for the UEs. The formulated problem is highly non-convex and difficult to solve directly. Hence, we divide the main problem into two sub-problems: the antenna activation sub-problem and the power allocation sub-problem. Then, we solve the antenna activation sub-problem utilizing a distance and spatial correlation-based algorithm. Meanwhile, the resource allocation sub-problem is solved using a successive convex approximation (SCA)-based algorithm. Numerical results show that our proposed framework can achieve around$\mathbf{6 0 - 9 0 \%}$performance gains over its time division duplex (TDD) where the uplink and downlink transmissions are served in different orthogonal time slots.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Root Cause Analysis for Wireless Networks Using Causal Knowledge Graphs and a Large Language Model.
abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is a critical task in the incident management of wireless networks. Although RCA is essential for restoring and maintaining performance, it often requires substantial human effort. Conventional RCA approaches, such as rule-based and troubleshooting-based methods, cannot capture causal relationships across multiple incident tickets. This is a critical limitation because incidents or performance degradation in wireless networks often arise from the cascading effect of diverse factors, such as software/hardware/environmental conditions and interactions among multiple base stations and user equipment. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel automated RCA framework that extracts causal knowledge graphs (KGs) from incident ticket documents using a large language model and applies them for inference. Our step-by-step KG construction method, tailored for RCA, automatically captures causal links spanning multiple documents. Comparative evaluations with a conventional retrieval-augmented generation approach showed that our framework significantly improves 5-point scale scores assigned by human experts for comprehensiveness (from 2.79 to 3.18), hallucination mitigation (from 3.09 to 3.31), and explainability (from 2.69 to 3.12) on a real-world dataset.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Agentic AI-Assisted Network Management for User-Centric Cooperative Satellite Communications.
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTN), including low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, form an essential pillar of next-generation (xG) networks for providing ubiquitous connectivity across the space-air-ground. As LEO satellite networks advance toward mega-constellation systems, cooperation among satellites becomes essential to suppress the surge of handovers between spot beams and satellites. In this paper, we propose a large language model (LLM)-assisted intelligent management framework for xG LEO satellite networks. By harnessing the exceptional pattern recognition and generative capabilities of LLMs to learn the intrinsic relationship between satellite-user equipment (UE) geometry, network control decisions, and achievable rates, we can efficiently manage satellite cooperation with minimal fine-tuning. Furthermore, we develop an iterative finetuning mechanism to continuously refine the LLM with online network observations and feedback, thereby maintaining robust decision-making under time-varying satellite-UE topology and traffic dynamics. From extensive simulations, we demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves substantial rate enhancement over conventional multi-satellite systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On-the-Fly NLoS Detection for Wireless Positioning: Combinatorial Data Augmentation Approach.
abstract: 6G demands wireless positioning to be realized in an on-the-fly manner, enabling a user equipment (UE) to be accurately and instantaneously localized without relying on predetermined statistical models or long-term datasets. The absence of such prior information makes it difficult to mitigate the unpredictable bias caused by non-line-of-sight (NLoS) links. To address this challenge, we propose a novel NLoS detection algorithm, termed combinatorial data augmentation-guided NLoS detection (CDA-ND), which builds upon our prior work. CDA-ND generates numerous preliminary estimated locations (PELs) from different gNodeB (gNB) combinations. When a target gNB is in NLoS, the resulting PELs naturally split into two clusters: one derived using the target gNB's distance measurement, and the other derived without it. The deviation between the two clusters is represented by a single vector, called the NLoS evidence vector (NEV), which serves as a key feature for computing an NLoS likelihood score. The proposed CDA-ND achieves high reliability in indoor factory environments, attaining precisions of 81.14 % and 88.28 % when the proportion of NLoS gNBs is 18 % and 56 %, respectively. As a result, a positioning algorithm integrating CDA-ND significantly improves positioning accuracy, achieving a 47.36 % reduction in mean absolute error under an NLoS-dominant condition.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: IQ Imbalance Compensation for Receivers With 1-Bit Quantization and Oversampling.
abstract: Leveraging broad frequency ranges, as they are available in the terahertz (THz) regime, for high-bandwidth communications makes the energy consumption of the receiver's analog-to-digital converter (ADC) a major challenge. To solve this problem, a promising approach is the use of ADCs with 1-bit amplitude resolution in combination with temporal oversampling. This coarse quantization, however, necessitates the redesign of most receiver algorithms. This work addresses the estimation and compensation of in-phase and quadrature (IQ) imbalance, a critical factor regarding the communication performance. It is shown that amplitude imbalance has no deteriorating effect on the communication performance, while the impact of phase imbalance is significant. To address this, an efficient unbiased estimator for IQ phase imbalance based on 1-bit quantized observations is derived, achieving the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Its accuracy, its robustness against inaccurate timing conditions, and its performance gains in case of oversampling are assessed. Furthermore, a guideline is derived, which either recommends or discourages compensation with regard to the expected variance of an individual estimate. Thereafter, this work discusses approaches to carry out the compensation of the estimated IQ imbalance. Eventually, simulations reveal the estimator's ability to significantly enhance communication performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On the Impact of Electromagnetic Interference and Inter-RIS Reflections in Beyond Diagonal-RIS.
abstract: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) have emerged as an enabling technology that provides greater control over wireless signal manipulation, resulting in improved connectivity and notable performance gains. Despite their potential, practical deployments are inherently vulnerable to external interferences such as electromagnetic interference (EMI) and inter-RIS reflections (IRR). This work specifically investigates one of the BD-RIS architectures, the fully connected RIS, and compares its performance with that of the conventional diagonal RIS under EMI, IRR, and their combined effects. A realistic system model is developed for a multi-RIS multi-cell network, incorporating spatial correlation among RIS-related channels. In order to improve the sum-rate performance, the phase-shifts of the RIS and BD-RIS are optimized using the Manopt toolbox. Simulation results demonstrate that BD-RIS consistently maintains superior performance across all adverse conditions, significantly outperforming traditional diagonal RIS configurations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A High-Precision Assisted Timing Support Mechanism for Edge Access Points.
abstract: This paper presents a standards-compliant Edge Access Point (EAP) architecture that delivers precise synchronization for emerging time-sensitive wireless applications in Industrial IoT, autonomous systems, and$\mathbf{5 G}$networks. To overcome the sub-microsecond accuracy limitations of existing wireless protocols, the proposed EAP is the first architecture that integrates the ITU-T Assisted Partial Timing Support (APTS) model with two innovations: (i) hardware-assisted Precision Time Protocol (PTP) time-stamping via an extended Timing Synchronization Function (TSF) counter, and (ii) wireless emulation of Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE). The design supports Telecom Grandmaster clock requirements through dual timing references, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) input and a PTP stream, ensuring Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) traceability within$\pm \mathbf{1 0 0 ~ n s}$. Simulation results demonstrate dynamic performance well within$\mathbf{\pm 1 0 0 ~ n s}$, with Oven-Controlled Crystal Oscillator (OCXO)-based holdover stability better than$\mathbf{1 0 0 ~ n s}$for up to four hours. Furthermore, client-side evaluations incorporating 10 ns transmit time-stamping error highlight substantial phase error reduction, while the wireless-recovered SyncE clock eliminates the need for high-stability (better than 1 ppm) local oscillators. These results establish the proposed EAP as a practical and robust solution for high-precision synchronization in next-generation wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RIS-Empowered CV-QKD THz MIMO Communications: SKR Analysis and Optimization.
abstract: A multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system where Alice transmits secret keys in the terahertz frequency range using continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD) to Bob via a wireless channel aided by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is considered in this paper. An eavesdropper, Eve, employs a Gaussian collective attack over the effective wireless channel in an attempt to steal the secret keys, while Bob makes use of homodyne detection and reverse reconciliation protocols for secret key reception and error correction. Novel expressions for this system's secret key rate (SKR) are derived, and a design framework to obtain the optimal phase shift matrix of the RIS maximizing the SKR performance is presented, which is solved via particle swarm optimization. Our performance evaluations demonstrate the advantages of employing MIMO and the proposed optimized RIS phase configuration for large numbers of reflecting unit elements to obtain higher SKR levels and transmission distance between Alice and Bob for the considered RIS-empowered CV-QKD THz MIMO wireless system.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Outage Analysis of OTFS-Based Cooperative U2U Communications System with Subcarrier Allocation.
abstract: This paper investigates the outage performance of an orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS)-based cooperative communication system assisted by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) under Nakagami-$m$fading channels. The considered system comprises a base station (BS) transmitting$N$subcarriers to an intermediate UAV (UAV1), which subsequently forwards$N-D$subcarriers to a second UAV (UAV2) and allocates the remaining$D$subcarriers to a cellular user (CU). Closedform analytical expressions are derived for the individual link and overall system outage probabilities for both Gaussian and Nakagami-$m$fading models. The analytical results are validated through extensive MATLAB-based Monte Carlo simulations. The effect of subcarrier allocation between the UAV2 and CU links is explicitly examined, highlighting the inherent trade-off in outage performance among the cooperative links. Numerical results further illustrate the effects of channel fading characteristics, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and subcarrier allocation on system reliability.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DESTIN: Dynamic Device Selection for Mobile Sensors-as-a-Service Platforms.
abstract: We introduce DESTIN, a dynamic device selection scheme for Mobile Sensor-as-a-Service (mSe-aaS) platforms, designed to ensure uninterrupted service delivery in dynamic environments. mSe-aaS platforms rely on multiple mobile devices equipped with heterogeneous sensors to support diverse and concurrent Internet of Things (IoT) applications. End-users are charged based on the utilization of shared resources such as sensors, devices, and supporting infrastructure. However, device mobility poses a significant challenge - sensors may become unavailable in specific regions as devices move, leading to potential service disruptions. To address this, DESTIN dynamically selects alternative devices to maintain service continuity. Unlike random or static selection approaches, DESTIN considers device heterogeneity, sensor availability, and contextual parameters to satisfy application requirements. The selection problem is formulated as a mathematical optimization task, solved using Lagrange multipliers and the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions to determine optimal device assignments. Simulation results demonstrate that DESTIN reduces energy consumption by approximately$\mathbf{3. 5 2 \%}$and$\mathbf{1 1. 4 8 \%}$for scenarios with$\mathbf{1 0}$and 20 sensors, respectively, while improving resource efficiency by 4.53 % and 8.46 %. These findings highlight DESTIN's effectiveness in enhancing both energy efficiency and resource utilization in mobile sensing environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Seamless Handover Mechanisms for Cf-Mmimo Networks in O-Ran: a Dapp Approach.
abstract: The Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) paradigm is reshaping the cellular networks through disaggregation, open interfaces, and intelligence, primarily managed by RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs). The RICs host xApps and rApps that operate at timescales varying from ten milliseconds to more than a second in order to perform network optimization. However, they lack a practical approach to execute realtime control loops requiring sub-ten-millisecond execution, made apparent by the need of distributed application for real-time control, called dApp in O-RAN architecture. This work proposes a novel mechanism that leverages dApps at the O-RAN Distributed Unit (O-DU) to execute handover (HO) control of mobile users in cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) networks. The proposed solution will utilize the D2 interface from the O-RAN specifications for efficient data queue transfers between serving multiple O-DUs. We evaluate our proposed seamless handover scheme through simulation and compare the performance with two baseline HO scenarios. The proposed dApp-driven seamless HO scheme illustrates the unique utilization of dynamic scaling capabilities of the O-DUs to duplicate data streams and eliminates handover-related packet drops and significantly reduces packet service delay compared to baseline approaches.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low PAPR Waveform Construction via Trellis Coded Modulation.
abstract: In this paper, a low Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) waveform framework is developed using a combination of Trellis Coded Modulation (TCM) and DFT-spread OFDM (DFT-s-OFDM). Under this framework, we introduce two low PAPR TCM designs: TCM-U and TCM-A. Significant PAPR and coverage improvements can be achieved compared with QPSK and QAM modulated DFT-s-OFDM. In addition, by applying frequency-domain codeword puncturing (FDCP) to the TCM codewords, tradeoffs between PAPR, spectral efficiency (SE), and coded block error rate (BLER) can be further optimized. Both designs support higher-order modulations, and offer consistent PAPR reductions and coverage enhancements for a wide range of SE. Furthermore, both TCM-U and TCM-A can be optimally decoded using low complexity, non-trellis-based decoders.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Open-Source 5G Testbed with Network Slicing: System Evaluation and Application Testing.
abstract: This work presents the development of an opensource standalone (SA) 5G testbed with end-to-end slicing, using open-source software on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware and software-defined radio (SDR). Key contributions include customized slice configurations in the 5G Core Network (5GC) and dedicated static resource allocation in the radio access network (RAN). The testbed is validated through slice isolation tests. Its utility is then demonstrated via a warehouse application featuring Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) on one slice and environmental sensors & actuators on another. Critical AGV response times are evaluated under mixed traffic conditions, showing robust slice isolation and superior performance over baseline networks. The testbed offers a scalable, cost-effective platform for 5G education, research, and application testing. It also highlights the transformative potential of such open-source testbeds in Industry 4.0.

title: Attention and Curiosity Based Reinforcement Learning Approach for Drone Collision Avoidance.
abstract: As drones are increasingly deployed in dense urban environments, real-time collision avoidance is crucial to ensure safe operation amid numerous static and dynamic obstacles. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) offers a promising solution in highly dynamic environments due to its ability to provide high adaptability and autonomous decision-making. However, conventional DRL algorithms often struggle due to inefficient exploration and a limited ability to prioritize relevant information. This paper introduces Curiosity and Attention with Reinforcement Learning (CARL), a DRL-based algorithm that integrates attention to dynamically focus on critical obstacles and curiosity to encourage exploration of novel states. Attention visualization provides insights into the agent's decision-making, while curiosity accelerates learning and improves interactions with the environment. Simulations comparing CARL to a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) baseline show a 76.5% reduction in static collisions, a 41.8% reduction in dynamic collisions, a 78% decrease in false positives, a 58.1% decrease in false negatives, and a 42.4% improvement in navigation efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Agent Data Collection and Delivery Under Intermittent Sensing with Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: We consider a scenario in which multiple mobile agents collect data from a fixed number of evasive phenomena in a prescribed environment. Once data is collected, the agents travel to one of several fixed access points (APs) to deliver the data. We consider a distributed setting with no direct communication among the agents. The agents are hindered both by noise in their sensing mechanisms and intermittent ability to collect sensing measurements due to environmental factors. We cast this problem as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) and use particle filters to perform belief-state estimation. We propose two methods to estimate the locations of the phenomena during periods where they are not directly observable. Using proximal policy optimization (PPO) with centralized training, decentralized execution (CTDE), we train each agent to provide reliable, real time data collection and delivery to the APs. We integrate the developed belief-state estimation methods with PPO and compare their performance, demonstrating strong cooperation, even in the noisy, distributed setting.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Channel Estimation for Pinching Antennas Systems using Deep Learning.
abstract: Pinching antennas (PAs) are novel type of antenna that leverage dielectric waveguides and electromagnetic coupling to mitigate large-scale path loss. Channel estimation in PA systems is highly challenging, as it represents an ill-posed problem due to the underdetermined nature of the channel characteristics. This creates a strong need for efficient estimation techniques. In this work, a deep learning framework is proposed that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with artificial neural networks (ANNs) to estimate channel coefficients on a per-antenna basis, thereby providing greater flexibility and adaptability to varying numbers of PAs in practical deployment scenarios. While the proposed CNN-ANN method delivers efficient performance compared to the conventional approach, it also has low computational complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Identifying Reliable Optimality Criteria for 3D Anchor Configuration Through FIM-Based Analysis.
abstract: In indoor localization, Angle of Arrival (AoA) estimation is often employed for high-accuracy positioning, where the location of a mobile device is determined by triangulation from the measured directions of incoming signals. This method fundamentally relies on a set of fixed infrastructure devices, known as anchors, to establish the reference directions. Optimizing the 3D placement of these anchors is critical for maximizing system accuracy. This paper addresses this challenge by identifying and validating the most reliable quantitative metric for evaluating 3D anchor configurations, including both anchor position and orientation. We first derive a comprehensive Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) model that incorporates the 3D position, 3D orientation, and specific antenna array structure. We conduct a large-scale simulation study across 715 diverse scenarios to compare the correlation between various FIM-based optimality criteria (such as A, D, and E-optimality) and the localization error (RMSE). The analysis reveals that A-optimality, which relates to the average estimation variance, exhibits the strongest Pearson correlation (0.9136) with RMSE, identifying it as the most reliable performance indicator. We then experimentally validate this finding in a real-world Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) AoA testbed. Results from four representative placement scenarios confirm that the A-optimality metric strongly correlates with the measured real-world localization performance, demonstrating its utility as an effective and validated tool for designing and evaluating 3D anchor placements.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: An Interference Analysis Algorithm Based on Inverse Transform Sampling for D2C and GSO Satellite Systems Operating in Reverse Band Mode.
abstract: Existing interference analysis primarily focuses on co-directional scenarios where non-geostationary orbit (NGSO) satellite systems and geostationary orbit (GSO) satellite systems coexist. However, the downlink frequency bands of some direct-to-cell (D2C) satellite systems overlap with the uplink frequency bands of GSO satellite systems, meaning that they operate in reverse band mode. This significantly differs from traditional interference scenarios, making it difficult for traditional algorithms to adapt. In this paper, an equivalent model is proposed to derive the probability distribution of the number of the interfering satellites and their spatial distribution. Furthermore, an interference analysis algorithm based on inverse transform sampling is presented. This replaces full enumeration calculations, thereby greatly improving computational efficiency. Finally, the actual operating parameters of the Starlink and Tiantong systems are employed to simulate and verify the algorithm. The results demonstrate that the algorithm reduces computation time by approximately 94%, with an average difference in Interference-to-Noise Ratio (I/N) of 0.0463 dB compared to the orbit extrapolation method. The effect of different parameters on I/N is also analyzed to provide a reference for the design of D2C constellations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Threat Detection in Ethereum Smart Contracts Using a Hierarchical Depthwise Graph Convolutional Neural Network.
abstract: Threat Detection Systems (TDSs), often deployed at the network layer, are limited in detecting application-layer threats, where logic-based vulnerabilities in smart contracts are increasingly exploited due to their immutable and critical nature. To address this, we construct a new dataset of practical attack patterns by extracting encoded information from data field from transaction hashes, converting them into opcodes, and representing them as graphs using a two-gram technique. We then design a Hierarchical Depthwise Graph Convolutional Neural Network (HDGCNN) that treats application-layer operations as documents and transactions as sentences to classify threat patterns. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HDGCNN achieves 92.4 % detection accuracy with only 0.8 % false alarms, outperforming traditional deep learning baselines and other graph-based models. Finally, we evaluate the graph representation to further illustrate the scalability and effectiveness of graph-based approaches for application-layer threat detection in blockchain systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: An Elastic Clustering Framework for Large-Scale WSNs Maximizing Network Lifetime.
abstract: Large-scale Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are applied in multiple domains, notably Precision Agriculture, Intelligent Traffic Management and Smart Hospital. A key task for these applications, long-term environment monitoring, relies on periodic data collection via network clustering. In applications like precision agriculture, large networks requires frequent topology updates to avoid hotspot issues at Cluster Heads (CHs), balance energy consumption, and meet QoS demands. Centralized topology maintenance at the Base Station ensures global energy efficiency but incurs costly networkwide control overhead in larger deployments. This undermines existing LEACH-derived and even recent protocols using treebased approaches, in terms of scalability. We propose PECEE, a framework combining centralized CH selection with local routing coordination, enabling elastic clustering for raw data collection. Simulations show that PECEE extends network lifetime from$\mathbf{5 0 \%}$to$\mathbf{9 0 \%}$compared to some notable solutions including GSTEB [11] in raw data collection simulations, and up to 200 % when data aggregation is used.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Study on Service Link Handover Optimization Algorithms for 5G NTN.
abstract: Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) have garnered significant interest from both industry and academia in recent years. These systems have the ability to cover some hard-to-reach ground areas, contrary to terrestrial networks (TNs). However, maintaining continuous service in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) based NTNs presents important challenges, especially with frequent service link handovers (SLHOs) due to satellite mobility that can create overhead because of signaling messages. This paper investigates mobility optimization strategies for 5G NTNs by studying some satellite selection algorithms: Best Beam, Longest Beam, Hysteresis and the proposed approach based on Integer Linear Programming (ILP). Our results demonstrate that while the Best Beam strategy maximizes throughput, it results in high overhead due to frequent handover occurrences. In contrast, the Longest Beam and Hysteresis strategies minimize handovers but sacrifice throughput. The ILP optimization approach is presented as a balanced solution by controlling handover occurrences while maintaining high throughput for user data traffic. Moreover, the ILP method is able to control the maximum number of satellite switches during a given time duration, which makes it valuable for resource-constrained networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MARBLE-Net: Learning to Localize in Multipath Environment with Adaptive Rainbow Beams.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems demand precise and efficient target localization, a task challenged by rich multipath propagation in complex wireless environments. This paper introduces MARBLE-Net (Multipath-Aware Rainbow Beam Learning Network), a deep learning framework that jointly optimizes the analog beamforming parameters of a frequency-dependent rainbow beam and a neural localization network for high-accuracy position estimation. By treating the phase-shifter (PS) and true-time-delay (TTD) parameters as learnable weights, the system adaptively refines its sensing beam to exploit environment-specific multipath characteristics. A structured multi-stage training strategy is proposed to ensure stable convergence and effective end-to-end optimization. Simulation results show that MARBLE-Net outperforms both a fixed-beam deep learning baseline (RaiNet) and a traditional k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) method, reducing localization error by more than 50\% in a multipath-rich scene. Moreover, the results reveal a nuanced interaction with multipath propagation: while confined uni-directional multipath degrades accuracy, structured and directional multipath can be effectively exploited to achieve performance surpassing even line-of-sight (LoS) conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: CP-Aided AFDM Channel Estimation for High-Mobility Scenarios.
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising multicarrier waveform for high-mobility scenarios due to its robustness against doubly-dispersive channels. However, accurate channel estimation remains challenging because delay and Doppler shifts are coupled in the discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT) domain. In this paper, unlike conventional AFDM channel estimation schemes that rely on a relatively large chirp parameter to maintain path separability in doubly-dispersive channels, we develop a CP-based channel estimation scheme without this requirement. This makes the proposed method more suitable for channels with large delay spreads, where conventional designs would otherwise suffer from high pilot overhead. Specifically, the cross-correlation between the cyclic prefix (CP) and the corresponding symbol tail is computed over multiple symbols and averaged to estimate the Doppler shifts. The path delays are then identified using pilots in the DAFT domain, based on which an equivalent channel matrix is constructed for DAFT-domain equalization. Crucially, we show that under random signaling, the phase of the CP cross-correlation depends only on the Doppler shifts and is invariant to multipath interference. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a Doppler normalized mean square error (NMSE) of$10^{-3}$at an SNR of 17 dB. Moreover, the proposed CP-AFDM scheme demonstrates superior BER performance over conventional multicarrier waveforms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Neural Networks-Enabled Channel Reconstruction for Fluid Antenna Systems: A Data-Driven Approach.
abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) offer substantial spatial diversity by exploiting the electromagnetic port correlation within compact array spaces, thereby generating favorable small-scale fading conditions with beneficial channel gain envelope fluctuations. This unique capability opens new opportunities for a wide range of communication applications and emerging technologies. However, accurate channel state information (CSI) must be acquired before a fluid antenna can be effectively utilized. Although several efforts have been made toward channel reconstruction in FASs, a generally applicable solution to both model-based or model-free scenario with both high precision and efficient computational flow remains lacking. In this work, we propose a data-driven channel reconstruction approach enabled by neural networks. The proposed framework not only achieves significantly enhanced reconstruction accuracy but also requires substantially lower computational complexity compared with existing model-free methods. Numerical results further demonstrate the rapid convergence and robust reconstruction capability of the proposed scheme, outperforming current state-of-the-art techniques.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Gradient-Based Fractional Doppler Estimation for OTFS Systems via Convex Correlation and Residual Functions.
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation has recently emerged as a promising technique for high-mobility communication scenarios, owing to its ability to represent time-varying channels more effectively in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain. However, accurate estimation of fractional Doppler shifts in the DD domain remains challenging. Existing methods often suffer from high computational complexity and limited accuracy. To address these issues, we refine the correlation- and residual-based optimization functions of the channel response. Benefiting from the convexity of these optimization functions in the integer interval, the proposed methods can accurately estimate fractional Doppler values through gradient ascent/descent with relatively low computational complexity. In addition, we derive a closedform expression of the single-path Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for OTFS systems to validate the estimator efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that the two proposed gradientbased algorithms are effective estimators for both fractional Doppler and channel response in the exclusive pilot case. Moreover, in embedded pilot scenarios, the residual-based optimization function outperforms existing algorithms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Optimal Power Control and Resource Unit Allocation for Cross-BSS IEEE 802.11be Networks.
abstract: In dense Wi-Fi networks, overlapping basic service sets (BSSs) suffer from severe resource contention and cochannel interference, which significantly constrains the network throughput. The new-generation Wi-Fi standard, i.e., IEEE 802.11be, introduces several groundbreaking mechanisms that open up new opportunities for throughput enhancements. This work exploits IEEE 802.11be features and introduces a novel cross-BSS design framework to maximize the average network throughput under quality-of-service constraints via joint optimization of transmit power and resource unit (RU) allocation. The formulated problem is highly challenging due to the piecewise modulation and coding schemes (MCS) mapping as well as the event-triggered interference. We characterize the transmit power by the thresholds that can trigger network state transitions and construct a lookup-based mapping between power and optimal RU allocation, thereby transforming the original problem into an equivalent mixed-integer linear program (MILP) that can get the optimal solution by standard solvers. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design significantly outperforms benchmark schemes and Wi-Fi 6 counterparts in terms of throughput and interference management, which provides guidelines for practical dense IEEE 802.11be deployment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Data Exchange Framework for Cooperative Edge Sensing.
abstract: Photographic sensing is a key enabling technology for smart space applications, requiring flexible data exchange mechanisms in distributed edge systems. This work presents a lightweight MQTT-based communication framework for distributed photographic sensing that enables efficient stream processing of CV-based time-sequenced data and cooperative mechanisms. Leveraging MQTT's publish/subscribe model and a structured topic hierarchy, the framework enables flexible logical topologies, including unicast, multicast, and broadcast. The design separates the control and data planes with appropriate Quality of Service (QoS) settings to ensure reliable command delivery and low-latency data exchange. Security is reinforced through TLS encryption, certificate-based authentication, and ACL-based access control. Based on this architecture, a distributed high-frame rate 3D sensing system was developed for a smart badminton court, capable of capturing shuttlecock trajectories and extracting players' shot-by-shot performance data. To evaluate the proposed architecture, three representative configurations, including centralized, Sensing-as-a-Service (SaaS), and fully distributed, were implemented and tested. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves excellent real-time performance and stability across all scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Physical-Informed Radio Map Estimation: An Environment-Aware Decomposition Approach.
abstract: High-resolution Radio Map Estimation (RME) is a key enabling technology for environment-aware communications. Existing deep learning approaches often treat the radio map monolithically, ignoring its intrinsic physical structure. In practice, radio maps exhibit a fundamental structural dichotomy: Predictable, smooth Line-of-Sight (LoS) regions and complex, stochastic Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) regions governed by multipath phenomena. In this paper, a physics-informed hybrid framework is proposed that decomposes the RME task according to this dichotomy. The framework employs a deterministic regression model to estimate the LoS component and a conditional generative model to estimate the NLoS component. For NLoS estimation, conditional flow matching is leveraged as an efficient and simulation-free alternative to computationally intensive diffusion models. Our framework is validated on a ray-tracing-based dataset. Experiments demonstrate that our hybrid approach significantly outperforms conventional schemes, validating our hypothesis that the decomposition of the problem based on its underlying physics leads to a more accurate and efficient model.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Drift-Plus-Penalty Based Queue Management for Edge LLM Inference with Repeated Sampling.
abstract: Inspired by recent advances in inference scaling laws, this paper proposes a novel edge large language model (LLM) inference framework that leverages repeated sampling to improve generation quality using relatively lightweight LLMs. However, excessive repeated sampling may lead to intolerable delays due to the limited computing capacity of edge servers. To address this tradeoff, this paper aims to develop a queue management scheme that carefully balances generation quality and delay. The system is modeled as multiple queues for batch processing, each consisting of sub-tasks representing individual samples and categorized based on output token lengths. The queue management problem is then formulated to maximize a time-averaged metric associated with generation quality under queue stability constraints. Applying the drift-plus-penalty method, the problem is decomposed into two subproblems: repeated sampling decision and queue scheduling, which are formulated as independent integer programs and admit efficient closed-form solutions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm adapts to task arrival rates within the feasible region, ensures generation quality, and provides a controllable tradeoff between delay and generation quality through an adjustable parameter.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MR-Former: Location-Agnostic RSRP Prediction Via Masked Reconstruction in Beam Space.
abstract: Accurate RSRP signal level prediction is crucial for network optimization but is fundamentally hindered by the sparse, heterogeneous, and location-agnostic nature of real-world Measurement Report (MR) data. This paper proposes a novel framework that reformulates RSRP signal level prediction as a self-supervised masked reconstruction task, operating purely within the RSRP beam space to obviate the need for geographical coordinates. We design a Transformer-based masked autoencoder and introduce Operational Relation Embedding (ORE), a novel feature augmentation strategy that injects domain-specific inductive biases into the model. Evaluated on two large-scale, real-world 5G datasets, our method achieves a prediction error of 3.50-3.56 dB Mean Absolute Error (MAE), significantly outperforming existing solutions. The model also demonstrates robust generalization, enabling predictive tasks for unseen network configurations, such as virtual site commissioning, and maintains exceptional stability over time. By enabling the creation of high-fidelity, location-agnostic coverage maps, our work provides a practical and scalable solution for building network digital twins. This work effectively solves the signal level prediction challenge, paving the way for advanced automated 5 G network optimization tasks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Passive Synthetic Aperture Equivalent Model and Localization for Spaceborne Squint Scenario.
abstract: In wireless emitter monitoring scenarios, space-borne passive localization technology has garnered significant attention due to its advantages such as wide-area coverage and all-weather operation. Conventional localization methods, such as Direction of Arrival (DOA) and Frequency Difference of Arrival (FDOA), rely on instantaneous measurements and process signals non-coherently over time. Consequently, their accuracy degrades significantly under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. In recent years, passive synthetic aperture (PSA) techniques have been applied to emitter localization, enhancing localization precision through coherent integration of the Doppler phase to achieve high processing gain. An accurate PSA method requires precise modeling of the Doppler history. However, existing models predominantly assume linear platform motion, which introduces a fundamental model mismatch by neglecting orbital and Earth curvature effects. This omission leads to inaccuracies in Doppler history reconstruction and ultimately limits their applicability in practical spaceborne missions. To address these limitations, this study first establishes an equivalent squint model for spaceborne passive localization scenarios, then provides rigorous definitions of the equivalent parameters, and finally proposes a PSA localization method tailored for spaceborne squint conditions, thus extending the applicability of the spaceborne PSA method to squint scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement in localization accuracy over conventional FDOA and DOA methods under low-SNR conditions, while maintaining high-precision localization capability despite large squint angles. The practical efficacy of the approach is further confirmed via a satellite experiment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Inference Offloading Strategy for Distributed Large Language Models in Industrial IoT.

title: An OFDM Waveform Design and Validation for mmWave Full-Duplex JRC Systems.
abstract: Full-duplex (FD) joint radar and communications (JRC) is a pivotal technology for future wireless networks. To realize effective integration of communication and sensing functionalities, an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform design based on the fifth-generation (5 G) new radio (NR) frame structure is proposed. First, the self-interference cancellation in the FD JRC system is discussed. Then, the equivalent cyclic prefix is applied for the first OFDM symbol in each slot to improve the range coverage. Additionally, the fast Fourier transform and chirp-z transform (FFT-CZT) method is used to enhance range accuracy. Finally, simulations and experiments on the millimeter wave (mmWave) FD JRC testbed are conducted to validate the feasibility of the proposed waveform.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Satellite Communications-Enabled Three-Tier Computing Task Offloading Optimization for Iot Via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to develop rapidly, the exponential proliferation of devices and the sharp growth of sensed data volumes are exerting unprecedented demands on networks to achieve extensive coverage, low delay, and high reliability. Traditional terrestrial communication networks find it difficult to meet these demands in remote and special areas, which prompts satellite communication to become a key supplement. Among them, low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites offer the advantages of low delay and superior real-time capabilities, while Geostationary Orbit (GEO) satellites offer wide coverage and stable links. Thus, the joint service of GEO and LEO has gradually become a trend. Nevertheless, a number of challenges in existing studies deserve further consideration: 1) numerous tasks are sensitive to delay; 2) tasks struggle with dynamic network environments; 3) limited computing resources are hard to allocate reasonably. Therefore, we introduce a Three-Tier Integrated Computing Network (TICN) framework in this paper to provide reliable communication and computing support for IoT, which is jointly composed of base station, LEO satellites, and GEO satellite to serve as computing sites (CSs). Given that the optimization goal involves minimizing delay and energy consumption, task offloading is modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP). As one of the multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithms designed for coordinating multiple agents, QMixing (QMIX) is adopted to solve the optimization problem. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme provides robust performance in diverse conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning Based Time-Domain Precoding Extrapolation for Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: Precoding in massive multiple-input-multipleoutput (mMIMO) systems relies on the accurate acquisition of downlink channel state information (CSI). However, when the number of antennas is large, obtaining accurate CSI data incurs significant pilot and feedback overhead. In this paper, we propose a transformer based precoding network (TPN) that infers the future precoding matrices by exploring the timefrequency characteristic of historical wireless channels. Next, we design a suitable precoding matrix switching scheme based on channel correlation to further reduce the pilot overhead. Moreover, we leverage the network pruning technique to reduce the computational complexity of the proposed TPN. From the simulations the sum-rate has been improved by 15% compared with the traditional zero-order holding method.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Speech Semantic Communication System Based on Mamba and Parallel Channel-Spatial Attention.
abstract: This paper proposes DeepSC-M, an end-to-end speech semantic communication framework built upon the revised Mamba state space model. DeepSC-M integrates three key modules to maximize semantic fidelity under channel impairments. Specifically, a parallel channel-spatial attention (PCSA) mechanism is proposed to jointly model multi-layered semantic cues across channels and spatial dimensions, enhancing feature representation richness. And then the linear-complexity Mamba architecture is employed to efficiently capture longrange semantic dependencies across audio frames, ensuring computational efficiency. There after, a three-level cross-layer fusion scheme is proposed to facilitate precise recovery of finegrained acoustic details, mitigating channel noise and minimizing semantic loss. Experimental evaluations across diverse channel conditions demonstrate that DeepSC-M significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior noise robustness and enhanced semantic fidelity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Link Adaptation for ISAC Systems over Imperfect Vehicle-to-Infrastructure Channels.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) technology holds significant promise for future vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) networks by enabling joint resource utilization. However, imperfect wireless channels with mixed line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) components pose challenges to reliable adaptive modulation (AM). Accordingly, this paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-driven link adaptation strategy for ISAC systems in such dynamic V2I environments. Unlike conventional pilot-dependent methods, our approach leverages historical radar echo signals to predict modulation modes, eliminating pilot overhead, and enhancing spectral efficiency. A convolutional soft actor-critic dueling network (Conv-SAC-D-Net) is designed to extract spatiotemporal features from multi-dimensional echo matrices, enabling accurate modulation selection while bypassing channel estimation and matched filtering. The framework dynamically balances capacity maximization and bit error rate (BER) constraints through a dual-policy mechanism, prioritizing reliability near mode-switching thresholds. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly enhances both channel reliability and spectral efficiency compared to traditional pilot-based AM schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RLCVP: Collaborative Vehicular Perception Against Data Fabrication Attacks.
abstract: Collaborative vehicular perception enables connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) to share sensing data such as light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point clouds for higher perception accuracy and speed, which has performance degradation against data fabrication attacks that send faked sensing data with random probability. In this paper, a spatial consistency check is proposed to verify received feature maps, which builds a test statistic based on the number of conflict object locations in point clouds to detect faked sensing data. The reinforcement learning-based collaborative vehicular perception scheme is further proposed to enhance accuracy and speed, which chooses collaborative CAVs based on the geometry inconsistency of object locations, the data quality, the channel gains and the CAV reputations. Simulation results in LiDAR-based object detection show performance gains over benchmarks in terms of perception accuracy and speed against data fabrication attacks that manipulate up to$\mathbf{1 0}$regions in point clouds.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Probabilistic Covert Communication in Wireless-Powered Relay Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates a covert wireless-powered relay (CWPR) system with the aid of a full-duplex receiver, where the receiver acts as a friendly jammer to protect subsequent communication activities from eavesdropping while simultaneously transmitting RF energy to charge the relay. Meanwhile, a prior probability transmission scheme based on link information has been proposed to determine whether to forward information. Then, we derive the minimum detection error probability (DEP) of the eavesdropper (Eve) in two phases. Furthermore, we analyze how the prior transmission probability and interference power jointly affect Eve's DEP, covert rate as well as energy efficiency. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed transmission scheme can indeed effectively enhance the energy efficiency, and a prior probability of 0.5 cannot yield the best covert rate.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Distributed Offloading Strategy Considering Information Freshness in Drone Swarms.
abstract: In future 6G networks, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) can provide efficient communication and computing services. But due to limited computing and battery resources, UAVs often need to offload tasks to edge base stations or Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. To make full use of drone networks, multihop communication can be used for computation offloading. In this process, User Equipment (UE) first offloads computation tasks to a local UAV. This UAV processes part of the task and offloads the rest to a neighboring UAV. This continues until the task is done. However, during multi-hop offloading, UAVs may experience state information lag because of unstable communication links. This paper proposes a distributed computation offloading method that combines a predictor with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). The predictor models state updates and predictions, and Lyapunov stability theory ensures its stability. To handle uncertainties in multi-hop UAV offloading, the Multiagent Bidirectionally-Coordinated Nets (BiCNet) is used to optimize task processing and resource management. Simulation results show that this method effectively reduces latency and energy consumption in multi-hop UAV computation offloading.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy-Efficient Access Mechanism for Contention-Based Industrial IoT.
abstract: To effectively balance the energy overheads of idle listening and collision retransmissions in energy-constrained industrial Internet of things (IIoT) scenarios, this paper proposes a medium access control (MAC) layer access mechanism based on optimal transmission probability regulation. In particular, by constructing a system energy efficiency model that precisely captures the dynamic reduction process of contending stations, we first formulate the optimization problem of maximizing system energy efficiency and demonstrate its mathematical equivalence to the per-station service time minimization problem, and derive the closed-form expression for the latter. Subsequently, leveraging fractional programming theory, we transform the equivalent optimization problem into a series of parametric subproblems and design an iterative algorithm with guaranteed global convergence to precisely solve for the optimal transmission probability. Simulation results validate the rapid convergence of the proposed iterative algorithm and reveal the coincidence of the optimal mechanism with the capacity-driven benchmark, thereby validating the theoretical analysis while quantifying significant energy efficiency gains over the standard mechanism.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Movable Antenna Advanced Wireless Sensing with Scannable Angle Range.
abstract: With the rapid advancement of wireless sensing, movable antenna (MA) technology has recently emerged as a promising solution to improve the performance of wireless sensing compared to conventional fixed-position antennas (FPAs). However, existing systems often encounter the angle ambiguity problem under large antenna spacing. In this paper, we propose a scannable angle range aware wireless sensing approach using an MA array. We define the scannable angle range in which both self interference and mutual interference are eliminated, thereby avoiding the angle ambiguity problem. The Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) is adopted as the performance metric for wireless sensing and is further optimized. To derive the optimal MA array configuration for any angle within the scannable angle range, we minimize the worst-case CRB in double-target scenarios. This results in a bi-level optimization (BLO) problem, which is solved via the projective implicit gradient descent (PIGD) method. Numerical results demonstrate that the optimized MA arrays considerably outperform traditional FPA arrays in wireless sensing applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low-Complexity Rate Optimization for Fluid Antenna-Assisted Symbiotic Radio Systems.
abstract: Symbiotic radio (SR) is a promising technology designed to meet the increasing demand for spectrum-efficient communication. However, the small size of backscatter devices (BDs) typically equipped with a single antenna, poses challenges in achieving sufficient diversity or spatial multiplexing, hindering the advancement of SR. To address this challenge, we introduce fluid antennas (FAs) into the SR, which can dynamically adjust their positions to create a favorable wireless environment, enabling small devices to overcome spatial constraints and achieve significant diversity gains. In this paper, we investigate the uplink performance of FA-assisted SR (FA-SR). First, we derive exact and novel rate expressions and formulate the corresponding weighted sum-rate (WSR) problems. The positions of FAs and combining vectors are jointly optimized to maximize the WSR. Furthermore, we develop the joint optimization methods using chaotic sequence-based adaptive particle swarm optimization (CSA-PSO). Nevertheless, the high computational complexity poses a challenge to their practicality. To this end, we propose the low-complexity progressive optimization framework (POF), in which we can divide the initial problem into three subproblems and progressively solve them to find local optimal solutions. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed POF significantly reduces computational complexity with marginal performance loss compared to the joint optimization methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fusing Situations of Massive Mobile Nodes Improves the LLM-Based Attack Prediction for AI-Native Edges.
abstract: AI-native edges rely on machine learning methodologies to intelligently manage edge applications and serve massive access nodes, and hence hold great promise for the upcoming 6G communications. However, the distributed nature of AI-native edges and a huge number of heterogeneous mobile devices greatly expand the attack surface, resulting in the system being more fragile under various malicious activities. Inspired by recent advances in large language models (LLMs), this paper proposes LLM-ATP, a novel method that explores LLMs for attack prediction in AI-native edges. Specifically, we present a crossfusion mechanism that captures the spatial and temporal relations of attacks among multiple mobile devices, thereby benefiting attack predictions for AI-native edges. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our proposed LLM-ATP.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Symbol-Synchronous Communication for Ultra-Low-Power Multi-Hop Ambient IoT Networks.
abstract: Ambient Internet of Things (A-IoT) devices, as a critical enabler of future green IoT networks, have attracted broad interest from both industry and academia due to their ability to operate without batteries and with low maintenance costs. To accommodate their dynamic and constrained energy budget, an ultra-low-power connectivity protocol is required. Due to the severely limited transmit power of A-IoT devices, multi-hop connectivity is an interesting paradigm to extend their range. However, commonly used protocols for multi-hop communication may not be suitable for A-IoT due to excessive overhead related to channel access procedures, coordinated routing, and tight time synchronization requirements. This paper presents a novel network connectivity protocol based on symbolsynchronous transmissions, which allows battery-less relay nodes to participate in the forwarding process in an ad-hoc manner, without the need for synchronization or coordination. This allows them to adapt their duty cycle to the available harvested energy. Simulation results show that the proposed protocol can ensure high reliability in data packet delivery while significantly reducing the energy consumption of each relay node. We also investigate the relationship between wake-up probability and network density. For example, a 400 -node network in a 625 m2area can achieve a packet error rate below 1% with an average awake time of 6% per node, achieving an energy consumption reduction of 88% compared to the baseline approach.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Queue-Aware RL Scheduling with Stability Bounds in Large-Scale Cellular Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates adaptive transmission scheduling in large-scale cellular networks under dynamic traffic and interference conditions. Using stochastic geometry to capture spatial interference and incorporating queue dynamics at each base station, we aim to minimize long-term transmission cost subject to a delay constraint, via a Lagrangian relaxation. The problem is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process and solved via lightweight online reinforcement learning algorithms that adapts decisions to traffic and channel conditions. In parallel, we derive a stability bound from baseline policies through meta-distribution analysis, which provides benchmarks for dynamic scheduling policies. Numerical results show that the RL-based policies hold the same stability region as the baseline, while reducing the long-term Lagrangian cost by 26-30% under moderate to heavy loads, and up to 42% under light loads.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Metamaterial Backscatter for Symbiotic Sensing and Communication.
abstract: The future 6 G network aims to integrate batteryfree Internet of Things (IoT) devices to acquire massive environmental data. However, current battery-free IoT devices are often limited to simple identification tasks and lack diverse sensing capabilities. Fortunately, metamaterial sensing tags can reflect cellular signals to facilitate high-sensitivity environmental sensing while simultaneously serving as a reflection surface to enhance user communication. However, this dual functionality creates an inherent trade-off, as the cellular signals must carry original data while being modulated by the tag for sensing, leading to resource competition. This paper proposes a symbiotic meta-backscatter system to explicitly manage this conflict. We first derive a lower bound for communication capacity and an upper bound for sensing mutual information as unified performance metrics. Based on these metrics, we formulate a multi-objective optimization problem (MOOP) to jointly optimize the metamaterial tag's physical design and the base station's beamforming matrix. Simulation results demonstrate that our framework offers flexible trade-off solutions between sensing accuracy and communication quality.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Unified Reference Signal Sequence Design for Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: To advance the commercialization of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) from 6G Day 1, sensing functionality should be supported with minimal impacts on communication performance. This requirement motivates the concept of communication-oriented ISAC (CO-ISAC) systems. As an important technical enabler, reference signal (RS) sequence should be designed for CO-ISAC systems by taking both communication and sensing into consideration. The widely-used ZadoffChu (ZC) sequence in communication system is a good baseline for enhancement. With various approaches for ZC sequence enhancement, existing analyses are all based on the periodic autocorrelation and cross-correlation of sequences in time domain. Additionally, questions regarding whether and how to enhance ZC sequences for CO-ISAC remain open. In this paper, a unified RS sequence based on ZC is proposed, which integrates multiple enhancement approaches. Leveraging this unified structure, the aperiodic auto-correlation is analyzed to derive a closed-form expression for peak-to-sidelobe ratio (PSLR) of each unified sequence. Furthermore, the periodic cross-correlation is derived to determine the length of zero-correlation zone (ZCZ) for a set of unified sequences. Simulation results show that by generating multiple sequences via cyclic shifts and modulation sequences based on small number of optimized root index of ZC sequences, the proposed unified RS sequences could achieve 13dB PSLR gain, 8dB integrated sidelobe ratio (ISLR) gain and 1dB peak-to-average-power ratio (PAPR) gain compared to the ZC sequences used in new radio (NR).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Domain Feature-Aware Transformer for CSI Prediction in MIMO-OFDM.
abstract: Accurate channel state information (CSI) is essential for enabling many key techniques in MIMO-OFDM communication systems. Channel prediction has been recognized as an effective approach to reducing estimation and feedback overhead.
