However, existing methods often treat CSI merely as a temporal sequence, without fully exploiting its inherent multi-domain characteristics. In this paper, we propose a Transformer-based parallel prediction framework that effectively captures static CSI features across spatial, frequency, and complex domains, as well as dynamic temporal dependencies over both short and long terms. Specifically, we design a Complex-Aware Feature Module (CFM) to represent complex-valued CSI, introduce a Multi-Dimensional Attention Module (MDAM) to extract domainspecific features, and improve the Transformer backbone to better adapt to complex CSI prediction tasks. Extensive experiments on QuaDRiGa-simulated datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing baselines in terms of both prediction accuracy and robustness.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dynamic Dictionary-Based OMP for Super-Resolution Sensing in OFDM-ISAC Systems.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) improves spectrum utilization and enables emerging 6 G applications (e.g., autonomous driving and smart manufacturing) by jointly supporting data transmission and environmental sensing. Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is attractive for ISAC due to its wide adoption and multicarrier structure, but conventional DFT-based processing yields coarse delay-Doppler resolution under bandwidth and sampling constraints. Compressed-sensing approaches such as orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) can exploit sparsity, yet fixed-grid dictionaries suffer from basis mismatch, while off-grid refinements are often computationally prohibitive. To address these challenges, we propose a dynamic dictionary-based OMP method that progressively refines the delay-Doppler grid around coarse estimates and employs a non-uniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT) to accelerate correlation evaluation on the resulting non-uniform grid, enabling super-resolution estimation without constructing a globally dense dictionary. Simulations demonstrate improved delay-Doppler estimation accuracy over FFT- and standard OMP-based schemes and a more favorable accuracycomplexity trade-off than ESPRIT, indicating suitability for realtime OFDM-ISAC sensing in practical 6G deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Lightweight and Secure Extended Authentication and Key Agreement Protocol for Direct-to-Cell LEO Satellite Constellations.
abstract: The emergent direct-to-cell Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellations promise ubiquitous LTE/5G access for mobile users without terrestrial base stations. However, it still faces fake satellite attacks during the bootstrapping process, stemming from the openness of satellite-terrestrial links and the substantially higher user access demands imposed by global coverage compared to terrestrial base stations. Existing protocols make optimistic assumptions regarding satellite trustworthiness. Moreover, their poor scalability results in performance bottlenecks when handling massive authentication requests within short timeframes. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight and secure extended authentication and key agreement (eAKA) protocol under the Dolev Yao model. The protocol integrates a certificateless signature scheme to resist fake satellite attacks, a lightweight AMAD-based batch authentication mechanism to improve efficiency, and a group key update mechanism based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) to support dynamic user management and enhance scalability. Rigorous analysis demonstrates the protocol satisfies satellite authentication security requirements. Compared with the benchmark, it reduces computational, communication, and transmission overhead by$17.24 \%, 36.77 \%$, and 50 %, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RAS: Reconfiguration-Aware Adaptive Video Streaming Over Satellite Networks.
abstract: Live streaming has experienced rapid growth in recent years. In the meanwhile, commercial companies such as SpaceX and Amazon are providing low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite network services to millions of global users. As a result, an increasing number of users are using LEO satellite networks (LSNs) to watch live streaming videos on their devices. The bandwidth however owns a low upper limit and exhibits significant fluctuations due to satellite handovers and atmospheric conditions compared to terrestrial networks. This poses a challenge for scenarios that rely on LSNs for live streaming as the existing adaptive video streaming system cannot adapt to such highly dynamic network conditions which leads to low link utilization and a high frequency of video bitrate switches. To address these challenges, we propose RAS (Reconfiguration-aware Adaptive video streaming over Satellite networks), including a novel adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithm designed specifically for LSNs and a reconfiguration predictor. RAS leverages the inherent nature of satellite links caused by reconfiguration events, which divide the time domain into a sequence of independent subintervals. Our evaluation demonstrates that RAS significantly reduces bitrate instability and improves quality of experience (QoE) in real world. Compared with state-of-the-art ABR algorithms, RAS improves mean QoE score by more than 60%, while reducing switching rate by over 65%.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: ALADCP: Attention-Based Late-Fusion Anomaly Detection for V2V Collaborative Perception.
abstract: Multi-agent collaborative perception has become a key enabler for autonomous driving, as it extends perception range and improves reliability through inter-vehicle sensing information exchange. However, this cooperative framework introduces critical security risks, particularly through posespoofing attacks where malicious agents deliberately report falsified positional information. A key vulnerability of the efficient late-fusion paradigm is that existing security approaches often reintroduce the very communication and computational overhead it aims to minimize, either by relying on auxiliary data or complex trust models. To address this gap while preserving efficiency, we propose an Attention-based Late-fusion Anomaly Detection model (ALADCP), designed for real-time defense in vehicle-tovehicle (V2V) collaborative perception. It leverages an attention mechanism to capture the complex spatial dependencies between collaborating agents and the ego vehicle's perceptual state. We evaluate ALADCP extensively on the OPV2V dataset through extensive experiments. Experimental results demonstrate that ALADCP effectively captures late-fusion structural patterns and achieves significantly higher anomaly detection accuracy than conventional fusion-processing baselines. These findings highlight ALADCP as a practical and efficient security defense for multiagent collaborative perception, facilitating safer deployment of autonomous driving systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fast and Generalizable Task Scheduling in Double-Layered Satellite Network: A Graph-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: With the development of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Double-Layered Satellite Networks (DLSNs), a key focus is the optimization of the collaboration of LEO satellites at different orbital altitudes for efficient task data transmission. This study mainly focuses on the task scheduling problem under LEO DLSN. The goal of this problem is to maximize the total task benefit under the limited inter-layer resource. This problem is modeled as solving the Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS) problem based on the conflict graph. For different scenarios, especially large-scale scenarios, traditional exact algorithms and metaheuristic algorithms require a long time to solve and have low computational efficiency. To improve computational efficiency and generalization ability, we convert the MWIS problem into a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and leverage the powerful feature extraction capabilities of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). We propose an approach based on GraphSAGE combined with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). Through comparative experiments with other DRL and metaheuristic algorithms, the results show the advantages of the proposed algorithm in terms of computing time, computing task benefits, and generalization ability.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Communication-Efficient Vehicle Sensing with Federated Learning Based on Critical Learning Period and Weight Clustering.
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent transportation systems (ITS), vehicle recognition has become essential for traffic management and security. While Federated Learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving solution by training models locally, it faces significant challenges regarding communication overhead and non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data, which hinder model convergence and real-time application. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel communication-efficient sensing sheme based on FL optimization method by Critical Learning Period (CLP) and Weight Clustering (WC). The proposed method groups federated nodes into subfederations using a clustering algorithm based on data distribution similarity to mitigate Non-IID effects. Furthermore, it utilizes CLP theory to optimize client selection during sensitive learning phases and employs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to compress local model updates. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively reduces communication overhead, accelerates convergence speed, and achieves superior accuracy in vehicle recognition tasks compared to benchmark algorithms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: ASTDroid: Abstract Syntax Trees Enhanced GNNs for Android Malware Detection.
abstract: With the rapid evolution of Android malware, accurately identifying concealed malicious behaviors has become a core challenge in mobile security. Existing detection methods primarily rely on application-level macro features and lack deep exploration of code semantics within functions. As Abstract Syntax Tree(AST) can characterize code structure and implementation logic for capturing fine-grained semantic information. This paper proposes ASTDroid, an AST semantics-enhanced Android malware detection method. The method first constructs malicious behavior subgraphs(MBS) centered on sensitive APIs, employing neighborhood expansion strategies to compress graph size by over 83 % while preserving typical malicious behavior patterns. Subsequently, it employs pre-trained Tree-LSTM models to recursively aggregate Abstract Syntax Tree node features for capturing local code semantic information, and integrates MBS global features with AST local semantic features to achieve multi-level behavioral representation and feature enhancement. Finally, enhanced features are fed into graph neural networks(GNNs) for end-to-end learning. Experimental results demonstrate that ASTDroid achieves$\mathbf{9 9. 5 0 \%}$detection accuracy and 98.68 % classification accuracy, significantly outperforming existing methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Target Imaging with OFDM Transmission for Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), through the joint reuse of spectrum, power, and hardware resources, empowers low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) to deliver high-rate data transmission and advanced sensing capabilities simultaneously. In this paper, we propose a novel ISAC framework that enables high-resolution inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging of multi-target (MT) while supporting multi-user (MU) communication via an orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform. Specifically, we first establish a unified channel model for joint communication and sensing, then analyze the echo components after decoding. Furthermore, we introduce motion compensation techniques and outline the image formation for MT. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed image formation, demonstrating the ability to capture dynamic target features while preserving reliable downlink transmission, paving the way for ISAC-enabled surveillance and traffic-monitoring applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive Covariance Change Detection for Fluid Antenna Systems under Partial Observation.
abstract: Acquiring accurate channel covariance matrices is a prerequisite for Fluid Antenna Systems (FAS) to achieve reconfigurable spatial diversity and interference suppression. However, in dynamic environments, these matrices are subject to abrupt changes, which must be detected promptly to maintain system performance. Unlike conventional multi-antenna systems, change detection in FAS is fundamentally constrained by the limited number of RF chains, leading to a “partial observation” problem where significant covariance perturbations may become statistically invisible (i.e., change blindness). In this paper, we propose a rapid covariance change detection framework tailored for FAS. We first formulate the problem as a sequential change detection task based on partial observations and derive the EPI, a tractable metric that quantifies the fraction of the perturbation energy captured by a specific port selection. Guided by this metric, we design an Energy-Aware Adaptive Protocol that dynamically switches between a passive monitoring mode-reusing communication ports to minimize overhead-and an active detection mode that triggers dedicated sensing ports only when the risk of blindness is high. Furthermore, a greedy spatial diversity algorithm is developed to optimize the active port selection for maximal change detectability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly reduces detection delay compared to static benchmarks and approaches the performance of full-array systems with minimal impact on spectral efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Modeling and Parameter Estimation of Air-to-Ground Channels Using a Mixture of Skew Normal Distributions.
abstract: With the rapid development of Air-To-Ground (A2G) communications, the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) has become an important enabling technology of future wireless communication systems. In complex urban environments, wireless links alternates between two typical contrary conditions, i.e., Line-of-Sight (LoS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS), due to channel dynamics caused by the UAVs' high mobility. To better understand the characteristics of A2G channels, we study its statistical modeling with samples of path loss collected through ray-trace-based simulation in 3D city maps. After in-depth empirical study, we use mixed skew normal mixture distribution as the fitting model and propose a conditional Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm to estimate the model parameters. Simulation results show that the proposed model effectively fits the skewness and heterogeneity of the path loss, which significantly contributes to design and performance evaluation of UAV communication systems, especially in urban regions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adversarial Training: Enhancing Out-of-Distribution Generalization for Learning Wireless Resource Allocation.
abstract: Unsupervised learning has been extensively adopted to train deep neural networks (DNNs) for learning wireless resource allocation. Yet, the performance of DNNs is vulnerable to distribution shifts between training and test data, e.g., wireless channels. In this paper, we propose an offline unsupervised training method to enhance the out-of-distribution (OOD) generalizability of DNNs. Inspired by adversarial training (AT), the method trains DNNs using progressively identified adversarial examples out of the training distribution. To reflect OOD degradation of a DNN in the context of unsupervised learning, we reformulate the optimization problem of AT. The proposed method is evaluated by learning hybrid precoding. Simulation results showcase the enhanced OOD performance of multiple kinds of DNNs with approximately 5\(\sim\)20\% improvement across various channel distributions, even when the samples only from a single distribution (e.g., Rayleigh fading) are used for training.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: ViChan: A Dataset Generation Framework for Vision-aided Channel Estimation with Deep Learning.
abstract: Channel estimation is imperative for system design in wireless communications and is commonly computationally intensive with non-negligible overhead. Vision information is potentially a helpful assist for channel estimation since physical environment significantly affects radio propagation. Moreover, deep learning models for computer vision support better scene understanding and thus is a proper candidate technique for vision-aided channel estimation while being well trained with sufficient data. With such motivations, in this paper, we proposed ViChan, a novel and low-cost framework for generating paired image-channel dataset, which integrates two off-the-shelf tools for wireless channel simulation and environment image capture, respectively. Though the two modules are independent with each other, they operates in parallel and no interaction needs to be designed with ViChan. With such a cost-effective approach, the ground-truth channel information can be associated with the real-world environment images via appropriately designed indexing. Such a solid dataset of paired image-channel samples promisingly enables vision-aided channel estimation through design and training of deep learning models, boosting awareness, perceptiveness and intelligence of wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: SAR-OLSR: A Stable and Adaptive Routing Protocol for Flying Ad Hoc Networks.
abstract: The performance of Optimized Link State Routing (OLSR) protocol deteriorates significantly when it is deployed in flying ad hoc networks (FANETs), especially when the node speed is very high. This is mainly because that the highspeed nodes make the change of network topology more drastic. Therefore, the end-to-end routes are very difficult to be established and maintained. Although many improvements of OLSR have been proposed recently, their performance is still unsatisfactory in highly dynamic scenarios, especially when there are nodes of different speeds within the network. This paper proposed SAR-OLSR, an improvement considering both stability and reactivity, which not only selects more stable relay nodes when making routing decisions, but also makes the update of network topology more adaptively. Simulation results show that the proposed improvement outperforms existing competitors and achieves almost the best performance with almost the lowest control overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Simulation and Hardware Implementation of Multi-Link Channels for Maritime UAV-USVs Communications.
abstract: With the growing demands for maritime development and transportation, the communication links between unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and unmanned surface vehicle (USV) face significant technical bottlenecks in reliability. In maritime communication environments, signal propagation paths are altered by evaporation ducts and sea waves. Moreover, when multiple terminals share the same maritime channel, user correlation further complicates the modeling and analysis of the communication system. This paper addresses the lack of hardware implementations for UAV-to-multi-USVs channel models in maritime environments and incorporates channel non-stationarity into the hardware design. An Advanced RISC Machines and Field Programmable Gate Array (ARM-andFPGA) architecture based on a ZYNQ7000 chip as the hardware platform is employed. The ARM processor enables flexible parameter configuration, cluster evolution, and signal propagation path generation, while the FPGA's parallel processing capability facilitates the generation of channel parameters. Using this hardware emulator, the effects of UAV height, wind speed, and USV speed on inter-user correlations are investigated. Finally, comparative analysis with software simulation results validates the accuracy and practicality of the channel emulator.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MmWave Beam Prediction with Data Augmentation.
abstract: Deep learning has achieved outstanding performance in millimeter-wave (mmWave) beam prediction, whereas acquiring the optimal beam labels for model training imposes excessive overhead. To address this issue, this paper proposes to adopt data augmentation to efficiently train the mmWave beam prediction models with limited data. Specifically, two different data augmentation, namely input augmentation and label augmentation, are investigated. For input augmentation, cyclic shifting, flipping, and noise injection are used to extend the data features. For label augmentation, to fully leverage the guidance of sub-optimal beams, a power function of normalized beam received amplitude is used to redefine the label, and an adaptive exponent scheduler is employed to facilitate the model optimization. Simulation results show that our proposed approach significantly outperforms the conventional supervised learning methods in terms of normalized beamforming gain and model convergence rate, especially with extremely limited data.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: High-Accuracy Ranging Scheme for ISAC-OFDM Systems with Adaptive Chirp-Z Transform.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a key technology for autonomous navigation. It employs orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) for high-precision ranging, yet its sensing performance remains constrained by the system's range resolution. To address these challenges, this paper presents a high-accuracy ranging algorithm for OFDM-ISAC that adaptively determines the Chirp Z-Transform (CZT)'s refinement region through spectral feature analysis. Our method begins with a coarse frequency estimate obtained via the complex periodogram. We then analyze the spectral characteristics to identify critical frequency subbands for refinement. Finally, an improved adaptive CZT is applied within the selected subband to generate refined frequency estimates. Our approach adaptively optimizes the analysis window based on local spectral features, effectively mitigating the picket-fence effect and noise sensitivity. Simulation results verify that our algorithm reduces the mean ranging error by approximately 40 % compared to the baseline complex periodogram method, demonstrating significant accuracy improvement. The proposed approach exhibits strong robustness across diverse signal-tonoise ratio (SNR) conditions without introducing substantial computational overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DRL-Enabled Latency-Aware UAV Relays for Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: The rapid deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations is accelerating the evolution of integrated satellite-terrestrial networks (ISTNs), enabling global applications to directly access the satellite backbone via inter-satellite links (ISLs), especially in remote areas. However, heterogeneous ground environments cause uneven distribution of ISTN traffic, leading to inevitable high-load nodes along ISL routes. Existing routing schemes often rely on ISL detours for load balancing, but the extended propagation distance significantly increases end-toend latency. To address this challenge, we propose a UAV-assisted relay framework that establishes UAV-satellite links (USLs) to bypass congested multi-hop ISL routes, thereby reducing delivery latency. A soft actor-critic deep reinforcement learning (SAC-DRL) strategy is developed to dynamically optimize UAV placement, accounting for time-varying ISTN topology and traffic conditions. Simulation results based on a practical constellation show that our method achieves over 17 % latency reduction compared with ISL-only routing under growing traffic demands, demonstrating the promise of UAV-assisted routing in ISTNs with highly dynamic traffic.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Chameleon: Adaptive MPQUIC Packet Scheduler in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks via Online Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: In Multipath Quick UDP Internet Connections (MPQUIC) transmission, the performance of the packet scheduler varies with changes in wireless network conditions. A single fixed scheduler struggles to maintain optimal performance across different scenarios. Inspired by the selection principles of online learning algorithms, this paper proposes Chameleon: an online learning adaptive scheduler for MPQUIC. Chameleon treats several representative schedulers as a candidate set. It employs the multi-armed bandit algorithm to select the currently optimal scheduler online at coarse-grained time slots, while the selected scheduler executes at fine-grained per-packet level. This hierarchical design balances rapid response with operational overhead. We implemented Chameleon in MPQUIC and evaluated it against other classical schedulers across multiple typical scenarios. Results demonstrate that Chameleon consistently ranks among the top and often achieves shorter completion times and higher throughput overall while maintaining lightweight implementation and ease of deployment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Divergence Meets Dispersion: Efficient Wideband Beam Training for XL-MIMO.
abstract: Wideband extremely large-scale MIMO (XLMIMO) is a key enabler for 6 G networks, providing high spatial resolution and strong beamforming gains at millimeter-wave frequencies. However, efficient beam training under wideband and near-field (NF) conditions remains challenging due to hardware constraints and complex propagation characteristics. To address this, we propose a diverging-and-dispersion effect-based wideband beam training scheme that mitigates the deviation sensitivity of conventional focusing beams. The diverging effect broadens spatial coverage, while the dispersion effect introduces frequency-dependent beam splitting, jointly enabling efficient coarse beam search with fewer subcarriers and improved spectral efficiency. Moreover, the diverging codeword relies solely on phase modulation with constant amplitude, reducing hardware complexity. We further design an efficient dual-function system architecture, allowing simultaneous beam training and communication over the entire antenna array. Building on it, a lowoverhead wideband NF beam training algorithm is developed, achieving performance comparable to optimal benchmarks while significantly reducing resource usage. Simulation results verify the proposed method's robustness and efficiency, making it a practical solution for next-generation 6G XL-MIMO systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Value of Information-Based LQR Cost Optimization for Sensing-Communication-Control Enabled Vehicular Networks.
abstract: As vehicular networks (VNETs) advance towards greater autonomy, the integrated design of sensing and control is essential for ensuring system stability. Nevertheless, current distinct designs often prioritize enhancing communication throughput or reducing latency independently, neglecting to consider their effects on control stability and cost efficiency. Therefore, this paper proposes a value of information (VoI)-based sensing-communication-control (SCC) system to address this gap in centralized VNETs. Specifically, we first propose a control-oriented VoI metric to measure the impact of information freshness and accuracy on system regulation. Subsequently, recognizing that optimal control relies on perfect state information, we decompose the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) cost into downlink control and uplink sensing components and formulate a penalty function to characterize the additional cost induced by sensing estimation errors. Finally, we formulate a min-max resource allocation problem, solved via a low-complexity algorithm that exploits monotonicity to ensure fairness. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly reduces worst-case LQR costs compared to benchmarks and reveals the inherent latencyperformance trade-off.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Spectral Estimation and Multi-Level Differential Self-Interference Cancellation for ISAC Systems.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems encounter severe self-interference when they transmit and receive simultaneously. To mitigate this challenge, we propose a joint spectral estimation and multi-level differential selfinterference cancellation (JSIC) algorithm. First, we combine a two-dimensional discrete fourier transform (2D-DFT) with a cell-averaging constant false alarm rate (CA-CFAR) detector to estimate the self-interference spectral. This joint estimation captures frequency offsets from hardware non-idealities, thereby improving the self-interference spectrum localization. Building on this estimate, we develope a multi-level differential cancellation algorithm, which utilizes multiple levels of differences to sequentially eliminate the self-interference components while retaining the sensing signal. Evaluated with measured data, the proposed JSIC algorithm outperforms current state-of-the-art algorithms in strong self-interference scenarios, demonstrating enhanced robustness and clear potential for deployment in nextgeneration ISAC systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Towards Energy-Efficient and Freshness-Sensitive WBANs Through Joint Scheduling and Power Control Via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: To enable accurate health condition assessments and prompt medical responses, wireless body area networks (WBANs) must timely delivery the status updates. However, this often requires frequent sensing and transmissions from biosensors, which substantially increase their energy consumption. In this paper, we study the trade-off between energy efficiency and information freshness by formulating a multiobjective optimization (MOO) problem that jointly minimizes energy consumption and the age of information (AoI) for each transmission session. To address these conflicting objectives, we propose training an intelligent agent that simultaneously optimizes scheduling and power control decisions under varying user preferences. Specifically, we reformulate the MOO problem as a multi-objective parameterized-action Markov decision process (MOPAMDP) and develop a preference-guided multi-objective parameterized deep$Q$-network (PG-MOPDQN) solution to approximate the Pareto front. Simulation results demonstrate that our PG-MOPDQN solution provides a more accurate Pareto front approximation than traditional multiobjective deep$Q$-network (MODQN), achieving performance close to the performance lower bound. Moreover, the proposed approach effectively adapts scheduling decisions and transmit power levels in WBANs according to user preferences for each session.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: SAP-User Association and Power Allocation in Cell-Free Massive MIMO-Enabled LEO Satellite Networks with Coverage Limitation.
abstract: Low-earth orbit (LEO) satellites have garnered significant attention for their potential to deliver global connectivity with low latency and high throughput. In the paper, we investigate cell-free massive multi-input multi-output (MIMO)-enabled LEO satellite communications. Unlike previous work which selects satellites from the entire satellite constellation, this work restricts selection to a subset of satellite access points (SAPs) that cover the user, referred to as the SAP-user association scheme. We consider a comprehensive channel model accounting for the impact of Doppler effects and time delay, and derive a closed-form expression of the system energy efficiency (EE). Based on it, we jointly optimize SAP-user association and downlink power allocation to maximize EE, subject to SAP coverage range constraints and total power limitations. Simulation results validate the accuracy of our theoretical derivations and highlight the superiority of the proposed joint optimization algorithm. Compared with previous works that optimize only standalone parameters, our method achieves significantly higher EE, with the performance advantage becoming increasingly in dense-user scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Pickup and Trajectory Optimization for Cellular Cargo UAV under Connectivity and Energy Constraints.
abstract: In the emerging low-altitude economy, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) show great potential for urban logistics. Existing works often decouple trajectory planning from task scheduling, neglecting the critical coupling between payloaddependent energy consumption, strict pickup time windows, and communication reliability with ground base stations (GBSs). To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Communication Reliability Value Picking with Time Windows (CRVP-TW) strategy, a novel two-stage optimization framework. First, we introduce an SNR-Aware Theta* algorithm combined with a radio map to generate flight paths that ensure continuous connectivity (SNR$\geq \gamma_{t h}$) while minimizing flight distance, thereby reducing travel time and energy costs compared to traditional grid-based or sampling methods. Second, utilizing the generated reliable travel cost matrix, we propose an adaptive hybrid genetic algorithm (AHGA) with a multi-constraint look-ahead decoder. This algorithm jointly optimizes the user visiting sequence and payload allocation to maximize the total collected value under strict time and energy budgets. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms baseline schemes. CRVPTW improves the total collected value by approximately$\mathbf{3 1 \%}$compared to greedy baselines under strict resource constraints, validating its robustness in ensuring communication reliability and energy efficiency for high-value logistics missions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Symbol-wise Methods to Improve Sensing Performance of Single Carrier Waveform.
abstract: Nonlinear power amplifier (PA) distortion and sensing performance are two critical concerns when using communication waveform for uplink sensing. In the first part of the paper, we prove that there is no communication signal base e.g., orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and single carrier (SC) that excels at both PA efficiency and sensing performance by solving a Pareto optimization problem using two relevant metrics i.e., integrated ranging sidelobe (EISL) and temporal power variance (TPV). In the second part, we seek to improve the sensing performance of SC. Specifically, we propose some symbol-wise methods to optimize the sidelobe of 2 dimensional periodic autocorrelation functions (2d P-ACF) of CP-SC (cyclic prefixd singlecarrier) in one coherent processing interval (CPI) while restricting the loss of communication performance. Simulation results are shown to validate our algorithms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Wireless Semantic Multicasting: A Framework for Efficient Multi-Modal Multi-Task Communications.
abstract: Supporting massive multi-user and multi-modal communication poses a significant challenge for future wireless networks. Multicasting and semantic communications are two effective ways to improve transmission efficiency. However, Existing semantic communication research predominantly relies on unicast, while traditional multicast is ill-suited for users with diverse semantic needs. In this paper, we introduce a novel wireless semantic multicasting (WSM) framework. By clustering users based on semantic similarity, WSM dynamically forms multicast groups that share a common semantic representation, thereby reducing redundant transmissions while preserving task relevance. To accommodate heterogeneous inputs and tasks, we design a sample-aware modality fusion mechanism and task-specific decoders, supported by a boosting-inspired training strategy that emphasizes hard samples. A lightweight rebalancing method further ensures fair task distribution across semantic groups during training. Experiments on multi-modal tasks—including image classification, text classification, and visual question answering—demonstrate that WSM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art unicast and traditional multicast baselines. Under fixed bandwidth, WSM achieves up to 10.81% improvement in average task accuracy while maintaining scalability as the number of users increases.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Large Language Models as Bidding Agents in Repeated HetNet Auction.
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of large language models (LLMs) as reasoning agents in repeated spectrum auctions within heterogeneous networks (HetNets). While auction-based mechanisms have been widely employed for efficient resource allocation, most prior works assume one-shot auctions, static bidder behavior, and idealized conditions. In contrast to traditional formulations where base station (BS) association and power allocation are centrally optimized, we propose a distributed auction-based framework in which each BS independently conducts its own multi-channel auction, and user equipments (UEs) strategically decide both their association and bid values. Within this setting, UEs operate under budget constraints and repeated interactions, transforming resource allocation into a long-term economic decision rather than a oneshot optimization problem. The proposed framework enables the evaluation of diverse bidding behaviors-from classical myopic and greedy policies to LLM-based agents capable of reasoning over historical outcomes, anticipating competition, and adapting their bidding strategy across episodes. Simulation results reveal that the LLM-empowered UE consistently achieves higher channel access frequency and improved budget efficiency compared to benchmarks. These findings highlight the potential of reasoningenabled agents in future decentralized wireless networks markets and pave the way for lightweight, edge-deployable LLMs to support intelligent resource allocation in next-generation HetNets.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dynamic Task Offloading with Active Inference and LLM Integration for Low-Altitude Networks.
abstract: With the rapid growth of low-altitude network technologies, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can efficiently perform aerial data collection, real-time monitoring, and autonomous operations in remote environments. This advancement enables seamless connectivity and enhanced performance for unmanned aerial systems. However, coordinating these tasks remains challenging because it requires translating humanreadable instructions into machine-executable plans while managing limited resources, which often leads to suboptimal scheduling, high latency, and excessive energy consumption in traditional methods. In this paper, we propose a dynamic task offloading and resource allocation approach that combines active inference with large language model (LLM) integration. It uses LLMs to create intuitive task graphs from natural language inputs, applies active inference to minimize variational free energy for adaptive offloading, and incorporates an incremental update mechanism to locally reschedule affected tasks, avoiding full recomputation. Extensive simulation results show that our proposed method has superior performance over mainstream deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms, reduces makespan and energy-delay product (EDP), and is more adaptable to dynamic scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Improvement of Sounding Reference Signal in Advanced TDD Massive MIMO System.
abstract: The performance of MIMO systems relies heavily on accurate channel state information (CSI), traditionally acquired through pilot-based estimation. However, this approach presents a fundamental trade-off: while increasing the number of reference signals enhances CSI accuracy, it also consumes valuable resources that could be allocated to data transmission. To address the critical challenge of pilot overhead in massive MIMO systems, this paper investigates channel-adding Reference Signal (SRS) schemes. We propose and evaluate several schemes in a 3GPPcompliant simulation environment, demonstrating significant performance gains over conventional fixed SRS configurations. We expect these schemes will be strong candidates for future massive MIMO system.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Performance Analysis of NOMA-Assisted Optical OFDM ISAC Systems with Clipping Distortion.
abstract: This paper studies the performance of optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM)-based multiuser integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems employing non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). Due to their inherent high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), OFDM waveforms are clipped to fit the limited dynamic range of the optical transmitters (e.g., light-emitting diodes (LEDs)), resulting in clipping distortion. To alleviate the impact of the distortion, we propose a novel transmitter architecture where the clipping processes are performed before NOMA superposition coding. We then analyze the performance of the proposed optical ISAC systems considering the effects of power allocation and clipping distortion. For the communication subsystem, we analyze the effect of NOMA on the achievable sum rate and bit error rate (BER). For the sensing subsystem, the root mean square error (RMSE) and Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) of estimating the transmission distance accuracy are obtained. Simulation results reveal that allocating more power to the strong user yields a higher sum rate, lower BER, and better sensing performance, whereas a more balanced power allocation among users results in degraded BER and sensing performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: SABR: A Stable Adaptive Bitrate Framework Using Behavior Cloning Pretraining and Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning.
abstract: With the advent of 5G, the internet has entered a new video-centric era. From short-video platforms like TikTok to long-video platforms like Bilibili, online video services are reshaping user consumption habits. Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) control is widely recognized as a critical factor influencing Quality of Experience (QoE). Recent learning-based ABR methods have attracted increasing attention. However, most of them rely on limited network trace sets during training and overlook the wide-distribution characteristics of real-world network conditions, resulting in poor generalization in out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose SABR, a training framework that combines behavior cloning (BC) pretraining with reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning. We also introduce benchmarks, ABRBench-3G and ABRBench-4G+, which provide wide-coverage training traces and dedicated OOD test sets for assessing robustness to unseen network conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that SABR achieves the best average rank compared with Pensieve, Comyco, and NetLLM across the proposed benchmarks. These results indicate that SABR enables more stable learning across wide distributions and improves generalization to unseen network conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Robust Non-Linear Transceiver Design for Multicarrier MIMO SWIPT.
abstract: This paper studies a power splitting (PS)-based multicarrier multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system with Tomlinson-Harashima precoding (THP). Under imperfect channel state information (CSI), our goal is to minimize the sum mean-square-error (MSE) subject to the transmit power and energy harvesting (EH) constraints. Since the formulated problem is non-convex, we propose an alternating optimization (AO)-based algorithm to jointly optimize the precoding matrices, feedback matrices, equalization matrices and PS ratio. Considering the high complexity of the AO-based algorithm, we also propose a low-complexity structural solution (SS)-based algorithm, which exploits the closed-form expressions of equalization matrices, feedback matrices and precoding matrices to establish an equivalent problem in terms of the power allocation and PS ratio. Then the equivalent problem can be solved by a two-layer optimization scheme. Simulation results show that the SS-based algorithm achieves an approximate sum MSE performance as the AO-based algorithm, and outperforms the non-robust design.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Secure Transmission Method of OTFS with Low Peak-to-Average Power Ratio Based on Polar Codes.
abstract: Driven by 6G next-evolution waveform (NEW) targets, orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) faces urgent peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and security challenges. To address the issues of high PAPR and insecure transmission in OTFS systems, this paper proposes a secure OTFS transmission method with low PAPR based on polar codes. Firstly, the secret keys are generated based on the feature of the wireless channel, which can be used as the initial value for the chaotic generator to produce more chaotic sequences. Then, the index values of the segmented chaotic sequences are placed in the optimal information bits of the polar codes. The remaining information is encrypted using the chaotic sequences corresponding to the index values. Finally, the encrypted result with the lowest PAPR is selected for OTFS transmission. Simulation results show that the legitimate receiver can accurately decrypt and decode the signal by using the proposed method. However, the eavesdropper can not obtain plaintext imformation without correct chaotic sequence. Besides, this method can significantly reduce the PAPR of the OTFS system, and the PAPR performance can be further optimized by adjusting parameters.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Message Passing Based Parameter Estimation in Cooperative MIMO-OFDM ISAC Systems.
abstract: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks, multiple base stations (BSs) collaboratively sense a common target, leveraging diversity from multiple observation perspectives and joint signal processing to enhance sensing performance. This paper introduces a novel message-passing (MP)-based parameter estimation framework for collaborative MIMO-OFDM ISAC systems, which jointly estimates the target's position and velocity. First, a signal propagation model is established based on geometric relationships, and a factor graph is constructed to represent the unknown parameters. The sum-product algorithm (SPA) is then applied to this factor graph to jointly estimate the multi-dimensional parameter vector. To reduce communication overhead and computational complexity, we employ a hierarchical message-passing scheme with Gaussian approximation. By adopting parameterized message distributions and layered processing, the proposed method significantly reduces both computational complexity and inter-BS communication overhead. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MP-based parameter estimation algorithm and highlight the benefits of multi-perspective observations and joint signal processing for cooperative sensing in MIMO-OFDM ISAC systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: V2X-Fusion: Multi-Modal BEV Perception with V2X Message Integration.
abstract: In an Intelligent Transportation System (ITS), collaborative perception plays a vital role in enhancing road safety. Most collaborative perception studies utilize images and point clouds for fusion decision-making. This may cause low sensing precision under Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) conditions. To address this issue, we propose a unified V2X-Fusion framework that leverages Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) messages to augment environmental perception. In particular, we propose two multi-modal cooperative perception modes: a lightweight model for real-time efficiency, and a comprehensive model for higher accuracy. These methods integrate image, point cloud, and V2X message to enhance road perception in complex traffic scenarios. In the fusion module, we construct bird's-eye view (BEV) representations for each modality. We employ a masking mechanism to distinguish between known and inferred regions to avoid semantic conflicts during fusion. We conducted extensive experiments on the nuScenes dataset. The results show that our methods significantly improve BEV perception accuracy, particularly in cases of occlusion and long-range targets.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Satellite Association and SFC Placement with Stability Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) mega-constellations enable global, low-latency connectivity but challenge the security function chain (SFC) orchestration due to fast-changing visibility, resource volatility, and heterogeneous quality of service (QoS) requirements. To tackle this issue, we present in this paper SATStab, a stability-aware orchestration framework that co-designs: (i) stability-regularized objectives penalizing configuration churn across time windows; (ii) temporal decoupling with visibility-aware repair and warm starts; and (iii) hierarchical decoupling that separates fast association decisions from slower SFC placement and resource allocation. We formulate SATStab as a mixed-integer non-linear programming (MINLP) problem and evaluate it with realistic LEO dynamics. We solve it through a two-stage approach, where in the first stage, we optimize satellite-user associations while in the second stage, we optimize SFC placements. Through extensive simulations, we show that, relative to a monolithic MINLP, SATStab reduces user-satellite handovers by 54.3%, satellite-ground station (GS) re-associations by 59.3%, and SFC migrations by 32.7%, while cutting solution time by 56.8% without degrading end-to-end (E2E) delay. These results prove the efficiency of SATStab in terms of resource orchestration and resilience.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Graph Neural Network for Proactive Anomaly Prediction in Dynamic Wireless Networks.
abstract: Dynamic wireless networks face evolving cyber threats that challenge reactive security paradigms. Proactive anomaly prediction requires modeling spatial-temporal attack propagation with uncertainty quantification, but existing dynamic graph neural networks use loosely-coupled architectures and static uncertainty mechanisms. We propose DST-BGNN (Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Graph Neural Network), featuring three key innovations: (1) tightly-coupled ST-GCN layers that jointly model spatial neighborhood aggregation and temporal state transitions within each convolution operation; (2) Dynamic Monte Carlo Dropout that adapts uncertainty quantification to time-varying model confidence; (3) a Random Walk with Restart module that refines predictions by explicitly simulating threat propagation over network topology. Evaluated on UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, and CTU-13 datasets, DST-BGNN improves F1-score by 2.1-3.8% and AUC-PR by 4.1-5.4% over state-of-the-art baselines. At 5-hour prediction horizon, it achieves F1=0.689 with 4.2% advantage. Ablation studies show BiLSTM contributes 4.8% F1 while dynamic dropout improves calibration by 26.7% (ECE: 0.161 → 0.118) without accuracy loss. Hyperparameter analysis confirms robust performance. With 824ms inference latency, DST-BGNN enables practical proactive security for wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Experimental Evaluation of 5G NR-U and Wi-Fi Coexistence in the 5 GHz Unlicensed Band Using SDR.
abstract: The operation of 5 G New Radio in unlicensed bands (NR-U) is a critical enabler for expanding wireless capacity. However, ensuring fair coexistence with incumbent Wi-Fi systems remains a significant implementation challenge. While numerous simulation studies have explored this topic, there is a lack of experimental validation using accessible, opensource hardware platforms. In this paper, we present a practical evaluation of NR-U and Wi-Fi coexistence using a SoftwareDefined Radio (SDR) testbed. We implement a standalone NRU gNodeB on the OpenAirInterface platform, incorporating Listen-Before-Talk (LBT) mechanisms to govern channel access. Preliminary discrete-event simulations were utilized strictly for parameter selection to ensure regulatory compliance before hardware deployment. The primary contribution of this work is the experimental verification of NR-U/Wi-Fi coexistence using an open-source SDR platform under real interference conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that properly configured NRU can coexist with Wi-Fi in the 5 GHz band, maintaining stable incumbent throughput and achieving a high fairness index (> 0.95). These findings provide empirical evidence supporting the feasibility of NR-U deployments using open-source SDR tools.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Lightweight Multimodal LLM-Based Intrusion Detection System for Open RAN.
abstract: Open Radio Access Network architectures introduce unprecedented openness and programmability through RAN Intelligent Controllers, expanding the attack surface beyond traditional volumetric threats. Most existing intrusion detection systems for fifth-generation mobile networks and ORAN rely primarily on numerical Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), often overlooking the security-relevant semantics embedded in logs and control messages. This paper proposes LLM4IDS, a semantic-aware and multimodal intrusion detection system that fuses lightweight Large Language Model (LLM) embeddings of textified events with traditional tabular KPIs in a compact Transformer-based classifier. Evaluated on the realworld OpenIreland O-RAN dataset and two classical IP network benchmarks (UNSW-NB15 and CICIDS2017), LLM4IDS consistently matches or surpasses strong tabular baselines while maintaining high efficiency. On OpenIreland, it reaches nearperfect detection (F1-score$\approx 1.0$) and yields large gains for application-layer and volumetric attacks compared to KPI-only models. Across datasets, the classifier maintains an approximately 4 MB footprint and sub-millisecond CPU inference latency; the frozen sentence-LLM encoder can be shared across tasks, and its embeddings can be cached or precomputed when required by the deployment pipeline. These results indicate that integrating semantic context through multimodal fusion can significantly enhance intrusion detection in O-RAN while remaining competitive on standard IP-based IDS tasks. To the best of our knowledge, this work is among the first to study a complete multimodal LLM-based IDS pipeline for O-RAN data with cross-domain evaluation on both O-RAN and classical IP benchmarks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Channel Charting in Smart Radio Environments.
abstract: This paper introduces the use of static electromagnetic skins (EMSs) to enable robust device localization via channel charting (CC) in realistic urban environments. We develop a rigorous optimization framework that leverages EMS to enhance channel dissimilarity and spatial fingerprinting, formulating EMS phase profile design as a codebook-based problem targeting the upper quantiles of key embedding metric, localization error, trustworthiness, and continuity. Through 3D ray-traced simulations of a representative city scenario, we demonstrate that optimized EMS configurations, in addition to significant improvement of the average positioning error, reduce the 90th-percentile localization error from over 60 m (no EMS) to less than 25 m, while drastically improving trustworthiness and continuity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to exploit Smart Radio Environment (SRE) with static EMS for enhancing CC, achieving substantial gains in localization performance under challenging None-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Sustainable and Intelligent Unified LPWAN-as-a-Service Framework for $\mathbf{6 G}$ IoT Using RedCap.
abstract: G Reduced Capability (RedCap) is a promising technology introduced to bridge the gap between legacy LPWAN technologies (i.e., NB-IoT, LTE-M, URLLC) and full 5G NR. However, 5G RedCap operates with fixed radio parameters and cannot dynamically adapt to changing service requirements. This paper proposes a Unified LPWAN-as-a-Service (ULaaS) framework that leverages existing provision of 5 G NR to optimize the RRC parameters, such as bandwidth part, power class, antenna configuration, and modulation scheme, to support legacy LPWAN technologies-inspired operational behaviours within a Single 5G RedCap device and policy-driven network architecture. The framework enables multi-persona operation by dynamically changing configurations through standard 5G management entities-specifically the Network Exposure Function (NEF), Policy Control Function (PCF), and Session Management Function (SMF). This software-driven approach aligns well with the 6 G design principles of intelligent control, hardware reuse, and resource-efficient networking, enabling the sustainable and intelligent Green Internet of Things. The implementation of ULaaS is realized on MATLAB-based waveform-assisted evaluation to demonstrate that the adaptive RedCap parameter tuning can effectively approximate the latency, throughput, and energyefficiency behavior of legacy LPWAN technologies. The results show that ULaaS can serve as a unified layer that enhances RedCap's flexibility for heterogeneous IoT deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Attribute-Based Physical-Layer Authentication in Next-Generation Wireless Networks.
abstract: Ensuring secure and effective authentication has become more and more important since wireless networks continue to grow in complexity and size. Traditional cryptographic methods, while robust, frequently result in significant computational and communication overhead. In this study, a framework for physical-layer authentication (PLA) is introduced for future wireless networks, utilizing various radio attributes and unsupervised clustering techniques to verify end devices. Our clusteringbased approach begins with systematic data preprocessingfeature selection, standardization, and outlier removal to address typical wireless data challenges like inconsistent scaling and environmental noise. Device signatures are constructed from sliding temporal windows, combining persistent mean values and intra-window feature correlations to capture both longterm device behavior and subtle attribute dependencies. Clustering algorithms, including K-Means and hierarchical densitybased spatial clustering of applications with noise (HDBSCAN), are evaluated for their ability to group devices and detect anomalies, with model selection driven by internal validity and interpretability. Experimental results from a 5 G testbed show that our multistage, data-driven methodology robustly separates devices and efficiently identifies anomalies, offering a practical and adaptive alternative to conventional authentication schemes for low-latency, high-density, and dynamic network deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Anti-Jamming Performance Analysis of LEO Mega-Constellations With Flexible User Association.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) mega-constellations are promising enablers of 6 G networks, offering high throughput, low latency, and global coverage. However, their low orbital altitude, publicly accessible ephemerides, and open wireless channels render them particularly vulnerable to uplink jamming attacks. While the massive number of LEO satellites provides spatial diversity that can be exploited through flexible user association for jamming mitigation, the resilience of such large-scale constellations against organized, coordinated jamming remains unexplored. This paper investigates the uplink performance of LEO mega-constellations under large-scale jamming attacks and derives a tractable expression for outage probability and average throughput using stochastic geometry. Numerical results reveal that when user association is fixed and known to adversaries, increasing satellite density yields negligible anti-jamming gains. In contrast, under flexible association unknown to jammers, the jammer density must scale with the satellite density to maintain a given outage probability, highlighting the effectiveness of flexible user association in enhancing network resilience.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On the Limitations of Ray-Tracing for Learning-Based RF Tasks in Urban Environments.
abstract: We study the realism of Sionna v1.0.2 ray-tracing for outdoor cellular links in central Rome. We use a real measurement set of 1,664 user-equipments (UEs) and six nominal base-station (BS) sites. Using these fixed positions we systematically vary the main simulation parameters, including path depth, diffuse/specular/refraction flags, carrier frequency, as well as antenna's properties like its altitude, radiation pattern, and orientation. Simulator fidelity is scored for each base station via Spearman correlation between measured and simulated powers, and by a fingerprint-based k-nearest-neighbor localization algorithm using RSSI-based fingerprints. Across all experiments, solver hyper-parameters are having immaterial effect on the chosen metrics. On the contrary, antenna locations and orientations prove decisive. By simple greedy optimization we improve the Spearman correlation by 5% to 130% for various base stations, while kNN-based localization error using only simulated data as reference points is decreased by one-third on real-world samples, while staying twice higher than the error with purely real data. Precise geometry and credible antenna models are therefore necessary but not sufficient; faithfully capturing the residual urban noise remains an open challenge for transferable, high-fidelity outdoor RF simulation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-LEO Satellite Transmission with Terrestrial Coexistence: A Coverage-Enhanced and Interference-Mitigated Framework.
abstract: The integration of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites with terrestrial base stations (TBSs) is envisioned as a cornerstone of future wireless networks. However, coexistence of dense terrestrial deployments with large-scale LEO constellations introduces a fundamental challenge: maximizing LEO throughput while strictly protecting terrestrial users from harmful interference. In this work, we propose a coverage-enhanced and interference-mitigated power allocation (CIPA) framework that adaptively controls the transmit power of multi-beam LEO satellites under interference constraints at TBS-served users. By jointly applying the Lagrangian dual and quadratic transforms, the originally non-convex problem is reformulated into tractable subproblems with closed-form auxiliary updates and convex power allocation, ensuring provable equivalence and efficient convergence. Extensive simulations on both synthetic deployments and real automatic identification system (AIS) maritime datasets demonstrate that CIPA not only achieves substantial throughput gains but also enhances user coverage by dynamically balancing load between LEO and TBS layers. Compared with existing benchmarks, CIPA yields at least 28.9% throughput improvement while remaining close to brute-force performance at a fraction of the complexity. These results highlight CIPA as a practical and near-optimal resource management solution for integrated terrestrial-satellite networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: FedLoad: Adaptive Partial Training for Model Heterogeneous Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) faces significant challenges in real-world deployments due to the heterogeneity of client devices and the high resource demands of training large models. This paper proposes FedLoad, a framework for model-heterogeneous FL that dynamically assigns pruned submodels to heterogeneous clients based on their system capabilities. FedLoad introduces an adaptive partial training mechanism that creates personalized submodels by pruning a shared global model. We design a contextual bandit that leverages non-sensitive client information to assign smaller models to resource-constrained clients while leveraging powerful clients to maintain accuracy. We evaluated our approach on two widely adopted datasets under various dynamic and heterogeneous system conditions. Results show that FedLoad reduces average round duration by up to 26.1 %, energy consumption by up to 33.6 %, and communication cost by up to 29.5 % compared to existing FL methods while achieving similar accuracy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Scheduler for B5G Networks.
abstract: The beyond fifth-generation (B5G) wireless networks has emerged as a revolutionary technology to envision large-scale access to high-speed communications across devices, thus paving towards a smart information society. One crucial component to facilitate this large-scale access in B5G networks is the scheduler. Inspite of the success of the current 5 G scheduling strategies, i.e., round-robin, best channel quality indicator (CQI), proportional-fair (PF), these strategies rely solely on fixed heuristics and are most likely to fall short in dynamic propagation environments that will shape up networks beyond 5 G. To address this challenge, we advocate a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) driven scheduler adhesive to the B5G standard. Specifically, in this work, we develop a third-generation project partnership (3 GPP) standard-compliant deep-Q network (DQN) based DRL framework to optimize the priority of the user equipments (UEs) in the network to enhance the net throughput in both uplink and downlink, while preserving fairness among the UEs. Simulation results substantiate the effectiveness of our DRL-based scheduler in achieving enhanced throughput and fairness compared to the existing standard schedulers.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Toward an Intrusion Detection System for a Virtualization Framework in Edge Computing.
abstract: Edge computing pushes computation closer to data sources, but it also expands the attack surface on resource-constrained devices. This work explores the deployment of the Lightweight Deep Anomaly Detection for Network Traffic (LDPI) integrated as an isolated service within a virtualization framework that provides security by separation. LDPI, adopting a Deep Learning approach, achieved strong training performance, reaching AUC 0.999 (5-fold mean) across the evaluated packet-window settings (n, l), with high F1 at conservative operating points. We deploy LDPI on a laptop-class edge node and evaluate its overhead and performance in two scenarios: (i) comparing it with representative signature-based IDSes (Suricata and Snort) deployed on the same framework under identical workloads, and (ii) while detecting network flooding attacks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Incremental Vision Transformers for Zero-Day Attack Detection in NextG Wireless Networks.
abstract: As wireless networks evolve into the backbone of modern society, they become increasingly exposed to emerging security threats. Although many works explore AI-based intrusion detection systems for 5 G wireless networks, the proposed algorithms are typically characterized by closed-set assumptions: once trained on a finite number of attack classes, they lack mechanisms for automatic updates on novel classes of attacks. This limitation becomes critical in scenarios where new threats emerge daily. To address this, we propose a framework for real-time detection of zero-day attacks. Our approach exploits Vision Transformers (ViT) to process network flows represented as images, enabling the capture of complex temporal and spatial patterns in data traffic. To cope with previously unseen attack classes, the ViT is equipped with a modular classification head that flags low-confidence samples as potential novel attacks. These samples are then processed with DBSCAN to discover new attack classes, thereby avoiding the need for full model retraining. The proposed model achieves an average F 1 -score of 94 %, showing performance comparable to existing computer vision-based intrusion detection system approaches. We further tested the incremental learning system with a Leave-One-ClassOut protocol. Under this setting, the framework achieves nearbaseline performance for several minority classes, and limited recovery for majority or overlapping classes. This shows that flow-based visual encoding combined with self-attention can support zero-day classification when the held-out distribution is well-separated in the embedding space.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Physical Layer Authentication for Wireless Powered Fog Computing Networks.
abstract: Wireless Powered Fog Computing (WPFC) networks face a critical challenge where resource-constrained fog nodes cannot support traditional cryptographic authentication for numerous IoT devices. This paper proposes a Physical-Layer Authentication (PLA) scheme exploiting channel state information for lightweight device verification while jointly optimizing communication resources. We formulate a mixed-integer non-convex optimization problem to maximize sum communication rate under authentication, energy, and quality-of-service constraints. An inflation-based algorithm is developed to achieve global optimality by leveraging the monotonic relationship between channel quality and scheduling decisions. Simulations demonstrate faster convergence than benchmarks, competitive sum rates, and higher detection probability against spoofing attacks, which provides a practical solution for secure WPFC deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On NOMA Short Packet THz Communications with Misalignment Error and Hardware Impairment.
abstract: Short packet communication (SPC) has gained increasing attention due to the demand for ultra-reliable and lowlatency applications such as the Internet-of-Things, Industry 4.0, and unmanned aerial vehicles. Unlike long-packet systems, SPC must transmit small data payloads quickly while ensuring high reliability, making it suitable for time-critical services. In this context, misalignment errors (ME) and transceiver hardware impairments (THI) have a stronger impact, as short blocklengths offer limited error correction capability. Ignoring these effects can significantly degrade system reliability and latency. This paper analyzes SPC performance in non-orthogonal multiple access systems over THz channels under diverse fading conditions while accounting for ME and THI. Novel probability density and cumulative distribution function expressions are derived using the Fox's H-function. Key performance metrics, including block error rate and delay outage rate, are evaluated for fixed and optimized antenna array configurations. The results show that antenna array optimization provides noticeable performance gains, and the analytical findings are validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Lightweight Dual-Level Fusion Network for MIMO Automatic Modulation Recognition.
abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWN) operate in untrusted open environments, making them vulnerable to malicious attacks. However, automatic modulation recognition (AMR) can identify the modulation schemes of unknown signals, thereby detecting illegal interference and safeguarding the security of wireless communication environments. Although deep learning (DL) has significantly improved AMR performance, research on its application in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems remains limited, and existing fusion strategies are confined to single fusion approaches. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a lightweight dual-level fusion network (LDLFN) architecture. The framework innovatively incorporates a depthwise separable convolution module to process signals from each receiving antenna in parallel, generating antenna-level feature representations and preliminary classification decisions. Subsequently, joint feature fusion and preliminary decision fusion are performed across antennas. Finally, the feature fusion results are combined with the preliminary decisions through a secondary fusion step to output a highly robust modulation classification outcome. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces computational cost by 60% and parameters by 25% compared to Triple-Skip Residual Neural Network (TRNN), while achieving an average accuracy improvement of 2.58%.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Matrix-Inversion-Free Expectation Propagation for Massive Connectivity.
abstract: This paper presents expectation propagation-conjugate gradient (EP-CG), a novel matrix-inversion-free EP framework designed for activity detection in massive connectivity scenarios. Conventional EP requires repeated inversions of large covariance matrices, becoming computationally prohibitive as the number of devices increases. In contrast, EP-CG computes the posterior mean via a few preconditioned CG iterations and estimates the required marginal variances using a Hutchinson diagonal estimator with Rademacher probe vectors. This approach reduces the cost per-iteration from$\mathcal{O}\left(N^{3}\right)$to$\mathcal{O}(U L N R)$. By demonstration, we further theoretically specify the number of probe vectors required to achieve a desired level of estimation accuracy. Numerical results confirm our analysis: EP-CG achieves detection accuracy comparable to standard EP with a remarkable complexity reduction, even when the number of users is very large.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Analysis of Localization and CoMP Transmission Performance in Integrated Sensing and Communication Networks.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology enables high-resolution sensing and high data rate communication through shared hardware, becoming a key enabler for future networks. However, this integration disrupts traditional system architecture, requiring coordination of sensing and communication under resource constraints and a unified framework to characterize their coupling. In this work, we propose a stochastic geometry-based modeling and performance evaluation framework for ISAC networks, where users and roadside units (RSUs) are modeled as a Matérn cluster process. Users send data to intra-cluster RSUs, which estimate and return the Cramér-Rao lower bound for localization performance evaluation. Upon successful localization, RSUs transmit data via coordinated multipoint, and the conditional communication coverage probability is evaluated. The overall performance is then derived using conditional probability and validated through simulations and numerical analysis.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Diffusion-Based DAG Service Orchestration in Multi-UAV-Enabled Edge Computing.
abstract: The growing demand for computation intensive and delay sensitive services has placed stringent orchestration requirement on mobile edge networks. Aerial Base Stations (ABSs), realized via Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), provide flexible coverage and enable efficient task offloading. However, dynamic network topology, terminal heterogeneity and complex task dependencies hinder optimal offloading and resource allocation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DDM, a distributed diffusion model for efficient service orchestration. Specifically, DDM represents interdependent service with Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) structure, facilitating tasks parallel execution. A diffusion-enhanced distributed Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework is also developed enabling adaptive task offloading. In addition, a convex optimization scheme for resource allocation scheme is incorporated to ensure fairness among edge servers. Experiment results show that DDM enhances 7.4 % transmission rate and 15.7 % system load balance while reducing 27.3 % service completion time compared with advanced baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MVX-ADF: A Dual-Stream Attention Framework for Multi-Modal Fusion in V2X Cooperative Perception.
abstract: Single-vehicle 3D perception struggles with occlusion and limited field-of-view. Despite the theoretical potential of multi-modal fusion and vehicle-infrastructure cooperation, the real-world constraints like asynchronous data and limited bandwidth hinder effective integration. We propose MVX-ADF, a novel MVX two-stage-based attention dual-stream fusion framework for collaborative perception. The core contributions are: 1) a Hierarchical Cross-Modal Attention (HCMA) module that adaptively fuses LiDAR and camera features within a two-stage detector at both proposal and refinement stages; and 2) a Delayed Feature Synchronization (DFS) strategy for efficient object-level fusion that explicitly handles temporal asynchrony and bandwidth constraints.
