On the DAIR-V2X dataset, MVX-ADF achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming single-modality and multi-modal baselines, with cooperative AP-3D of 58.41\%, while maintaining robustness under asynchronous conditions. This work provides an effective framework for practical V2X collaborative perception.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Tdgcn-Based Mobile Multiuser Physical-Layer Authentication for EI-Enabled IIoT.
abstract: Physical-Layer Authentication (PLA) offers endogenous security, lightweight implementation, and high reliability, making it a promising complement to upper-layer security methods in Edge Intelligence (EI)-empowered Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). However, state-of-the-art Channel State Information (CSI)-based PLA schemes face challenges in recognizing mobile multi-users due to the constantly shifting CSI distributions with user movements. To address this issue, we propose a Temporal Dynamic Graph Convolutional Network (TDGCN)-based PLA scheme, which employs Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to capture the spatio-temporal dynamics induced by user movements. Firstly, we partition CSI fingerprints into multivariate time series and utilize dynamic GNNs to capture their associations. Secondly, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) handle temporal dependencies within each CSI fingerprint dimension. Additionally, Dynamic Graph Isomorphism Networks (GINs) and cascade node clustering pooling further enable efficient information aggregation and reduced computational complexity. Simulations demonstrate the proposed scheme's superior authentication accuracy compared to seven baseline schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Permutation-Based Obfuscation for Secure Space Shift Keying in MIMO Systems.
abstract: A computationally secure physical-layer obfuscation framework is proposed for arbitrary multi-input multi-output systems, leveraging channel reciprocity in time-division duplexing operation. At each channel coherence interval, the transmitter and legitimate receiver independently estimate per-antenna fading powers and generate an identical permutation vector to reorder the constellation matrix. This implicitly refreshed key removes the need for explicit key exchange and adds negligible signaling overhead, while forcing an eavesdropper with an independent channel realization to decode using a mismatched constellation. This mismatch increases detection complexity, expanding the brute-force search space on the order of the factorial of the number of transmit antennas. This renders blind constellation recovery computationally infeasible. For analytical tractability, perfect channel state information is assumed, providing an upper performance bound; in practice, estimation errors and calibration mismatches may slightly reduce reliability while further hindering the eavesdropper. A complete system model is developed, and reliability and security are evaluated using average bit error rate, constellation-constrained mutual information, capacity benchmarks, information leakage, and equivocation. The framework is demonstrated with the space shift keying scheme and validated via analysis and Monte Carlo simulations. Results confirm that permutation-based obfuscation preserves link quality for legitimate users while substantially degrading the eavesdropper's ability to infer transmitted data.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Testbed Evaluation of AI-Based Precoding in Distributed MIMO Systems.
abstract: Distributed MIMO (D-MIMO) has emerged as a key architecture for future sixth-generation (6G) networks, enabling cooperative transmission across spatially distributed access points (APs). However, most existing studies rely on idealized channel models and lack hardware validation, leaving a gap between algorithmic design and practical deployment. Meanwhile, recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-driven precoding have shown strong potential for learning nonlinear channel-to-precoder mappings, but their real-world deployment remains limited due to challenges in data collection and model generalization. This work presents a framework for implementing and validating an AI-based precoder on a D-MIMO testbed with hardware reciprocity calibration. A pre-trained graph neural network (GNN)-based model is fine-tuned using real-world channel state information (CSI) collected from the Techtile platform and evaluated under both interpolation and extrapolation scenarios before end-to-end validation. Experimental results demonstrate a$15.7 \%$performance gain over the pre-trained model in the multi-user case after fine-tuning, while in the single-user scenario the model achieves nearmaximum ratio transmission (MRT) performance with less than 0.7 bits/channel use degradation out of a total throughput of 5.19 bits/channel use on unseen positions. Further analysis confirms the data efficiency of real-world measurements, showing consistent gains with increasing training samples, and end-to-end validation verifies coherent power focusing comparable to MRT.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enhancing Capacity in Mixed Traffic: Delay-Aware Control Gain Adjustment Strategy.
abstract: With the rising prevalence of Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) in transportation systems, the demand for advanced traffic management strategies has surged. However, the influence of communication delays on traffic characteristics and capacity remains insufficiently explored. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a mixed-traffic flow model that explicitly integrates communication delays and examines their interaction with control gains through systematic quantitative analysis. The results reveal that communication delays negatively affect traffic capacity, and a critical delay threshold is identified, beyond which CAVs lose their traffic flow advantages over HumanDriven Vehicles (HDVs). Additionally, the influence of control gains on road capacity is quantitatively examined, and an optimization strategy for dynamically adjusting control gains based on communication delays is proposed. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and strategy, offering insights for improving traffic capacity in mixed-traffic environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization for Active ND-RIS-Assisted DFRC Systems with Movable Antenna Arrays.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a key enabling technology for future 6 G networks by allowing radar sensing and wireless communication to coexist within a unified framework. In this paper, we investigate an active non-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (ND-RIS)-assisted dual-functional radar-communication (DFRC) system aided by a movable antenna (MA) array at the base station (BS). By jointly exploiting the electromagnetic flexibility of active ND-RIS and the spatial adaptability introduced by MA positioning, the proposed architecture enables enhanced control over both signal propagation and spatial beamforming. We formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the minimum radar beampattern gain subject to user signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirements, BS transmit power constraints, active RIS amplification limits, and physical antenna separation constraints. The resulting problem is highly non-convex due to the coupled design variables and hardware-induced constraints. To address this challenge, an alternating optimization framework is developed, where the transmit covariance matrix, active ND-RIS reflection matrix, and MA positions are optimized iteratively using semidefinite relaxation, quadratically constrained quadratic programming, and successive convex approximation techniques. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed MA-assisted active ND-RIS framework significantly outperforms conventional passive RIS and fixed-position antenna baselines in terms of radar beam-pattern sharpness, communication robustness, and sensing-communication trade-offs, highlighting its potential for next-generation ISAC systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dynamic Server Allocation Under Stochastic Switchover on Time-Varying Links.
abstract: Dynamic resource allocation to parallel queues is a cornerstone of network scheduling, yet classical solutions often fail when accounting for the overhead of switching delays to queues with superior link conditions. In particular, system performance is further degraded when switching delays are stochastic and inhomogeneous. In this domain, the myopic, Max-Weight policy struggles, as it is agnostic to switching delays. This paper introduces Adaptive Channel and switch-aware Index (ACI), a non-myopic, frame-based scheduling framework that directly amortizes these switching delays. We first use a Lyapunov drift analysis to prove that backlog-driven ACI is throughputoptimal with respect to a scaled capacity region; then validate ACI's effectiveness on multi-UAV networks with an Free-Space Optical (FSO) backhaul. Finally, we demonstrate how adapting its core urgency metric provides the flexibility to navigate the throughput-latency trade-off.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Design of near-ML Performance PAC Codes with Moderate SCL Decoding Complexity.
abstract: The performance of successive cancellation list (SCL) decoding for polar and PAC codes is upper bounded by that of the Maximum-Likelihood (ML) decoder. Notably, as the list size increases, SCL decoding asymptotically approaches ML performance. This raises a key question: what is the minimal list size required to achieve ML performance? While short codes require only moderate list sizes, the required list size may become larger as the code length increases. In this paper, this challenge is addressed from a code design perspective. By leveraging the binary decoding tree enumerating candidate paths and evaluating their Difference to True Path Metric (DTPM), we propose a novel frozen bit selection method that ensures that near-ML performance is achieved with practical list sizes while maintaining good distance properties.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Online Client Association and Adaptive Modulation in Hierarchical Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving training, but it often suffers from substantial communication delay. Hierarchical FL (HFL) mitigates this by inserting edge servers (ESs) between clients and cloud servers. Prior HFL work typically optimizes global accuracy under idealized assumptions of reliable links and perfect knowledge of communication and computation capabilities. These assumptions overlook noisy links, where symbol errors corrupt model updates, and the coupling between client association and modulation in online settings. This work aims to minimize the number of training rounds via joint, online control of (i) client-ES association and (ii) perclient adaptive modulation-mode selection. The central challenge is twofold. First, to make effective association decisions under unknown, time-varying computation and channel conditions. Second, to balance upload speed against reliability. We propose BiBandit-HFL, an online algorithm that casts the problem as coupled bandits: a multi-player multi-armed bandits for client-ES association and a per-client multi-armed bandits for modulationmode selection. Simulation results show that BiBandit-HFL has faster convergence compared with online baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Diffusion Model - Assisted Task-Oriented Semantic Communication with DRL-Based Resource Optimization.
abstract: This paper presents a task-oriented semantic communication network (TOSCN) that integrates the Task-Oriented Channel Denoiser (TOCD), a diffusion-model-based module designed to enhance the semantic robustness of transmitted features. By adaptively adjusting the number of denoising steps, TOCD balances the latency-accuracy trade-off, improving task performance under poor channel conditions while minimizing redundant computation in favorable environments. We formulate a joint optimization problem of bandwidth, transmit power, and denoising time to maximize long-term transmission efficiency and model it as a Markov decision process (MDP). A deep reinforcement learning (DRL)–based resource allocation scheme is then developed to learn adaptive policies that allocate resources according to real-time channel states, buffer conditions, and accuracy requirements. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms both DRL baselines and greedy allocation methods across multiple accuracy constraints. The results confirm that combining diffusion-based denoising with DRL-driven optimization achieves robust, accuracy-aware, and resource-efficient task-oriented communication, offering a promising direction for next-generation intelligent wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Reverse-Path-Aware Multicast Optimization in BATMAN-adv for HaLow Mesh Networks.
abstract: Multicast forwarding in wireless mesh networks is often bandwidth-inefficient and unreliable over low-rate links such as IEEE 802.11ah (HaLow). BATMAN-adv, a Layer-2 Mesh Routing Protocol, handles multicast by either flooding packets or converting them into multiple unicasts. While effective in high-rate networks, these approaches create severe redundancy and congestion in constrained environments. We propose a reverse-path-aware multicast optimization for BATMAN-adv that transmits multicast packets as broadcasts and selectively rebroadcasts them only when a node lies on the reverse routing path. This design leverages BATMAN-adv's Originator Message (OGM) based routing state for forwarding decisions without adding control overhead. Testbed experiments over HaLow network show up to 90% reduction in broadcast overhead in dense topologies while maintaining high delivery ratios. To enhance performance under loss-prone links, we also include an optional lightweight redundancy mechanism that duplicates multicast packets at the source, improving reliability for real-time traffic without retransmissions or protocol modifications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: GSERB: A Novel Attention-Integrated Ghost Residual Block for Enhanced DoA Estimation.
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight neural architecture for efficient direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation, built upon a novel Ghost Squeeze-and-Excitation Residual Block (GSERB). The proposed block integrates Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention directly into the Ghost feature generation process, enabling selective channel enhancement while minimizing redundant feature computation. Unlike conventional attentionaugmented convolutional networks, the GSERB amplifies informative ghost feature channels prior to fusion with intrinsic representations, thereby improving feature discrimination and representational efficiency. Experimental results showcase that this integration enhances the model’s ability to capture spatial–spectral dependencies while maintaining a compact design. The resulting network, named GSERB-DoANet, achieves an effective balance between accuracy, scalability, and computational efficiency for real-time multi-source DoA estimation in wireless sensing applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RL-Driven Congestion Control in SDN-NDN.
abstract: While Named Data Networking (NDN) enables in-network caching and multipath retrieval, native adaptive multipath often generates redundant traffic, and NLSR (NamedData Link-State Routing)-based best-route forwarding is cacheunaware and control-intensive. Moreover, when the content catalogue far exceeds cache capacity, frequent evictions lead to persistent upstream fetches and residual congestion. In this paper, we address congestion-aware routing for Software-Defined NDN (SDN-NDN). We model the problem as a congestion-weighted Multi-Commodity Flow Problem (MCFP) with capacity and demand constraints, reformulate it as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), and propose a centralized reinforcement-learning (RL)-based flow-splitting scheme at the SDN controller. The RL policy leverages the controller's global view and content-map-derived cache signals to allocate traffic across a small set of candidate paths, while a one-shot capacity-projection step ensures feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RL approach consistently improves delay, throughput, and cache-hit ratio compared with native multipath and bestroute strategies, approaching the performance of an offline optimal benchmark while maintaining low control overhead and controlled parallelism.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning-Based Zak-OTFS Receiver with Embedded and Interleaved Pilots.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based receiver architecture for joint input-output (I/O) relation estimation and signal detection in Zak transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) systems. Embedded and interleaved pilot frames are considered, where pilot and data symbols coexist in a given frame and interfere with each other. A fully-connected deep neural network (DNN) is trained to jointly learn the effective delay-Doppler (DD) channel and optimize detection performance as a single task. The proposed deep learning approach is found to effectively handle inter-symbol interference and achieve better bit error rate performance compared to conventional methods that perform the channel estimation and signal detection tasks separately. Even with reduced guard region overhead in embedded pilot frames (high throughput and increased interference), the proposed receiver is found to deliver robust performance, while traditional techniques perform poorly. Further, the deep learning-based receiver is shown to work effectively with interleaved pilot frames, which offer the benefits of increased throughput (due to no guard region between pilot and data) and reduced peak-to-average power ratio.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: HQ-CNN: Hybrid Quantum-CNN for Precise Radio-Based Indoor Tracking in mmWave Networks.
abstract: Radio-based indoor localization is vital for the Internet of Things (IoT) applications such as smart healthcare. However, existing methods often require intrusive infrastructure or lack sufficient resolution for through-wall tracking. To address this, we propose a hybrid quantum-convolutional neural network-based framework (HQ-CNN) for high-precision localization in massive MIMO environments. The primary motivation for exploiting quantum-inspired techniques is to reduce model size and computational overhead through quantum data encoding, which is essential for resource-constrained IoT devices. Accordingly, the framework first extracts temporal channel state information, such as angle of arrival (AoA), to generate dynamic Angle-Delay Profiles (ADPs), capturing interactions with both static and moving objects. A generative adversarial network (GAN)-based frame prediction is employed for noise suppression and ADP refinement. The core innovation lies in the integration of a hybrid quantum-CNN, which improves learning from high-dimensional ADPs while maintaining low computational and memory overhead on a traditional GPU-based computer. Evaluations on DeepMIMO show the framework outperforms baselines in scalability and competes with their accuracy. This work demonstrates the potential of hybrid quantum-classical technologies for precise radio-based tracking.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Optimizing Erasure Coding and Node Allocation for Blockchain Storage: A Guided Decomposition Approach.

title: Toward Generalizable Device Identification with Radio Frequency Fingerprint.
abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprint (RFF) is a widely investigated methodology for identifying wireless devices. It refers to unique signal characteristics caused by hardware imperfections in a device's radio front-end. While deep learning models have shown strong performance in classifying known devices using RFF, they struggle to generalize to unseen devices. It often produces overlapping and cluttered feature representations. In this work, we propose using the FlexiPrint framework with a contrastive center loss to extract features from any new devices and cluster them. We conduct experiments on a dataset of 25 devices transmitting Wi-Fi signals. We train different supervised models using 20 devices for comparison. We then test those models on the remaining 5 devices and show that our proposed approach can extract features from the unknown devices beyond the training set with a Silhouette clustering score of 0.6209, which is significantly higher than the baseline model with a score of 0.0441. We also visualize the learned features using t-SNE, which further confirms the improved clustering of device features, demonstrating the potential generalizability to new devices.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Misalignment-Induced Fading Mitigation for Buoy-To-Uav Fso Link Using Angular Diversity Receiver.
abstract: This paper considers a sea-surface buoy-toUnmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) free space optical (FSO) system impacted by the hovering of the UAV and random surface waves. The probability density function (PDF) of the channel fading coefficient under link misalignment is derived. To address the misalignment issues, a novel angular diversity receiver (ADR)assisted FSO system is introduced, which leverages multiple PDs and a selection combining (SC) technique. The proposed system exploits ADR's angular diversity to maximise diversity gain and reduce fading. Using the derived PDF, the results for the outage probability with SC are presented. This quantifies the performance enhancement offered by the system. Numerical results confirm the proposed diversity system's superior performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Quantized-Echo Detection Framework for Deceptive Jamming in Wireless Sensing Systems.
abstract: Deceptive jamming poses a critical threat to wireless sensing systems by intercepting and replaying deceptive echoes that mimic legitimate target returns, causing conventional Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detectors to fail. Existing countermeasures either rely on low-noise conditions or require multiple antennas and specialized waveforms, limiting their applicability in resource-constrained single-echo scenarios where target scattering coefficients are unknown. This paper proposes the Quantization Artifact Test (QAT), a detection framework that exploits the high-order harmonics and spectral discontinuities introduced by the 1-bit quantization process inherent to lowcost jammers. QAT is formulated as a Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) that estimates unknown scattering gains and noise power via maximum likelihood, comparing the resulting test statistic against a threshold calibrated to the desired false-alarm rate. Simulation results demonstrate that QAT achieves higher detection probabilities as compared to feature-based schemes across varying jamming strengths. The proposed method provides a computationally efficient solution for deceptive jamming detection without requiring additional hardware resources.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Carrier Frequency Offset Robust Beam Tracking Scheme in Coordinated Multi-Point ISAC Systems.
abstract: Coordinated multi-point (CoMP) offers substantial enhancements for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. However, oscillator mismatches among base stations result in carrier frequency offsets (CFOs), which degrade system performance. This paper investigates the impact of CFO on CoMP-enabled ISAC systems and proposes a robust beam tracking scheme to mitigate these effects. Specifically, closedform expressions for both the achievable communication and radar estimation rates are derived to facilitate a quantitative assessment of CFO-induced performance loss. Based on this analysis, a multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) ISAC beam tracking problem that aims at maximize the communication rate subject to radar estimation constraints is formulated. To address the high complexity of convex optimization, this problem is reformulated and solved using a combination of Riemannian manifold optimization and conjugate gradient algorithms. Simulation results validate that the proposed algorithm significantly enhances the robustness of both communication and sensing performance in the presence of CFOs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Room-Level Localization in Multistory Buildings via Multimodal Adaptive M-Estimation with LoRa.
abstract: Long-Range (LoRa) technology offers low-power, cost-effective, and long-range connectivity, making it an attractive solution for large-scale deployments. However, achieving indoor location at room level in complex multi-story buildings using a sparse LoRa infrastructure remains a significant challenge for scalable IoT applications. Existing LoRa-based methods often struggle with severe multipath effects and non-line-ofsight (NLOS) propagation. This paper presents a multimodal adaptive M-estimation method that fuses the time difference of arrival (TDoA) and the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) to address these challenges. The method employs an obstruction-aware multi-loss propagation model to interpret RSSI measurements, accounting for structural obstructions and Fresnel-zone shadowing. An iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) algorithm with Cauchy loss and modality-specific median absolute deviation-based scale estimation dynamically reweights TDoA and RSSI measurements to suppress NLOS and multipath outliers. This adaptive fusion mechanism enables robust position estimation by leveraging the geometric constraints of TDoA along with the fine-grained spatial variability captured by the obstruction-aware RSSI model. Extensive real-world evaluations in multistory buildings demonstrate that the method achieves reliable localization with limited infrastructure, delivers high roomlevel accuracy, and outperforms existing baselines. The method also exhibits consistent cross-building performance, robustness to packet loss, and near real-time computational efficiency, confirming its practicality for large-scale IoT deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: 5GC-Bench: A Framework for Stress-Testing and Benchmarking 5G Core VNFs.
abstract: The disaggregated, cloud-native design of the 5G Core (5GC) enables flexibility and scalability but introduces significant challenges. Control-plane procedures involve complex interactions across multiple Virtual Network Functions (VNFs), while the user plane must sustain diverse and resource-intensive traffic. Existing tools often benchmark these dimensions in isolation, rely on synthetic workloads, or lack visibility into fine-grained resource usage. This paper presents 5GC-Bench, a modular framework for stress-testing the 5GC under realistic workloads. 5GC-Bench jointly emulates signaling and service traffic, supporting both VNF profiling and end-to-end service-chain analysis. By characterizing bottlenecks and resource demands, it provides actionable insights for capacity planning and performance optimization. We integrated 5GC-Bench with the OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5GC and deployed it on a real 5G testbed, demonstrating its ability to uncover resource constraints and expose cross-VNF dependencies under scenarios that mirror operational 5G deployments. To foster reproducibility and further research, we release publicly all the artifacts.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Deep and Transfer Learning Approach for Handover Management in O-RAN.
abstract: Despite advancements in the Open-Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture and its applications, handover management remains an open problem without a comprehensive methodology for orchestrating seamless cell transitions within the O-RAN context. Existing predictive handover algorithms have not been designed inherently with scalability in mind, which is crucial for large-scale cellular networks where a Radio Intelligent Controller (RIC) can manage multiple distributed cells. In addition, their static model architectures limit adaptability to dynamic RAN topologies, making them irresponsive and impractical for real-world deployments. To address these challenges, we propose an O-RAN-compliant algorithm with an adaptive and flexible design that can be implemented as an xApp in the Near-Real-Time RIC to facilitate high-accuracy predictive handover decisions. We demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art predictive handover methods, achieving over 95 % classification accuracy in large-scale networks while reducing the number of handovers by 46 % compared to the standard 3GPP handover algorithm. Moreover, it adapts effectively to dynamic RAN topologies with a varying number of base stations, requiring at least 30 % less retraining time while maintaining high accuracy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Study on Synchronization of Multi-Modal Services Over 5G: From Application Layer to RAN.
abstract: Emerging multi-modal services (MMS) integrate time-aligned video, audio, and haptic flows, requiring tightly inter-flow synchronization for good user experience. While the 5QI framework of 5G offers low-latency quality of service (QoS) via packet delay budget (PDB), it remains unclear if default PDBs sufficient for MMS needs. Specifically, synchronization loss between two real-time communication media components in the same MMS, as defined in 3GPP TS 26.113, is hard to measure at the radio access network (RAN). This paper identifies how RAN queuing causes synchronization loss, proposes measurable shortterm and long-term synchronization loss metrics, denoted as STSL and LTSL respectively, and shows why current mechanisms may fail to meet the synchronization thresholds in 3GPP TR 22.847. To bridge this gap, we proposes the Synchronization-Aware Windowed Delay-based Proportional Fair (SAW-DPF) scheduler, which leverages two parameters currently under discussion in 3GPP: Multi-modal Service ID (MMSID) to group related QoS flows, and synchronization thresholds (SyncTh) to bound LTSL and STSL between two QoS flows. SAW-DPF adjusts flow weights to keep inter-flow delay differences within SyncTh, while ensuring fairness with background traffic. In simulations with one MMS and heavy background traffic, The SAW-DPF cuts LTSL from around 40 ms to under 10 ms and eliminates STSL violations exceeding 20 ms, outperforming the legacy delay-proportional fair (DPF) scheduler which lacks synchronization awareness.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On the Performance of Cognitive RSMA-Enabled Large-Scale MEC Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we consider a cognitive rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) scheme for uplink large-scale cellular mobile edge computing (MEC) scenarios, where coexisting cellular user equipments (UEs) and internet of things (IoT) sensor devices (SDs) offload computation tasks to MEC access points (MAPs). This scheme enables multi-user transmission to adapt to channel conditions and interference levels by splitting computation tasks and adjusting the corresponding power allocation. Under the uplink Poisson cellular network model, we derive the expression for the average rate successful transmission probability (RSTP) using a stochastic geometry-based approach. We then obtain the average overall latency of completing offloaded tasks via queueing theory. Simulation results validate the accuracy of our analytical derivations. The results further demonstrate that the cognitive RSMA scheme outperforms the benchmark nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme in terms of both average RSTP and latency performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: An Entropy-Driven Gradient Variance Attack on Automatic Modulation Classification.
abstract: Deep learning-based automatic modulation classification (AMC) systems have been widely studied, recent studies demonstrate their vulnerability to adversarial attacks. However, in practical wireless communication scenarios, such attacks often fail due to channel-induced perturbation distortion and poor transferability in multi-user heterogeneous scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose an Entropy-Driven Variance Gradient Sign Method (EVGSM) for effective adversarial attacks. Our approach integrates a diversity loss term with the cross-entropy loss to form an Entropy-Diversity Balanced Loss (EDBL), preventing adversarial samples from converging to the trivial solutions under channel fading. Simultaneously, a Momentum-based Gradient Variance Tuning (MGVT) mechanism enhances gradient exploration diversity, mitigating fading effects and improving transferability across diverse scenarios. Empirical evidence demonstrates that EVGSM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in wireless environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low-Overhead CSI Feature for Fingerprint Localization.
abstract: We develop a low-overhead Channel State Information (CSI) feature that enables to reveal the physical geometry of a Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) environment with more accuracy than with the Channel Impulse Response (CIR). The proposed feature is based on statistical and representative information contained in the CIR, as well as Time Difference of Arrival (TDoA) information. In addition, we devise the CSI feature such that the required communication overhead and computational complexity, for applications such as localization, are lower compared to using the CIR. To that end, the proposed feature is used for fingerprint localization and compared with other state-of-the-art features. Simulation results show that the proposed feature, which reduces the communication overhead by 98.05% compared to using the CIR, achieves sub-meter localization accuracy, which is comparable to or higher than that of other state-of-the-art features with higher overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Qudit Selection for Amplitude Damping Quantum Channel.
abstract: Amplitude-damping (AD) noise, which models energy relaxation and spontaneous decay, is a dominant source of decoherence in quantum systems such as atoms, ions, photonics, and superconducting qubits. While the qubit (two-level) AD channel has been extensively analyzed, its generalization to higherdimensional systems (qudits) remains less explored despite their practical relevance. This paper develops a systematic framework to evaluate and compare the performance of qubits and qudits under amplitude-damping noise. Closed-form expressions are derived for several fidelity measures, including computational basis, equal superposition, and Haar-average fidelities. We then numerically estimate the single-letter coherent information$Q_{1}$as a lower bound on the quantum capacity. A normalized performance score combining fidelity and capacity is proposed to identify optimal qudit dimensions across different damping probabilities. Simulation results reveal that higher-dimensional systems can outperform qubits in low-noise regimes, while qubits remain more robust under strong damping. The resulting “recommendation map” offers practical guidance for the experimental selection of qudit dimension in amplitude-damping environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Digital Twin Predictive Csi for Downlink Miso-Noma: a Lstm-Driven Ppo Approach.
abstract: We study digital twin (DT)-assisted downlink multiple-input single-output (MISO) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) control under time-correlated fading and imperfect channel state information (CSI). A DT tracks the geometry of user equipment (UE) and provides an imperfect CSI history, from which a two-layer long short-term memory (LSTM) network predicts the one-step-ahead CSI. A proximal policy optimization (PPO) controller observes the used CSI (imperfect or predicted), UE locations, and previous-slot rates, and outputs beam directions with a softmax power split; minimum-rate and successive interference cancellation (SIC) requirements are handled as soft penalties, while all rates and SIC checks are computed on the true physical CSI. In evaluation, DT-enabled control achieves a mean episode return of an 8.10 % improvement against the DTdisabled baseline, alongside a substantially lower CSI mismatch.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Networked ISAC for 3D Air-Corridor: Joint UAV Trajectory and Beamforming Design.
abstract: This paper investigates air-corridor-constrained UAV trajectory planning and beamforming optimization for networked integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with distributed ground base stations (GBSs). A single UAV flies within a predefined air-corridor while receiving cooperative downlink communication from multiple distributed GBSs, which simultaneously conduct sensing over a designated monitoring airspace. A joint optimization problem is formulated to maximize the long-term average communication rate of the UAV subject to power limitations, point-wise sensing energy requirements, UAV kinematic constraints, and strict air-corridor compliance. To address the strong coupling and non-convexity between the UAV trajectory and the ISAC beamforming design, we develop a constrained proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework. For a fixed trajectory, cooperative communication and sensing beamforming are optimized via semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and fractional programming (FP). The UAV trajectory optimization is structured as a nested process. A PPO-based reinforcement learning outer loop for policy guidance is tightly integrated with an inner loop of beamforming, which integrates the air-corridor constraints into the decision process. Numerical results verify that the proposed air-corridor-constrained ISAC design substantially enhances the UAV's average communication rate compared with benchmark schemes, demonstrating its effectiveness for environment-adaptive ISAC in distributed low-altitude networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enabling Reliable and Scalable Urban Air Mobility Communications Through 6G Network Slicing.
abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) is emerging as a cornerstone of next-generation transportation, relying on seamless, reliable, and high-throughput wireless connectivity for both safety-critical and passenger-oriented services. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the feasibility of enabling UAM communications through future 6 G Terrestrial Network (TN) leveraging network slicing. Dedicated slices are envisioned for safety-critical Command and Control (C2) communications, onboard passenger services, and terrestrial users, each with tailored resource allocation and quality-of-service guarantees. A comprehensive performance analysis is carried out to assess the coexistence of aerial and ground links under diverse traffic loads, user densities, and transmission conditions, demonstrating the capacity of 6 G networks to sustain C 2 communications while balancing resource efficiency for non-C2 and terrestrial services. These findings provide valuable insights for the design of scalable, slice-aware 6 G architectures capable of supporting the coexistence of aerial and terrestrial communications in future UAM ecosystems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Modelling Quantum Networking with Teleportation.
abstract: We present a simple teleportation-based quantum internet framework with a centralized server architecture. Our model formalizes qubit transfer protocols while using stochastic differential equations to capture entanglement decoherence under both Markovian and non-Markovian noise. We quantify key performance metrics-entanglement generation rate, throughput, and security-validating our predictions through Qiskit simulations. The modular design addresses critical quantum networking challenges: fidelity-latency trade-offs, scalable entanglement distribution, and eavesdropping resilience. Future extensions incorporate multi-hop topologies with quantum repeaters and fault-tolerant error correction, establishing a foundation for scalable quantum networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DRL-Based Coupling-Aware Secure S-UAV System Leveraging Collaborative Beamforming.
abstract: Small-sized UAVs (S-UAVs) face challenges in secure, energy-efficient data transfer due to limited energy and eavesdropping threats. We propose a collaborative beamforming (CB) system where multiple S-UAVs form a Virtual Antenna Array (VAA) to beamform data to an Edge Server (ES) while nullsteering eavesdroppers, explicitly accounting for mutual coupling (MC) in close formations. The optimization problem of VAA formation is addressed using Multi Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning - Transformer with Bagging(MADRL-T+B), which integrates a Transformer encoder and critic bagging. Simulations study the effect of inter-S-UAV spacing, and path loss on the system and shows the effectiveness of MADRL-T+B algorithm over existing methods in secrecy rate, and energy efficiency, achieving a 5.6 % average improvement in scalability and an average 21 % increase in training stability under high numbers of S-UAVs, and low SNR, respectively.

title: Lightweight Neural Network Distillation for Real-Time CAN Bus Intrusion Detection in Vehicles.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A THz with VLC Assisted ISAC System Under the Impact of Human Blockages.
abstract: The terahertz (THz) and visible light communication (VLC) technologies are poised to become key enablers of sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks due to their ability to support ultra-high data rates and broad spectrum availability. This work investigates a THz-access point (THz-AP) with VLC-access point (VLC-AP) assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, specifically under human induced blockages. We begin by formulating the total signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in the THz/VLC-AP enabled hybrid system by selecting the maximum SNR among all available access points (APs). Additionally, we optimize the semi-angle at half power of the VLC-AP to enhance received signal strength and achieve more uniform illumination coverage. Extensive performance evaluations are conducted to examine key metrics such as spectral efficiency (SE), outage probability, average sensing rate, and average communication rate. A 3D visualization of the THz-AP-based sensing process is also presented to illustrate the detectable and non-detectable user locations within the environment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel Algorithm for Automated Service Graph Generation in Cloud/Edge-Native Systems.
abstract: Cloud/edge-native computing is a novel paradigm designed to reduce the deployment, management, and orchestration complexities of monolithic systems. This paradigm breaks down complex systems into a collection of microservices to fulfill applications' requirements and it is becoming popular in 6 G network-based systems, such as in envisioned use cases of mobile immersive reality. When following the cloud/edgenative computing paradigm, the pipeline of immersive reality systems is implemented through a collection of microservices deployed over the cloud/edge continuum. One challenge is to find microservice compositions capable of fulfilling the user's application requirement. This is done by determining the possible collection of microservices composition capable of handling user's demands. While several studies investigated the deployment of microservices and the automated generation of service compositions, less focus has been devoted to the convergence time of designed algorithms, which is critical given the time-sensitive nature of 6 G envisioned use cases. This paper designs a novel algorithm for service composition in edge-native computing. The proposed algorithm implements a memoization component to reduce search space when determining compatibility service graphs. Preliminary results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms traditional depth first search (DFS) by 87 % in terms of processing time while finding the same compatibility service graphs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Spectral Efficiency Analysis of Multi-User Pinching-Antenna Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates a multi-user pinching-antenna (PA) system, where a single PA is activated on each waveguide. With the maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming, the system spectral efficiency (SE) is studied, where the inter-user interference term complicates the analysis of the SE. To overcome this obstacle, the stationary phase point method (SPPM) is applied to obtain an analytically tractable form of the SE. The analysis reveals that the average inter-user interference can be negligible with a large waveguide spacing even using the MRT. This insight makes the simple MRT appealing for PA-based multi-user communications. Finally, the theoretical analysis is verified through simulations. Our numerical results confirm that 1) with the aid of SPPM, the approximation of the system SE is accurate; 2) and while increasing the waveguide spacing helps reduce the average inter-user interference, it might degrade the SE due to the increased signal propagation path loss.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low-Complexity Overlapped Subarrays Based Hybrid Precoding for Beam Squint Mitigation in Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: While the fully－connected architecture delivers superior performance，it incurs substantial hardware costs． The overlapped subarrays（OSA）structure has emerged as a promising analog structure in massive multiple－input multiple－ output（MIMO）systems，significantly reducing the number of phase shifters while maintaining performance close to that of the fully－connected counterpart．This paper presents a low－complexity OSA－based hybrid precoding scheme for multiuser massive MIMO－OFDM systems．By exploiting the subarrays－overlapped properties inherent in the OSA struc－ ture，we develop a residual－canceled block iterative（RC－BI） algorithm that circumvents nonlinear constraints to design the analog precoding．Then，to tackle beam squint－induced performance degradation in wideband systems，we design a subcarrier－agnostic analog precoding initialization and a two－ stage digital precoding scheme．This design effectively mitigates multiuser interference and frequency－selective impairments， ensuring robust performance across the entire OFDM sub－ carrier bandwidth．Numerical results validate that our OSA－ based scheme achieves notable advantages in terms of spectral and energy efficiency than classic structures．The proposed algorithm also significantly mitigates the beam squint and reduces computational complexity than two state－of－the－art hybrid precoding designs．
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Detect Error Performance for Satellite Aerial Terrestrial Integrated Cognitive Networks with NOMA and Non-Ideal Limitations.
abstract: Covert transaction (CT) is the popular topic investigated these years. In this research, we study the CT for the satellite aerial terrestrial integrated cognitive networks (SATICNs), particularly, in order to enhance the spectrum efficiency and resource utilization, cognitive technology and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme are used in the SATICNs to improve the system covert performance. Besides, to consider the practical scenarios, the non-ideal hardware, non-ideal channel estimation and the co-channel interferences are also investigated for the SATICNs. In addition, a new defined detection error probability (DEP) is proposed for the CT of the considered system. Furthermore, by considering these factors, the closed-form expression for the DEP is also obtained. Finally, several representative Monte Carlo simulations are derived to evaluate the impacts of system and channel parameters on the covert system performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Topoedge: Topology-Grounded Agentic Framework for Edge Networking Code Generation and Repair.
abstract: TopoEdge is a topology-grounded, edge-deployable framework for end-to-end software-defined networking (SDN) configuration generation and repair, motivated by the brittleness of configuration artefacts under topology variation and by strict operational constraints on latency, privacy, and on-site execution. TopoEdge represents each target topology as a routerlevel graph and embeds it using a contrastively trained graph neural network (GNN), enabling nearest-neighbour retrieval of a verified reference configuration paired with an executable Python driver (a Topotest/pytest test script that orchestrates the emulated network and checks protocol assertions). The target topology, retrieved reference topology, and reference driver are assembled into a topology-grounded retrieval-augmented generation context (TopoRAG), which grounds a distributed, executioncentric generate-verify-repair loop coordinated by a central controller and realised by three role-specialised agents: (i) a Planning agent that produces a topology-consistent configuration plan and a per-device skeleton; (ii) a Generation agent that materialises executable configuration artefacts, including device configurations and the driver; and (iii) a Verification agent that runs the FRRouting Topotest/pytest harness, compresses failures into a compact trace, and emits localised patch directives for iterative repair.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cooperative MARL and Heterogeneous Onboard Computing for LEO Satellite Routing.
abstract: Routing in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks is challenged by highly dynamic topologies and variable link qualities, particularly impacting latency-sensitive and lossintolerant applications. Conventional routing protocols often fail to adapt effectively to these dynamic conditions. This work presents PM-MAPPO, a novel framework integrating a spatio-temporal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm with a heterogeneous onboard computing architecture utilizing CPU, GPU, and FPGA resources. Specifically, the algorithm leverages a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to process spatial topology, a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) to capture temporal dynamics, and a predictive masking mechanism for forward-looking decisions. Operating under the Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) framework, this allows each satellite, acting as an agent, to make cooperative routing decisions using local observations to jointly optimize network-wide end-to-end delay and packet drop rate. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed PM-MAPPO approach substantially outperforms conventional routing protocols like OSPF. Performance gains include up to a 68.2 % reduction in packet drop rate and approximately 27.6 % lower end-to-end latency, highlighting the solution's effectiveness for dynamic LEO satellite networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: EWM-TOPSIS Based Weighted Graph Pilot Assignment for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks.
abstract: In this paper, a novel weighted graph pilot assignment scheme based on entropy weight method (EWM) and technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) is proposed for cell-free massive multiple-input multipleoutput (CF m-MIMO) networks with user heterogeneity. This is the first pilot assignment work in CF m-MIMO networks subject to multi-dimensional heterogeneity of user equipments (UEs), e.g., mobility speed, activation probability and serving priority. By employing EWM-TOPSIS to assess each UE's contribution to the total spectral efficiency (SE) based on its multi-dimensional heterogeneity, the proposed EWM-TOPSIS based weighted graph pilot assignment (ETWGPA) scheme enables pilot reuse among neighboring UEs with good channel conditions only, while assigning saved orthogonal pilots to neighboring UEs that contribute greatly to the total SE. By characterizing pilot contamination among UEs using multi-criteria of EWM-TOPSIS, i.e., multidimensional heterogeneity of UEs and number of common serving access points between UEs, the proposed ETWGPA scheme constructs a weighted interference graph and assigns the pilot with the least interference to each UE sequentially. Simulation results show that the proposed ETWGPA scheme outperforms the state-of-the-art schemes in terms of SE, energy efficiency, while ensuring higher UE fairness and lower complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Feature Importance-Aware Dual-Branch Coding for Task-Oriented Uav Adaptive Transmission.
abstract: Semantic communication is considered a key enabling technology for 6G. However, in UAV scenarios with limited bandwidth and low SNR, conventional single-branch image transmission cannot effectively balance efficiency and task performance. To overcome this, we propose an importanceaware dual-branch joint source-channel coding (I-DBJSCC) framework for UAV semantic image adaptive transmission. The framework incorporates a dual-branch semantic coding (DBSC) module that employs MobileNet and ViT to extract local precision and global consistency features. A gradient-based task activation mapping (Grad-TAM) mechanism is proposed that leverages task-quality feedback to evaluate feature importance, enabling adaptive prioritization of task-relevant information. To optimize transmission under varying channel conditions, we propose a dual-branch joint semantic-channel transmission (DJSCT) mechanism that collaborates with the I-DBJSCC encoder to adaptively select the transmitted semantic features based on available resources. Furthermore, a dual-branch proximal policy optimization (D-PPO) algorithm is proposed to adjust semantic feature transmission ratios. Experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly improves task-oriented semantic spectral efficiency and achieves substantial gains in image reconstruction quality compared with state-of-the-art baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enhancing RIS-Assisted SWIPT with Extended Null Space and Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: This work exploits the degrees of freedom offered by the null space of the time-varying cascaded channel between the base station and information users (IUs), as mediated by an intermediate reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), to transmit an additional energy signal to energy users (EUs) concurrently with the data transmission to the IUs. Specifically, an extended null space (ENS) based design is proposed for a RISassisted simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system, enabling simultaneous information and energy transfer. The proposed framework formulates a multi-objective optimization problem aiming to jointly maximize the harvested power of the EUs and the data rates of the IUs. To solve this problem, a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm is developed and implemented. Simulation results demonstrate that the DDPG-based ENS design consistently outperforms state-of-the-art SWIPT schemes by improving the IUs' sum-rate and the total equivalent sum-rate (ESR) of the entire system, while maintaining competitive performance for the wireless power transfer.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Task-Oriented Semantic Communication for Satellite Remote Sensing Images with Channel Feedback.
abstract: Remote sensing images play a crucial role in many fields such as military reconnaissance and geological exploration. However, the limited bandwidth of satellite-toground communication channels struggles to support massive data transmission. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a task-oriented semantic communication framework for satellite remote sensing images with channel feedback. The proposed transmission framework includes a semantic feature extraction module, a semantic feature selection module, a joint sourcechannel encoding and decoding module, and a task module. The semantic feature extraction module can effectively extract global context features and local detailed features via transformer block and residual blocks, respectively. The semantic feature selection module can select task-relevant features according to signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) obtained from channel feedback. The joint source channel encoding and decoding modules can further improve the transmission robustness. By transmitting task-relevant semantic features while discarding redundant information, our method significantly improves transmission efficiency while preserving downstream-task performance. The extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves higher classification accuracy than state-of-the-art methods on the NWPU-RESISC45 and AID datasets.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Performance Analysis of zeARIS Communications with Adaptive Gain.
abstract: This paper proposes a zero-energy active reconfigurable intelligent surface (zeARIS) with adaptive gain. By dynamically adjusting the signal amplification gain, the zeARIS overcomes the multiplicative fading effect and prevents outages in wireless energy harvesting, thereby enhancing the performance. The closed-form expressions for the connection outage probability (COP) and secrecy outage probability (SOP) are derived to evaluate the reliability and security, while an asymptotic analysis is conducted to gain further insight. The results show that the COP performance of zeARIS continuously improves as the transmission power of the receiver increases, while it reaches a bottleneck as that of the transmitter increases. Conversely, the SOP performance deteriorates continuously with increasing receiver transmission power, and similarly reaches a bottleneck as the transmitter transmission power rises. Particularly, the reliability of zeARIS consistently surpasses that of the selfpowered RIS with fixed gain.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive RIS Control for Mobile mmWave NLoS Communication Using Single-Bit Feedback.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are emerging as key enablers of reliable industrial automation in the millimeter-wave (mmWave) band, particularly in environments with frequent line-of-sight (LoS) blockage. While prior works have largely focused on theoretical aspects, real-time validation under user mobility remains underexplored. In this work, we propose and experimentally evaluate an adaptive beamforming algorithm that enables RIS reconfiguration via a low-rate feedback link from the mobile user equipment (UE) to the RIS controller, operating without requiring UE position knowledge. The algorithm maintains the received signal power above a predefined threshold using only a single-bit comparison of received power levels. To analyze the algorithm's performance, we establish a simulation-based Monte Carlo (MC) optimization benchmark that assumes full UE position knowledge, accounts for practical hardware constraints, and serves as an upper bound for performance evaluation. Using a hexagonal RIS with 127 elements and 1-bit phase quantization at 23.8 GHz, we validate the proposed approach in a semi-anechoic environment over a$60 \text{cm} \times 92 \text{cm}$area. The results demonstrate that the singlebit feedback-driven algorithm closes much of the performance gap to the MC upper bound while achieving up to 24 dB gain in received power compared to an inactive RIS baseline. These findings highlight the practical potential of feedbackbased adaptive RIS control for robust mmWave non-line-of-sight (NLoS) communication with mobile users.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Scalable Implementation of Adaptive Linear Channel Estimators for OFDM Systems on RF System-on-Chip.
abstract: Accurate channel estimation is essential to establish a reliable wireless connectivity. Traditional estimators such as least squares (LS) offers a low-complexity solution but at the cost of inferior estimation accuracy. Whereas minimum mean square error (MMSE) yields a superior estimate but at the cost of higher complexity. Further, their efficient hardware implementation for real-time baseband processing remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we propose an hardware efficient adaptive channel estimation framework for frame-based orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems, that bridges the performance-complexity trade-off between LS and MMSE estimators. The proposed framework adaptively switches between LS and MMSE estimators based on real-time channel conditions, thereby achieving an optimal balance between estimation accuracy and resource utilization. The framework is implemented on the radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) platform, where we focus on designing custom, AXI4-Stream-compatible cores integrated within the programmable logic (PL) to enable pipelined, high-throughput processing of complex OFDM symbols. Post-synthesis results indicate that the proposed implementation requires approximately 23% less LUTs, 72% less power and 6% lower latency in comparison to MMSE, while delivering the same performance. This hardware-in-the-loop validation confirms the practical viability of the design for future 5G/6G systems, with scalability toward massive MIMO architectures.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Unfolded Hybrid Beamforming for NOMA-Enabled Joint Sensing and Communication.
abstract: We propose integrating Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) into hybrid beamforming (HBF) for JCAS in multi-user scenarios, as an alternative to conventional Spatial Division Multiple Access (SDMA). The framework is analyzed in terms of achievable sum rate, energy efficiency, and beamforming complexity. System performance is optimized for sum rate maximization using Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) and Deep Unfolding-based optimization, and extended to wideband OFDM systems to support practical broadband 6G networks. Results demonstrate that NOMA-assisted HBF effectively balances efficiency, complexity, and sensing capability. The integration of joint communication and sensing in 6 G can thus transform wireless networks into pervasive intelligent infrastructures, enabling both human-centric and machinedriven applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Predictive Handover Optimization Using Hybrid Radio Propagation Modeling for 5G and Beyond.
abstract: Conventional handover events in 5 G NR networks, namely A3 and A5, are reactive in nature, which often leads to ping-pong effects and Handover Failures (HOF) under highmobility conditions, respectively. In this work, we present a novel predictive handover framework that anticipates cell transitions using precomputed, location-specific received signal strength maps. These maps capture the expected ReferenceSignal Received Power (RSRP) for every location in a specific deployment scenario, and such maps can be generated for all standardized deployments. Our RSRP map generation methodology combines (a) ray-casting over clutter data from OpenStreetMap (OSM), (b) custom shadow fading model, (c) stochastic path loss models defined in 3GPP TR 38.901, and (d) a novel application of Gaussian spatial smoothing as a substitute for conventional Layer 3 (L3) filtering. By embedding such maps into decision-making, handovers can be triggered before link quality deteriorates. Our handover algorithm significantly reduces potential HOFs by 88 %, avoids ping-pong events, initiates handovers earlier by a median of 3.3 seconds compared to A5, and maintains minimal link quality degradation under various mobility conditions. Evaluation with Sionna Ray Tracing model under identical environmental and clutter conditions shows that our method and Sionna matched by 84.1 % in potential handover locations. Additionally, our approach identifies valid handover points missed by Sionna and provides wider decision windows, which facilitate error-free operation of the predictive handover algorithm. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to demonstrate that Gaussian smoothed RSRP maps can potentially serve as the basis for efficient proactive handovers in 5 G NR and beyond.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Designing Modulation for Approximate Digital Over-the-Air Computation.
abstract: Over-the-air computation (OAC) computes functions directly over a multiple-access channel (MAC), reducing communication in distributed systems. It exploits the linear superposition of simultaneous transmissions, allowing the receiver to obtain an aggregate (e.g., a sum) in one channel use. In digital OAC, however, the superpositions so far investigated may induce excessive overlappings among the constellation points. Preventing these overlaps requires careful constellation design. In this paper, we study the design of digital modulation for OAC and show that the problem of avoiding overlaps among the received superimposed constellation points-so that distinct function values remain distinguishable-can be equivalently formulated as minimizing the maximum computation error over a heavy-tailed channel noise. We then introduce a simple digital modulation scheme that minimizes the mean computation error under power and noise constraints. Under maximum-likelihood decoding, we construct convex surrogates and solve them via projected-gradient iterations. The framework naturally holds for common noise models (Gaussian, Lomax) and a broad class of symmetric desired functions. Empirical results demonstrate competitive mean-squarederror performance relative to existing digital OAC baselines, while achieving substantially lower computational complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Device-Specific Anomaly Detection Via Transfer Learning in Edge Networks.
abstract: Network anomaly detection is an active research area, with numerous solutions that utilize statistical methods, neural networks, and other machine learning methods. Autoencoders, in particular, have shown great performance by learning representations solely from benign traffic, enabling the detection of zero-day attacks. In this paper, we propose a methodology that uses transfer learning to train autoencoders specifically tailored to individual network devices, thereby improving detection performance over general autoencoder models trained on aggregated network data. Furthermore, benchmarking results indicate that the lightweight device-specific model is suitable for inference on resource-constrained devices, suggesting its feasibility for real-time anomaly detection on edge devices. We compare the device-specific model with the general model by evaluating them against 12 different attack types. The results demonstrate that the proposed method shows promise in improving the anomaly detection performance. The device-specific model outperforms the general model for certain attacks, while achieving similar performance in others.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Joint Rate-Energy Optimization in NOMA BackCom Networks.
abstract: The rapid growth of low-power Internet of things (IoT) devices calls for communication paradigms that jointly ensure spectrum efficiency and energy sustainability. Backscatter communication (BackCom) integrated with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is a promising enabler, but its performance is tightly coupled to realistic energy harvesting (EH) dynamics and the adaptive control of backscatter nodes (BNs). In this paper, we investigate a NOMA based BackCom uplink system, where multiple EH enabled BNs powered by a dedicated continuous-wave (CW) transmitter, operating under a practical non-linear EH model. To effectively balance the achievable data rates and the battery dynamics of the BNs whose stored energy must also support sensing operations, we formulate the problem as a sequential decision-making task and address it using deep reinforcement learning (DRL). By optimizing the BNs reflection coefficients and power-sharing factors in real time, DRL policies learn to sustain battery levels, prevent energy outages, and maximize throughput across dynamic channel and EH conditions. Comparative evaluation of advanced DRL algorithms, including deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), prioritized experience replay DDPG (PER-DDPG), combined experience replay DDPG (CER-DDPG), twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3), proximal policy optimization (PPO), soft actor-critic (SAC), and recurrent soft actor-critic (RSAC), demonstrates that off-policy algorithms achieve faster convergence and superior energy-aware sum-rate performance, while linear EH assumptions significantly overestimate system capabilities. The results highlight that DRL-driven optimization offers a robust pathway to practical, self-sustaining NOMA BackCom networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Task Offloading in 3D Edge Computing Networks.
abstract: Computational offloading in three-dimensional (3D) edge computing networks occurs both horizontally and vertically, enabling simultaneous use of terrestrial and aerial platforms. Selecting optimal nodes and allocating computing and transmission resources for task offloading is NP-hard, particularly when considering task partitioning, replication, and parallel offloading to improve latency and reliability. This paper proposes an evolutionary solution that jointly optimizes task partitioning and replication, node selection, and resource allocation, while accounting for potential failures in computation, bidirectional transmissions, and result fusion at the user device. The proposed approach is evaluated in terms of latency, reliability, energy consumption, and efficiency under varying task dimensions, partition counts, and replica limits. Results show that our solution achieves better tradeoffs between latency, energy consumption, system robustness, and efficiency and outperforms baseline methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Secrecy Communications for Ambient Backscatter Assisted NOMA Systems with Friendly Jamming.
abstract: This paper investigates secrecy communications for an ambient backscatter communication (AmBC) assisted nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system, which consists of a source node, a backscatter device (BD), a pair of near and far users, an eavesdropper (Eve) and a friendly jammer. In particular, the source node serves a pair of NOMA users with the aid of a BD, and the Eve intends to wiretap the confidential message transmitted to users. We propose a friendly jamming based secure transmission scheme under imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC) at both legitimate users and the Eve. To this end, a friendly jammer transmits artificial noise (AN) to the Eve with the aid of the BD. By applying the mathematical tools of Gaussian-Chebyshev quadrature, closed-form expressions for the connection outage probability (COP) and the secrecy outage probability (SOP) of a pair of NOMA users are derived under imperfect SIC, revealing that our friendly jamming scheme improves the transmission performance of NOMA users. Numerical results corroborate the theoretical analysis and confirm that the proposed scheme achieves superior performance compared with existing schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Covert Communications for IRS-Assisted NOMA Networks with Finite Blocklength.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the covert communications in intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks with finite blocklength. In particular, we characterize the worst-case detection performance of the warden (Willie), where the optimal detection threshold is employed by the Willie. Leveraging the gamma distribution and the likelihood-ratio test, the closed-form expression for error detection probability of Willie is derived, and the corresponding optimal detection threshold is obtained. We then develop a resource allocation scheme satisfying the quality-of-service requirement of the legitimate user and the covertness constraint of Willie. Specifically, the phase shifts of the IRS, the power allocation coefficients of users, and the transmission blocklength are jointly optimized to maximize the effective covert throughput (ECT) of the system. Simulation results verify the correctness of our theoretical analysis and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed scheme in terms of the ECT performance compared with the existing scheme.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enhancing 360° Video Streaming with Stream Scheduling Policies Over HTTP/3.
abstract: 360° video streaming is rapidly advancing, with emerging applications in immersive communications envisioned for 6G Networks. However, dynamic user VR navigation (e.g., with head-mounted displays) under variable network conditions remains challenging, leading to severe stalls and quality degradation. In this work, we experimentally evaluate 360° video streaming over state-of-the-art protocols such as HTTP over QUIC, i.e., HTTP/3, focusing on the impact of stream scheduling. We implement and evaluate scheduling policies in two classes: (1) explicit priority, coordinated with QUIC, which dynamically prioritises 360° video tile requests based on temporal and spatial criteria; and (2) implicit priority, confined to the application layer and hidden from QUIC, relying on request order strategies. In realistic experiments with network emulation and 360° user navigation, we observe that explicit priority policies applying temporal criteria to urgent tiles reduce stall time by up to 81 % while maintaining competitive video quality compared to application-only stream scheduling.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Disrupting Multi-Robot Coordination: Strategic Sybil Attack on Exploration Algorithms.
abstract: Cooperative exploration in multi-robot systems is vital for mission-critical tasks such as search and rescue, mine detection, and surveillance. These systems depend on wireless communication, making them susceptible to Sybil attacks, where a single adversarial robot forges multiple fictitious identities to mislead the team. While prior work has largely addressed static or centralized MRS settings, it often neglects the strategic placement of Sybil identities, assuming arbitrary positioning. This paper introduces two novel algorithms for stealthy and effective Sybil robot placement in distributed MRS. We show comparative analysis of random placement and the proposed strategies, and comparatively evaluate both algorithms using distance metrics and their disruptive potential. Furthermore, we design and execute a Sybil attack within a cooperative exploration framework and present extensive simulation-based analysis. Results reveal key vulnerabilities in existing exploration algorithms and emphasize the need for security-aware MRS design.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Covert Routing with DSSS Signaling Against Cycle Detectors.
abstract: This paper investigates covert multi-hop communication in wireless networks where an adversary employs a cyclostationary (cycle) detector to reveal hidden transmissions. The covert route employs direct sequence spread spectrum (DSSS) signaling to ensure either maximum end-to-end covertness maximization or minimum latency minimization-under quality-of-service (QoS) and link budget constraints. Optimal bandwidth, transmit power, and spreading gain for each hop jointly satisfy reliability and either rate or covertness requirements. We show the equivalence between the covertness and the detection SNR gain-based widest-path formulations, and, hence, enabling efficient route computation. Numerical simulations in a realistic 3D environment illustrate that (i) end-to-end latency increases exponentially with the covertness requirement, (ii) the end-to-end latency increase is super-linear with the packet size M, and (iii) cycle and energy detectors impose different latency behavior as a function of the message length and the covertness requirement. The proposed framework provides important insights into resource allocation and routing design for covert networks against advanced detection adversaries.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DCoRE-QML: Communication-Efficient and Robust Distributed Quantum Machine Learning.
abstract: Distributed quantum computing provides scalability while offering advantages such as enhanced noise mitigation and higher fidelity. Leveraging this, distributed quantum machine learning (DQML) can provide better solutions to practical machine learning (ML) tasks, in contrast to classical ML and single-device QML performance. A key objective in DQML is to reduce inter-node communication costs, thereby enhancing efficiency, accuracy, and mitigating communication-induced noise. Existing communication-optimization approaches are generally application-agnostic and do not address the specific demands of QML circuits-especially quantum neural networks (QNNs), which require iterative training, large input sizes, and gradientbased updates. We propose DCoRE-QML, a framework designed for distributed QML that minimizes communication overhead while accounting for network dynamics (link and node failures) to improve robustness. It employs localized data encoding, delayed weight updates, compression techniques, and persistent entanglement purification to improve performance and fidelity.
