Experimental results indicate that it outperforms generic state-of-the-art solutions for QNN circuits, with higher fidelity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DRIFT-CL: A Continual Learning Framework with Advanced Drift Detection for Intrusion Detection in Evolving Networks.
abstract: Traditional static intrusion detection systems (IDS) struggle with concept drift and catastrophic forgetting in evolving network environments. This paper proposes DRIFT-CL, a driftaware continual learning framework for IDS that integrates: (1) a real-time drift detection mechanism monitoring loss, accuracy, and confidence; (2) an importance-weighted experience replay to prioritize rare attacks; and (3) an interpretable neural architecture with attention for feature importance analysis. Evaluations on InSDN, DNN-EdgeIIoT, and CICDDoS2019 demonstrate backward forgetting below 2.4 % and high detection accuracy (99 % on InSDN, 68-82% on IoT datasets), with robust performance under simulated concept drift, making DRIFT-CL suitable for real-world network security deployment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Doppler Frequency Estimation in Tensor-Based Modulation Via Post-CPD Maximum Likelihood.
abstract: Tensor-Based Modulation (TBM) is a novel wave-form design enabling efficient unsourced massive random access(UMAC) for future wireless networks. By leveraging tensoralgebra and Canonical Polyadic Decomposition (CPD), TBMallows to perform blind user separation at the receiver. However,the impact of Doppler frequency shifts on TBM has not yetbeen addressed. This paper shows that Doppler effects remainencoded mode-wise within the TBM factors, and hence do notdisrupt the blind user separation approach. Furthermore, theDoppler shifts associated to each user can be accurately esti-mated through a post-CPD per-user Maximum-Likelihood (ML)estimator. Simulation results show that the proposed approachonly requires a limited number pilot symbols while achievingaccurate Doppler recovery at low SNRs, thereby restoring thedecoding performance to a level nearly identical to the ideal zero-Doppler case. This makes the proposed approach well suited forshort-packet URLLC and IoT scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: QoS-Aware Energy Optimization via Cell Switching in Heterogeneous Networks.
abstract: The growing demand for mobile data services in dense urban areas has intensified the need for energy-efficient radio access networks (RANs) in future 6G systems. In this context, one promising strategy is cell switching (CS), which dynamically deactivates underutilized small base stations (SBSs) to reduce power consumption. However, while previous research explored CS primarily based on traffic load, ensuring user quality of service (QoS) under realistic channel conditions remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose a novel optimization-driven CS framework that jointly minimizes network power consumption and guarantees user QoS by enforcing a minimum received power threshold as part of offloading decisions. In contrast to prior load-based or learning-based approaches, our method explicitly integrates channel-aware information into the CS process, thus ensuring reliable service quality for offloaded users. Furthermore, flexibility of the proposed framework enables operators to adapt system behavior between energy-saving and QoS-preserving modes by tuning a single design parameter. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves up to 30% power savings as compared to baseline methods while fully maintaining QoS under diverse network conditions. Scalability and robustness of the proposed method in realistic heterogeneous networks (HetNets) further highlight its potential as a practical solution for sustainable 6G deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Data Generation for Unseen Ground Truth Using $\beta$-Variational Autoencoders: A Synthetic Approach for Real-Time Positioning Systems.
abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based solutions for Indoor positioning systems (IPS) in IoT environments are gaining momentum due to their wider applications, such as navigation, surveillance, asset tracking, and smart industries. However, the accuracy of the positioning system relies on the data that is used for training the machine learning model. The model requires a large amount of ground truth location data to perform robust indoor positioning. The process of collecting such data in an IoT environment is a challenging task in large-scale deployments. The proposed work aims to address this challenge using a synthetic data generation method, Beta variational autoencoders$(\beta$-VAE) for unseen ground positions. The model is trained with real-time IoT data collected from known ground truth positions in a UWB-based localization environment. The model learns noise from the IoT data in known ground positions and uses it to generate similar IoT data for in-between unknown positions in the same environment. This method addresses the data scarcity problem and reduces the manual data collection process, making ML-based indoor positioning feasible for large-scale deployments. The presented method is compared with other synthetic data generating methods, such as Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), Diffusion models, and Variational Autoencoders (VAE). The evaluation study shows that the data generated by the proposed work matches the real-time data with high accuracy. The work is also evaluated by generalizing the generated data with real-time inferences collected on the same unseen ground locations. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system for ML-based indoor positioning systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Resource Provisioning Optimization Concept for Software Core Networks.
abstract: The increased demand for wireless applications will require the 6 G Systems to have support for heterogeneous communication services but with a limited amount of resources. 6G technology should have the potential to accommodate many devices, facilitating scalability in resource management strategies across diverse industries or sectors such as healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, etc. The growing use of 5 G networks demands smooth operation due to its wide range of applications from mobile broadband to IoT services. There is a need for efficient and effective load-balancing mechanisms to support the exponential growth in the number of users connecting to software networks and ensure the continuity and availability of network services. In this article, we discuss how resource provisioning for software networks can be optimized with the help of defining policies and predictive ML models. To realise the concept, a 5 G software core network is deployed using the Fraunhofer FOKUS Open5GCore toolkit.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Client-Edge Association and Resource Allocation for Hierarchical Federated Learning in Wireless Sensor Networks.
abstract: While Federated Learning (FL) enables distributed clients to collaboratively train a shared model without exchanging raw data, Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) extends this framework by introducing multiple edge aggregators under a central cloud coordinator. This paper addresses the joint user association and resource allocation problem for a hierarchical FL architecture in networks where base stations or edge aggregators have overlapping coverage areas. We develop a round-level energy–latency minimization problem and show that, once client–edge associations are fixed, the continuous resource allocation subproblem is convex. The solver updates device compute frequencies, allocates node and backhaul band-width, and resolves the remaining one-dimensional quantities with monotone searches. To optimize discrete associations under partial coverage, we propose a monotone local search (MLS) algorithm that iteratively refines assignments by re-solving the continuous subproblem after single-client moves. Compared with a near-exact branch-and-bound (B&B) solver and a greedy load-balancing (GLB) baseline, the proposed method attains sub-percent optimality gaps while offering significant runtime reduction, and improves over the greedy baseline by roughly ten to twenty percent on medium and large instances. Simulation results on randomly generated partial-coverage networks confirm the scalability and practicality of the proposed analytical HFL framework for wireless sensor deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Experimental Investigation of Symbol Error Rate in Cost-Effective Full-Duplex RoFSO System.
abstract: This work experimentally demonstrates a cost-effective full-duplex radio-over-free-space optics (FD-RoFSO) system, realized at an overall cost of approximately $ 1600 only, using a commercially available low-cost optical transceiver. The proposed FD-RoFSO setup operates over a shared optical path in a controlled laboratory environment by employing a single pair of collimator lenses to reduce hardware complexity and overall system cost significantly. Higher-order$M$-ary modulation schemes are utilized to enable efficient data transmission by encoding multiple bits per symbol, and a custom-designed frame and phase synchronization algorithm ensures precise post-demodulation error analysis. The symbol error rate (SER) is comprehensively evaluated across different modulation schemes, modulation orders, and data rates, providing a practical and accurate assessment of system performance. Experimental results demonstrate the adaptability of the proposed FD-RoFSO system to various modulation formats and highlight its potential for robust, scalable, and efficient next-generation commercial optical wireless communication.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Bayesian Learning for Sparse Channel Estimation in Underwater Visible Light DCO-OFDM Systems.
abstract: This work introduces a novel framework for channel impulse response (CIR) estimation in sparse multipath environments for direct-current-biased optical OFDM (DCOOFDM) based underwater visible light communication (UVLC) systems, employing Bayesian learning (BL) methods. Initially, the CIR of the UVLC channel is formulated by accounting for absorption and scattering effects. To incorporate turbulence, the CIR is further modulated by a fading coefficient modeled by the lognormal distribution, which effectively captures weak oceanic turbulence. Building upon this, a BL-driven estimation strategy is proposed to exploit the inherent delay-domain sparsity of the multipath CIR in DCO-OFDM UVLC systems. The approach requires only a limited set of pilot subcarriers, thus lowering the pilot overhead compared to conventional channel estimation (CE) schemes. Performance evaluation is carried out using the Oracle-MMSE (O-MMSE) benchmark and the Bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound (BCRLB). Simulation results confirm that the proposed BL-based estimator, even with reduced pilot requirements, consistently outperforms both classical and sparse CE techniques in terms of normalized mean-square-error (NMSE) and bit error-rate (BER).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On the Theory of Semantic Information and Communication for Logical Inference.
abstract: First-Order Logic (FOL), also called first-order predicate calculus, is a formal language that provides a framework to comprehensively represent a world and its present state, including all of its entities, attributes, and complex interrelations, irrespective of their physical modality (e.g., text, image, or sensor data). Grounded in this universal representation, this paper develops a mathematical theory for semantic information and communication tailored to tasks involving logical reasoning and inference. For semantic communication, our framework distinguishes between two fundamental components: the physical cost of transmitting symbols of the FOL language and the logical content those symbols represent. A calibrated measure for semantic content is proposed, which allows for the consistent comparison of information value across different logical systems. This measure quantifies the degree to which a message reduces uncertainty about the true state of the world. Building on this measure, semantic entropy, conditional and mutual information metrics are defined. These metrics are then used to formulate optimizable objectives for semantic communication, designed to preserve the information most relevant for logical reasoning task at the receiver while adhering to a transmission budget. The framework's operational value is demonstrated through experiments in semantic compression, where the proposed objectives are used to manage the trade-off between transmission cost and the preservation of logical content; and deductive inference, where increasing world-state awareness improves deduction performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Spatio-Temporal Delta-Sigma Modulation for Massive MIMO with Low-Resolution DACs.
abstract: Going toward extreme multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna systems, each individual radio frequency (RF) chain will require cost and energy efficient implementations. While low resolution digital-to-analog converters (DACs) present a straightforward path toward achieving this goal, the introduced quantization error will lead to degraded performance. In this paper, we propose the use a spatio-temporal delta sigma modulation (DSM) placed upstream of the converter in a downlink massive MIMO-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) scenario. Its role is to shape quantization noise in frequency and in space, casting it toward unused directions and frequency resources. At the heart lies an optimization based design of the modulator’s noise transfer function (NTF) using available channel state information (CSI). A constraint to shape quantization noise away from adjacent frequency bands is studied as well. Numerical results show that the additional temporal dimension enables better error vector magnitude (EVM) performance than the recently thriving spatial DSM. Additional filtering is however still required to reach spectral masks set by current communication standards.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Unleashing Sensor-Aided Environment Awareness for Beam Management in Beyond-5G Networks: an Openairinterface Experimental Platform.
abstract: Large antenna arrays and beamforming techniques are key components for exploiting the spectrum-rich FR2 bands in next-generation mobile communication networks. Given the site-specific spatio-temporal variations of the mm-wave channel, non-RF sensor inputs and environment awareness can be leveraged to greatly enhance beam management decisions, e.g. via machine learning (ML) techniques. However, the current literature lacks open platforms to gather datasets for the training of such ML techniques and to evaluate novel beam management approaches in real-time, real-world scenarios and full-stack endto-end networks. In this work, we present our SDR-based experimental platform based on OpenAirInterface and are the first to integrate popular low-cost antenna array transceivers, beam sweeping capabilities, and a highly-modular sensor framework and associated interfaces into such a full-stack experimental platform. This enables beam management experimentation in real-world, real-time scenarios and facilitates gathering datasets necessary for developing ML-based beam management protocols that incorporate environment awareness via sensor modalities.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Stochastic Two-Hop Message Delivery Scheme for Uav-Assisted Disaster Recovery IoT Networks.
abstract: Owing to their flexibility, agility, high-level mobility and rapid deployment, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have marked, across disaster life-cycles, their efficiency in monitoring, damage assessment, search and rescue, but, above all, facilitating communication between survivors and rescue teams. This letter presents an emergency scene where surviving IoT devices scattered across a severely affected disaster site, sense and generate situational awareness (e.g., images and data) and damage assessment messages, which are crucial for first responders' interventions. In the absence of networking/communication infrastructures (e.g., damaged base stations, roadside units, etc), UAVs present themselves as potential message carriers from the considered site to a Mobile Command Vehicle (MCV) deployed farther from the edge of the considered site to ensure its safety. In this context, owing to the clear infeasibility of establishing continuous data communication paths between on-site devices and the MCV, a Stochastic Two-hop Message Delivery (STMD) scheme is presented where hovering UAVs are opportunistically exploited as physical message carriers between a fixed source UAV, S, which collects and buffers on-site IoT-generated messages and the destination MCV, D. STMD probabilistically assesses the suitability of incoming UAVs within S 's range and dictates the release of messages only to those UAVs that contribute to minimizing the average message transfer delay. The message release condition is described mathematically together with a first-step expression of the message release probability. Extensive simulations are conducted to gauge the proposed STMD's merit.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fair and Efficient Dynamic Vehicle Routing via Maximum Nash Welfare.
abstract: This paper presents a new routing algorithm designed to tackle congestion in urban road networks, using a framework called Maximum Nash Welfare (MNW) that focuses on indivisible goods. Unlike traditional methods that simply find the shortest routes for individual drivers, our approach uses the MNW fairness and efficiency principles to distribute vehicles more evenly across different paths, especially when congestion is identified. We conducted simulations using the SUMO traffic model, and the results show that our method significantly reduces average travel times, reduces queue lengths, and minimizes idle times compared to conventional routing strategies. In this way, we are able to strike a balance between fairness, individual user satisfaction, and the overall efficiency of the road network.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning Aided Near-Field Beam Prediction for U6G XL-MIMO Multipath Systems.
abstract: The upper-6 GHz (U6G) extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) system is regarded as a promising technology for sixth generation (6 G) systems, whilst it presents inevitable challenges for beam training. The large number of antennas and near-field effect result in high pilot overhead that is not applicable to time-varying scenarios. The existence of multiple paths will also compromise the spectral efficiency (SE) of single-path beamforming schemes. To address these challenges, a DL-aided near-field beam prediction scheme is proposed. A cooperative near-field codebook is designed, while a lightweight multi-task long short-term memory (MT-LSTM) network is established on the user equipment (UE) side. By reserving preceding training results, only a single beam needs to be newly trained in each frame to precisely predict the optimal beamforming vector for near-field multiple-path channels, thus greatly reducing the pilot overhead. Simulation results prove that the proposed scheme can significantly enhance the SE, while requiring only a signal pilot to be trained in each frame.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Pinching Beamforming Design for Integrated Sensing and Multicast Communications.
abstract: This paper studies a pinching-antenna system (PASS)-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework, where pinching beamforming is realized by adaptively adjusting the pinching-antenna (PA) positions along waveguides to simultaneously multicast common information and perform target localization. Specifically, a maxmin fairness (MMF) criterion and the Bayesian Cramer-Rao bound (BCRB) are formulated to quantify the multicasting and sensing performance, respectively. Based on these metrics, a sensing-centric joint design framework is developed to minimize the BCRB subject to multicast quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. A sequential element-wise alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is proposed to efficiently optimize the PA positions for pinching beamforming. Numerical results demonstrate that: (i) the proposed PASSenabled ISAC framework achieves substantially improved sensing accuracy compared with conventional multiple-input multipleoutput (MIMO) schemes while guaranteeing multicast service requirements; and (ii) the localization performance is consistently enhanced as the number of deployed PAs increases.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cache Update in Recommendation-Aware Leo Satellite Networks Via Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: As demand for personalized content keeps growing in fast-changing environments, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks need smarter caching methods than traditional approaches. In this paper, we present a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based cache update strategy designed for recommendation-aware LEO satellite-edge networks. The aim is to cut down on inter-satellite and ground station transmissions while improving user Quality of Experience (QoE). Instead of treating user requests as fixed, we model them as a step-by-step process shaped by past activity, real-time recommendations, and changing satellite coverage. The DRL agent uses information about satellite position, cache space, and recent user interests, and learns a reward that balances higher cache hit rates with lower transmission costs. We evaluated the proposed method against three standard baseline Random caching, Least Recently Used (LRU), and Least Frequently Used (LFU). In a Starlink-like scenario with 20 satellites and 200 mobile users, our approach achieved up to 80% higher cache-hit rate and 23.5% lower intersatellite transmission cost, while consistently maintaining strong alignment with user preferences.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Q-Codec: Reinforcement Learning based Adaptive Encoding for Real-Time Streaming of Immersive Aerial Videos.
abstract: In this work, we address the problem of real-time streaming of 360° videos over an air-to-ground (A2G) wireless channel between an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and a ground user. Each video frame must be delivered within a strict deadline from its generation time; otherwise, it is dropped. To maximize the user's quality of experience (QoE), we develop a reinforcement learning (RL)-based encoding parameter selection policy that dynamically adjusts the encoding rate, based on the A2G wireless channel state, video content, and buffer occupancy. Specifically, the proposed RL agent, termed Q-Codec, learns to adapt both the video resolution and the quantization parameter (QP) of the encoder to optimize QoE while minimizing frame drops. We benchmark the performance of the Q-Codec against two fixed resolution schemes that always transmit videos at either the lowest$(640 \times 480)$or highest resolution$(3840 \times 2160)$, which serve as performance bounds. Experimental results show that Q-Codec achieves performance close to the upper bound, demonstrating the effectiveness of RL-based adaptive encoding for real-time streaming of aerial omnidirectional videos (ODVs).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: CIDO-FANet: Channel-Robust RF Fingerprinting Identification for 5G Devices.
abstract: Radio-frequency fingerprinting identification (RFFI) can strengthen wireless security, but studies in 5G New Radio (NR) are scarce, and performance often degrades under channel variation. We propose a channelrobust RFFI framework for 5 G NR. First, we introduce a Channel-Independent Differential Operator (CIDO) that derives channel-invariant device features from NR demodulation reference signals (DMRS), suppressing channel distortion while preserving device traits. Second, to accommodate NR's flexible resource mapping and exploit frequency-domain dependence, we design the Frequency-domain Autocorrelation Network (FANet), which handles variable-length frequency inputs and employs frequency-domain attention for improved discrimination. Finally, using data from five commercial 5G NR devices collected across diverse environments and times, our method attains consistently high accuracy and markedly better cross-channel generalization than the baselines. These results indicate a practical path toward reliable RFF-based device identification in dynamic$\mathbf{5 G}$NR settings.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning-Based Angle-Difference Feedback with Vector Quantization for MIMO WLAN Systems.
abstract: To achieve higher throughput in the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless local area network (WLAN), a station (STA) needs to compress channel state information (CSI) and feed it back to an access point (AP) in an efficient manner. This paper presents a novel deep learning (DL)-based CSI feedback framework for MIMO WLAN systems, which improves feedback efficiency by employing an encoder-decoder network to compress and reconstruct the angle parameters of the CSI. In our framework, a trainable vector quantization (VQ) module is used after the encoder network and jointly trained with both encoder and decoder networks. Based on this, an angle-difference feedback strategy is applied, designed to exploit the temporal correlation of the sequential angle parameters. In our framework, STA selectively feeds back the difference between the current and previous angle parameters when the difference is sufficiently small. To this end, a novel VQ structure is proposed to compensate the quantization error of previous feedback, addressing the challenge of error-propagation. Simulation results show that our framework outperforms the standard method for MIMO WLAN systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Movable Antenna-Aided Beamforming and Dual-Scale Mobility Optimization in UAV Systems.
abstract: Integrating movable antennas (MAs) onto an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) unlocks a powerful dual-scale mobility paradigm for enhancing multi-user downlink communications. In this paper, we investigate the joint optimization of base station (BS) active beamforming, macro-scale UAV deployment, and micro-scale MA positioning to maximize the system's sum rate. The formulated non-convex problem is tackled using an alternating optimization (AO) framework that decouples it into three subproblems. Specifically, the fractional programming (FP) technique is leveraged to transform the beamforming subproblem into a standard quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP). For UAV deployment, a successive convex approximation (SCA) based method is developed to optimize its location by managing large-scale channel gains. To address the intricate coupling in MA positioning, we propose a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) algorithm that iteratively solves a convex surrogate problem for each antenna's position via SCA. Numerical results validate the convergence of our proposed algorithm and demonstrate that exploiting dual-scale mobility significantly enhances the sum rate compared to key benchmarks, including systems with conventional fixed-position antennas (FPAs) and the classic Projected Gradient Ascent (PGA) algorithm.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Latency-Optimized OFDM Systems via Wavelet Transform.
abstract: The evolution of wireless communication systems shifts away from being purely throughput-driven towards embracing additional objectives to broaden the range of applications. Latency is one of those new objectives considered in primary communication standards such as cellular and WiFi. Achieving low system latency requires a latency-focused optimization across all communication layers. A key latency contributor in today's OFDM-based systems is the transmitter- and receiversided Inverse Fourier Transform (IFFT) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), accounting for up to 20 % of the physical-layer latency. Inherent data dependencies of the FFT algorithm create latency constraints, necessitating the exploration of alternative approaches. In this paper, we investigate an alternative OFDM system based on Wavelet Transform (WT) and Wavelet Packet Transform (WPT) in the realm of low-latency communication and compare its latency as well as hardware complexity against the Fourier Transform baseline. Therefore, accurate latency and area models of the (Inverse) Discrete Wavelet and (Inverse) Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform are presented, all built upon optimized hardware architectures. The resulting quantitative comparison indicates a reduction in the latency-area product of up to 68 % highlighting that WT-based OFDM systems are particularly wellsuited for low-latency applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Competitive Pricing in Differentiated Networks.
abstract: We study the problem of competitive pricing in networks where users choose between service providers based on quality, price, and individual preferences. Specifically, we consider differentiated networks, where fewer users are willing to pay higher prices compared to those opting for lower-priced services. This contrasts with the case of undifferentiated networks, where the user population is assumed to be uniformly distributed across all preferences. Characterizing the solution in terms of strict Nash equilibrium prices, we show that differentiated networks are stable, while undifferentiated networks are not. Through a numerical study, we further demonstrate that the revenue accrued by each provider at equilibrium is proportional to the quality of service they offer.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cancelling Inter-AP-Interference for UL Channel Estimation in Virtual FD CF-mMIMO Systems.
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems are being envisioned as an evolution of multi-cell massive MIMO systems, which aim to provide higher spectral and energy efficiencies and facilitate a uniform quality of service (QoS). Recently, CF-mMIMO systems are modeled as a virtual full duplex (vFD) systems, where the access points (APs) independently switch between the uplink and downlink mode to serve all the uplink and downlink users concurrently. This further enhances the overall QoS. However, several issues, like channel estimation, interference suppression, signal detection, etc., need to be addressed to realize such systems. In this work, we focus on devising a strategy for estimating the uplink channel in the presence of concurrent downlink transmissions. For this, we propose an AP mode selection and inter-AP-interference cancellation method to improve the quality of channel estimates, which enhances the signal to interference plus noise ratio, consequently boosts spectral efficiency (SE). Using simulations, we show that the proposed scheme minimizes the normalized mean square error for two pilot assignment schemes, namely, random and user group schemes. The proposed method outperforms with existing method in terms of the average spectral efficiency (SE) for different values of signal-to-noise ratio.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy Efficient for Holographic RIS-aided NOMA Near-Field Short-Packet Communication System.
abstract: In this work, we investigate the performance of a holographic reconfigurable intelligent surface (HRIS)-aided downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network for energy-efficient (EE) short-packet near-field (NF) communications. In particular, we aim to maximize the EE of a multiuser downlink NOMA system by jointly designing the transmit beamforming at the BS and the phase-shift matrix of the HRIS, while explicitly accounting for delay determined by packet size and target packet error probability. Due to the non-convexity of the formulated problem, a sub-optimal iterative solution is developed which efficiently addresses the joint optimization through a combination of alternating optimization (AO), the Dinkelbach method, and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques. The efficacy and convergence of the proposed algorithm are validated via extensive numerical simulation. Furthermore, we also discuss the impact of key system parameters, such as HRIS reflecting elements, minimum quality of service (QoS) constraints, transmit power budget, and number of users. The potential of HRIS in integration with NOMA, space division multiple access (SDMA), and orthogonal multiple access (OMA), for short packet downlink transmission is demonstrated.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: WCFL: Robust and Resource-Efficient Federated Learning Using Model Weight Caching.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, but it faces two persistent challenges: robustness against malicious or faulty clients and efficiency under heterogeneous resource constraints. We propose WCFL, a novel framework that leverages model weight caching to jointly address these challenges. First, client updates are compared against cached historical weights to detect anomalous or adversarial behavior. Second, after global aggregation, the server uses cached model states to selectively transmit updates, skipping negligible differences for resource-limited clients based on bandwidth, compute, energy, and latency profiles. This cachingdriven strategy strengthens resilience to Byzantine attacks and reduces unnecessary communication. Theoretical analysis shows that WCFL preserves the convergence rate of FedAvg with a bounded resource-dependent bias. Empirical results on standard benchmarks demonstrate that WCFL achieves accuracy comparable to FedAvg while reducing communication cost by up to 40 %, making federated learning both robust and resourceefficient.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: TinyML-driven Edge Intelligence for Sustainable IoT in 6G Networks.
abstract: The push toward sustainable and more ubiquitous connectivity has started to place new demands on sixth-generation 6 G networks, and this is already visible in dense IoT settings. Requirements related to large-scale connectivity and ultra-low latency still have to be met. But this does not happen in isolation. Strict environmental constraints add another layer of difficulty. Intelligence is therefore being moved closer to where data is generated, partly because there are few other practical options. In this context inference is carried out locally on ultra-low power microcontrollers through Tiny Machine Learning, and the shift keeps coming up for obvious reasons. Data transmission toward centralized cloud platforms is reduced and privacy improves, although these benefits are not always evenly felt. To keep things grounded a few application areas are touched on, including healthcare, smart agriculture, disaster monitoring, and intelligent transportation, even if they are not all discussed in the same level of detail. These examples show that privacy aware services can still function even when energy limits are tight. Some issues, however, are still clearly there. These include limited power resources, differences among hardware platforms, extra communication cost, and models that do not always generalize well. Because of this, research interest is gradually moving toward directions like neuromorphic TinyML, RIS-aware edge intelligence, and metrics that reflect green AI goals. Overall, TinyML appears to offer a realistic path toward intelligent and environmentally responsible Green IoT systems that align with 6 G ambitions and wider sustainability targets such as those highlighted in COP26.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy-Efficient Zero-Touch Operation Via Cell Utilization XApp on RIC-TaaP.
abstract: The Near-Real-Time RAN Intelligent Controller is a key component of the Open RAN (O-RAN) architecture for optimizing RAN performance via applications called xApps. In this paper, we present an empirical design and implementation of an xApp that leverage the capabilities of the proposed RIC Testing as a Platform (RIC-TaaP). We specifically focus on an Energy Saving (ES) xApp in a Proof-of-Concept (PoC) to demonstrate the effectiveness to automate the RAN at this timescale. The ES xApp addresses carrier and cell switch on/off, dynamic monitoring of per-cell PRB utilization, and selective offloading and deactivating of underutilized cells or carriers. This practical implementation demonstrates how E2 capabilities can achieve energy savings while maintaining network Quality of Service (QoS) in a zero-touch operational setting. Testing results confirm that the ES xApp can reduce energy consumption by showing list of minimal impact on QoS Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), thereby illustrating the practical value of Near-RT RIC-driven control. Our study provides an open-source, reproducible evaluation of Near-RT RIC capabilities with a concrete energy efficiency application, laying the groundwork for further innovation in intelligent RAN management.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: QoS-Aware Radio Resource Allocation in UAV-Assisted NOMA Networks with Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic Learning.
abstract: In UAV-aided NOMA cellular networks, the joint optimization of user association, trajectory planning, and power allocation poses significant challenges due to high-dimensional continuous action spaces, dynamic user mobility, and stringent QoS requirements. We address this complex resource allocation problem by proposing a two-stage optimization framework integrating distance-aware clustering with multi-agent deep reinforcement learning. Specifically, we formulate a QoS and fairness radio resource optimization for throughput maximization in a UAV-aided NOMA cellular offloading network. We develop a distance-aware dynamic user clustering (DDUC) algorithm to ensure NOMA-compatible user grouping. We propose a multi-agent soft actor-critic (MASAC) framework to enable collaborative learning among UAV agents through experience sharing, incorporating tiered QoS penalty mechanisms and fairness constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that DDUC outperforms K-means by ensuring NOMA-specific constraints, while MASAC achieves superior scalability across different UAV fleet sizes and maintains approximately 99 % QoS satisfaction while significantly improving the system throughput when comparing with other benchmarks by at least 67 %.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Federated Learning-Based Network Traffic Prediction for Digital Twin in Next-Generation Networks.
abstract: Digital twins have been employed for predictable network planning and routing on the next-generation network. One of their most significant applications is network traffic prediction, which offers operators a clear view of the network's state. This paper addresses the issue of network traffic prediction. Given the high cost associated with traffic data transmission, we propose a novel distributed approach that leverages federated learning and graph-constrained group testing. Federated learning can enhance the cost efficiency of transmitting raw network traffic data from each node performing network traffic sampling to the operator. To tackle the problem of redundant training samples, we introduce a mechanism based on graph-constrained group testing to select a subset of clients for local training. This mechanism employs a random walk algorithm to construct a measurement matrix that aids in determining the client subset. Extensive experimental evaluations show that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: HF Skywave Massive MIMO Communications with Interference Sparsity-Aware Turbo Receiver.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a low complexity turbo receiver for high frequency (HF) skywave massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. By leveraging the beam based channel model (BBCM), we reveal the interference sparsity of HF skywave massive MIMO systems. Exploiting the interference sparsity, we provide a condition of extracting sufficient observation for signal detection. Motivated by this condition, we construct the interference user terminal (UT) set (IUS) and extract the observation vector from the received signal after matched filtering (MF) for each UT. Then, a low-dimensional interference sparsity-aware detector (ISD) is separately designed for each UT, and the interference sparsity-aware turbo receiver (ISTR) is subsequently formulated using ISDs. Further, we develop an efficient implementation of the ISTR, involving approximate computations of the ISD and the signal reconstructed by ISD. Simulation results confirm that the proposed ISTR achieves excellent performance with relatively low complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Near-Field Terahertz Covert Communications Against Randomly Distributed Eavesdroppers.
abstract: We study the near-field Terahertz (THz) covert communications against a randomly distributed eavesdropper with unbounded noise uncertainty. First, we model the eavesdropper as randomly and uniformly distributed in a disc centered on the transmitter. Then, we derive a closed-form expression of the eavesdropper's received power by leveraging Fresnel integrals to approximate near-field phase variations. Furthermore, we analyze the system performance metrics, including the average covert probability, average covert outage probability, and covert rate. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy of our analysis and reveal a non-monotonic relationship between the average covert outage probability and the radius of the eavesdropping area, further indicating that an optimal communication distance exists to minimize the average outage probability for each specific radius of the eavesdropping area, thereby providing guidelines for secure wireless networks deployment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Improving Multicarrier Systems With Intentional Frequency Offsets and Optimized Power Allocation.
abstract: This work investigates the use of intentional frequency offsets to improve spectral efficiency in multicarrier systems. By introducing controlled non-orthogonality through frequency offsets, we propose an orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM)-based non-orthogonal multicarrier scheme. The received signal is decomposed into interference-free subchannels through linear precoding and post-coding. We analyze the subchannel characteristics in terms of strength and power consumption, and derive the optimal power allocation that maximizes spectral efficiency under frequency-selective fading channels. Simulation results show that the proposed system significantly improves spectral efficiency compared to OFDM and existing non-orthogonal multicarrier schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Medium Access for Multi-Cell ISAC through Scheduling of Radar and Communication Tasks.
abstract: This paper focuses on communication, radar search, and tracking task scheduling in multi-cell integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks under quality-of-service constraints. We propose a medium access control framework that multiplexes these tasks while optimizing radar scan patterns through an interference-aware scheduling algorithm. Specifically, the proposed framework employs time-domain task scheduling and beam selection, formulated as an assignment problem, to mitigate inter-task and inter-cell interference, respectively. Simulations show that our solution guarantees target communication throughput, sensing target detection probability, and sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio with improved resource efficiency over baseline schemes, highlighting the benefits of coordinated scheduling in multi-cell ISAC.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Optimization of Resource Usage in Blockchain Networks to Meet High Throughput: A Hybrid Pull-and-Push-Based Approach.
abstract: The rapid expansion of decentralized applications (DApps) has significantly impacted Ethereum blockchain ecosystems, notably reflected in the dramatic increase in transaction volumes. As transaction volumes increase, the average block size also grows, leading to longer propagation times across the network. Larger block sizes require more bandwidth and computational resources to propagate and validate, increasing latency and potentially causing bottlenecks within the network. Consequently, managing and optimizing block sizes becomes essential to maintaining acceptable propagation time and ensuring high performance and reliability as blockchain networks scale. To maximize effective throughput while minimizing block propagation delays and operational overhead, we propose a novel hybrid push-and-pull block propagation mechanism, tailored specifically for structured blockchain networks. The proposed approach strategically reduces direct peer-to-peer (P2P) connections between nodes by transitioning block broadcasting tasks from conventional randomized P2P interactions to a more efficient server-client communication model. Performance evaluations through simulations demonstrate that our mechanism significantly outperforms traditional randomized P2P broadcasting methods, achieving notable reductions in both block propagation delay and computational costs incurred by nodes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Aim5B: AI Integrated Semantic Framework for 5G and Beyond Network Management.
abstract: Scalable, interpretable, and intelligent network monitoring and management are critical for 5 G and future networks. This paper introduces Aim5B, an AI-integrated semantic framework for 5 G and beyond network management to address these challenges. Aim5B processes unstructured logs from key$\mathbf{5 G}$core network functions, and transforms them into a knowledge graph aligned with the semantic structure of control-plane events. Leveraging a large language model (LLM), Aim5B enables natural language queries to be translated into Cypher graph queries, facilitating precise log retrieval, event analysis, temporal correlation, and statistical summarization-without relying on static parsing rules or predefined dashboards. Integrated on a real private 5G testbed, Aim5B achieved the full performances in precision, recall, F1, and Jaccard metrics, across various detailed, domain-specific queries per network function component. Furthermore, it significantly reduces management traffic-by approximately 99.9 %-through targeted, event-specific querying. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of Aim5B as an intelligence-driven solution for real-time, scalable network observability in future mobile systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Physical Inspired Intelligent Detection for Drone Geological Survey in Low-Altitude Networks.
abstract: Accurate and efficient detection of rock cores in field geological surveys is essential for infrastructure planning, while it remains hindered by the labor-intensive nature of manual labeling and the inefficiency of existing detection models. Besides, in low-altitude drone networks, onboard computational resources are severely constrained, and transmitting raw images incurs excessive communication overhead. To address this challenges, this paper presents a drone detection framework based on YOLO11-OBB for rock core annotation. Through considering the physical properties of rock core, the proposed method utilizes the multi-head framework. The proposed method achieves a mean average precision of 0.994 at an intersection over union threshold of 0.5(mAP@0.5), while delivering real-time inference at 136.88 frames per second, making it suitable for deployment on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Experimental results show that the model-assisted workflow reduces the average annotation time per image from 120 seconds under pure manual labeling to less than 30.14 seconds. This work effectively bridges high-precision geological perception with energy-efficient drone-edge computing.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Channel-Robust RFF for Low-Latency 5G Device Identification in SIMO Scenarios.
abstract: Ultra-low latency, the hallmark of fifth-generation mobile communications (5G), imposes exacting timing demands on identification as well. Current cryptographic solutions introduce additional computational overhead, which results in heightened identification delays. Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) identifies devices at the physical layer, blocking impersonation attacks while significantly reducing latency. Unfortunately, multipath channels compromise RFF accuracy, and existing channel-resilient methods demand feedback or processing across multiple time points, incurring extra signaling latency. To address this problem, the paper introduces a new RFF extraction technique that employs signals from multiple receiving antennas to address multipath issues without adding latency. Unlike single-domain methods, the Log-Linear Delta Ratio (LLDR) of co-temporal channel frequency responses (CFRs) from multiple antennas is employed to preserve discriminative RFF features, eliminating multi-time sampling and reducing acquisition time. To overcome the challenge of the reliance on minimal channel variation, the frequency band is segmented into sub-bands, and the LLDR is computed within each sub-band individually. Simulation results indicate that the proposed scheme attains a 96.13% identification accuracy for 30 user equipments (UEs) within a 20-path channel under a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 20 dB. Furthermore, we evaluate the theoretical latency using the Roofline model, resulting in the air interface latency of 0.491 ms, which satisfies ultra-reliable and low-latency communications (URLLC) latency requirements.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid-Action Task Offloading in Integrated Ground-Air-Space Networks for Smart Farming: A Cooperative Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: Integrated Ground-Air-Space Networks (IGASNs) utilizing UAVs and LEO satellites are pivotal for seamless remote smart farming connectivity. This paper investigates resource management within this hierarchical architecture, incorporating a dynamic SNR-dependent video compression model. The challenge is formulated as a joint optimization problem in a hybrid action space to minimize a composite cost of latency, energy, QoS violations and system sustainability in a heterogeneous system. To address this, this paper introduces a multi-agent Hybrid-Action Rainbow DQN (HA-RDQN) algorithm designed for dynamic cross-layer optimization. Evaluated in a high-fidelity simulation framework featuring both terrestrial and satellite backhauls, HA-RDQN improves system performance by approximately 30% over standard RDQN and doubles the performance of baselines. The results demonstrate the proposed approach's superior scalability and robustness for sustainable integrated ground-air-space applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: OMTS: Ordered Multipath Traffic Scheduling for Elephant Flows in Distributed AI Training Clusters.
abstract: With the rapid development of generative AI, network communication has become a critical bottleneck in distributed AI training clusters. The network traffic is characterized by a small number of high-bandwidth flows in AI workloads. Therefore, Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) has been widely adopted due to its low-latency and highbandwidth characteristics. However, RDMA's sensitivity to out-of-order packets and requirement for lossless networks conflict with existing traffic scheduling mechanisms. Current flowlevel, packet-level, and flowlet-level scheduling schemes applied to RDMA lead to severe tail latency and out-of-order packet problems, causing network performance degradation. To address these challenges, we propose Ordered Multipath Traffic Scheduling (OMTS), a novel framework that ensures inorder delivery of elephant flows while minimizing tail latency. OMTS employs a reliable proximal policy optimization (PPO)based multipath traffic scheduling (PMTS) algorithm in the control plane. It collects real-time network state and generates scheduling decisions by minimizing tail latency under in-order delivery constraints. The constraint maintains packet ordering by accounting for path delay differences. In the computation plane, the sender splits elephant flows into multiple subflows and assigns them to distinct paths based on the scheduling decisions. These subflows will be transmitted along the assigned paths in the network plane. This end-network cooperation enables global traffic scheduling. Experimental results demonstrate that OMTS significantly reduces tail latency and mitigates out-oforder packet issues compared to existing traffic scheduling schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Optoelectronic Precoding for Wideband Multiuser Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: Conventional hybrid architectures for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) employ a phase-shifter network (PSN) together with multiple true-time-delay (TTD) units for wideband precoding. However, their phase-only control imposes unimodular constraints, which exacerbate the non-convexity of precoder design and limit system performance. To overcome this hardware bottleneck, an optoelectronic base station (OE-BS) architecture is proposed, exploiting optical joint amplitude-phase control to enable flexible precoding and enhanced performance. The core idea is to replace the PSN and TTD with an optical network composed of an optical analog network (OAN) and an optical delay network (ODN). The OAN realizes amplitude-phase control, while the ODN introduces frequency selectivity, jointly eliminating the unimodular constraint that hinders analog domain design. Based on the OE-BS architecture, a hybrid precoding algorithm is developed for wideband multiuser massive MIMO systems, with simulation results demonstrating near-optimal achievable sumrate performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: An Eigen-Based High-Precision AoA Estimation for Frequency-Mixing RIS-Assisted Positioning.
abstract: The decoupling feature of frequency-mixing reconfigurable intelligent surface (FMx-RIS) offers a new perspective for channel estimation and positioning in multiple RIS scenarios. This paper proposes a high-precision user equipment (UE) positioning framework using FMx-RIS. By leveraging the frequency-specific “fingerprint” embedded in each reflective path, the proposed method effectively decouples the channels and eliminates path ambiguity. We derive an intrinsic relationship between the received signal and the angle of arrival (AoA), and develop an iterative algorithm that achieves near-CramérRao Bound (CRB) accuracy of angle estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that, with parallel extraction of AoA from multiple UE-RIS links, the framework supports highly precise UE positioning, even in low-SNR regimes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: High-Accuracy Electromagnetic Parameter Calibration for Ray Tracing Based Channel Modeling by Chaos-Enhanced Gray Wolf Optimization.
abstract: High-fidelity channel models, often based on raytracing (RT), are essential for designing next-generation wireless systems such as 6G networks and digital twin channel. The accuracy of these models hinges on calibrating their electromagnetic (EM) material parameters. However, this calibration presents a complex and high-dimensional optimization challenge. To address this challenge, we propose an algorithm specifically for the electromagnetic parameter calibration for RT based channel modeling, called the Chaos-Enhanced Gray Wolf Optimizer (CGWO). It combines the collaborative search of swarm intelligence with the ergodic properties of chaos theory. Furthermore, an adaptive chaotic local search (CLS) strategy is introduced to prevent the optimizer from getting stuck in local optima and converging prematurely. We validate our algorithm using channel data obtained from measurements conducted in indoor corridor scenarios. The results demonstrate that compared to standard Gray Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), CGWO offers significant advantages in convergence speed, accuracy, stability, and scalability. For example, CGWO achieves a final Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.8 dB, a notable improvement over GWO (2.3 dB) and SA (2.8 dB). As the number of calibration parameters increased from 1 to 6, CGWO demonstrate enhanced optimization capabilities. These validate that CGWO is a powerful and efficient solution for high-fidelity channel modeling.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Dynamic Optimization of PER-UE RAN Parameters Based on Latency Tolerance Via Deep Learning.
abstract: There is an increasing need to precisely satisfy the quality of service (QoS) requirements of each user equipment (UE) to ensure the stable use of industrial applications. The open radio access network (RAN), standardized by the O-RAN Alliance, offers enormous potential for flexible resource management to address diverse QoS requirements. Despite studies showing that machine learning can effectively automate RAN operations through cell/slice-level control, improving the performance of industrial applications via fine-grained per-UE RAN control remains an open challenge. We propose a deep learning-based method for dynamically optimizing per-UE RAN parameters in the O-RAN framework, leveraging a near-real-time RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC). The method predicts the latencyviolation probability and adjusts RAN parameters to support time-varying latency requirements for each UE. In simulations, mobile robots were remotely controlled from a server over a 5G network. The results demonstrate that the excess latency count could be reduced to one-quarter or less of that achieved using conventional RAN parameter settings.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Task Allocation for Multi-AUV Cooperative Hunting.
abstract: Cooperative hunting has emerged as a challenging task in complex underwater environments, involving multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) jointly performing the subtasks of searching, tracking and capturing. However, existing approaches typically deal with these subtasks in isolation, lacking a unified and adaptive task allocation framework capable of responding to rapidly changing target behavior and limited communication. In this paper, we propose a novel hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework that jointly optimizes task allocation and action execution in an end-to-end manner. The high-level policy employs QPLEX to adaptively allocate each AUV to a specific task based on local observations and shared state information. The low-level policy, built on MADDPG, executes task-specific actions to perform the allocated tasks. By integrating discrete task allocation with continuous action control, the proposed framework effectively reduces action space dimensionality and enhances decision-making flexibility. Simulation results show that our method can effectively accomplish the multi-AUV cooperative hunting task, outperforming baselines in terms of cooperative performance and hunting efficiency.

title: Lyapunov-Based Time-Division ISAC for Vehicular Cooperative Perception.
abstract: The efficient coordination of sensing and communication resources presents a critical challenge in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) cooperative perception (CP). In this paper, we propose a time-division-based resource allocation scheme for joint sensing and communication to enable CP among connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). To evaluate sensing accuracy, a Kalman filtering (KF) based model is introduced for target state estimation. In this model, the uncertainty of the state estimate is quantified using differential entropy. An increase in this uncertainty raises the sensing queue backlog. We then formulate an optimization problem that jointly allocates the sensing and communication time and bandwidth, and determines the millimeter wave (mmWave) beam directions to maximize the long-term average cooperative perception success rate (CPSR) across all CAVs, while ensuring the sensing queue stability and reliable CP data transmission. Using Lyapunov optimization, the original stochastic optimization problem is transformed into a deterministic per-period optimization problem, which is then solved iteratively via an alternative approach. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves an improvement of 16.35 % in sensing coverage rate (SCR) and a gain of 15.04 % in CPSR compared to a stand-alone algorithm, while maintaining superior performance in high-density and multi-CAV scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Transmit and Receive Beamforming Design for Cell-Free ISAC MIMO Systems.
abstract: In this paper, a joint transmit and receive beamforming design for cell-free integrated sensing and communication multi-input multi-output systems is proposed. The dualfunctional base stations (BSs) can simultaneously communicate with downlink users and sense the target of interest, while the effects of line-of-sight links among BSs and self-interference at each BS on the sensing performance are fully taken into account. By adopting the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) as the performance metric for both sensing and communication, we formulate an optimization problem that aims to maximize the sensing SINR subject to communication SINR constraints, a total transmit power constraint, and interference-nulling constraints. To address the resulting non-convex and coupled problem, we develop an alternating optimization algorithm in which the receive beamformer is obtained via null-space projection, whereas the transmit beamformer is computed by reformulating the problem as a semidefinite program and applying semidefinite relaxation. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: PP-FedTrust: Securing Federated Learning Against Adaptive Poisoning Attacks.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is increasingly considered for ultra-reliable low-latency communications and secure 6 G RANs where edge devices train shared models under tight latency and privacy constraints. FL operates over non IID client data with heterogeneous distributions and quality. This complicates convergence and blurs the boundary between benign irregularities and malicious behavior. Attackers can compromise clients or inject Sybil participants to submit manipulated updates that poison the global model. The impact can be untargeted with broad accuracy collapse or targeted through backdoors that misclassify trigger inputs while keeping aggregate accuracy deceptively high. Existing defenses rely mainly on robust aggregation and often assume few adversaries or clear attack evidence in every round or access to a clean validation set. They also overlook early training phases where small degradations can cause lasting harm which is critical for URLLC control loops and RAN automation. In this paper, We propose PP-FedTrust, a practical framework that combines game theoretic aggregation, incentive aware client objectives, and model side verification to improve robustness under realistic constraints. The server applies similarity penalized reweighting with online replicator dynamics to suppress collusion while retaining useful signal under non IID participation. Clients optimize an objective that penalizes deviant updates and aligns with server hints, exposing rotating adversaries without accessing client data. The model layer protects top k sensitive parameters, applies selective homomorphic encryption, and projects away misaligned drifts. A fairness regularized schedule adaptively blends Multi Krum preferences with Trimmed Mean fallback. Experiments on standard benchmarks show improved robustness, stability, and accuracy over FedAvg, Krum, Trimmed mean and Median.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: BWiFi: An Intelligent Framework for Optimizing User QoE in Next-Generation Wi-Fi Mesh Networks.
abstract: The IEEE 802.11 (Wi-Fi) standard continues to evolve with next-generation mesh technologies that enhance coverage, reliability, and user experience. Home Wi-Fi usage has grown by over 40 % in recent years, driven by remote work and latency-sensitive applications such as video calls, gaming, and real-time collaboration. However, users still experience inconsistent performance across zones, making it difficult to locate areas that offer stable connectivity. To address this, we present BWiFi, an intelligent framework for identifying and recommending the best Wi-Fi zones in mesh networks. Unlike conventional RSSI-based analyzers, BWiFi integrates cross-layer Wi-Fi quality and application-level metrics to infer spatial QoE patterns, providing actionable guidance rather than passive measurement. The approach systematically collects Wi-Fi quality and application-level performance metrics, applies clustering with heuristic scoring, and ranks zones based on their suitability for latency-critical applications. Real-world evaluations in home and office environments demonstrate up to a$\mathbf{1 3 - 1 7} \mathbf{~ d B}$improvement in Signal-to-Noise Ratio, a 4 % reduction in Packet Error Rate, and an average latency decrease of 15 ms. Real-time tests using Microsoft Teams and PUBG Mobile further confirm that BWiFi effectively enhances user Quality of Experience in next-generation Wi-Fi mesh deployments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: 5G-TSN Time Synchronization: An Empirical Study.
abstract: The integration of Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) with fifth-generation (5 G) networks is crucial for enabling lowlatency and deterministic communications in applications like vehicle-to-everything, smart manufacturing, edge computing, and cloud-based machine learning. To realize this integration, a common approach is to develop TSN translators within the 5 G system (5GS). Among the TSN standards, IEEE 802.1AS provides systemwide time synchronization, and the translators for this standard are essential because wireless synchronization can be significantly degraded compared to wired networks. The paper presents the implementation and evaluation of TSN translators, focusing on the time synchronization of IEEE 802.1AS. The results show a promising sub-microsecond synchronization accuracy, and the analysis provides comprehensive insights into the factors affecting time synchronization over 5 G networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Placement Delivery Array Design for Coded Caching Scheme in Partially Cooperative Device-to-Device Networks.
abstract: Device-to-device (D2D) communication is a promising technique for next-generation wireless cellular communication systems. This paper studies coded caching in a partially cooperative D2D network, where only a subset of users transmit, while all request files. In all existing partially cooperative D2D coded caching schemes, each file must be divided into subfiles, referred to as the subpacketization level, which grows exponentially with the total number of users. For practical implementations, it is desirable to have schemes with reduced subpacketization levels. We propose an array known as a partially cooperative D2D placement delivery array (PC-DPDA), which describes the placement and delivery phases of a partially cooperative D2D coded caching scheme. Low subpacketization level schemes can be obtained by constructing appropriate PC-DPDAs. The placement delivery array (PDA) was proposed as a tool for designing coded caching schemes for broadcast networks. A wide range of PDA classes has been constructed in the literature. We propose a construction of a PC-DPDA from any given PDA, thereby obtaining several classes of PC-DPDAs. We show that an existing partially cooperative D2D coded caching scheme, which has an advantage over other known schemes in terms of operating memory regime, corresponds to a class of PC-DPDAs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fundamental Trade-Off and Resource Allocation for Cell-Free ISAC Under Fronthaul Constraints: A Deterministic Equivalent Analysis.
abstract: Cell-free integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a promising paradigm for future wireless networks, utilizing distributed access points (APs) to enable ubiquitous communication and high-resolution sensing. However, the substantial data exchange over fronthaul links between the APs and the central processing unit (CPU) introduces a critical bottleneck. This paper investigates the fundamental performance limits of a fronthaul-constrained cell-free ISAC system. Specifically, we consider a practical scenario where both the channel state information (CSI) and the sensing echo signals are quantized prior to being forwarded to the CPU. Leveraging large-dimensional random matrix theory (RMT), we derive closed-form deterministic equivalents for the downlink communication achievable rate and the sensing Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). The analytical results reveal an inherent trade-off between communication and sensing performance, dictated the allocation of the limited fronthaul capacity. Furthermore, we provide key insights into the optimal fronthaul resource partitioning strategy that maximizes the overall system performance. The proposed analytical framework circumvents the need for extensive Monte Carlo simulations, offering an efficient and accurate tool for system analysis and design.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Online Incremental Guard-Band Adaptive Scheduling for Time-Sensitive Networking.
abstract: Emerging time-sensitive applications demand deterministic delivery with low latency and bounded jitter. The IEEE 802.1 Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) standard employs Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF) with guard bands and offsets to ensure predictability. However, static guard-band configurations lead to wasted bandwidth, poor adaptability under dynamic traffic, and costly global recalculations, which undermine realtime guarantees. We propose an online incremental guard-band adaptive scheduling method that eliminates these inefficiencies. The approach introduces a Guard Band Aware Scoring (GBAS) scheme to prioritize candidate paths, determines minimal feasible guard bands and offsets via difference constraints and binary search, and confines adjustments to the affected subgraph instead of the entire network. Extensive simulations show that the proposed method significantly improves flow acceptance, reduces bandwidth wasted by guard bands, and sustains millisecondlevel runtime, thereby meeting the stringent online scheduling requirements of TSN.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: HFL-FlowLLM: Large Language Models for Network Traffic Flow Classification in Heterogeneous Federated Learning.
abstract: In modern communication networks driven by 5G and the Internet of Things (IoT), effective network traffic flow classification is crucial for Quality of Service (QoS) management and security. Traditional centralized machine learning struggles with the distributed data and privacy concerns in these heterogeneous environments, while existing federated learning approaches suffer from high costs and poor generalization. To address these challenges, we propose HFL-FlowLLM, which to our knowledge is the first framework to apply large language models to network traffic flow classification in heterogeneous federated learning. Compared to state-of-the-art heterogeneous federated learning methods for network traffic flow classification, the proposed approach improves the average F1 score by approximately 13%, demonstrating compelling performance and strong robustness. When compared to existing large language models federated learning frameworks, as the number of clients participating in each training round increases, the proposed method achieves up to a 5% improvement in average F1 score while reducing the training costs by about 87%. These findings prove the potential and practical value of HFL-FlowLLM in modern communication networks security.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A POMDP Framework for Remote Tracking in Pull-Based Systems with Imperfect Sensing.
abstract: We consider a real-time tracking system where a Markov source is monitored by two heterogeneous sensors. Upon command, sensors send their observations to a remote sink over error-prone channels. We assume each sensor exhibits state-dependent sensing accuracy and may occasionally fail to detect/sense the source state. We assess the performance via a generic distortion function meant to capture the specific goal of the end application. We derive optimal sink-side command policies to minimize the long-term average of a weighted sum of distortion and transmission costs. To model the uncertainty due to sensors' miss-detections and packet losses, we formulate the problem as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), which we then cast into a belief-MDP. Since the belief evolves continuously, the belief space is discretized into a finite grid, and the belief value is quantized to the nearest grid point after each update. This leads to a finite-state MDP, which is solved using the relative value iteration algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed policy significantly outperforms benchmark strategies and highlights the importance of accounting for state-dependent sensing reliability in sensor scheduling.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Sharing Disaster Information Using Mobile Cache at Disaster.
abstract: In recent years, Japan has faced an increasing frequency of large-scale natural disasters. To ensure rapid evacuation and improve survival rates, information on blocked or damaged roads must be promptly shared among evacuees. Delay-Tolerant Networks (DTNs), which enable data exchange via direct communication between mobile devices without relying on infrastructure, offer a promising solution. However, frequent communication in DTNs leads to significant power consumption, which is critical during disasters where battery resources are limited. This study proposes a disaster information-sharing system that designates a subset of devices as Mobile Cache (MC) to actively disseminate data, while others communicate passively to reduce overall energy consumption. Simulation experiments using a Multi-Agent Simulation (MAS) framework evaluate the impact of the proposed approach on evacuation completion rates and total energy consumption.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Block-Level Nonlinear Interference-Exploiting Precoding for PSK: Beyond CI-SLP and CI-BLP.
abstract: This paper investigates constructive interference (CI)-based waveform design for phase-shift keying (PSK) symbols under relaxed block-level power constraints in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. Existing linear CI precoding methods, including symbol-level precoding (SLP) and block-level precoding (BLP), are limited by stringent symbol-level power budgets or insufficient block-level degrees of freedom (DoFs). To address these issues, we propose a nonlinear waveform optimization framework that maximizes the minimum CI gain across each block. The optimal waveform is derived in closed form via the Lagrangian function and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, explicitly expressed with respect to the dual variables. Furthermore, the original problem is reformulated as an equivalent and tractable quadratic programming (QP) problem, and an improved alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm with a linear-time projection scheme is developed to efficiently solve it. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithms outperform conventional CI-SLP and CI-BLP approaches, especially for large block lengths and high-order modulations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Surplus-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Service Placement in Mobile Edge Computing.
abstract: In a Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) setup, Service Providers (SPs) often do not own the edge infrastructure, since it is managed by independent Infrastructure Providers (IPs). This separation requires economic negotiation for service placement under resource and cost constraints, involving dynamic coordination between the SP and the IP with asymmetric information and differing goals. Centralized or static models fail to capture strategic behavior and private preferences, making negotiationbased approaches essential. We model MEC placement as a finite-horizon bargaining game and implement a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) framework. The SP learns dynamic pricing under partial observability, whereas IPs follow various concession strategies. To encourage fair and efficient agreements, we apply reward shaping based on a Nash-log-based surplus with time decay, along with a demand-aware feasibility filter that excludes economically infeasible negotiations. Experiments on real MEC traces show that our method increases the SP surplus by 29.2 %, increases the agreement rate by 9.8 % and lowers the negotiated prices by 35 %, while converging in fewer rounds.
