These results show that our reinforcement learning (RL) based bargaining approach provides a scalable and adaptive solution for decentralized MEC placement under behavioral and economic uncertainty.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Trajectory Designs for UAV Relaying with LEO Satellites: Incorporating Practical Constraints.
abstract: This work explores UAV trajectory design for relaying communications between satellites and ground terminals, addressing frequent link failures caused by low elevation angles of departing satellites and environmental blockages. To ensure realistic applicability, the design incorporates practical constraints such as satellite orbits and ground tracks, maximum UAV flying speed, maximum acceleration, satellite beam coverage, and other key factors. Given the complexity of the environment, an exhaustive search for an optimal trajectory is impractical. Instead, we propose a reinforcement learning-based approach to optimize UAV trajectories while considering these real-world constraints. In a simulated Earth-Centered, Earth-Fixed (ECEF) coordinate system with practical settings, the proposed UAV trajectories achieve over four times the achievable rate compared to scenarios without UAV assistance and up to 35 % improvement over a fixed, well-positioned UAV. Additionally, the time-variant interactions between moving satellites and the trained UAV trajectories provide insights into why the UAV follows its learned path, reinforcing the reliability of the proposed approach. These results highlight the advantages of the proposed trajectory design, making it a promising initial reference for UAV relay trajectory planning with LEO satellites in real-world applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Post-Fall Immobility Detection Using Millimeter-Wave Radar and Point Set Representation Learning.
abstract: With population aging, accurate and continuous human monitoring is increasingly important. Millimeter-wave radar enables contactless, privacy-preserving sensing, making it well-suited for detecting emergencies such as falls. However, motion-based radar fall detection methods often struggle to handle the complexity and variability of real-world falls, limiting their practical applicability. In this study, we propose a millimeter-wave radar-based post-fall immobility detection method that integrates multi-step radar signal processing with a point set deep learning model. By targeting zero-Doppler signals from immobile persons, the method accurately distinguishes between lying and seated-on-floor postures. Ablation analyses reveal the contributions of input features and model components. The proposed approach provides rapid, high-accuracy, and privacy-preserving fall detection, supporting advanced monitoring in healthcare and assisted living environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Standard Condition Number-Based Robust Signal Detection with Whitening under Uncertainty.
abstract: Robust signal detection in colored noise with unknown covariance is essential in radar, cognitive radio, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), and quantum sensing applications. This paper develops a unified analytical framework for the Standard Condition Number (SCN) detector, which employs the ratio of the largest to smallest eigenvalues of the whitened sample covariance matrix. The framework jointly covers both ideal conditions in which the training and sensing noise statistics are identical and disturbed conditions in which interference or jamming alters the sensing covariance. Despite the SCN's practical relevance, its finite-sample false-alarm and detection behavior has not been analytically characterized. Using random matrix theory (RMT), we derive general expressions for these probabilities, provide closed-form results for special cases, and show that the SCN preserves the Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) property under covariance mismatch. Analytical and simulation results confirm that the proposed unified framework delivers consistent detection performance and greater robustness than conventional eigenvalue- and LRT-based detectors.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning Augmented Wireless Channel Estimation: Over the Air Training and Validation.
abstract: Deep learning (DL) based wireless physical layer (PHY) has been shown to outperform conventional PHY, especially when trained using appropriate synthetic datasets or when mathematical modelling of the wireless environment is complex. However, training DL PHY using real radio signals (real dataset) is challenging since the channel impulse response is unknown. In this work, we develop an end-to-end training and validation framework for the DL-based PHY using software-defined radio (SDR). We demonstrate the significance of real-dataset-based training for wireless PHY performance and explore a fine-tuning approach to address the limited availability of real datasets. For resource-constrained edge platforms used for PHY deployment, we proposed a novel augmentation approach where we augment conventional baseband signal processing with lightweight DL. Experimental results using the SDR testbed show that finetuning DL-based receivers with limited OTA data significantly improves real-world generalisation. Compared to state-of-theart end-to-end DL PHY, the proposed approach reduces the number of parameters by 85 % and multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations by 99 %, improves inference speed by eight times, and is modulation-agnostic. Further, the proposed approach offers up to 40 % higher throughout.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Inverse Learning Assisted V2I Communication for Intent Based 6G ISAC Vehicular Networks.
abstract: G communication is expected to bring unprecedented advancements in the capabilities and efficiency of vehicular networks. However, the advent of 6 G will also introduce significant changes in the operation of vehicular communication infrastructures such as roadside units (RSUs), including the incorporation of autonomous intent-based network paradigm and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) capabilities. While ISAC enables sensing and communication capabilities within a single 6 G network node, intent-based network design paradigm ensures that network nodes such as RSUs, act as autonomous cognitive agents to fulfill the objectives of their respective communication service providers. This paradigm shift necessitates the development of vehicle to infrastructure (V2I) communication strategies that learn the sensing-assisted communication and the autonomous decision-making strategies of RSUs. In this context, this paper proposes ATIL, a data-centric approach for inverse learning the strategies of an autonomous intent-based 6G ISAC RSU node. The ATIL-based adaptive communication strategy is demonstrated for two vehicular micro-cloud applications namely predictive scheduling for cooperative data downloading and cluster head selection. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed ATIL-based approach outperforms existing nonlearning based strategies in terms of throughput and packet loss for vehicular micro-cloud applications, and ATIL outperforms both parametric and machine learning methods that could be adopted for inverse learning.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Neural-Network Based Change-Point Detection for Binary Linear Block Codes.
abstract: We study the problem of change-point detection (CPD) in the received noise-affected data when the transmitter switches from one channel code to the other channel code at an unknown time instant. Such scenarios arise in adaptive modulation and coding (AMC), where the transmitter dynamically switches between different channel codes. For the CPD problem for channel codes, we estimate the change point (CP) in two stages. In stage-1, we apply suitable preprocessing to the received data and obtain a coarse estimate of the CP using the processed data. Around this coarse CP estimate, we then analytically find the confidence interval where the true CP lies with high (or desired) probability. In stage-2, we then focus on the unprocessed data corresponding to this confidence interval, and use neural network (NN)-based framework to refine the previously estimated coarse CP. In our work, we also address the case when the channel noise parameter is unknown, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed approach. The validity and performance of the proposed two-stage method is demonstrated through a variety of simulations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cross-Layer Performance Analysis of P-EDCA.
abstract: Modern Wi-Fi applications require tight latency bounds and predictable throughput, and they rely on a mix of transport protocols (e.g., TCP Cubic, BBR, New Reno, and UDP) whose performance is highly sensitive to MAC-layer behavior. The forthcoming 802.11bn amendment introduces Prioritized EDCA (P-EDCA) to reduce latency for high-priority traffic, yet its crosslayer impact on transport performance remains insufficiently understood. This paper evaluates the performance of TCP and UDP traffic operating over both EDCA and P-EDCA. Our results show that (i) both TCP and UDP traffic exhibit strong sensitivity to P-EDCA configuration, with uplink tail latency varying widely; (ii) best-effort TCP flows experience throughput degradation when competing with P-EDCA voice flows; (iii) ban dwidth fairness between TCP and UDP improves as TCP starvation is mitigated using P-EDCA; (iv) the relative performance of TCP congestion control algorithms shifts depending on the MAC-layer policy; and (v) the performance of high-throughput UDP voice flows degrades when the eligibility conditions for invoking$\mathbf{P}$EDCA are relaxed. These findings illustrate how MAC-layer latency optimizations propagate to the transport layer in nonintuitive ways, highlighting the need for cross-layer tuning in next-generation Wi-Fi systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Comparison of Methods to Experimentally Validate Information-Theoretic Physical Layer Security.
abstract: In information-theoretic security, we have the problem that we do not impose any computational constraints on the attacker, but rather have constraints ourselves if we try to validate information-theoretic security in simulations. We know that the maximum likelihood strategy is the optimal strategy for validating distinguishing security, but it is impractical to validate security with larger encoding randomness. In this paper, we present a new list generation algorithm for the authors' validation method and compare it with other possible validation algorithms such as ordered reliability bits guessing random additive noise decoder (ORBGRAND), ordered statistic decoder (OSD), mutual information neural estimator (MINE), and non-parametric entropy estimator toolbox (NPEET). For the simulations we use a seeded modular coding scheme and compare the security performance of the algorithms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive Hybrid RF/FSO Uplink Design for HAP-Assisted UAV Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates a cooperative two-hop uplink architecture for multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications, where a high-altitude platform (HAP) acts as a relay between UAVs and a ground station through hybrid radio frequency (RF) and free-space optical (FSO) links. To enhance link reliability under weather-dependent FSO degradation, a dynamic adaptive combining (DAC) mechanism is introduced to jointly exploit FSO and sub-THz channels on the HAPground backhaul. An integrated optimization framework is developed to maximize the overall hybrid RF/FSO capacity while ensuring fairness among multiple UAVs. The framework simultaneously optimizes UAV trajectories, bandwidth and power allocation, HAP transmit power distribution, and DAC coefficients under stringent backhaul and energy constraints. The resulting formulation is highly nonlinear and nonconvex due to coupled trajectory and resource variables. To address this, an inner-approximation (IA) algorithm is proposed, which iteratively convexifies the problem and guarantees convergence to a stationary solution. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms conventional selection combining and hard-switching baselines, achieving higher throughput and robustness across diverse atmospheric and mission conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: An Efficient and Scalable Framework for Validating Functionality of IoT/Embedded Devices.
abstract: With the growing usage of IoT devices in critical applications, guaranteeing reliable operation and smooth protocol compatibility remains a significant concern. There are several testing solutions available; however, their scope is limited, focusing on compliance rather than practical integration. Furthermore, traditional validation approaches often do not include functionality testing at several levels for IoT and embedded devices. To address this gap, we developed an efficient and scalable framework, a comprehensive solution for evaluating IoT/embedded device operation at the physical, network, and application levels. Our proposed solution allows for the smooth integration and efficient operation of connected resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we presented the scalable and efficient architecture for validating the functioning of DUTs at many levels. We also developed test cases for several communication protocols (UART, I2C, and CAN) to ensure that they worked properly, but we demonstrated loopback, parity, and a few electrical tests on the embedded board and PXIe hardware using LabVIEW to evaluate how well the UART communication protocol worked. The findings show that UART has been validated and is operating in accordance with norms.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Location-Aware RIS-AN Adaptation for Physical-Layer Security and Energy Efficiency.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and artificial noise (AN) are promising techniques for enhancing physical-layer security in 6G wireless networks. However, their effectiveness strongly depends on user geometry and blockage, where a single fixed configuration may improve secrecy in one scenario but degrade it in another. This paper proposes a location-aware adaptive selection framework that dynamically switches among four practical schemes based on the network geometry, namely NoRIS/NoAN, NoRIS/AN, RIS/NoAN, and RIS/AN scheme. A lightweight genetic algorithm (GA) jointly optimizes base station (BS) precoding, AN power allocation, and RIS phase shifts under quantized phase constraints and realistic power consumption model. Two design objectives are considered: maximizing secrecy capacity (SC) and secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization. Simulation results show that the proposed adaptive selector outperforms the best static baseline (Best-Static) across blockage levels, achieving lower secrecy outage, higher SEE, and broader secure coverage. The analysis further reveals that the schemes with AN dominate under moderate blockage, RIS-assisted schemes dominate under high blockage, and the RIS/AN scheme only dominates only over limited angular regions. These finding highlight the effectiveness of simple geometry-aware adaptation for robust and energy-efficient physical-layer security.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Joint Routing and Slot Scheduling for TSN and UAV Integrated Networks.
abstract: The integration of Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has attracted extensive research interest due to their potential to support emerging mission critical and latency sensitive applications. However, these TSN-enabled UAV applications, including industrial inspection and emergency response, necessitate communication mechanisms capable of simultaneously delivering high throughput and guaranteeing strict end-to-end delay bounds. This requirement becomes particularly challenging under dynamic wireless conditions, where maximizing throughput inherently conflicts with ensuring deterministic latency. To this end, we formulate a joint routing and time-slot scheduling optimization problem aiming to maximize a weighted sum of throughput and delay. Subsequently, we develop a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based scheduling algorithm to efficiently solve this formulated problem. Specifically, the algorithm jointly determines flow prioritization, routing paths, and time-slot offsets, leveraging a constraint-compliant mechanism to resolve optimization conflicts. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior throughput while strictly adhering to the deterministic delay bounds required by TSN, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Transceiver and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Design in mmWave MU-MISO Systems with Hardware Impairment and Imperfect CSI.
abstract: This paper investigates a millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiuser multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) transceiver system assisted by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). Furthermore, potential hardware impairments (HWI) and imperfect channel state information (CSI) are considered in the system model, reflecting realistic implementation constraints. The objective is to achieve user fairness, and thus reduce inequality among users, by jointly optimizing the transceiver beamforming and discrete RIS phase shifts to minimize the worst-case mean square error (MSE) across all users, thereby strictly ensuring user fairness. To solve this non-convex min-max problem, we develop an alternating optimization (AO)-based algorithm that iteratively decouples the coupled variables, enabling tractable and efficient subproblem solutions. Simulations demonstrate rapid convergence within 31 iterations and up to 15% worst-case MSE reduction compared to benchmarks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Cross-Layer Protocol for Missing Tag Identification Under Probabilistic Cloning Attacks in Large-Scale RFID Systems.
abstract: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) serves as a core technology in Internet of Things (IoT) applications such as retail management, industrial warehousing, and object tracking. Accurately identifying missing tags in such systems is essential to prevent economic loss and protect information security. However, existing identification protocols perform poorly under probabilistic cloning attacks, in which counterfeit tags intermittently impersonate missing genuine tags. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes the Missing Tag Identification Under Probabilistic Cloning Attacks (MPCA) protocol, a cross-layer protocol for missing tag identification under probabilistic cloning attacks. MPCA dynamically chooses between two response modes by precomputing and comparing their average execution time. Then it employs a marker vector to assign and filter slots for tags, and introduces differentiated response strategies to reduce time overhead. Furthermore, MPCA leverages physical-layer signal analysis via an enhanced DBSCAN algorithm to resolve collision slots into parallel identification opportunities by accurately estimating the number of concurrent tag responses. We provide rigorous theoretical analysis to derive optimal parameters that balance execution efficiency and identification reliability. Extensive simulations demonstrate that MPCA can maintain required identification reliability while reducing execution time by up to 50.9% compared to state-of-the-art protocols.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Agent Sac Enabled Beamforming Design for Joint Secret Key Generation and Data Transmission.
abstract: Physical layer key generation (PLKG) has emerged as a promising solution for achieving highly secured and lowlatency key distribution, offering information-theoretic security that is inherently resilient to quantum attacks. However, simultaneously ensuring a high data transmission rate and a high secret key generation rate under eavesdropping attacks remains a major challenge. In time-division duplex (TDD) systems with multiple antennas, we derive closed-form expressions for both rates by modeling the legitimate channel as a time-correlated autoregressive (AR) process. This formulation leads to a highly nonconvex and time-coupled optimization problem, rendering traditional optimization methods ineffective. To address this issue, we propose a multi-agent soft actor-critic (SAC) framework equipped with a long short-term memory (LSTM) adversary prediction module to cope with the partial observability of the eavesdropper's mode. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared with other benchmark algorithms, while effectively balancing the trade-off between secret key generation rate and data transmission rate. The results also confirm the robustness of the proposed framework against intelligent eavesdropping and partial observation uncertainty.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Efficient Resource Allocation and Service Migration in MEO Rosette Constellation Satellite Networks.
abstract: As an emerging paradigm in next-generation network architectures, satellites equipped with edge servers have attracted increasing attention. With the growing demand for low-latency and wide-area seamless coverage, they have emerged as a promising technology. However, their mobility and limited resources necessitate an efficient resource allocation and service migration strategy. Most existing studies have focused on Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, which typically handle low traffic volumes and overlook service diversity. Moreover, resource allocation and service migration are inherently interdependent problems that require joint optimization. To address this challenge, we propose a joint optimization model for resource allocation and service migration in a Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) rosette constellation. Our approach integrates a queuing framework for practical issues such as handover failures and packet loss. We optimize resource allocation and service deployment by formulating the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and employing an enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)based algorithm. Simulation results validate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches regarding system reward and service success rate.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enhancing Secret Key Generation for UAV Communications via Codeword Reconstruction.
abstract: With the rapid advancement of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), ensuring the security of communication links among UAVs has become crucial. In this paper, we propose a novel physical layer key generation scheme based on channel codeword reconstruction. In UAV communications, the high mobility of aerial nodes leads to short channel coherence time, which together with noise causes inevitable channel estimation errors. These errors significantly degrades the performance of wireless channel-based key generation. Therefore, we propose a codeword construction algorithm that achieves a polarization characteristic, which effectively segregates reliable keys from unreliable ones. Compared to the existing quantization-based key generation scheme, our approach maximize the utilization of raw channel information and employ soft-decision decoding to generate key. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme reduces the key disagreement rate for legitimate users and increases the number of consistently generated keys. Furthermore, our method ensures a lower key consistency rate for eavesdropper, which guarantees system security.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: UAV Cooperative Transmission in Low-Altitude Heterogeneous Networks Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: In low-altitude heterogeneous networks, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) provide flexible relay services for mobile users, while base stations act as the main nodes for network access and task aggregation. When the coverage of the ground base station is insufficient or compromised, the aerial base station can operate as an independent air access node to provide wide-area connectivity and reliable data transmission. However, the system still faces challenges such as the randomness of user mobility, the uncertainty of task generation, and the limited and heterogeneous communication resources. To address these issues, we propose a low-altitude heterogeneous cooperative transmission framework. Specifically, we propose to jointly optimize the trajectory and dynamic user association of UAVs to maximize the task completion throughput, which is formulated as a mixedinteger nonlinear programming problem. Therefore, we propose multi-agent hybrid proximal policy optimization algorithm combined with many-to-one Gale-Shapley dynamic matching method (MOGS-MAHPPO). The optimization problem is decomposed into a long-term UAV trajectory planning subproblem and a short-term mobile user association subproblem. The MAHPPO algorithm is applied to solve the long-term subproblem, and MOGS dynamic matching method is utilized for the shortterm subproblem. Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves task completion rate by up to 17.8 % over existing benchmark methods, demonstrating its effectiveness and practical value.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel User Authentication Scheme Via Led Spectral Fingerprinting.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel authentication method based on the spectral fingerprint characteristics of light-emitting diode (LED). The spectral fingerprint of LED originating from manufacturing process variations is analyzed. A method for constructing a simple spectrometer is presented, and its measurement accuracy is verified to meet the identification precision requirements, enabling it to replace large and expensive professional spectral measurement equipment. A multi-stage support vector machine (SVM) classification algorithm based on feature extraction combined with mathematical modeling is proposed. A mathematical model of the spectral profile is established using a combination of Gaussian and asymmetric Lorentzian functions. Several key shape features are extracted from the spectral profile through function fitting. These features are then used to train one-class SVM. Employing a multi-stage structure and anomaly detection, the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 98.4 %, a precision of 100 %, and a recall rate of 97.8 %. Compared with an algorithm based on neural networks, the proposed method maintains high accuracy while featuring a simpler algorithmic structure, lower resource consumption, faster inference, and better physical interpretability.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Two-Stage Joint Decision Framework for Low-Latency XR Service Delivery Under Cloud-Edge-End Collaboration.
abstract: As immersive applications grow, the need for ultra-low-latency eXtended Reality (XR) in smart-city and industrial settings is rising. However, existing network transmission schemes still suffer from uneven wireless resource allocation, cloud-edge congestion, and packet loss, limiting Quality of Service (QoS). To address this, we propose a two-stage joint decision framework for low-latency XR delivery under cloud-edge-end collaboration, with separate strategies for cloud-edge and edge-end transmission. For the cloud-edge transmission, we design a graph Transformer-enhanced actor-critic-based cloud-edge routing algorithm (GTAC) that uses Transformer sequence modeling to encode graph-structured network states and produce adaptive routes. For the edge-end transmission, we design a penalized grey wolf optimizer-based fine-grained edge wireless resource allocation method (PGWO) with frame as the decision unit and mini-slot as the minimum resource allocation granularity, which converts the constrained problem into an unconstrained objective, rapidly approximates feasible spectrum and power allocations, and markedly reduces end-toend delay. Compared with the existing advanced benchmark algorithms, our method lowers the cloud-edge transmission latency by 21.70%-44.07% and the edge-end transmission latency by 37.05%-86.45%, while significantly improves system throughput as well as XR delivery efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Robust Radio Frequency Fingerprint Extraction and Identification for LoRa Low-Power Devices.
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) has emerged as a promising approach to enhance the security of LoRa device access. However, achieving lightweight and robust RFF extraction and identification for resource-constrained LoRa devices remains a critical challenge. To address this issue, this paper proposes a comprehensive framework that integrates signal processing and machine learning to enable efficient RFF extraction and identification. Firstly, cyclic correlation spectrum are employed to capture device-specific characteristics while mitigating high-power noise. Then, exploiting the quasiflat fading property of LoRa channels, a logarithmic-domain infinitesimal approximation algorithm is developed to suppress channel effects. Finally, a linear discriminant analysis-based redundancy elimination strategy is combined with a lightweight classifier to achieve both computational efficiency and high recognition accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves strong adaptability to channel dynamics, maintaining an average recognition accuracy of over$\mathbf{9 7 \%}$across diverse environments and temporal intervals, while incurring low computational and energy costs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Multi-Layer BATS Code for Multi-Hop Networks with Partial Channel Status Information.
abstract: Batched sparse (BATS) code, consisting of an outer code and an inner code, is a promising network coding approach that can achieve network capacity asymptotically. However, the superior performance of BATS code highly depends on the outer code design, necessitating optimizations using accurate and global channel status information (CSI). If only partial CSI can be obtained, the performance of BATS code may suffer significant degradation. In this paper, we investigate a general multi-hop erasure network model comprising major nodes and minor nodes. Major nodes with higher computational capabilities can perform both outer and inner coding, while minor nodes are restricted to simpler inner coding. Each major node can acquire only partial CSI regarding the link between itself and its adjacent major nodes. With this model, we propose a multi-layer BATS (ML-BATS) coding scheme employing a two-phase encoding mechanism. In the encoding phase, the major nodes sequentially apply outer coding to received and stored packets, while the minor nodes only perform inner coding within each received batch. The outer coding at a major node, together with the inner coding at minor nodes until the next major node, constitutes a coding layer. During decoding, a failure in one layer may propagate to subsequent layers, resulting in a high probability of decoding failure. Thus, we introduce a complementary phase, in which major nodes generate small-degree batches to help restart the decoding process. We analyze the decoding performance and formulate optimization problems to optimize the degree distribution for each major node, maximizing the transmission efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MLBATS code shows superior performance compared to the existing network coding schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Efficient CSI Feedback with Scalable Codebook Design for 6G XL-MIMO.
abstract: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multipleoutput (XL-MIMO) is a fundamental enabler for sixthgeneration (6 G) wireless systems, as large antenna arrays unlock substantial spatial multiplexing gains. To obtain timely and accurate channel state information (CSI) at the next-generation NodeB (gNB), the widely used discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-based codebook serves as an efficient benchmark, yet its non-hierarchical indexing limits scalability and, under fast channel variation that forces frequent CSI updates, drives high CSI feedback overhead. To support efficient CSI feedback for 6 G XL-MIMO, we propose a fast Fourier transform (FFT)-inspired scalable codebook grounded in the Cooley-Tukey factorization of the DFT matrix. Each global DFT beam is represented exactly as a composition of lower-dimensional DFT components coupled by stage-wise twiddle factors, which exposes a natural prefix-suffix index hierarchy. This structure supports multitimescale CSI feedback: coarse indices remain stable over longer intervals, while refinement indices are updated more frequently, thereby reducing the average feedback overhead. Numerical evaluations confirm that the proposed design achieves exact DFT reconstruction and reduces average feedback overhead by approximately$30-60 \%$compared to conventional DFT and Kronecker-based separable DFT construction schemes, demonstrating its effectiveness for efficient CSI feedback in 6G XLMIMO systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Stochastic Network Calculus Analysis of SPMA for Delay-Sensitive Industrial IoT Networks.
abstract: The Statistical Priority-based Multiple Access (SPMA) protocol is particularly well-suited for accommodating massive concurrent access and fulfilling differentiated traffic priority requirements in large-scale industrial scenarios. However, existing performance analyses of SPMA have long focused on packet loss rate and throughput, lacking systematic research on its delay characteristics. This paper conducts a Stochastic Network Calculus (SNC) analysis of SPMA, filling the gap in the theoretical analysis of its delay performance for mission-critical industrial applications. First, a homogeneous Poisson point process is used to model the network topology, and techniques such as binary exponential backoff and time-frequency hopping are incorporated to analyze the burst success probability of SPMA. Second, based on the moment generating function-based SNC theory (MGF-SNC), a numerical upper bound of the statistical delay violation probability (SDVP) is derived, and a delay minimization model is constructed. Finally, the impact of key parameters on the delay performance of SPMA networks is analyzed. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, demonstrating that a tight SDVP upper bound can be obtained, providing theoretical support for optimizing deterministic latency in next-generation IIoT networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Compressed Multiband Sensing in FR3 Using Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers.
abstract: Joint detection and localization of users and scatterers in multipath-rich channels on multiple bands is critical for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in 6G. Existing multiband sensing methods are limited by classical beamforming or computationally expensive approaches. This paper introduces alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-assisted compressed multiband sensing (CMS), hereafter referred to as ADMM-CMS, which is a novel framework for multiband sensing using uplink quadrature amplitude modulation-modulated pilot symbols. To solve the CMS problem, we develop an adaptive ADMM algorithm that adjusts to noise and ensures automatic stopping if converged. ADMM combines the decomposability of dual ascent with the robustness of augmented Lagrangian methods, making it suitable for large-scale structured optimization. Simulations show that ADMM-CMS achieves higher spatial resolution and improved denoising compared to Bartlett-type beamforming, yielding a 34 dB gain in per-antenna transmit power for achieving a 0.9 successful recovery probability (SRP). Moreover, compared to performing compressed sensing separately on the constituent 7 GHz and 10 GHz sub-bands, ADMM-CMS achieves reductions in delay root mean squared error of 34.46% and 40.76%, respectively, at -41 dBm per-antenna transmit power, while also yielding improved SRP. Our findings demonstrate ADMM-CMS as an efficient enabler of ISAC in frequency range 3 (FR3, 7-24 GHz) for 6G systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Computation-Efficient Multi-Scale Multi-Granularity Framework for Mobile Traffic Forecasting Via Hierarchical Coherence.
abstract: With emerging infrastructure paradigms such as AI-RAN, next-generation mobile networks are expected to support unprecedented user density and transmission speeds. The resulting massive mobile traffic necessitates real-time prediction at base stations (BSs), enabling a wide range of optimization tasks essential for network efficiency, including anomaly detection, resource allocation, and congestion control. Achieving accurate predictions requires integrating both global trend dependencies and local temporal variations in traffic streams. However, the limited computational resources at BSs are insufficient to support high-capacity models that process long-scale and fine-grained time series while maintaining low latency. To address this bottleneck, we propose MSMG, a Multi-Scale and Multi-Granularity framework for mobile traffic forecasting. MSMG aggregates traffic measurements at multiple levels, each handled by a distinct predictor: upper levels capture coarsegrained but long-term dependencies, while lower levels preserve fine-grained but short-term variations. This hierarchical design allows MSMG to flexibly assign suitable models to each level, thereby reducing average computational cost while maintaining predictive accuracy. To reconcile these heterogeneous predictors into a holistic view of mobile traffic, we exploit hierarchical coherence-an intrinsic structure across aggregation levels. We formulate this coherence as a conditional optimization problem w.r.t. the predictors' outputs and solve a reconciled forecast. We further transform this optimization into a differentiable module that supports consistent gradient flow, which enables joint forecasting and reconciliation in an end-to-end manner. Extensive evaluations on a public mobile traffic dataset demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Predictive Handover and Resource Allocation in Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks.
abstract: Satellite-terrestrial integrated networks (STINs) have emerged as a promising solution for providing global coverage and seamless connectivity. However, the high mobility of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites creates a highly dynamic topology, posing severe challenges for mobility management and resource allocation. In such scenarios, inevitable delays between network measurement and decision execution often render STIN mobility management ineffective, which further causes outdated handovers, link failures, and degraded quality of service (QoS). To address these issues, we propose a joint predictive handover and resource allocation method based on the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. Specifically, by integrating LSTM into the PPO agent, the proposed method captures temporal dependencies in network dynamics and enables foresighted decisions that mitigate the negative effects of high mobility of LEO satellites and also reduce unnecessary handovers. Numerical simulation results show that compared to the benchmark methods, the proposed method achieves higher system sum rate, better load balancing, and lower link failure rates, implying that it enables more effective handover and resource allocation decisions through optimal service node selection and dynamic subcarrier assignment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive Beam Hopping for Over-the-Air Online Federated Learning in LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates over-the-air (OTA) computation federated learning (FL) in low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, where we propose a novel joint design of adaptive beam hopping and power control to maximize the long-term total amount of training data. This problem is challenging due to the non-convex coupling between beam hopping patterns, power control, and global mean squared error (MSE) constraints, as well as the dynamic satellite coverage. To address these difficulties, we develop a proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based deep reinforcement learning framework that learns efficient scheduling policies. In particular, the proposed method jointly optimizes beam hopping patterns and transmission power, while incorporating MSE-aware reward shaping to balance data utilization and aggregation accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PPO approach achieves faster convergence, higher reward, and superior FL performance in terms of test accuracy and training loss, compared with soft actor-critic (SAC), deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), and a greedy baseline.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Auto-Scaling and Load-Aware SDNFV Architecture for 5G User Plane Functions.
abstract: The fifth-generation (5G) core network requires high scalability and performance to support rapidly increasing traffic demands and latency-sensitive applications. However, existing implementations often lack mechanisms for seamless and real-time scaling of User Plane Functions (UPFs), which leads to inefficient resource utilization and potential service disruption. This paper presents a scalable and session-aware UPF deployment framework that leverages Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV). The proposed architecture integrates Kubernetes-based orchestration, Prometheus-driven monitoring, and P4-enabled traffic steering to dynamically adjust UPF instances while preserving session continuity. A Packet Forwarding Control Protocol (PFCP) proxy and a migration-aware load balancer are designed to ensure consistent state synchronization and resource-aware traffic distribution. Experimental evaluation demonstrates nearlinear throughput scalability, seamless session continuity during scale-in, and effective overload mitigation. These results confirm the feasibility of dynamic UPF scaling in cloud-native 5G core networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: ReaLM: Real-Time Channel Prediction with Distilled LLM.
abstract: In the realm of next-generation wireless communications, real-time and accurate channel state information (CSI) prediction remains a major challenge due to the complex, dynamic, and noise-prone nature of wireless environments. To tackle these difficulties, we propose ReaLM, an efficient framework that adapts and compresses large language models for channel prediction tasks. We fine-tune the Llama model with a time-frequency data fusion feature extraction module, enabling more effective spatiotemporal sequence modeling of CSI. After training, we design a knowledge distillation strategy to reduce the high computational latency and heavy parameter load of large language models, compressing the model by 62% and accelerating inference by 58%. During training, we apply data augmentation and noise injection to improve the model's antiinterference capability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReaLM outperforms traditional baselines in low-SNR and crossenvironment scenarios, establishing itself as a robust and efficient solution for 6G real-time channel prediction.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: An ICAN Signal Authentication Method Based on Multi-Satellite Two-Way Time Transfer.
abstract: The development of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite internet is accelerating the Integration of Communication and Navigation (ICAN), thereby establishing LEO constellations as a cornerstone of modern Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) services. However, satellite downlink signals are highly vulnerable to repeater spoofing attacks. Traditional data-layer authentication methods are ineffective at detecting this threat, posing a significant risk to the security of PNT services. To address this vulnerability, we propose a Multi-Satellite Two-Way Time Transfer (MSTWTT) authentication method, which detects spoofing by comparing anomalies in the clock offsets measured between the user and multiple satellites. Specifically, the ICAN signal's interactive nature enables precise clock offset measurement, while repeater spoofing inherently introduces an unforgeable and detectable delay due to signal path alteration. To detect this, the Multi-Satellite Spoofing Detection Algorithm (MSSDA) is proposed. MSSDA combines the Huber loss function and sparse signal processing to adaptively establish the threshold while maintaining robustness. Lastly, simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with traditional approaches, MSTWTT demonstrates significant improvements in both authentication efficiency and robustness.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Secrecy Energy Efficiency Maximization for RIS-Assisted UAV-MEC Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Approach.
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle carrying mobile edge computing server (UAV-MEC) is expected to provide strong computational capability, reliable and flexible connectivity, and high adaptability to ground networks. Reducing energy consumption and improving information secrecy are severe challenges faced by emerging wireless communication systems. In this work, we investigate a secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted UAV-MEC networks by jointly optimizing the RIS phase shift, UAV trajectory, UAV cruising time, and the ground user (GU) scheduling. The block coordinate descent (BCD) approach is used to convert the optimization problem into two tractable subproblems, which can be solved by the Dinkelbach algorithm and the double deep Q-network (DDQN), respectively. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly improves the secrecy energy efficiency compared to benchmark methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive FEC with Deep Recurrent Q-Networks for Low-Earth Orbit Satellite Networks.
abstract: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, while essential for data services in mobile and remote scenarios in the forthcoming sixth-generation (6 G), suffer from intrinsic dynamics like frequent handovers and channel variability that severely challenge transport-layer reliability. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a packet transmission scheme based on adaptive forward erasure correction (FEC) that integrates streaming codes with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). We employ a deep recurrent Q-network (DRQN) to dynamically orchestrate the transmission of repair packets based on real-time channel state information, thereby achieving an optimal balance between bandwidth efficiency and transmission reliability at the transport layer. The proposed system is validated using real-life Starlink traces via a trace-driven emulation platform built upon Linux's eBPF technology. Experimental results demonstrate improved latency-overhead trade-offs over the conventional fixedinterval FEC, providing adaptive transport-layer error control for the next-generation satellite networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Semantic Inference Over the Air: An Efficient Task-Oriented Communication System.
abstract: Empowered by deep learning, semantic communication marks a paradigm shift from transmitting raw data to conveying task-relevant meaning, enabling more efficient and intelligent wireless systems. In this study, we explore a deep learning-based task-oriented communication framework that jointly considers classification performance, computational latency, and communication cost. We evaluate ResNets-based models on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets to simulate real-world classification tasks in wireless environments. We partition the model at various points to simulate split inference across a wireless channel. By varying the split location and the size of the transmitted semantic feature vector, we systematically analyze the trade-offs between task accuracy and resource efficiency. Experimental results show that, with appropriate model partitioning and semantic feature compression, the system can retain over 85\% of baseline accuracy while significantly reducing both computational load and communication overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Foldable Antenna Arrays for Massive MIMO Communications.
abstract: This paper investigates foldable antenna arrays (FAAs) as a reconfigurable architecture enabling dynamic beam steering through mechanically adjustable folding angles. To explore their potential in massive MIMO systems, we develop a field-response-based channel model that explicitly captures the impact of folding angles on the channel characteristics. Based on this model, we derive the deterministic equivalent of the ergodic achievable sum-rate and formulate a folding-angle optimization problem for rate maximization. To overcome the analytical intractability of direct optimization, we propose a twostage optimization framework. In the first stage, a differentiable position-angle to rate surrogate (PARS) network learns the mapping from user positions and folding angles to the rate. In the second stage, the trained surrogate is exploited for gradient-based optimization to determine near-optimal angles. This framework enables direct inference of favorable folding angles from user locations without repeated channel training. Simulations verify that the proposed method achieves near-optimal performance with low complexity while outperforming conventional fixed arrays.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hierarchical Asynchronous Federated Learning over Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks.
abstract: With the emerging 6 G paradigm where AI services operate over decentralized and resource-constrained edge infrastructure, performance of distributed learning algorithms remains a significant challenge. This paper proposes HAFL, a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite-assisted hierarchical asynchronous Federated Learning (FL) framework, enabling resource-limited terrestrial clients to collaborate via Ground-Satellite Links (GSLs). Within this framework, LEO satellites serve multiple roles: as edge servers aggregating and broadcasting models, as clients accelerating training, and as high-throughput relays managing inter-satellite routing through Inter-Satellite Links (ISLs). Unlike conventional synchronous Jacobian-type updates, HAFL employs asynchronous Gauss-Seidel-type updates to enhance convergence speed. We provide theoretical convergences for convex, strongly convex, and nonconvex objectives, respectively, and formulate optimization problems to jointly determine optimal hyperparameters to minimize global training latency. Evaluations demonstrate that HAFL achieves faster initial convergence and comparable final performance for benchmark DNNs and datasets, offering promising FL systems across remote areas with 6 G technologies, but much less global rounds and communication cost.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Secure Cell-Free Massive MIMO ISAC Systems: Joint AP Selection and Power Allocation Against Eavesdropping.
abstract: This paper investigates a cell-free massive multiple-input-multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system that addresses the critical challenge of information leakage to potential eavesdroppers located within sensing zones. A novel access point (AP) selection strategy is proposed, which partitions the distributed APs into two functional groups: communication APs (C-APs), dedicated exclusively to data transmission, and sensing APs (S-APs), responsible for target detection and eavesdropper suppression. Closed-form expressions for the achievable communication rate, eavesdropping rate, and mainlobe-to-average-sidelobe ratio (MASR) are derived to evaluate system performance. Two complementary optimization problems are formulated using the successive convex approximation (SCA): (i) maximizing user rates under security constraints and (ii) minimizing eavesdropping rates while satisfying quality of service (QoS) requirements. The proposed joint optimization framework determines the optimal AP operational modes and power allocation across communication and sensing links. Extensive numerical results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate significant performance gains, revealing inherent trade-offs among communication efficiency, sensing accuracy, and security. These insights offer practical guidelines for designing secure CF-mMIMO ISAC systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Uncertainty-Aware Bi-Level Robust Beamforming Optimization for 6G Cell-Free RAN.
abstract: In this paper, we study the robust downlink beamforming for cell-free networks through a bi-level scheme, where the upper level maximizes the network worst-case user rate, while the lower level selects channel estimation errors within a bounded uncertainty set to minimize users' signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios (SINRs). To enable tractable design, we derive the closed-form worst case bounds for both the desired-signal and multi-user interference terms, and collapse the bi-level program into a tractable single-level reformulation that admits an outer loop search for one-dimensional SINR with inner loop for second-order cone programming (SOCP) feasibility checks that provides strong robustness guarantees. We also propose a low-complexity bi-level adversarial projected-gradient (BAPG) method that directly updates the beamformers using adversarial CSI selections, achieving a favorable robustness and complexity trade-off. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods consistently outperform the baseline MRT method under CSI errors, with an improvement of the worst-case max-min rate by 119.6% on average, while also reduces the running time by over two orders of magnitude.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Flow-Aware Autonomous Learning for Availability Optimization in Time-Sensitive Networks.
abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN), with its high reliability and low latency, is widely applied in industrial automation, audio-video transmission, and other domains, serving as a core technology for deterministic communication. As TSN is extended to complex scenarios such as the Industrial Internet and immersive video interaction, its architecture must adapt to resource-constrained, low-performance devices and legacy terminals. However, the complexity of the TSN protocol and the high hardware requirements hinder full protocol support, resulting in black-box flows that lack timing and priority semantics. In heterogeneous flow scenarios, static allocation-based scheduling leads to resource inefficiency and high packet loss, thereby restricting TSN performance and compatibility. To address the limitations of existing TSN mechanisms in handling heterogeneous traffic, where burst flows from resource-constrained devices unpredictably compromise deterministic guarantees, this paper proposes HFAS, which preserves time-triggered(TT) determinism and enhances overall network availability. Specifically, HFAS employs a CNN-LSTM model to capture flow patterns and temporal sequence for accurate classification. Based on these classifications, an adaptive cyclic queuing and forwarding (A-CQF) mechanism enables dynamic priority migration, mitigating CQF scheduling conflicts and absorbing burst traffic. Simulation results demonstrate that, in mixed-topology and multi-load scenarios, HFAS increases the TT scheduling success rate by approximately 12 % and reduces burst packet loss by nearly 71 %, thereby confirming its effectiveness in resource-constrained environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Scale Decision Algorithms for UAV Anti-Jamming Communication without Common Channel.
abstract: This paper focuses on the challenge of achieving anti-jamming communication in multi-UAV networks without a common channel. We formulate an optimization problem that maximizes communication utility, which is defined by normalized throughput and synchronization overhead, through the joint optimization of the available channel set (ACS), channel and power. Based on the idea of multi-scale decision, we propose an adaptive ACS decision algorithm and a branching QMIX algorithm (ABQMIX), where cluster head (CH) and cluster members (CMs) are treated as heterogeneous agents. At the time frame scale, CH adaptively selects a high-quality and appropriately sized ACS based on observations of channel status and the evaluation of the communication utility. At the time slot scale, CMs make distributed decisions on channel and power allocation via an agent network enhanced by a branching architecture. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the adaptive ACS scheme in improving network performance. Moreover, the branching QMIX reduces the action space dimensionality and enhances communication utility.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Integrated Sensing and Semantic Communication with Adaptive Source-Channel Coding.
abstract: Semantic communication has emerged as a new paradigm to facilitate the performance of integrated sensing and communication systems in 6G. However, most of the existing works mainly focus on sensing data compression to reduce the subsequent communication overheads, without considering the integrated transmission framework for both the SemCom and sensing tasks. This paper proposes an adaptive source-channel coding and beamforming design framework for integrated sensing and SemCom systems by jointly optimizing the coding rate for SemCom task and the transmit beamforming for both the SemCom and sensing tasks. Specifically, an end-to-end semantic distortion function is approximated by deriving an upper bound composed of source and channel coding induced components, and then a hybrid Cramér-Rao bound (HCRB) is also derived for target position under imperfect time synchronization. To facilitate the joint optimization, a distortion minimization problem is formulated by considering the HCRB threshold, channel uses, and power budget. Subsequently, an alternating optimization algorithm composed of successive convex approximation and fractional programming is proposed to address this problem by decoupling it into two subproblems for coding rate and beamforming designs, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms the conventional deep joint source-channel coding-water filling-zero forcing benchmark.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Efficient Dual-UAV Trajectory Design and Communication Scheduling for Jamming-Aided Physical-Layer Secure Communication.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a secure communication network assisted by two unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), where one UAV serves as a mobile transmitter for multiple ground users (GUs), and the other acts as a cooperative jammer to suppress a ground eavesdropper. To enhance secrecy fairness, we aim to maximize the minimum secrecy throughput among GUs by jointly optimizing UAV trajectories and communication scheduling under mobility and collision avoidance constraints. Due to the continuous-time nature of UAV mobility and the spatiotemporal coupling between the transmitter and jammer, the original problem is infinite-dimensional and non-convex. To address this, we introduce a collaborative successive hover-andfly (SHF) structure and reconstruct the UAV trajectories with a finite number of hovering and turning points. To solve the remaining non-convex problem, we introduce a minimum-distance approximation to reduce the infinite anti-collision constraints to a finite set, and adopt concave lower-bound approximations for the secrecy throughput. An efficient iterative algorithm based on successive convex approximation is developed. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of our scheme over time-discretized and no-jamming benchmarks in terms of secrecy and complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: GE-Free BP-OSD for Short 5G LDPC Codes.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a two-stage beliefpropagation ordered statistics decoding (BP-OSD)-like algorithm, referred to as BP-LCGCD, tailored to 5G low-density paritycheck (LDPC) codes. When standard BP decoding fails, a modified BP (mBP) with an iteration limit determined by the code's girth and a normalization factor is performed to generate reliable posterior log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) in the pre-processing stage. In the post-processing stage, a locally constrained guessing codeword decoding (LC-GCD) module uses these posterior LLRs from mBP to produce candidate codewords without online Gaussian elimination (GE), where numerous invalid test error patterns (TEPs) are skipped by the introduced local constraints. To predict the performance, we derive an upper bound on FER and employ a saddlepoint method to compute its dominant tail-probability term. Furthermore, we propose an offline EXIT-chart-based method to select a fixed quasi-reliable basis, where variable nodes with the highest mutual information are chosen. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GE-free BP-LCGCD significantly outperforms standard BP, achieves FER very close to GE-based BP-OSD, and approaches the finite-length bound across multiple code rates for 5G LDPC codes, while requiring significantly fewer re-encodings and eliminating the need for online GE.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Gaussian Elimination-Free OSD via Pre-Stored Matrices.
abstract: This paper proposes an improved ordered statistics decoding (OSD) algorithm, termed OSD with pre-stored systematic matrices (PSM-OSD), which completely avoids online Gaussian elimination by utilizing multiple pre-stored systematic generator matrices (SGMs) and selecting one based on the received sequence for decoding. To further improve the search efficiency, the local-constraint mechanism is combined with the PSM-OSD, resulting in the LC-PSM-OSD. We also propose a saddlepointbased numerical method to evaluate a tight upper bound of the FER. Furthermore, leveraging our saddlepoint approximation method, we address two critical challenges to optimize the proposed decoding algorithms: 1) Matrix-selection criteria are evaluated across sum-reliability, max-min-reliability and coveragemaximization rules. We demonstrate that the introduced sumreliability rule yields the best performance among the considered methods, and exhibits the smallest gap to the ML performance; 2) Number of pre-stored matrices is set by our saddlepoint analysis, which determines the minimal number of SGMs needed to approach the ML performance. Numerical results and analysis demonstrate that the proposed algorithms are effective across various coding schemes including random linear codes and BCH codes. Moreover, the results show that the proposed LC-PSM-OSD can closely approach the finite-length capacity over almost all code rates for random linear codes, and outperforms conventional OSD, guessing codeword decoding (GCD), and LC-GCD.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multipath Constrained Deep Channel Prediction Model for Indoor Radio Environment Mapping and Radiation Source Localization.
abstract: High-precision indoor radio environment maps are essential for next-generation wireless sensing, spectrum management, and secure IoT applications. However, traditional methods struggle with complex indoor multipath effects and require extensive, time-consuming data collection. To address these challenges, we propose a deep channel prediction model with physical constraints, achieving radio environment maps prediction accuracy within 6 dB at a fine spatial resolution of 0.5 m. To further improve efficiency, we introduce a gradient adaptive sampling strategy that adjusts the sampling density based on the signal strength distribution gradients. Additionally, our three-stage RF source localization algorithm refines the accuracy, achieving an average localization error of just 0.61 m. This approach not only enhances the accuracy of radio environment maps but also significantly improves efficiency, making it highly suitable for advanced communication system applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: PND3QN: A Deep Reinforcement Learning-driven Routing Selection Framework for Network-on-Chip.
abstract: Increasing complexity and integration density in modern chip designs expose limitations of traditional bus-based interconnects for multi-core architectures. Network-on-Chip (NoC) mitigates this bottleneck, but rising core counts intensify packet transmission delays, degrading NoC latency and power efficiency. While numerous routing algorithms demonstrate efficacy, no single solution achieves universal optimality across diverse traffic patterns, topologies, and performance objectives. Intelligent algorithm selection thus constitutes a critical yet underexplored research direction. This paper introduces a novel Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-driven routing selection framework for NoC. Targeting latency minimization under uniform random traffic, the approach dynamically selects optimal routing algorithms for varying injection rates. Our simulations conducted on gem5 simulator demonstrate the method's effectiveness in identifying latency-minimizing routing algorithms across injection rates while achieving notably faster convergence than existing methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: ISAC-Enabled Covert Communications Under Sensing-Specific CSI.
abstract: Given that the acquisition of warder-related channel state information (CSI) is challenging but critical for covert communication system design, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology presents a promising pathway to address this issue. In this work, an ISAC-enabled covert communication architecture is proposed, where the location of the warder is estimated and the sensing-specific CSI is characterized for beamforming optimization. Specifically, the sensing results exhibit a deterministic impact on covert communication, establishing a fundamental coupling between sensing and covert communication functions. Besides, the sensing accuracy performance and the transmission covertness performance are analyzed for the subsequent system design. Further, a weighted optimization problem is formulated for achieving improved trade-offs between communication and sensing performance. This non-convex problem is solved by the sequential convex approximation-based algorithm, where the lossy$\mathcal{S}$-procedure is employed to handle the location uncertainty. Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed scheme over various benchmarks. Furthermore, there exists an optimal communication-sensing weighting factor that maximizes the covert rate.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Optimal Transmit Beamforming for MIMO ISAC with Unknown Target and User Locations.
abstract: This paper studies a challenging scenario in a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system where the locations of the sensing target and the communication user are both unknown and random, while only their probability distribution information is known. In this case, how to fully utilize the spatial resources by designing the transmit beamforming such that both sensing and communication can achieve satisfactory performance statistically is a difficult problem, which motivates the study in this paper. Moreover, we aim to reveal if it is desirable to have similar probability distributions for the target and user locations in terms of the ISAC performance. Firstly, based on only probability distribution information, we establish communication and sensing performance metrics via deriving the expected rate or posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB). Then, we formulate the transmit beamforming optimization problem to minimize the PCRB subject to the expected rate constraint, for which the optimal solution is derived. It is unveiled that the rank of the optimal transmit covariance matrix is upper bounded by the summation of MIMO communication channel matrices for all possible user locations. Furthermore, due to the need to cater to multiple target/user locations, we investigate whether dynamically employing different beamforming designs over different time slots improves the performance. It is proven that using a static beamforming strategy is sufficient for achieving the optimal performance. Numerical results validate our analysis, show that ISAC performance improves as the target/user location distributions become similar, and provide useful insights on the BS-target/user association strategy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Block-Sparsity-Aware Message Passing Algorithm for Wavenumber-Domain Holographic MIMO Channel Estimation.
abstract: In this paper, we study the channel estimation (CE) of holographic multiple-input multiple-output (HMIMO) systems in non-line-of-sight (NLoS) environments, and propose an efficient message passing-based CE method by utilizing the block-sparsity of the equivalent wavenumber-domain (WD) channel. Concretely, based on the quantization of cluster centers, a probabilistic model is first presented to capture the blocksparsity in the lattice ellipses of plane wave at the transceiver and thus in the 2D WD channel matrix. Then, the hybrid generalized approximate message passing (GAMP) algorithm is employed to estimate the channel, where a carefully-designed message passing module is incorporated into the GAMP module to handle the block-sparsity. Finally, simulation results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed CE algorithm.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Task-Oriented Adaptive Semantic Communication with Multi-Modal Fusion for UAV Object Tracking.
abstract: Efficient processing and transmission of multisource visual data are critical for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based applications in complex environments. However, transmitting high-volume visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) images over bandwidth-limited wireless channels remains challenging. This paper proposes a Task-Oriented Adaptive Semantic Communication framework (TAMF-SC) with Multi-Modal Fusion to address the challenges of high-volume data transmission and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions in UAV RGB-IR systems. The framework adopts an end-to-end architecture that performs cross-modal fusion and semantic encoding of RGB and IR features, transmitting semantic features for downstream tasks and high-quality fused image reconstruction. An SNR adaptive module dynamically adjusts the per-channel feature gains according to the estimated channel SNR, emphasizing critical semantic features while suppressing noisy ones, thereby enhancing robustness under varying channel conditions. At the receiver, the received semantic features are first decoded and then utilized for both fused image reconstruction and object tracking. Simulation results show that the proposed TAMF-SC framework outperforms representative baselines, achieving improved object tracking accuracy, measured by Mean Success Rate (MSR) and Mean Precision Rate (MPR), as well as high-fidelity fused image reconstruction under Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading channel scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Collaborative Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Anti-Jamming Communication in UAV-Assisted Data Collection Systems.
abstract: The advancement of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology has driven their widespread deployment as aerial relays for ground nodes (GNs) in jamming environments. However, dynamic jamming patterns and the inherent mobility of UAVs result in differentiated quality-of-service (QoS) for GNs in UAV-assisted data collection systems. We formulate a joint optimization problem that aims to maximize the fairness throughput of the system, subject to constraints on GNs association, UAV trajectory planning, and channel allocation. To address this problem, we develop a heuristic attention-enhanced QMIX (HAEQMIX) algorithm, which achieves GNs association through a heuristic fairness access method, and the attention-enhanced QMIX (AEQMIX) scheme adaptively aggregates heterogeneous node features for trajectory design and channel selection. Simulation results demonstrate that our algorithm exhibits superior anti-jamming capabilities and achieves the highest fairness throughput across various node densities, outperforming state-of-the-art works.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Light-Weight Low-Latency Transmission Mechanism for Reliable Wi-Fi Multicast.
abstract: Existing IEEE 802.11-based WLAN multicast techniques suffer from two critical limitations: poor reliability and low transmission rates. Numerous WLAN multicast protocols have been proposed to address these issues. However, these protocols are typically designed for video streaming applications and do not consider strict reliable transmission. They also fail to account for the presence of outlier nodes within multicast groups. In this paper, we proposed an innovative multicast transmission mechanism based on IEEE 802.11ac, called the Light-Weight Low-Latency Transmission Mechanism for Reliable Wi-Fi Multicast (LLRHM). It significantly improves reliable multicast efficiency through directional MCS probing, the outlier node identification, and a hybrid unicast-multicast transmission mechanism. Simulation results show that, compared with traditional multicast, LLRHM reduces average latency by up to 53.49% in the presence of one bottleneck or outlier node.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Age of Information in Short Packet Multi-Connectivity Links.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate multi-connectivity (MC) schemes in the context of status update systems with short payloads. We use the Age of Information (AoI) as the performance metric. Due to short payloads, transmission errors must be taken into account. In addition to the well-known schemes of packet duplication, message splitting, and multiplexing, we propose a codeword splitting scheme, in which each status update is jointly encoded across multiple channels. We derive closedform expressions for the average AoI for the different schemes and optimize their corresponding parameters. We show that the AoI of the multiplexing scheme is a convex function in the offset parameters and use this result to prove that for homogeneous channels, multiplexing outperforms packet duplication, and codeword splitting outperforms multiplexing. Analytical comparisons and numerical evaluations show that the codeword splitting scheme achieves the lowest average AoI when joint coding is feasible. In scenarios where joint coding is not feasible, whether message splitting or multiplexing results in a lower average AoI depends on the specific parameters.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Covertness Analysis in LEO Mega Constellations.
abstract: The aggregated interference from co-channel satellites in low earth orbit (LEO) mega constellations provides a shield to prevent signal detection by adversaries. In this paper, we propose an analytical framework to evaluate the fundamental covertness performance against the eavesdropper in LEO mega constellations with the aid of stochastic geometry. Specifically, the probability distribution of the interference power is first obtained via its Laplace transform, and then the covert probability is derived to characterize the transmission covertness. The results show an explicit relationship between the minimum covert probability and the transmit powers of satellite transmitter and interfering satellites, and reveal that the increasing altitude of the eavesdropper decreases the minimum covert probability.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Trajectory and Beamforming Design for Secure UAV Relay Communication Via Constrained Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) play a critical role in modern wireless communication systems. This study addresses the secrecy rate optimization problem in a UAVassisted relay system, where a UAV serves as a mobile relay to amplify and forward (AF) confidential information. To ensure quality of service (QoS) for legitimate users, a minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) threshold is introduced. However, these constraints significantly increase the complexity of the optimization problem. To tackle this challenge, we model the problem as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) and propose a solution using the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm augmented with a Lagrangian multiplier mechanism (SAC-Lag). This approach effectively learns cost functions to satisfy the constraints while optimizing the secrecy rate. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms benchmark algorithms by maintaining a high average secrecy rate and substantially reducing the duration of SINR constraint violations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Signal Augmentation and Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Automatic Modulation Classification.
