abstract: To address the challenge of limited labeled data in Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC), we propose a Signal Augmentation and Pseudo-labeling (SAP) framework for semi-supervised learning. The key problem lies in effectively utilizing both labeled and unlabeled signal data to improve classification accuracy across varying signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) levels. Existing semi-supervised methods often lack specifically designed augmentation techniques for signal samples and effective pseudo-label generation methods. SAP combines advanced data augmentation with pseudo-labeling strategies, enhancing feature extraction and achieving superior classification performance. Experimental results demonstrate that SAP outperforms existing semi-supervised techniques, achieving an overall accuracy of 56.07% and peaking at 83.31% at 8 dB SNR, thereby significantly advancing the adaptability and intelligence of modern communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multimodal Information Bottleneck Guided Task-Agnostic Semantic Communications.
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has shown great potential to improve communication efficiency and provide user-centric services by exploring semantic meanings behind digital bits. However, the performance of SemCom is highly dependent on the network design and training methods, which neglect the interaction between communications and intelligent tasks. Moreover, when the task changes, models have to be redesigned and updated. To overcome these issues, we propose a task-agnostic SemCom (TASC) framework that can handle diverse tasks with multiple modalities. Aiming to explore the interplay between communications and intelligent tasks from an information-theoretical perspective, we propose a multimodal information bottleneck (MIB) principle to learn minimal and sufficient unimodal and multimodal information effectively by discarding redundancy while preserving task-related information. Specifically, two MIB variants are presented, namely univocal MIB and syncretic MIB, to focus on different perspectives of information constraints. To further reduce the communication overhead, we develop an adaptive semantic feature transmission method by considering dynamic channel conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed TASC outperforms traditional communications as well as the specific SemCom system, and achieves better rate-distortion performance, validating the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed TASC.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Risk-Aware Learning for Digital Twin Placement in Non-Stationary Hierarchical Edge Computing.
abstract: A Digital Twin (DT) is a virtual replica of a physical system (PS), such as an Internet-of-Things (IoT) device, enabling the analysis and prediction of the PS's dynamics. To maintain accuracy, a DT frequently synchronizes with its PS, by processing status updates sent from the PS. Therefore, the incurred synchronization latency is impacted by both, communication and computation resources. Due to being computationally demanding, DTs are commonly hosted on edge servers (ESs) in Mobile Edge Computing (MEC). To increase scalability and flexibility of MEC systems, hierarchical architectures distribute computation resources across multiple tiers of ESs between base stations and cloud. Hierarchical MEC gives rise to the DT placement problem, i.e., the selection of an ES for hosting the DT. The selection must consider the synchronization latency, which should remain below critical thresholds to ensure DT accuracy and thus, successful synchronization. DT placement is challenging, because the synchronization latency is impacted by the dynamic and statistically non-stationary MEC system characteristics, such as communication channels and server loads. Furthermore, additional overhead is caused by migrating DTs between ESs. To address these challenges, we propose a novel risk-aware Multi-Armed Bandit algorithm that adapts to piece-wise stationary environments. Our approach minimizes synchronization cost, defined as a weighted sum of synchronization latency and energy consumption, while reducing the risk of synchronization failures and limiting DT migration overhead. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed algorithm achieves a similar synchronization cost, compared to state-of-the-art baselines, while achieving a significantly smaller synchronization failure rate and migration overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Towards a Mobile Network Measurement Suite for Remote Driving and Indoor Use Cases.
abstract: In this paper, we present a measurement suite designed for straightforward signal measurement campaigns in indoor environments that also allows precise localization of these measurements. The measurement suite is adapted specifically to facilitate both parking garages and floor environments, considering different characteristics of both settings. The indoor environment measurement framework builds upon the features of the open source Open Mobile Network Toolkit combined with the everguide indoor localization system. For indoor parking garages, our suite implements the Simple Network Management Protocol for network measurements, utilizing automotive LiDAR sensors for the localization task. Thereby, it can be used to survey networks for remote driving use cases. The system supports passive measuring of signal quality indicators such as RSSI, RSRQ and RSRP alongside network properties like CellID and PLMN. The evaluation of our concept for a measurement suite demonstrates its applicability across both environments, providing flexibility and reliability in diverse indoor settings.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Distributed Beamforming Design for User SINR Fairness in LEO Multi-Satellite Cooperative Systems.
abstract: Thanks to their seamless global coverage and highly flexible inter-satellite cooperation, cooperative Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations have emerged as a cornerstone for achieving ubiquitous 6G connectivity and represent a prominent research frontier in satellite communications. This paper studies a LEO multi-satellite cooperative downlink communication system. The system comprises multiple LEO satellites, all of which non-coherently transmit to all users located within the service region. In this setup, our objective is to maximize the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) at users, subject to the transmit power constraints at the satellites. Firstly, we propose a centralized precoding design based on a successive convex approximation (SCA). By introducing auxiliary variables, we transform the non-convex parts of the original problem into convex ones via Taylor approximation. On this basis, we combine the framework of SCA with alternative direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to design a distributed algorithm. Through simulations, we demonstrate that our designed distributed algorithm yields nearly identical optimal solutions to the centralized algorithm, all while achieving SINR fairness across users.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Diffusion-Driven Learning Framework for Enhanced Predictive Channel Modeling in 6G Wireless Communications.
abstract: To overcome the limitations of spatially sparse channel measurements and the poor generalization of conventional predictive models, this paper proposes a prior-enhanced predictive framework that integrates generative augmentation and prior-guided prediction within a unified architecture. We propose a space-time-frequency (STF) diffusion algorithm that generates synthetic channel data while preserving key statistical characteristics. Then we focus on a novel prior-aware prediction module that operates on a low-dimensional manifold extracted from measured channel state information. An innovative composite learning scheme is introduced, in which diffusion-generated structural priors are fused into the predictive pipeline, raising the accuracy limit of prediction and significantly improving robustness across diverse channel environments. Extensive experiments on real-world channel measurements further validate our approach, demonstrating its strong potential for advanced wireless communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Resource-Aware Federated 3D Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Scene Reconstruction.
abstract: Three-dimensional Gaussian splatting (3D-GS) has emerged as a promising technique for large-scale scene reconstruction due to its high rendering efficiency and fidelity. However, training large-scale 3D-GS models at wireless networks faces significant challenges due to limited communication, computation, and graphics processing unit (GPU) memory resources. This paper investigates a novel resource-aware federated learning framework for large-scale 3D-GS model training under such constraints. Specifically, we develop a latency- and memoryaware model lightweighting mechanism that adaptively selects and prunes Gaussian points to balance rendering quality and training overhead. Specifically, we quantitatively evaluate the importance of different Gaussian points and exploit a novel importance-to-latency ratio criterion to determine the optimal number of pruned points under memory and communication latency constraints. Extensive experiments on large-scale scenes show that the proposed design significantly accelerates convergence, maintains high rendering quality, and reduces training latency compared to state-of-the-art federated 3D-GS baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: AERO: Adaptive Semi-One-Class Ratio-Fusion Learning for Device-Free Robust Wireless Sensing.
abstract: Device-free human presence detection has attracted increasing attention in smart environments. However, existing supervised learning approaches require extensive labeled data, which limits scalability. While one-class classification methods alleviate this issue by relying primarily on empty-room data and detecting anomalies from human-induced fluctuations in wireless channel state information (CSI), their temporal robustness in long-term deployment remains largely underexplored. In this paper, we present AERO: Adaptive sEmi-one-class RatiO-fusion learning for robust device-free human presence detection. AERO introduces a two-stream autoencoder (AE) that jointly leverages CSI amplitude and phase, and a ratio-fusion mechanism that explicitly models their intrinsic physical relationship for richer and more discriminative feature learning. To mitigate time-varying CSI drift, AERO further incorporates a lightweight adaptive calibration strategy that continuously adjusts the decision boundary without retraining, ensuring robustness under long-term deployment. Extensive experiments in two distinct indoor environments demonstrate that AERO achieves average detection accuracies of 99.3 % in the bedroom and 95.3 % in the conference room. Compared with state-of-the-art benchmarks, AERO improves accuracy by approximately 10 % over C-MuRP, by 23 % over Deep-SVDD, and by up to 37 % over OC-SVM. These results confirm that AERO provides both superior accuracy and strong robustness, making it a practical and scalable solution for long-term device-free human presence detection using wireless signals.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Active RIS-Aided Secure ISAC with Artificial Noise for Sensing Performance Optimization.
abstract: This paper investigates physical layer security in active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems. We propose a secure transmission scheme exploiting the synergy between artificial noise (AN) and active RIS, in which the RIS amplification offsets the AN power overhead while the AN masks the information leakage risks that could be worsened by the amplification. The objective is to minimize the target's parameter estimation Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) under communication quality of service (QoS) and secrecy constraints. We develop an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm using semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and majorization-minimization (MM) methods, supplemented by a computational complexity analysis. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme surpasses passive RIS baselines in security performance, while also establishing a performance upper bound under the assumption of perfect channel state information (CSI) and revealing the inherent trade-off between sensing and security.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: LQC: Cross-Layer Congestion Control Algorithm Based on Online Learning and Driver-Queue.
abstract: With the rapid development of wireless and heterogeneous networks, traditional congestion control (CC) algorithms often struggle to adapt to time-varying wireless links and diverse application requirements. In recent years, learningbased CC approaches have demonstrated significant potential, but they still suffer from high overhead, slow convergence, and poor generalization to unknown network conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a cross-layer, two-level CC algorithm. The core idea is as follows: in user space, an online learning module leverages NIC driver residual queue length to quickly capture network states and application requirements, enabling adaptive adjustment to congestion trends; in kernel space, a classical congestion control algorithm is employed to fine-tune the congestion window (cwnd). These two levels of control work in coordination, allowing the sender to more promptly and accurately track time-varying wireless links and to achieve efficient transmission across diverse network scenarios. Experimental results on real Wi-Fi networks show that, under the same network conditions, LQC can improve throughput by up to$38.5 \%, 26.1 \%$, and 11.5% compared with Orca, BBR, and CUBIC, respectively, while reducing delay by up to 27.9%,$\mathbf{2 1. 0 \%}$, and$\mathbf{3 1. 9 \%}$.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: TD-PBFT: A TDMA-Assisted Fast and Reliable PBFT Consensus Algorithm for VANETs.
abstract: Data sharing in distributed connected vehicles faces security issues such as data forgery, which endangers road safety. Although solutions have been proposed based on the consensus algorithms such as practical Byzantine fault tolerance (PBFT), they rely on infrastructures and face challenges of a highly dynamic network topology, which leads to a low success ratio and high delay. Here, we propose the Time DivisionPBFT (TD-PBFT) algorithm that utilizes a distributed TDMA algorithm to coordinate the PBFT interaction process to achieve fast and reliable consensus for distributed connected vehicles. To improve the consensus speed, we design the temporary occupation method of the time slot as well as the leader node selection method based on the information of neighboring nodes and dynamically adjust the occupancy of the time slot for the nodes involved in the consensus. To improve the success ratio, we utilize the occupancy safety of time slot for selecting consensus nodes. We conduct theoretical analysis and extensive simulations to evaluate TD-PBFT. Simulation results show that the proposed TD-PBFT increases the success ratio by 26% and reduces the consensus delay by 35% compared to the original PBFT with TDMA.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Synchronization-Aware Cooperative MIMO for Kappa-Mu Faded Underwater Channels Using Hybrid Acoustic and Magnetic Induction.
abstract: Acoustic transmission is widely adopted for longrange underwater communications; however, its performance is constrained by the inherent limitations of narrow bandwidth, high delay, and strong multi-path sensitivity. Cooperative MIMO can enhance underwater data rates, but its deployment is limited by strict synchronization demands and severe multi-path effects in realistic underwater channels. This paper proposes a synchronization-aware cooperative MIMO framework for kappamu shadowed underwater channels using a hybrid acoustic and magnetic-induction (MI) architecture. An MI-based master-slave mechanism enables precise timing and frequency alignment, while a kappa-mu shadow fading model with synchronization error representation is established. The framework integrates STBC encoding, MRC reception, and closed-form BER and capacity analysis. Simulation results confirm that the hybrid approach enhances reliability and throughput over purely acoustic systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: REM-Diff: Conditional Diffusion for UAV-Based Radio Map Construction in Urban Environments.
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of wireless devices and the increasing scarcity of spectrum resources, efficient spectrum utilization and intelligent management have become critical research topics. One promising approach involves constructing a comprehensive Radio Environment Map (REM) from a limited number of Received Signal Strength (RSS) measurements. Inspired by the recent success of generative AI, we propose REM-Diff, a novel diffusion model-based framework for REM construction conditioned on environmental context. Our approach integrates observed RSS data, building layout information, and sampling masks as conditional inputs to guide the generation process. A U-Net architecture is trained to predict the noise added during the diffusion steps. Furthermore, we adopt the Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model (DDIM) to accelerate the sampling process during inference. Additionally, we have developed an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) trajectory simulation algorithm to generate diverse sampling patterns for synthetic datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that REM-Diff achieves superior accuracy compared to baseline methods, particularly under severely sparse and non-uniform sampling conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy Minimization of Connectivity-Aware Cargo Unmanned Aerial Vehicles.
abstract: In this paper, we study a cellular-connected unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted cargo delivery system. Benefiting from the wide distribution of cellular base stations (BSs), the delivery of cargoes by cellular-connected UAV is expected to break through the dilemma of the limited flight range of traditional point-to-point communication UAV. However, there are two main challenges at present, namely: 1) The signal generated by the cellular BSs cannot cover all the low-altitude airspace, and the UAV cannot guarantee the cellular communication connection all the time. 2) When the UAV serves multiple users, it is difficult to plan the delivery sequence of cargoes to minimize the energy consumption of the UAV. To solve this problem, we propose a two-step algorithm. Initially, the ant colony optimization for energy consumption minimization (ACO-ECM) is proposed to obtain the cargo delivery sequence. Next, we use the rapidly-exploring random trees star (RRT*) algorithm to optimize the trajectory to ensure the communication connection of the UAV. The numerical results show that the proposed algorithm can ensure the communication connectivity of UAV while reducing the energy consumption of UAV by about$\mathbf{1 0 \% - 3 5 \%}$compared with the benchmark algorithm.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Age-Driven Joint Optimization for UAV Swarms via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Real-time monitoring in remote areas presents critical challenges for time-sensitive missions such as emergency response and disaster surveillance, necessitating autonomous UAV swarms with stringent information timeliness requirements. For this end, we adopt a Leader-Follower UAV swarm architecture, in which Follower UAVs act as both sensing platforms and communication relays, thereby establishing a fully airborne network without reliance on ground infrastructure. To enhance information timeliness, we adopt an age-driven formulation quantified by the Age of Information (AoI), within which sampling decisions, buffer scheduling, and routing selection are jointly optimized under dynamic topology and partial observability. Accordingly, we model this problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP), and develop an enhanced multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithm that employs specialized policy networks to decompose coupled decision-making into coordinated sub-tasks. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed approach significantly reduces average AoI compared to baseline algorithms while maintaining competitive performance in conventional network metrics including packet delivery ratio (PDR) and throughput.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Generalizing the Outage Minimization Problem in Wireless Random Caching: An Alpha Utility Perspective for Managing Content Popularity-QoS Disparity.
abstract: The swift advancement of wireless edge caching is important for enabling a wide range of timely wireless delivery services, including video content, datasets, prompts for generative contents, etc. However, the majority of existing studies concentrate on optimizing cache hit rates or cache outage probability, resulting in limited investigation into the performance bottleneck brought by the disparity between content popularity and Quality-of-Service (QoS) requirements for wireless contents delivery. Motivated by this, we tackle this fundamental yet overlooked disparity problem in the scenario of wireless random caching (WRC) networks. Particularly, we first reformulate the classical system outage probability (SOP) minimization problem, revealing that this optimal SOP is upper bounded by a MaxMin problem of this disparity. Then, we propose a novel reconstruction and generalization of this classical SOP minimization using the alpha-utility. This generalization innovatively employs the tunable parameter, alpha, which systematically controls the trade-off between two conflicting objectives: the optimization of the Physical Performance Indicator (PPI) and the SOP minimization. Subsequently, to obtain the optimal solution under this new generalized framework, we propose a novel and efficient Bisection-based joint Popularity and PPI-aware Random Caching Algorithm (BPRCA). Numerical simulations validate our analyses, demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed BPRCA in adjusting the intended performance trade-off while maintaining low algorithmic complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Joint Optimization Transmission Scheme Based on BATS Code for Multipath Transmission.
abstract: Multipath transmission, an effective low-latency technology, has been widely adopted in wireless networks such as the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). However, in resource-constrained multi-hop erasure networks, conventional retransmissions and network coding fail to improve multipath transmission performance effectively. In such scenarios, batched sparse (BATS) code provides an efficient solution thanks to its superior performance. In this paper, we apply BATS code to multipath transmission and propose three schemes, with particular emphasis on a joint optimization scheme (JOMP-BATS). This scheme jointly optimizes the degree distributions across multiple paths based on packet loss and transmission rate of each path. Furthermore, it leverages the decoding information exchange across batches from different paths in the BP decoding process to reduce transmission overhead. To evaluate the decoding performance, we extend the And-Or tree analysis to derive the asymptotic decoding probability. Then, we construct a linear optimization model for finite input packets to find the optimal degree distribution for each path. Simulation results show that the JOMP-BATS scheme outperforms other proposed schemes in terms of transmission overhead and delay with the same decoding objective. In the multipath transmission scenarios with heterogeneous packet loss and transmission rates, this scheme effectively improves overall transmission performance by coordinating multiple paths.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Covertness and Secrecy Design for Wireless Communications Under Active Attacks.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the covertness and secrecy of wireless communications under an active attacker scenario, where attackers perform simultaneous detection/eavesdropping and jamming. To guarantee the covertness and secrecy of transmissions, both detection and eavesdropping attacks are mitigated using physical layer security techniques. To depict the covertness and secrecy performance of the system, we model the covertness outage probability and the secrecy outage probability, and then analytically characterize the optimal covert secrecy rate (CSR) under an artificial noise (AN)-based transmission scheme. Extensive numerical results demonstrate the achievable CSR performance and reveal the impact of active attacks on system security in the context of the AN-based scheme.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: UAV-Enabled Covert and Secure Communication Against Cooperative Detection and Eavesdropping.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DEEL: Diffusion-Enhanced Energy and Latency Trade-Off for Low-Altitude Emergency Networks.
abstract: In post-disaster scenarios where terrestrial infrastructure is destroyed, Low-Altitude Emergency Networks, which are a critical application of Low-Altitude Intelligent Networks (LAIN), offer a rapidly deployable and resilient solution. Leveraging their mobility and Line-of-Sight (LoS) capabilities, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) serve as essential nodal platforms. However, their operation face a fundamental trade-off between limited battery endurance and stringent low-latency service demands. Existing studies often optimize energy efficiency and latency reduction separately or rely on rigid linear weighting schemes, limiting adaptability. To address this, we jointly optimize UAV trajectories, task allocation, and resource management using a multi-objective multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework enhanced by a Generative Diffusion Model. This integration enables efficient exploration in high-dimensional, dynamic environments, producing Pareto-optimal policies that balance energy consumption and delay. Simulations demonstrate superior convergence stability, strong adaptability to diverse operational preferences, and a substantial system cost reduction of up to 62.68%.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: PowerCloak: Differential Privacy-Based Power Perturbation for Location Privacy in UAV-Enabled Wireless Powered Communication Networks.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs) require UAVs to acquire the location of ground user equipments (UEs) via localization technologies. However, the untrustworthiness of UAVs raises serious location privacy concerns. In this paper, we propose PowerCloak, a truncation differential privacy (DP)-based power perturbation mechanism for location privacy protection. PowerCloak perturbs the UE's transmit power during UAV-based UE localization by injecting artificially controllable Gaussian noise, and further truncates the perturbed power within a realistic range$\left[P_{\min}, P_{\max}\right]$to avoid exposing the perturbation behavior. PowerCloak interferes with the UAV's received signal strength (RSS) measurements, thereby increasing the uncertainty of the estimated UE position. On this basis, we reveal and analyze an intrinsic connection between the properties of Gaussian noise and DP. We then formally prove that PowerCloak satisfies$\epsilon$DP guarantees. We evaluate the location privacy protection level by deriving the position error bound (PEB). Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed PowerCloak effectively enhances the UE location privacy while imposing only comparatively small impacts on communication performance and the amount of replenished energy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Structure-Aware Grouping with Adaptive Greedy Scheduling for Belief Propagation in Loopy Graphs.
abstract: Belief Propagation (BP) on factor graphs with dense periodic short cycles is a fundamental challenge, leading to poor convergence and high error floors. The maximumlength sequence (m sequence) factor graph, a special LDPClike structure with critical applications in 5 G NR, provides a canonical exemplar of this challenge. While conventional BP schedules fail due to message oscillations, even advanced Informed Dynamic Scheduling (IDS) algorithms are impaired by greedy-group and silent-variable-node phenomena. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Adaptive Greedy Group Layered Decoding (A-GGLD) algorithm. The proposed algorithm uniquely combines a Structure-Aware Check-Node Grouping Framework (SACGF) to disrupt feedback cycles with an Adaptive Greedy Scheduling Mechanism (AGSM) and Message Damping Mechanism (MDM) to ensure stable convergence. As a result, AGGLD not only significantly reduces computational complexity compared to conventional IDS methods but also achieves a nearly 2.7 times lower error floor and reaches a target Bit Error Rate (BER) of 10−5with a 0.7 dB gain over the best-performing algorithm. This work thereby establishes a novel paradigm for decoders to tackle the fundamental challenge of periodic cycles in general LDPC factor graphs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hilbert-Wavelet Signal Representation and Supervised Contrastive Learning for Robust Cross-Day WiFi Authentication.
abstract: WiFi device authentication at the physical layer remains challenging because wireless channels vary with time and environment. This paper proposes a robust framework that integrates Hilbert-Wavelet signal representation with supervised contrastive (SupCon) learning to achieve robust cross-day WiFi authentication. We first apply the Hilbert transform to convert In-phase and Quadrature (IQ) samples into analytic signals, and then employ wavelet thresholding to obtain denoised envelope features that emphasize hardware-induced fingerprints while reducing noise. We further design a multi-modal framework that combines raw IQ, envelope, spectrogram, and scalogram representations with SupCon earning to improve authentication accuracy. Extensive experiments on a large-scale public WiFi dataset validated the effectiveness of the proposed framework, where it improved average cross-day accuracy by 14.6% over convolutional neural network (CNN) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) baselines and achieved consistent gains across precision, recall, and F1-score, demonstrating robustness in wireless environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Towards Native Intelligence: 6G-LLM Trained with Reinforcement Learning from NDT Feedback.
abstract: Owing to its comprehensive understanding of upperlayer application requirements and the capabilities of practical communication systems, the 6G-LLM (6G domain large language model) offers a promising pathway toward realizing network native intelligence. Serving as the system orchestrator, the 6G-LLM drives a paradigm shift that fundamentally departs from existing rule-based approaches, which primarily rely on modular, experience-driven optimization. By contrast, the 6G-LLM substantially enhances network flexibility and adaptability. Nevertheless, current efforts to construct 6G-LLMs are constrained by their reliance on large-scale, meticulously curated, humanauthored corpora, which are impractical to obtain in real-world scenarios. Moreover, purely offline-trained models lack the capacity for continual self-improvement, limiting their ability to adapt to the highly dynamic requirements of wireless communication environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel training paradigm termed RLDTF (Reinforcement Learning from Digital Twin Feedback) for 6G-LLMs. This framework leverages network digital twins to generate reward signals based on orchestration outcomes, while employing reinforcement learning to guide the model toward optimal decision-making dynamically. Furthermore, we introduce a weighted token mechanism to improve output accuracy. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that our proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in orchestration accuracy and solution optimality.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Ray Antenna Array Enhanced Low-Altitude ISAC: Performance Analysis and Beamforming Design.
abstract: The low-altitude economy (LAE) heavily relies on aerial vehicles, yet these platforms remain vulnerable to environmental and security risks, necessitating robust airspace monitoring. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) as one of the key technologies of 6G provides potential solutions for safe LAE. However, conventional antenna arrays face limitations in cost, scalability, and coverage, especially directly above the base station, due to hardware complexity and degraded angular resolution. By exploiting the recently proposed ray antenna array (RAA), this paper considers a RAA-enhanced low-altitude ISAC system. RAA architecture employs multiple ray-arranged arrays directly connected without phase shifters, significantly reducing hardware costs while supporting flexible beamforming via dynamic ray selection. Moreover, RAA can provide uniform angular resolution and eliminates coverage holes, making it particularly suitable for low-altitude ISAC. In this paper, we formulate an optimization problem for joint ray selection and beamforming to enhance sensing coverage under communication constraints. An efficient alternating optimization algorithm is proposed to solve this problem. Analytical and simulation results demonstrate that RAA achieves higher sensing signal-to-noise ratio compared to traditional arrays, offering a cost-effective and high-performance solution for achieving low-altitude ISAC.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Channel-Aware OTA Diagnosis of a Defective Cluster in RIS via Noisy Twenty Questions.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) are envisioned as a key enabler for 6 G networks; however, they are susceptible to clustered hardware impairments. Traditional circuit-level element-wise diagnosis approaches are invasive and infeasible for RIS with a large number of elements. In this paper, we propose a channel-aware over-the-air (OTA) diagnosis framework that localizes the boundaries of a contiguous cluster of defective RIS elements using one-bit feedback. Specifically, we first propose a dual-slot pilot transmission protocol to extract the responses of defective elements from the measurement signals. Subsequently, we formulate the boundary localization problem as a noisy twenty questions problem, and develop a dyadic posterior matching (DyaPM) algorithm to solve the resultant problem with logarithmic complexity. Furthermore, we incorporate an SNR-dependent probability of lie into the DyaPM algorithm to improve belief updates, which is in contrast to prior works that rely on a fixed probability of lie. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed diagnosis framework enables a correct detection probability exceeding 90 % even at an SNR of$-15 \mathbf{~ d B}$and asymptotically approaches the efficiency of the noiseless bisection search as the SNR improves.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: APFLy: A UAV Trajectory Optimization Algorithm via Artificial Potential Field for IoT Data Collection.
abstract: Recently frequent natural disasters such as floods, wildfires, and earthquakes could make traditional ground communication network damaged, resulting in “information isolated island”. To this end, we propose a lightweight and efficient unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory optimization algorithm-APFly, for the post-disaster IoT data collection task. APFly combines artificial potential field (APF) with dynamic bandwidth allocation and real-time speed control for the first time, achieving a joint optimization of data collection and resource conservation. By mapping the remaining data of nodes and the channel capacity into a continuous field, APFly can guide the UAV to adjust its speed in real time, and dynamically allocate bandwidth based on OFDM technology to achieve parallel communication among multi-nodes. The algorithm complexity is linear$\mathbf{O}(N K)$and is suitable for environments with limited computing resources after disasters. The simulation results show that, compared with the traditional methods, APFly can save energy consumption, task finish time and path length by up to$\mathbf{5 3. 9 \%, ~ 5 4. 3 \%}$and 49.8%, and has good real-time performance and scalability.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Spectrum and Device State-Aware Anti-Jamming Resource Allocation for Dynamic Uav Networks.
abstract: Securing communication links against malicious jamming has become critical with the widespread deployment of mobile unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks. However, most existing UAV network anti-jamming methods rely solely on spectrum observations, overlooking the channel aging phenomenon induced by high mobility of UAVs. This paper presents a new joint spectrum and power allocation anti-jamming scheme based on the spectrum and device state-aware dueling double deep Qnetwork (SDSA-DDQN) for dynamic UAV networks. First, we construct a high-fidelity dynamic UAV environment model to simulate realistic non-linear link outages by incorporating the channel aging mechanism and a Sigmoid-based reliability factor. Using this model, the anti-jamming resource allocation problem is formulated as a Stackelberg game. To extract multi-modal features, we design a hybrid dueling network utilizing a parallel convolutional neural network (CNN) and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) architecture. We fuse spectrum observations with device mobility states and thus, the agent can effectively decouple aging-induced errors from interference. Finally, we integrate the double DQN framework with the prioritized experience replay (PER) mechanism. As a result, value overestimation can be mitigated and training convergence is significantly accelerated. Simulation results demonstrate that our scheme offers significant advantages over the state of the art in terms of convergence speed and system utility.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: WVSC: Wireless Video Semantic Communication with Multi-Frame Compensation.
abstract: Existing wireless video transmission schemes directly conduct video coding in pixel level, while neglecting the inner semantics contained in videos. In this paper, we propose a wireless video semantic communication framework, abbreviated as WVSC, which integrates the idea of semantic communication into wireless video transmission scenarios. WVSC first encodes original video frames as semantic frames and then conducts video coding based on such compact representations, enabling the video coding in semantic level rather than pixel level. Moreover, to further reduce the communication overhead, a reference semantic frame is introduced to substitute motion vectors of each frame in common video coding methods. At the receiver, multi-frame compensation (MFC) is proposed to produce compensated current semantic frame with a multi-frame fusion attention module. With both the reference frame transmission and MFC, the bandwidth efficiency improves with satisfying video transmission performance. Experimental results verify the performance gain of WVSC over other DL-based methods e.g. DVSC about 1 dB and traditional schemes about 2 dB in terms of PSNR.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MML-Based 3D Channel Fingerprints Construction for Low-Altitude Communications.
abstract: Low-altitude communication systems function as key enablers for the evolution toward 6 G wireless networks. As an emerging technology for low-altitude transmission, 3D channel fingerprints (3D-CF) are capable of supporting the acquisition of channel state information (CSI), eliminating redundant channel estimations and reducing computational overhead. In this paper, we propose a multimodal learning (MML)-based framework to construct 3D-CF. Specifically, we first model 3D-CF as a collection of CSI-tuples, with each tuple containing the position of a low-altitude vehicle (LAV) and its associated statistical CSI. Then, given the different data modalities of prior information such as LAV positions, CSI measurements, and geographic environment maps, the 3D-CF construction problem is framed as a multimodal regression task. Accordingly, we propose an efficient multimodal architecture that is modularized to process data with heterogeneous structures, which comprises a correlation-based multimodal fusion (Corr-MMF) module, a multimodal representation (MMR) module, and a CSI regression (CSI-R) module. Finally, the complexity of the proposed algorithm is analyzed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves higher 3D-CF construction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods for various communication scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: In-Orbit Collaborative Computing Method for Real-Time Tasks in Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks.
abstract: With the rapid evolution of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite Internet, onboard intelligent applications impose increasingly stringent requirements on real-time task processing capability. However, a systematic theoretical basis for determining the minimum collaborative computing resources required to satisfy given reliability constraints is still lacking. To address this issue, this paper proposes a modeling and analytical framework for inorbit collaborative computing of real-time tasks. A dual-layer satellite architecture with functional separation is considered, where one layer is responsible for remote sensing and task triggering, while the other layer provides distributed computing resources for collaborative processing. By integrating a marked Poisson point process, a coupling model between collaborative node scale and spatial beam coverage is established. Based on Amdahl's law, a parallel processing model is then developed to characterize the relationship between collaborative node count and task latency. Closed-form expressions for the minimum required number of collaborative nodes and the corresponding optimal satellite search radius under quality-of-service constraints are derived. Monte Carlo simulations validate the accuracy of the proposed model. The results quantitatively characterize the relationship between task reliability requirements and satellite parameters, providing theoretical support for resource planning and rapid resource bounding in satellite networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Vision-Augmented LLM for Communication Beam Steering Compensation.
abstract: High altitude platform (HAP) millimeter wave (mmWave) links are sensitive to wind-induced attitude shaking. Small roll, pitch, or yaw tilts will misalign narrow communication beams and markedly reduce the gain of the array antenna. In this paper, we propose a vision-augmented large language model (VA-LLM) that forecasts short-horizon attitudes and pre-steers communication beams before misalignment occurs. Specifically, we design a five-channel vision module to render multivariate flight data into pseudo-RGB images with reversible instance normalization (RevIN) and backbone-aligned normalization. We design a learned cross-variable attention (CVA) branch to condense intra-timestep channel relations into a compact token set. Concurrently, we explore a time-series-aware prompt-as-prefix (PaP) to inject frequency, amplitude, and top-$K$-based periodic statistics from the input flight-data window into the token set. After fusing vision-augmented, learned, and text tokens, a frozen LLM refines the representation; a lightweight temporal mixer with axis-wise heads directly regresses future roll/pitch/yaw, which are mapped to continuous steering angles for the array antenna. On real flight test data, VA-LLM improves the average signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR)-type array-gain ratio by 6.56 % over the baseline, achieves a 7.31 % gain over the baseline at the 12step horizon, and yields up to 14.10 % gains over the ablations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: SAASN: A Spatially-Aware Adaptive Scheduling Network for Large-Scale Multi-UAV Tasking.
abstract: Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a potent paradigm for large-scale multi-UAV task scheduling. However, existing frameworks often suffer from static architectures lacking adaptive reasoning and inefficient, fixed-rhythm training strategies. To address this, we introduce the Spatially-Aware Adaptive Scheduling Network (SAASN), a hierarchical DRL framework overcoming these limitations via synergistic, adaptive mechanisms. First, we design a novel allocator featuring a Global-Local Fusion Gate, which dynamically arbitrates between sparse local attention and dense global attention to enable a more robust and flexible spatial representation. Second, we enhance the planner with a Value-Weighted Depotcentric Context Module, imbuing the agent with an economic awareness that leads to more profitable routing decisions. Finally, we develop an advanced Policy Diagnosis-driven Asynchronous Training Curriculum (PSATS), which intelligently governs the hierarchical learning process by diagnosing the allocator's policy state to trigger the planner's training asynchronously and to dynamically adapt training parameters. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SAASN establishes a new state-of-the-art, significantly outperforming strong baselines in solution quality and training efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Secrecy Rate Maximization for IRS-Aided MIMO Systems via Unfolded Product Riemannian Gradient Descent Network.
abstract: This paper investigates the secrecy rate (SR) maximization problem in intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The problem is non-convex, and existing optimization and deep learning methods often suffer from slow convergence and limited interpretability. To overcome these issues, we propose a model-driven network based on deep unfolding, termed the unfolded product Riemannian gradient descent network (UPRGD-Net). Specifically, we first develop an efficient PRGD algorithm to solve the SR maximization problem, and then unfold its iterations into trainable network layers. The step sizes, which are crucial for both convergence and performance, are treated as learnable parameters and optimized in an unsupervised manner. By learning the step sizes, our approach not only accelerates convergence but also improves model interpretability. Numerical results show that UPRGD-Net outperforms conventional optimization and learning-based methods in SR performance and computational efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Service-Aware Adaptive Beam-Hopping Scheduling for Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks.
abstract: LEO satellite communication serves as a key technology for global wireless coverage, with its performance heavily dependent on efficient beam scheduling. To address the challenges of unknown service distribution and resource constraints in practical systems, this paper proposes a service-aware adaptive beam-hopping scheme. By integrating satellite image feature extraction with deep reinforcement learning based on a generalized memory pool, we innovatively achieve adaptive beam scheduling under unknown cell service demand conditions. The proposed method employs pre-trained ResNet and variational autoencoders to extract image features that implicitly characterize service demands, while utilizing a generalized memory pool to enhance algorithm performance. Simulation results demonstrate that under unknown distribution conditions, the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms traditional methods in both throughput and delay performance, achieving approximately 39.1% reward improvement and reaching 75.2% of the theoretical upper bound, while simultaneously meeting the computational latency requirements for onboard real-time decision-making.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Beamforming and Time-Slot Allocation for Spectrum Sharing in Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: The integration of satellite and terrestrial networks can provide ubiquitous connectivity and efficient spectrum utilization. This paper investigates a spectrum sharing scenario for satellite and terrestrial downlinks. Terrestrial users (TUs) are directly served by small base stations (SBSs) and coexist with satellite users (SUs) under a time division multiple access (TDMA) protocol. To address the severe co-channel interference between satellite and terrestrial transmissions, we formulate a joint beamforming and time slot scheduling problem, aiming to maximize the weighted sum rates of the SU and TU. This problem is highly non-convex due to the coupling between the continuous beamforming vectors and the discrete scheduling variables. To address this challenge, we develop an alternating optimization framework. Specifically, the beamforming subproblem is solved via successive convex approximation (SCA) and second-order cone (SOC) reformulation, while the time slot scheduling subproblem is addressed via integer linear programming (ILP). Simulation results demonstrate that this approach significantly improves the achievable sum rate compared to traditional schemes while ensuring fairness between satellite and terrestrial users.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Multi-Objective Topology Optimization Scheme for MEO/LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: Double-Layer Satellite Networks (DLSNs), which integrate Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) and Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, offer enhanced capabilities for global coverage and resilient communications. This paper investigates the InterLayer Links (ILLs) assignment problem, explicitly considering the disruptive impact of Sun Transit Outage (STO). The problem is formulated as a multi-objective optimization model that aims to minimize both the link switching frequency and the load transmission level. To solve it, a Multi-Objective Topology Allocation (MOTA) algorithm based on particle swarm optimization is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MOTA algorithm significantly outperforms other benchmarks. Specifically, it effectively mitigates STO impact, achieving a lower residual load in LEO and a higher successfully transmitted load to MEO.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Single-UAV Synthetic-Aperture Passive Localization via Spatial Vector Backprojection.
abstract: High-precision passive localization with a single airborne platform remains challenging due to low SNR, navigation errors, and attitude jitter. Traditional single-UAV methods suffer from limited accuracy and weak elevation observability, while multi-UAV schemes—though improving geometry—introduce synchronization and configuration constraints. To address these issues, this paper proposes a spatial-vector backprojection(SVBP) algorithm for single-aircraft, single-antenna passive localization. Exploiting platform motion to form a virtual synthetic aperture, SV-BP builds a trajectory-consistent spatial guidance vector directly from the measured flight path and performs coherent backprojection via subspace projection over the region of interest, enabling high-precision localization. The scene is parameterized by slant range and squint angle, and solved with a compact coarse-to-fine$R-\theta$search that reduces computational load while preserving resolution. Simulations demonstrate marked accuracy gains over representative singlestation methods and strong robustness to YPR(yaw, pitch, and roll) jitter and navigation perturbations, indicating promising potential for onboard, real-time deployment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Pseudo-Random Asynchronous Multi-Satellite Cooperative Transmission Scheme for Cohesive Clustered Satellite Networks.
abstract: Asynchronous interference mitigation has great potential for efficient multi-satellite cooperative transmission (MSCT) in cohesive clustered satellite networks. In this paper, we propose a pseudo-random asynchronous MSCT (PRA-MSCT) scheme to enhance the ergodic sum rate of asynchronous MSCT. We design a normalized waiting delay control mechanism to reshape the delay difference between satellites and user equipment (UEs), thereby maximizing the benefits of time asynchrony to mitigate inter- and intra-satellite asynchronous interference. We formulate an optimization problem for cooperative precoding and delay control to maximize the ergodic sum rate under power constraint of satellites. To address the decision coupling that complicates optimal problem-solving, we propose a graph neural network (GNN)-empowered PRA-MSCT approach, enabling satellites to make autonomous decisions based on their local observations. Simulation results demonstrate that the PRAMSCT scheme significantly improves the sum rate and computation efficiency compared to existing asynchronous MSCT schemes. Additionally, the GNN-empowered cooperative precoding approach can be applied effectively to both synchronous and asynchronous scenarios, with or without delay control.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Layered High-Definition Map Delivery: Accuracy-Aware Transmission via Cooperative V2X.
abstract: High-Definition (HD) maps play a vital role in ensuring safe autonomous driving. Although HD maps can provide high-accuracy information, they contain significantly larger data volumes, leading to high communication requirements and increased transmission latency for resource-constrained vehicular networks. At the same time, the high mobility of vehicles results in rapidly varying channel status, which would hinder the timely delivery of maps. To address these challenges, an accuracy-aware HD map transmission scheme is proposed to enable the timely delivery of layered maps via cooperative vehicle-to-everything (V2X) links, including vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communications. Specifically, to evaluate the accuracy of maps delivered to vehicles, an Average Map Accuracy Level (AMAL) function is defined, and a latency-constrained AMAL maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize transmission link selection and HD map layer allocation accordingly. To identify optimal transmission links, a dynamic sub-topology extraction algorithm is designed, which can reduce the complexity of link selection. Theoretical analysis proves that selecting links within the sub-topology can improve the accuracy level of transmitted maps. Based on these optimal links, an accuracy-aware map assignment algorithm is developed to maximize the AMAL under latency constraints, and its solution is proven to be optimal. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme can significantly enhance the AMAL and the weighted service ratio, while maintaining high computational efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: NLOS-Identified RSS Localization via Enzyme Action Optimization.
abstract: With the continuous advancement of the 6th generation (6G) communication technology, the demand for locationbased services (LBS) has become critical. As a mainstream technique in wireless localization, received signal strength (RSS) localization has received significant attention. However, most existing RSS-based methods cannot obtain effective positioning in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environments due to the multipath effect. In this paper, a new NLOS-identified RSS positioning method via Enzyme Action Optimization (EAO) is proposed. We first derive a signal detection theory-based NLOS identification criterion by leveraging multiple RSS measurements. Depending on the prior probabilities information, the Generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) and Neyman-Pearson (NP) criterion are respectively adopted to derive the decision criterion. Then, we propose an EAO-based RSS (EAO-RSS) positioning algorithm. The algorithm mimics the binding and catalytic processes of enzymes with substrates to dynamically adjust candidate estimates in search of the global optimum. As a result, accurate RSS-based localization can be achieved under NLOS condition. Simulation results show that the proposed method can improve positioning accuracy by more than 3.85% compared with the state-of-the-art.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Joint Access Control and Resource Allocation Scheme for LEO Satellite Network.
abstract: With the increase requirements of global seamless coverage, the low earth orbit (LEO) networks have become a vital part of the sixth generation (6G) network due to the advantages of wide coverage over the earth and relatively low latency. However, LEO networks still suffer the critical issue on multi-user access control and resource allocation. In this paper, we formulate an optimization problem of joint access control and resource allocation in LEO satellite scenarios to improve system throughput and avoid frequent handovers of ground users, which is non-deterministic polynomial-time hard (NP-hard). To solve this formulated challenging problem, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based framework which employs proximal policy optimization (PPO) and introduces the long short-term memory (LSTM) layers to capture the time-dependent features of satellite trajectories. The simulation results have demonstrated the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed algorithm compared to benchmark schemes in addressing the access control and resource allocation issue.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Movable Arrays of Rydberg Sensors: Modelling and Optimization.
abstract: Movable antenna arrays are a new paradigm that offers enhanced performance to future wireless systems. Compared to a fixed array, the flexibility and reconfigurability of a movable antenna array enables better performance in detecting signals with multiple carrier frequencies and from various directions. The Rydberg atomic sensor is another emerging optical technology that is sensitive to radio frequency (RF) signals. Capitalizing on its portability and the ability to detect signals with multiple carrier frequencies, the Rydberg sensor is a promising device for movable arrays. As the first paper to study the combination of atomic sensors and movable antenna arrays, we propose two new algorithms (golden-Search algorithm and basic firefly algorithm) to control the design of a two-dimensional (2-D) movable Rydberg sensor array. In addition, we also propose the novel boost-firefly method to enhance the design of two or more subarrays for decoding different carrier frequencies simultaneously. Simulation results reveal that the proposed algorithms can achieve better performance for both single array and multiple subarray designs compared to fixed array and randomly-designed array benchmarks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Domain-Adaptive mmWave Radar for Contactless Sleep Apnea Detection.
abstract: Non-contact sleep apnea (SA) detection using millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar is a promising solution for long-term home monitoring but faces significant challenges from cross-domain variability and signal heterogeneity. This paper presents UCRDA, an unsupervised domain adaptation framework designed to bridge the gap between reliable contact-based physiological signals and noisy mmWave radar data. To tackle the semantic instability of noisy radar signals, we propose a prototype-based contrastive learning mechanism that extracts discriminative semantic representations within each domain. We further introduce a nearest-neighbor cross-domain alignment module to explicitly enforce category-level consistency between the source and target domains without requiring target labels. Additionally, gradient reversal-based adversarial learning is employed to suppress domain- and clinical-variable-related confounding factors, promoting domain-invariant feature representations. Evaluations on the large-scale MESA and OMuSense23 datasets demonstrate that UCRDA achieves superior classification accuracy and robustness compared to existing baselines, paving the way for reliable contactless SA screening. Code is available at: https://github.com/eecdxu/UCRDA.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fluid Antenna-Enhanced Flexible Beamforming.
abstract: Fluid antenna systems encompass a broad class of reconfigurable antenna technologies that offer substantial spatial diversity for various optimization objectives and communication tasks. Their capability to enhance spatial resolution within a fixed physical aperture makes fluid antennas particularly attractive for next-generation wireless deployments. In this work, we focus on the beamforming problem using a two-dimensional planar fluid antenna array. Since both narrow-beam and broad-beam patterns are essential in practical communication networks, enabling flexible beamforming through fluid antennas becomes an important and interesting research direction. We establish a unified and flexible framework that connects arbitrary beam-pattern synthesis with fluid-antenna port selection. The resulting formulation transforms beam-pattern reconstruction into a sparse regression problem, which is addressed using a tailored compressive sensing algorithm designed to operate efficiently with the fast Fourier transform (FFT). Furthermore, to ensure physically consistent phase modeling in the desired beam, we introduce an iterative FFT-based phase retrieval method. Owing to its structure, the proposed phase-refinement procedure exhibits low computational complexity and rapid convergence, requiring only one FFT and one inverse FFT per iteration. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed flexible beamforming framework. Compared with conventional fixed-array architectures, fluid antennas exhibit significantly improved beam-pattern reconstruction accuracy, highlighting their potential for high-resolution and adaptive beamforming in future wireless systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: On Performance of Fluid Antenna Relay (FAR)-Assisted AAV-NOMA Wireless Network.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the performance of a fluid antenna relay (FAR)-assisted downlink communication system utilizing non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). The FAR, which integrates a fluid antenna system (FAS), is equipped on an autonomous aerial vehicle (AAV), and introduces extra degrees of freedom to improve the performance of the system. The transmission is divided into a first phase from the base station (BS) to the users and the FAR, and a second phase where the FAR forwards the signal using amplify-and-forward (AF) or decode-and-forward (DF) relaying to reduce the outage probability (OP) for the user maintaining weaker channel conditions. To analyze the OP performance of the weak user, Copula theory and the Gaussian copula function are employed to model the statistical distribution of the FAS channels. Analytical expressions for weak user's OP are derived for both the AF and the DF schemes. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, showing that it consistently outperforms benchmark schemes without the FAR. In addition, numerical simulations also demonstrate the values of the relaying scheme selection parameter under different FAR positions and communication outage thresholds.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Semantic Communication-Enabled Cooperative BEV Semantic Segmentation Frame in Internet of Vehicles.
abstract: The precision of Bird's Eye View (BEV) semantic segmentation directly affects the decision-making reliability of autonomous driving systems. However, existing methods encounter significant challenges in feature redundancy suppression, channel robustness enhancement, and multi-vehicle feature alignment. To tackle these issues, this paper presents a Semantic Communication-Enabled Cooperative BEV Semantic Segmentation Framework (SCC-BEVSS). First, we establish a variational optimization objective grounded in Information Bottleneck (IB) theory to extract compact semantic features from multi-view images, effectively reducing feature redundancy in BEV representations. Second, a Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) scheme is designed to ensure reliable transmission of semantic features under IoV low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Finally, we introduce a multi-level feature fusion mechanism that incorporates a feature space calibration module and an attention enhancement module to address spatial misalignment issues in multi-vehicle cooperation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework surpasses existing methods with notable gains in mean Intersection over Union (mIoU).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Analytical Modeling of Energy Consumption for a LoRaWAN Class B Node.
abstract: This paper proposes an analytical model to evaluate the energy consumption of a Class B end node (EN) in LoRaWAN, a low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) standard. Based on the state transitions of Class B nodes, the current consumption and duration of each state are defined to estimate the daily energy consumption. A theoretical expression is then derived to estimate the battery lifetime of the EN as a function of parameters such as initial battery capacity, spreading factor, beacon period, and ping-slot interval. The formulation inherently includes Class A operation, which is mandatory for ENs. Numerical analyses are conducted to evaluate the impact of various Class B-related parameters on the EN's lifetime. Furthermore, when the Class B cycle becomes sufficiently long -effectively disabling downlink operation- the results converge to those of Class A, confirming the validity of the derived expression.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: New Insights Into Positioning Performance Metrics for Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: The rapid expansion of Low-Altitude Networks (LANs) has underscored the critical role of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC). However, the positioning performance of multi-site Base Station (BS) collaborationa-prerequisite for reliable UAV operations and surveillance-remains insufficiently explored. To address this, we propose a novel linear metric to quantify ISAC positioning accuracy. Starting with the derivation of positioning error lower bounds under a single-site signal model, we employ optimal information fusion theory to formulate a linear assessment metric tailored for collaborative environments. The validity of this approach is corroborated by both experimental results and industrial field deployments, establishing a robust framework for optimizing ISAC systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Covert Ultraviolet Communication Design When Warden Observes Sparse Signals in Time Domain.
abstract: We propose a covert ultraviolet communication scheme assuming that the eavesdropper does not know the transmission time slot of Alice-Bob link. The covertness and achievable rate of Alice-Bob link are analyzed. Under the covertness constraints on Warden, we propose to optimize the frame structure to maximize the achievable rate. Numerical and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the designed system.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: SWIPT with Probabilistic Amplitude Shaping of 5G LDPC Coded Modulation.
abstract: In this paper, we present theoretical analyses and a new scheme for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). From the information theory perspective, we define the infinite-length energy-information (E-I) region for the power splitting-based SWIPT system with finite-alphabet inputs. Moreover, we also define the finite-length E-I region and derive the lower bound on the upper boundary (capacity) by the derived random coding bound (RCB) for SWIPT. For practical coded modulation, we propose a new SWIPT scheme based on the probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS) with low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. In this scheme, the constant composition distribution matcher (CCDM) of the PAS is employed to adjust the distribution of channel inputs to enable wireless power transfer (WPT), while the 5G LDPC code is employed to support reliable wireless information transfer (WIT). Simulation results show that: 1) the proposed SWIPT scheme with 5 G LDPC coded PAS closely approaches the lower bound of the finite-length capacity; 2) the proposed SWIPT scheme can achieve more than 20 % improvement of the power transfer performance over the conventional bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) scheme.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Two-Timescale Uplink Channel Estimation for Networked ISAC Systems Using Downlink Assistance and Cooperative Sensing.
abstract: This paper studies a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) networked integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, in which multiple base stations (BSs) cooperatively serve a user equipment (UE). In such systems, accurate channel state information (CSI) is critical for both communication and sensing. To achieve accurate CSI with low overhead, a two-timescale uplink channel estimation scheme is proposed. It exploits slow-varying angular parameters and fast-varying channel gains arising from large-scale and small-scale propagation, respectively. In the largetimescale phase, we exploit the temporal correlation of the channel to extract UE location via downlink cooperation and uplink cooperative sensing. During the downlink stage, the angles of the BSs are estimated at the UE using the discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) method. Based on these estimates, a codebookbased transmit beamforming is designed for uplink pilot signals. During the uplink stage, the angles and time delays of the UE are sequentially estimated at the BSs by applying the DFT method to the received directional pilot signals. Subsequently, these local estimates are forwarded to the fusion center, where an extended Kalman filter (EKF)-based fusion method is proposed to enable cooperative sensing of the UE. Based on the fused results, a codebook-based combining method is designed to enhance uplink reception. In the small-timescale phase, we propose a cooperative sensing-aided orthogonal matching pursuit (CSAOMP) algorithm, which leverages the location prior obtained from the largetimescale phase to enable channel estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms benchmarks in channel estimation accuracy and achieves performance approaching that under ideal CSI conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: LLM-Empowered Covert Control in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) are expected to support safety-critical control, yet they face a core challenge that reliable closed-loop performance must be guaranteed under explicit covert communication constraints and pronounced mobility. In such networks, a UAV must deliver control packets while remaining undetectable to an active warden. In this paper, we investigate a sensing-assisted covert wireless control system in which a UAV equipped with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) capability serves multiple ground-controlled plants in the presence of a mobile warden. The design objective is to ensure linear quadratic regulator (LQR) performance while satisfying covertness requirements under transmit-power and mobility constraints. To cope with the resulting sophisticated optimization problem, we develop an end-to-end beamforming framework based on an encoding-decoding network that maps historical channel information to predictive beamformers, and we further enhance its training through a large language model (LLM)-guided strategy. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves lower control cost and stronger covertness than conventional deep-learning-based beamforming benchmarks in representative low-altitude scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: HMNet: A Hybrid Multi-Resolution Network with Local Uniform Quantization for Low-Complexity CSI Feedback.
abstract: Efficient channel state information (CSI) feedback is essential for massive MIMO systems, yet existing methods remain limited by the trade-off between reconstruction accuracy and computational complexity. This paper proposes HMNet, a hybrid multi-resolution network that parallelizes convolutional and attention branches to capture local and global channel features with low computational cost. In addition, a lightweight local uniform quantization (LUQ) scheme is introduced, which divides the normalized codeword range into two intervals and applies uniform quantization within each to enhance precision in high-energy regions while maintaining stable gradient flow. Simulation results demonstrate that HMNet achieves up to 45.24 % reduction in FLOPs under extreme compression, while maintaining competitive NMSE compared with fusion-based baselines. With quantization, LUQ achieves up to 15.83 % NMSE improvement and exhibits smoother performance degradation as well as stronger robustness in outdoor channels. These results confirm that the proposed HMNet+LUQ framework attains an effective balance between accuracy and complexity, enabling practical and deployable CSI feedback for future wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Base Resizing for Rate-Adaptive Digital Semantic Communication.
abstract: Digital semantic communication systems, which often leverage the Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQVAE) framework, are pivotal for future wireless networks. In a VQ-VAE-based semantic communication system, the transmission rate is directly governed by the size of a discrete codebook known as knowledge base (KB). However, the KB size is a fixed hyperparameter, meaning that adapting the rate requires training and storing a separate model for each desired size—a practice that is too computationally and storage-prohibitive to achieve truly granular rate control. To address this, we introduce a principled, zero-shot KB resizing method that enables on-the-fly rate adaptation without any retraining. Our approach establishes a global importance ranking for all vectors within a single, large parent KB by uncovering its inherent semantic hierarchy. This is achieved via a three-step framework: 1) embedding KB vectors into hyperbolic space to reveal their hierarchical relationships; 2) constructing a master semantic tree using a minimum spanning tree algorithm; 3) enabling instant resizing by iteratively pruning the least important leaf nodes. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our method achieves reconstruction quality nearly identical to that of dedicated KBs trained from scratch, while demanding only a fraction of the computational budget. Moreover, our approach exhibits superior robustness at very low rates, where conventional KBs suffer from catastrophic failure. Our work resolves a fundamental limitation of VQ-VAE-based semantic communication systems, offering a practical and efficient path toward flexible and rate-adaptive semantic communication.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Latency Minimization for Secure RSMA-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-assisted secure mobile edge computing (MEC) network, where an edge user (EU) employs the RSMA technique to securely offload its computation task to multiple helper users (HUs) that may act as internal eavesdroppers. Specifically, to ensure the confidentiality of task segments, each offloaded task segment to one HU must remain confidential from unauthorized access by other HUs. In other words, each HU not only functions as a legitimate receiver to decode its desired message but also as a potential internal eavesdropper to intercept other HUs' messages. Under this setup, we aim to minimize the total system latency by jointly optimizing the task offloading ratio, commonmessage transmission rate, and precoder matrix, while satisfying the secure offloading and power constraints. To address the resulting non-convex problem, we develop an iterative algorithm that integrates block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA). Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed design outperforms existing benchmark schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Generative AI Empowering Collaborative HD Map Refinement in Vehicular Edge Computing.
abstract: High-definition (HD) maps provide lane-level geometric information to improve the robustness of localization, perception, and motion planning for autonomous vehicles (AVs). However, maintaining HD maps accurate in urban environments requires substantial computational and financial costs, bringing a heavy burden for automakers. To confront these challenges, we investigate collaborative HD map refinement under a vehicular edge computing (VEC) paradigm, where a Map Service Provider (MSP) collaborates with multiple Vehicle Information Providers (VIPs). We first propose an incentive mechanism that encourages VIPs to share key perception features.
