We then design a credibility-aware sequential evidence fusion framework that aggregates local perception posteriors from heterogeneous VIPs, thus producing a global estimate of road condition. Furthermore, we leverage conditional diffusion to reconstruct affected regions, avoiding costly full-map reconstruction. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes and NGSIM datasets indicate that our approach offers a comprehensive and precise portrayal of road conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Design of Unsourced Random Access System Through Flexible Modulation and Detection.
abstract: On-off division multiple access (ODMA) is a newly proposed technique for unsourced random access (URA). Existing ODMA schemes restrict to binary phase shift keying (BPSK) modulation and suffer from increasing interference and degraded performance when the number of active users is large. To address this issue, in this paper we design and optimize the ODMA-based URA system through flexible modulation selection. We investigate the relationship between the error performance and the access density of the system. By choosing an appropriate modulation order based on the number of active users, we achieve a trade-off between the single-user performance and the multi-user interference. A generalized receiving algorithm is derived for arbitrary modulation schemes. Numerical results show that the proposed system outperforms the existing ones for large numbers of users and exhibits great potential for massive connectivity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Redundancy-Aware, Delay-Constrained Candidate Coordination for Opportunistic Routing in Low-Altitude Networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: AdaptHFL: A Dual-Level Adaptive Optimization Framework for Hierarchical Federated Learning.
abstract: Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) has emerged as a prominent framework for jointly addressing communication overhead and statistical heterogeneity, which are the core design elements of current Federated Learning systems. However, HFL triggers new challenges in client assignment and the decision to choose different levels of aggregation frequency among clients, edge, and cloud. This paper proposes an Adaptive Hierarchical Federated Learning (AdaptHFL) framework to handle the above issues jointly. First, we advocate the inter-edge similarity metric as our client assignment strategy to minimize edge model divergence, which amplifies HFL's inherent advantages on non-IID data. Then, we design an HFL framework booster by dynamically balancing local training iterations and edge aggregation frequency. Experimental results demonstrate that our AdaptHFL framework has superior model accuracy, 7 % higher than other baselines, on various non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) scenarios. In addition, our proposed dual-level adaptive mechanism can reduce time consumption by 28 % and flexibly complement state-of-the-art client assignment approaches to improve the HFL system's convergence speed further.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: AI Explainability for Adaptive Mmwave Beam Configuration in Dynamic Vehicular Environments.
abstract: Vehicular millimetre-wave (mmWave) networks suffer from beam misalignment and throughput degradation due to high mobility, blockages, and interference-challenges that static beam strategies cannot address. This paper addresses adaptive beam configuration in dynamic vehicular scenarios through reinforcement learning (RL), i.e. Deep Q-Network (DQN) and Q-learning, to jointly optimise base station placement, beam direction, and beamwidth for maximum system sum-rate. Recognising that the lack of interpretability in learned policies remains a critical barrier to operator trust and practical deployment, we integrate a novel multi-agent large language model (LLM) explainability layer that processes user queries in parallel through specialised agents, hence combine numerical logs, scenario rules, and visual outputs into concise, human-understandable explanations. This unified framework demonstrates how high-performance RL optimisation and transparent explainability can be combined to build trust and facilitate practical deployment in future 5G/6G vehicular networks and Open RAN environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Revisiting In-Network Caches on Constrained IEEE 802.15.4 IoT Hardware: Reproducible Testbeds and Future Research Motivation.
abstract: In-network caching is a promising approach to aid multi-hop Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), where intermediate nodes not only forward data but also store it for later requests. This paper presents a baseline, hardware-based experimental evaluation of the benefits of in-network caching in a multi-hop network consisting of constrained microcontroller-class devices on a hardware testbed based on the IEEE 802.15.4 radio technology. A scenario of a fixed-size file delivery from a designated source to a destination node across multiple relay nodes that cache and forward content is employed for baseline establishment. We focus on practical feasibility, reproducibility, and end-toend service performance. With a probabilistic caching strategy and operating under limited memory constraints, we find that end-to-end service performance (as total transmission time) is improved by at least 10% and the number of transmissions within the network required to transmit the entire file is reduced by at least 20%. These findings establish a realistic performance baseline for in-network caching on constrained Internet of Things (IoT) hardware and highlight its potential as a low-complexity optimization for industrial multi-hop WSN deployments. We outline the potential for future research avenues based on the need for lightweight caching mechanisms in improving communication overhead in resource-constrained IoT networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RIS-Assisted MIMO System Design: A Low Complex MIMO Precoder Selection Method.
abstract: By intelligently reconfiguring wireless propagation environment, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) can enhance signal quality, suppress interference, and improve channel conditions, thereby serving as a powerful complement to multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architectures. However, jointly optimizing the RIS phase shifts and the MIMO transmit precoder in 5G and beyond networks remains largely unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by proposing a singular value ($λ$)-based RIS optimization strategy, where the phase shifts are configured to maximize the dominant singular values of the cascaded channel matrix, and the corresponding singular vectors are utilized for MIMO transmit precoding. The proposed precoder selection does not require mutual information computation across subbands, thereby reducing time complexity. To solve the $λ$-based optimization problem, maximum cross-swapping algorithm (MCA) is applied while an effective rank-based method is utilized for benchmarking purposes. The simulation results show that the proposed precoder selection method consistently outperforms the conventional approach under $λ$-based RIS optimization.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Resource Allocation for D2D-Enabled NOMA Cellular Networks with Composite Signal.
abstract: The integration of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and device-to-device (D2D) communication is regarded as a promising technology to improve performance for nextgeneration networks. In this paper, we focus on the scenario where cellular users are empowered with superposition coding to simultaneously communicate with both the base station (BS) and their paired device (PU). The associated resource allocation problem is formulated as a non-convex mixed integer programming problem, which is hard to solve within a reasonable time. The problem is decomposed into subcarrier assignment and power control subproblems. We propose a swapenabled Gale-Shapley and centralized iterative power allocation algorithm (SGS-CIPA), designed to jointly optimize subcarrier assignment and power allocation. The simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves significant improvements in system capacity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel Low-Complexity Dual-Domain Expectation Propagation Detection Aided AFDM for Future Communications.
abstract: This paper presents a dual-domain low-complexity expectation propagation (EP) detection framework for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) systems. By analyzing the structural properties of the effective channel matrices in both the time and affine frequency (AF) domains, our key observation is the domain-specific quasi-banded sparsity patterns, including AF-domain sparsity under frequency-selective channels and time-domain sparsity under doubly-selective channels. Based on these observations, we develop an AF-domain EP (EP-AF) detector for frequency-selective channels and a time-domain EP (EP-T) detector for doubly-selective channels, respectively. By performing iterative inference in the time domain using the Gaussian approximation, the proposed EP-T detector avoids inverting the dense channel matrix in the AF domain. Furthermore, the proposed EP-AF and EP-T detectors leverage the aforementioned quasi-banded sparsity of the AF domain and time domain channel matrices, respectively, to reduce the complexity of matrix inversion from cubic to linear order. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed low-complexity EP-AF detector achieves nearly identical error rate performance to its conventional counterpart, while the proposed low-complexity EP-T detector offers an attractive trade-off between detection performance and complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enforcing IoT Security Properties in Smart Buildings: A Solution Based on a Publication Policy and the Blockchain Technology.
abstract: With the rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT), smart buildings are becoming increasingly widespread. However, along with the convenience and connectivity provided by heterogeneous IoT devices in smart buildings come critical challenges including transparency, trust, and data security. Blockchain (BC) technology offers promising capability to address these concerns through its decentralized and immutable nature. This paper proposes a Blockchain-based architecture for managing IoT data in smart buildings, dynamically enforcing security properties like authentication, data integrity, data traceability, and robustness to cyber-attacks. We propose a security protocol that specifies all communication exchanges among the system's components. Furthermore, we provide a publication policy that dictates the criteria that IoT data must meet before being accepted by the BC network. Each transmitted transaction should be verified and validated by the BC network. Our solution combines a Blockchain with a time-series database to ensure the enforcement of the required security properties while maintaining efficient data publication and access performance. A simulation is conducted to assess the performance of our solution.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Reference Nonlinear Transform Source-Channel Coding for Wireless Image Semantic Transmission.
abstract: We propose a multi-reference nonlinear transform source-channel coding (MR-NTSCC) system to improve the rate-distortion (RD) performance by introducing multi-dimensional contexts into the entropy model of the state-of-the-art (SOTA) NTSCC system. Improvements in RD performance of the proposed MR-NTSCC system are particularly significant in high-resolution wireless image transmission under low bandwidth constraints, compared with the existing NTSCC+ system. The proposed multi-reference entropy model leverages correlations within the latent representation in both spatial and channel dimensions. In the spatial dimension, the latent representation is divided into anchors and non-anchors in a checkerboard pattern, where anchors serve as reference to estimate the mutual information between anchors and non-anchors. In the channel dimension, the latent representation is partitioned into multiple groups, and features in previous groups are analyzed to estimate the mutual information between features in previous and current groups. Taking mutual information into account, the entropy model provides an accurate estimation on the entropy, which enables efficient bandwidth allocation and enhances RD performance. Comprehensive experiments are conducted to verify the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) performance of the proposed MR-NTSCC model superior to SOTA methods over both additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel and Rayleigh fading channel.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Construction of Protograph LDPC Codes for Shaped Signaling over STBC-MIMO Channels.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Spatial-Temporal Topological Decoupling Method in Battery-Free Sensor Networks.
abstract: The Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) technology makes it possible to realize energy sustainable Battery-free SWIPT-enabled Sensor Network (BSSN). However, it is difficult to achieve the trade-off between scalability and long-term energy sustainability due to the dynamic spatialtemporal variations in data and energy flows. To this end, a Spatial-temporal Topological Decoupling Method in Batteryfree Sensor Networks (STD-BSN) is proposed. Specifically, the proposed approach combining Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) is presented, which constructs multi-dimensional influence weight matrices based on Historical Data Pearson Correlation Analysis (HD-PCA) and integrates AHP-derived weight vectors as prior knowledge into SBL to form an AHP-SBL model for accurate data-energy forecasting. Experimental results demonstrate that AHP-SBL achieves significant improvements in network lifetime and throughput compared to state-of-the-art approaches, with throughput enhancements of$\mathbf{8 0. 3 2 \%, ~} \mathbf{5 2. 3 4 \%, ~} \mathbf{4 9. 7 2 \%}$, and$\mathbf{2 9. 7 1 \%}$over LEACH, LEACHR, HHCA, and GWOA-CH respectively in large-scale network scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: 3D Coverage Maximization via Aerial BS Navigation, Beamforming, and Spectrum Allocation: An Integrated DRL/Optimization Solution.
abstract: In this paper, we aim to enhance three-dimensional (3D) coverage in aerial communication systems, where an uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted base station (UAV-BS) supports downlink transmission to aerial users (AUs). Unlike existing works that assume an idealized isotropic antenna at the UAV-BS, we consider a practical directional antenna whose gain varies with elevation angle. After deriving an analytical expression for the antenna gain, we formulate the 3D coverage maximization problem as a Markov decision process (MDP) to jointly optimize the UAV-BS navigation, beam pattern, and spectrum allocation. Then, we propose a deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm, termed integrated learning/optimization for aerial coverage maximization (ILO-ACM), which integrates spectrum allocation into the sequential decision-making process of the MDP to overcome the hybrid action space and dimension imbalance problem. Simulation results verify that the proposed ILO-ACM algorithm achieves substantial coverage performance gains compared to benchmark schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Near-Field Beam-Split-Aware Channel Estimation in THz Massive MIMO-OTFS Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of nearfield terahertz (THz) channel estimation in massive multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) systems under the impact of the beam split phenomenon. We first derive the frequency-domain input-output relationship of a massive MIMO-OTFS system in the presence of near field beam split. Subsequently, the near-field channel estimation problem is formulated as a sparse recovery problem, for which a beam-split-aware dictionary is constructed. By explicitly modeling beam-split effects within the dictionary, conventional compressed sensing algorithms can be directly leveraged for channel state information (CSI) estimation in THz regimes, without requiring customized beam-split-aware estimators. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed dictionary enables accurate and efficient sparse estimation of the near-field CSI in THz OTFS systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Costs and Incentives for Data Owners to Participate in Federated Learning Seen Through Game Theory.
abstract: Federated learning enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a global machine learning model without sharing raw data, providing improvements of privacy and confidentiality. However, if client participation is voluntary and costly, certain nodes may decide not to contribute to the global training and rely on their local classification only. In this paper, we apply coalition game theory to represent this scenario and explore whether network-wide cooperation is pursued by all nodes, depending on the quality of their data and the communication cost. Stable coalitions are represented as Nash equilibria, for which we compute the achieved performance. We validated our proposed approach to an extensive set of four public datasets commonly used for benchmarking (HuGaDB, Adult, Spambase, and KDD99), and two different FL techniques, FedLR and FedFor. We argue how transmission cost, and possibly introduced network incentives, can tune the gap between the training quality in a coalition or as standalone units.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multipoint Wi-Fi Fingerprinting Indoor Localization via Transformer-Based Graph Attention.
abstract: Wi-Fi fingerprinting has become a widely adopted technique for indoor localization, as alternative attributes such as channel state information (CSI) and time-of-arrival (ToA) remain limited in practice. However, existing fingerprinting methods suffer from sudden performance degradation in dynamic indoor environments, since they typically neglect the temporal correlation of user locations and the variability of signal patterns across buildings and floors. In this paper, we propose a graph-based indoor localization framework that models user trajectories and leverages received signal strength indicator (RSSI) data from multiple steps. By aggregating temporal context through Transformer-based graph attention layers, the proposed approach achieves improved robustness to outliers and sudden fluctuations, thereby reducing positioning error. Moreover, we introduce a two-stage architecture consisting of a building classification submodel followed by building-specific regression models, which enhances adaptability to environmental changes such as the addition of new access points or buildings. Experimental results on the UJIIndoorLoc and UTSIndoorLoc datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing baselines in both positioning accuracy and floor classification. These findings indicate that trajectory-aware multipoint fingerprinting constitutes a promising direction for developing robust and scalable indoor positioning systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid Lyapunov-Based Scheduling for Heterogeneous Traffic in 5G Industrial Environments.
abstract: The hybrid data traffic characteristics in 5 G industrial networks pose significant challenges for radio resource scheduling. Schedulers based solely on throughput or fairness are unsuitable for providing guaranteed deterministic service for URLLC applications. This paper proposes a novel hybrid scheduling framework designed to enforce a strict Quality of Service (QoS) hierarchy. The proposed method employs a two-tiered logic, integrating a non-preemptive Strict Priority (SP) tier for URLLC traffic with a second tier governed by Lyapunov optimization for managing all other traffic. The Lyapunov-based scheduler uses a Weighted Max-Weight metric, driven by queue backlogs, channel conditions, and QoS weights, to maintain system stability. We implement and evaluate this framework with the Simu5G simulation tool, modelling an indoor factory environment with multiple Autonomous Guided Vehicles (AGVs). Results show that our hybrid scheduler meets the bounded latency of 10 ms for critical control traffic, outperforming both traditional and state-of-the-art approaches in terms of end-to-end latency and jitter. Furthermore, it showcases superior resource efficiency by achieving 40 % higher goodput compared to traditional methods like MAXCI.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Array Configuration and Signal Processing for RIS-Assisted Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems.
abstract: In richly scattering environments such as intelligent transportation and intelligent manufacturing factory, the line-ofsight paths in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems are frequently blocked, which significantly degrades sensing accuracy. Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has emerged as a promising technology to reshape the wireless propagation environment to improve ISAC performance. However, the full activation of RIS elements entails high power costs and heavy channel estimation burdens, which makes it difficult to preserve large aperture gains and high angular resolution. To address this challenge, we propose a coprime sparse RIS (CS-RIS) array configuration and develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)–based signal processing algorithm for the azimuth and elevation angles of multiple targets in richly scattering environments. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared with traditional equally spaced RIS array configuration, the proposed CS-RIS achieves significant gains in both unambiguous range and angular resolution. Moreover, the proposed CNN-based signal processing algorithm significantly outperforms the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm in target estimation accuracy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning-Powered Behavioral Authentication and Anomaly Detection for UAV Systems.
abstract: Exploiting Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) path information to monitor trajectory behavior provides a powerful means to ensure in-flight UAV authenticity, detect anomalies and identify malicious control or spoofed commands before they cause severe consequences. In this paper, we propose a novel behaviorbased UAV authentication and anomaly detection framework that leverages high-fidelity and real-world-inspired flight scenarios to obtain a comprehensive trajectory dataset. From the resulting dataset, behavioral features are extracted and processed by a deep learning classification pipeline that captures temporal dependencies and enables continuous real-time authentication under diverse mission conditions, without relying on predefined paths or static communication features. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deep learning-based authentication approaches outperform other existing approaches in terms of precision, recall and F1-score, especially the LSTM-based authentication scheme by achieving 96% precision and 95% recall in detecting suspicious UAVs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Service Function Chain Routing in LEO Networks Using Shortest-Path Delay Statistical Stability.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations have become a critical enabler for global coverage, utilizing numerous satellites orbiting Earth at high speeds. By decomposing complex network services into lightweight service functions, network function virtualization (NFV) transforms global network services into diverse service function chains (SFCs), coordinated by resource-constrained LEOs. However, the dynamic topology of satellite networks, marked by highly variable inter-satellite link delays, poses significant challenges for designing efficient routing strategies that ensure reliable and low-latency communication. Many existing routing methods suffer from poor scalability and degraded performance, limiting their practical implementation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel SFC routing approach that leverages the statistical properties of network link states to mitigate instability caused by instantaneous modeling in dynamic satellite networks. Through comprehensive simulations on end-to-end shortest-path propagation delays in LEO networks, we identify and validate the statistical stability of multi-hop routes. Building on this insight, we introduce the Stability-Aware Multi-Stage Graph Routing (SA-MSGR) algorithm, which incorporates pre-computed average delays into a multi-stage graph optimization framework. Extensive simulations demonstrate the superior performance of SA-MSGR, achieving significantly lower and more predictable end-to-end SFC delays compared to representative baseline strategies.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: CRLB and Parameter Estimation for OFDM-ISAC with Non-Uniform Sparse Resource Allocation.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) holds great promise in expanding the applications of wireless communication networks. However, in current communicationcentric systems, the time-frequency resources available for sensing may be limited, and also usually non-uniformly and sparsely distributed across the time-frequency domain. Such a non-uniformity destroys the “thumbtack-shaped” ambiguity function of the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform, leading to degraded sensing performance. To this end, this paper explores the parameter estimation algorithm for OFDM-ISAC systems with non-uniform sparse resource allocation. Specifically, for the single target case, we derive the closed-form Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for parameter estimation as a function of resource indices. Furthermore, we show that simply filling unused resource locations with zeros and applying the classic periodogram estimation is equivalent to maximum likelihood (ML) estimation, which is asymptotically optimal. For the multi-target case, we generate a virtual resource using the autocorrelation function of the original signal, which exhibits a significantly larger virtual bandwidth compared to the original signal, at the cost of higher peak-to-sidelobe ratio (PSLR). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the conventional periodogram method for non-uniform sparse resource allocation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel Pilot Scheme for Uplink Channel Estimation in XL-MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper designs a novel pilot scheme for extralarge massive MIMO (XL-MIMO) systems, by leveraging the spatial non-stationarity introduced by the large aperture of the extremely large aperture arrays (ELAA). The spatial nonstationarity results in distinct visibility for different users at ELAA, particularly those located far apart, which reduces inter-user interference. This property motivates our novel pilot scheme to group users with distinct visibility regions to share the same frequency subcarriers for channel estimation, hence reducing pilot overhead while accommodating numerous users. Specifically, the proposed pilot scheme employs frequencydivision multiplexing for inter-group channel estimation, while intra-group users - benefiting from strong spatial orthogonality from the distinct visibility region - are distinguished by shifted cyclic codes, similar to code-division multiplexing. Additionally, we propose a low-complexity channel estimation algorithm within a turbo Bayesian inference framework, where the channel support of each user at the ELAA features clustered sparsity in the antenna-delay domain and is modeled by a 2 -dimensional (2-D) Markov random field. Simulations show that the proposed pilot scheme and algorithm allow the XL-MIMO system to support more users, and deliver superior channel estimation performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: HSASCom: A Point Cloud Semantic Communication System with SNR-Adaptive Hierarchical Feature Transmission.
abstract: The point cloud is widely used in applications such as autonomous driving, augmented/virtual reality (AR/VR), and digital twins. However, its large data volume, irregular structure, and inherent sparsity pose significant challenges for wireless transmission. Conventional transmission methods typically suffer from limited compression efficiency, high sensitivity to channel conditions, and substantial redundancy. In this paper, we propose a point cloud semantic communication system, HSASCom, to overcome the limitations of conventional point cloud transmission. First, we introduce an end-to-end point cloud semantic communication framework that integrates hierarchical semantic-feature extraction, SNR-adaptive transmission, and semantic-guided reconstruction. By employing a joint source-channel coding architecture, HSASCom mitigates the cliff effect and reduces redundancy. Second, we propose a dual-branch attention mechanism that jointly captures local geometric details and global semantic context. An SNR-aware unequal-error-protection strategy dynamically allocates bits to prioritize critical semantic features under low-SNR conditions and to preserve fine details at high SNR. Extensive experiments on the ShapeNet dataset demonstrate that HSASCom maintains a D1-PSNR above 36 dB and a D2-PSNR above 41 dB across a 0-20 dB SNR range, and achieves up to 70.14% average bit rate saving, thereby exhibiting superior robustness and transmission efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Implementation of a Broadband ISAC System Based on Real-Time Channelization and DoAAided Beamforming Optimization.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is a key technology for next-generation wireless systems. However, achieving real-time broadband processing and practical deployment remains a significant challenge. This paper presents a hardware-software co-design prototype system using an eight-channel antenna array and a Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC) to bridge this gap. On the hardware side, a pipelined multi-channel channelization structure implemented in programmable logic decomposes a$\mathbf{2 0 0 ~ M H z ~ b r o a d b a n d ~ s i g n a l ~ i n t o ~ e i g h t ~} \mathbf{2 5 ~ M H z}$narrowband channels, effectively overcoming the high-throughput data bottleneck. On the software side, a joint algorithm utilizes Sample Matrix Inversion (SMI) for Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation and Second-Order Cone Programming (SOCP) for adaptive beamforming, processing the narrowband data. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves accurate DoA estimation and significant interference suppression, with a suppression ratio exceeding 60 dB. Compared with other optimization methods, this method significantly improves communication performance. This work provides a practical and efficient implementation framework for broadband ISAC, facilitating the transition from theory to deployment.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Downlink Outage Probability Analysis in Cooperative LEO-LAP Enabled Space-Air-Ground Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Traditional vehicular network communication infrastructure is limited by road obstructions and insufficient deployment density, making it difficult to efficiently ensure communication performance in complex traffic scenarios. To address this issue, this paper proposes a space-air-ground integrated vehicular network architecture, which constructs a three-dimensional network by integrating low earth orbit (LEO) satellites, low-altitude platforms (LAPs), and ground vehicles. Additionally, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) technologies are combined to enable the efficient cooperative transmission of information and energy. However, the multi-tier and multi-node network architecture increases interference between links, making it difficult to directly quantify the downlink outage probability. To overcome this challenge, this paper first establishes a system model based on NOMA transmission and a hybrid time-switching/power-splitting (TS/PS) protocol, and proposes an antenna selection criterion with the objective of maximizing energy harvesting at LAP nodes. Based on this, a dynamic power factor allocation mechanism is designed, and the downlink transmission performance is analyzed. Furthermore, this paper derives a closed-form expression for the downlink outage probability based on the Rayleigh fading and co-channel interference channel models of the satellite-LAP-vehicle link. By applying the central limit theorem, a Gaussian approximation solution is proposed. Simulation results show that the approximation solution matches well with the closed-form expression, with an average error of 6.2 %. In addition, the proposed scheme outperforms state-of-the-art schemes in terms of the downlink outage probability under various network conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation in VQA-Oriented UAV Semantic Offloading.
abstract: Visual question answering (VQA) plays an important role in enhancing situational awareness, while unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) provide flexible platforms to support such semantic communication tasks. This paper investigates resource allocation for VQA in UAV-assisted semantic communication networks. In the proposed framework, both UAV and user equipment (UE) adopt deep semantic communication (DeepSC)-VQA to encode semantic features, which are then offloaded to a multi-access edge computing (MEC) server for inference. To jointly optimize the energy consumption and the latency of the whole system, we develop a hybrid proximal policy optimization (HPPO) algorithm with a tailored reward function that coordinates the UAV trajectory, radio resource allocation, and semantic offloading. Simulation results show that the HPPO-based scheme consistently outperforms conventional reinforcement learning benchmarks, achieving a superior balance between the energy consumption and the latency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for AIGC Service Caching in UAV-Enabled Edge Networks.
abstract: The provisioning of AI-generated content (AIGC) services based on diffusion models in UAV-enabled edge networks presents significant challenges due to intensive computation demands, high-dimensional model semantics, and limited caching and communication capabilities. To address these issues, we propose a diffusion-aware collaborative caching and computation offloading framework that leverages the semantic generality and noise-level similarity of latent representations in diffusion models. High-noise latent states with broader adaptability are selected as reusable cache units to reduce redundant inference and improve content generalization. Moreover, a similarity- and frequency-aware cache cost model is developed to evaluate content utility under dynamic request patterns. A multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG)based learning scheme is designed to jointly optimize cached content selection, computation scheduling, and UAV cooperative strategies. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves cache hit rate and reduces service delay and energy consumption compared with DQN, LRU, and No-cache baselines, confirming its effectiveness for supporting scalable and efficient AIGC service delivery.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multidimensional Resource Allocation Based on Hierarchical Asynchronous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Power Line Inspection.
abstract: This paper addresses the collaborative resource scheduling problem in Low-Altitude Economy (LAE) scenarios, with a focus on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted power line inspection tasks. Existing approaches to the joint coordination of caching, communication, and interference management often lack adaptability to dynamic mission requirements and suffer from decision coupling across domains. To handle the differentiated Quality of Service (QoS) demands of UAVs and to counter the eavesdropping threats of adversarial UAVs, a hierarchical asynchronous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework based on Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG), is proposed, termed LAE-MADDPG-HA. The framework decomposes optimization into two layers: a caching agent first determines QoS-differentiated service caching strategies and thereby influences the UAV–Ground Base Station(GBS) association, while a power agent subsequently allocates communication and jamming power based on the updated network state. This asynchronous mechanism enables effective information flow between agents while avoiding temporal conflicts in resource allocation. The simulation results under realistic inspection scenarios demonstrate that LAE-MADDPG-HA significantly improves the accuracy of the inspection service, the security of communication and the performance of transmission latency compared with baseline algorithms including MADDPG, hierarchical MADDPG without asynchronous coupling, and multiagent PPO (MAPPO), validating its robustness and effectiveness in complex and interference-prone LAE environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cross-Splitting-Based Information Geometry Approach for Xl-Mimo Uplink Detection.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel approach called cross-splitting-based information geometry approach (CS-IGA) for signal detection in extra-large-scale multi-input and multioutput (XL-MIMO) systems. In conventional information geometry approach and the Bayes-optimal approximate message passing (AMP) method, the complexity per iteration scales linearly with$M N$, where$M$is the number of BS antennas and$N$is the number of transmitted data streams. To reduce the complexity per iteration to the order of$N^{2}$, which suits the XLMIMO, we propose a matrix splitting of the natural parameters in the posterior probability density function (PDF). The number of splittings is$N$. In deriving the CS-IGA, we show that each splitting corresponds to a computation with complexity in the order of$N$. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the conventional IGA and the Bayes-optimal AMP in terms of bit error rate (BER) performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: PRACH Preamble Design for 6G Wireless Systems.
abstract: Motivated by cutting-edge applications such as the massive Internet of Things, next-generation wireless networks are expected to accommodate millions of devices per square kilometer. Such massive access places rigorous demands on the design of physical random access channel preambles, which are required to possess high capacity, Doppler robustness, and ideal correlation properties. However, existing sequences that meet these criteria are usually hindered by prohibitive detection complexity. To tackle this challenge, a Kronecker-product structured (KPS) sequence is proposed that naturally embeds a multi-segment structure, enabling the low-complexity detection. Furthermore, a two-stage low-complexity detection algorithm is proposed, which decouples inner and outer correlations and simplifies the Doppler compensation process in order to substantially reduce the computational overhead. Simulation results demonstrate that employing KPS sequences with the proposed detection algorithm achieves accurate detection while maintaining low overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: QoE-Driven Real-Time Video Bitrate Adaptation for Two-Tier Edge Networks.
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous demands for high-definition videos, caching popular contents at edge nodes has emerged as an effective approach to reducing end-to-end transmission latency. By deploying finite caching capacity at edge nodes, network congestion over backhaul links is relieved, and the quality of experience (QoE) is enhanced. Considering this fact, we propose a cache-based and QoE-driven video quality adaptation framework. Specifically, a two-tier collaborative video caching architecture is designed to hierarchically and partially cache popular videos across small-cell base stations (SBSs) and important users (IUs) for coordinated content deliveries. This architecture operates across two time scales. In the long-term scale, an active popularity based caching strategy is conducted to the two tiers of caching nodes. In the short-term scale, we construct a multi-metric instantaneous QoE model and employ the Lagrange duality method to solve the QoE maximization problem. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed real-time quality adaptation method significantly outperforms traditional algorithms, achieving up to 105.2% higher QoE than non-adaptive video delivery policy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Adaptive LLM Inference in 6G Vehicular Networks via Layer Pruning and Offloading.
abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) in 6 G vehicular networks is hindered by their substantial computational demands and the dynamic nature of wireless resources. Unlike existing methods that employ rigid compression strategies, this paper first conducts a systematic study on layerwise redundancy, where contiguous Transformer layers with high cosine similarity are identified and replaced with lightweight surrogate networks. Experimental results on the LLaMA-2 model establish a clear correlation between similarity and performance degradation, providing a principled basis for compression. Building on these findings, we further employs a tailored Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm to dynamically manage the inference pipeline. The proposed algorithm jointly optimize adaptive layer segmentation and offloading, as well as resource allocation based on the pre-validated replacement strategy. Simulations demonstrate that this integrated approach significantly reduces inference latency while strictly controlling accuracy loss, offering a robust and practical solution for LLM services in nextgeneration vehicular systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Harnessing Poiseuille Flow for ISI-Resilient Molecular Communication: A Spatio-Temporal Focusing Approach.
abstract: In fluidic channels such as blood vessels, the non-uniform velocity profile of Poiseuille flow introduces severe inter-symbol interference (ISI) in molecular communication. This paper proposes an innovative “spatio-temporal focusing” transmission mechanism that harnesses rather than purely counteracts the flow's properties. By leveraging the flow's velocity gradient and molecular diffusion, we optimize the transmitter's radial release position to synchronize molecules transported in different velocity layers, enabling their focused arrival at a downstream receiver. We first establish a channel model based on the advection-diffusion equation in cylindrical coordinates. We then analytically derive the channel impulse response and an expression for the system's bit error rate (BER), for which a closed-form approximation is provided. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate that, compared to the conventional on-axis release strategy, our spatio-temporal focusing mechanism significantly reduces signal pulse broadening. This leads to a dramatic suppression of ISI and lowers the BER by several orders of magnitude. This work offers an efficient physical-layer solution to enhance the reliability of molecular communication in fluidic environments, with significant potential for applications such as targeted drug delivery and in vivo nanosensor networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Drift-Aware Updating: An Edge-Device Cooperative RL Framework for Robust and Low-Overhead BCI Adaptation.
abstract: The reliable deployment of mobile Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) is fundamentally constrained by the perceptual nature of Electroencephalography (EEG) acquisition, where the sensed neural signals evolve continuously due to physiological, cognitive, and environmental factors, as well as the limited resources of wearable devices. While server-assisted adaptation can mitigate such perception-driven concept drift, it imposes significant communication and computational overhead. Existing solutions typically rely on rigid, periodic update schedules that fail to dynamically balance decoding accuracy against system costs. To address this, we propose a Drift-Aware Device-Server Framework driven by Reinforcement Learning (RL). In this architecture, an RL agent monitors distributional shifts in the perceptually acquired EEG signals and autonomously selects from a tiered set of maintenance actions, ranging from no-update to varying degrees of model retraining. By decoupling continuous sensing from expensive computation, the learned policy optimizes the longterm trade-off between inference reliability and resource consumption. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms static baselines, reducing computational load by$\mathbf{7 4 \%}$and data transmission by 20 % while achieving superior decoding accuracy. This establishes a scalable, energy-efficient paradigm for sustaining robust BCI operation in resource-constrained wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: OMP-Assisted CBAM Network-Based Channel Estimation for OTFS Systems.
abstract: Orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) modulation effectively supports high-mobility communication scenarios, and the sparse nature of its delay-Doppler (DD) channel makes the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm widely applicable for channel estimation. However, the performance degradation of OMP under noisy conditions motivates deep learning (DL) alternatives, which still lack effective attention mechanisms for discriminative feature extraction. This paper proposes an OMP-assisted convolutional block attention module network (O-CBAM-Net) for channel representation learning. The proposed O-CBAM-Net leverages lightweight OMP-based sparse priors and a CBAM-based dual-attention mechanism to capture the sparse locations, complex gains, and two-dimensional structural distribution of dominant propagation paths. Residual connections are incorporated to enhance feature representation and learning stability. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed O-CBAM-Net consistently outperforms OMP and DL baselines over a range of signal to noise ratios (SNRs) while maintaining a balanced performance-complexity tradeoff. Specifically, at an SNR of 20 dB, O-CBAM-Net achieves approximately a 3.5 dB normalized mean square error (NMSE) gain over OMP. In addition, strong robustness under varying mobility conditions is demonstrated.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Universal Block Error Rate Bound for Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) offer genuine simplicity for communication network design by eliminating expensive hardware overhead and reducing the complexity of access protocol architectures. Through the discovery of significant spatial diversity within a compact antenna space, FASs enable the implementation of reconfigurable-antenna-based architectures. However, current state-of-the-art studies rarely investigate the impact of finite blocklength constraints on FAS-based designs, leaving a gap in both analytical modeling and the establishment of a solid, universally applicable performance metric for finite blocklength fluid antenna systems (FBL-FAS). In this work, we focus on the study of FBL-FAS and, more importantly, derive a block error rate (BLER) bound that serves as a general and practical performance benchmark across various FAS architectures. The proposed BLER bound is computable both with and without an explicit statistical model, meaning that the BLER performance can be characterized analytically or empirically under model-aware or model-free system scenarios. Moreover, when the statistical model is known, the analytical results derived from the proposed BLER bound exhibit strong alignment with the empirical findings, demonstrating the remarkable simplicity, accuracy, and universality of the proposed BLER bound.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Age of Information Analysis of Mobile Edge Computing for Integrated HAP and UAV Networks.
abstract: In future wireless networks, mobile edge computing (MEC) is regarded as a promising paradigm to support the processing of computationally intensive and age-sensitive tasks. In particular, when the ground base stations or infrastructure are damaged, MEC can be deployed on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and high altitude platforms (HAPs) to provide edge computing services. However, the real-time performance and reliability analysis of MEC networks are significantly challenged by the spatially random distribution of devices and the timevarying dynamics of wireless channels, especially under various transmission mechanisms. In this work, we are devoted to analyzing the peak age of information (PAoI) performance of MEC networks where the UAV and HAP jointly provide computing services. Specifically, devices located within the UAV's coverage are served by the UAV, while those outside the UAV's coverage are served by the HAP under a retransmission mechanism. We first derive the distance distribution between the devices and the HAP or UAV. Based on the obtained spatial and temporal characteristics, the service capability of data transmission is characterized accordingly. Furthermore, we analyze the retransmission probabilities of Device-to-UAV and Device-to-HAP by evaluating the successful communication probability. Then, the upper bound of the PAoI violation probability is derived via stochastic network calculus. Finally, simulation results validate the theoretical analysis under various MEC network parameters.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Demand-Driven Adaptive Max-Min Resource Allocation for Wi-Fi OFDMA Networks.
abstract: Ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC) over Wi-Fi orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA) networks is challenged by rapid channel fluctuations and the high complexity of conventional Max-Min resource allocation. This paper proposes an adaptive Max-Min framework that continuously monitors channel quality, triggering optimization only when reliability degrades and restricting each update to a carefully selected subset of users. This demand-driven strategy preserves Max-Min fairness while reducing computational effort and signaling overhead by an order of magnitude compared to traditional periodic Max-Min. It also outperforms representative heuristic allocators. Validation using measured industrial channel traces demonstrates that our approach sustains URLLC-grade reliability and latency under realistic mobility and spectrum conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Stochastic Geometry Analysis of Vision-Based Collaborative Environment Perception with Distance-Dependent Sensing.
abstract: Collaborative vision-based perception has emerged as a pivotal enabler for autonomous driving. Collaborative vision extends perception beyond individual line-of-sight limits via inter-vehicle communication. Despite notable progress in perception and fusion algorithms, the lack of a tractable analytical framework hinders a principled understanding of collaborative perception performance at the system level. Considering distance-dependent sensing, this paper proposes a rigorous analytical framework for collaborative vision-based perception by using a stochastic geometry method, where the road topology is characterized by a Poisson line process (PLP). In this work, we begin by formulating the single-vehicle perception probability based on a photon-counting imaging model that captures the impact of distance-dependent sensing on perception performance. We then derive the rate coverage probability of V2V transmissions for collaborative perception data exchange. Furthermore, we analytically characterize the mean area fraction of a typical vehicle, representing the expected portion of the environment within a radius$\mathcal{D}_{p}$that a typical vehicle can successfully perceive through collaboration. This work provides the first tractable system-level analysis of collaborative vision-based perception that accounts for sensing physics.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low-Complexity Precoder Design for Massive MIMO LEO Satellite Multicast Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a low-complexity precoder design for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite multicast communications. Both weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization and max–min fairness (MMF) criteria are considered. By exploiting the fact that the optimal precoders lie in a low-dimensional subspace, the high-dimensional spatial-domain problem is equivalently reformulated into a reduced-dimensional form without any loss of optimality. Building upon this reformulation, efficient algorithms with guaranteed convergence are developed under the penalty dual decomposition (PDD) framework. In particular, a one-time precomputation scheme is introduced to eliminate per-iteration matrix inversions by reusing precomputed factors, thereby further reducing computational complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed design achieves superior performance with significantly lower complexity, demonstrating its effectiveness for massive MIMO LEO satellite communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hierarchical Federated Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Wireless Distributed Systems.
abstract: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) provides an effective framework for decision-making in collaborative wireless distributed systems, such as distributed manufacturing networks where IoT-enabled agents coordinate to optimize production under dynamic and partially observable environments. However, common Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE) approaches incur high communication costs and require full observability, which poses scalability challenges, especially under the limited communication resources characteristic of MTC. To address these challenges, a hierarchical federated reinforcement learning framework is introduced, integrating edge-level Critic Rotation and traditional Global Averaging within a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) setup. Critic Rotation enables structured value sharing while preserving local adaptability, thereby reducing the reliance on centralized training. Global Averaging enhances model consistency across agents without excessive communication overhead. Empirical evaluations in a multi-factory setting demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves computational costs comparable to independent DDPG while significantly lower than Multi-Agent DDPG (MADDPG). Meanwhile, the communication overhead remains marginally lower than MADDPG's overhead, making it a scalable and efficient alternative for multi-agent reinforcement learning in distributed environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RSM Suppression Via Joint 2-D LFM Modulation and Mismatched Filter Design.
abstract: In pulse-based dual-function radar-communication systems, conventional linear frequency modulation (LFM) waveform design struggles to achieve high data rate while preserving desirable characteristics of signal. To enhance the data rate while preserving radar detection performance, this paper proposes a joint waveform-filter design framework in which a 2-D modulation is implemented by modulating information into both initial frequency and chirp rate of an LFM signal. However, this modulation alters the spectra of signals across pulses, which induces range sidelobe modulation effect and degrades range resolution consistency. To mitigate these degradations, we develop an adaptive common-bandwidth cyclic algorithm in the design of mismatched filter which enables flexible tradeoff between key radar metrics such as signal-to-noise ratio loss and peak sidelobe level ratio. In particular, this algorithm can adaptively select spectrum-compatible reference template based on the characteristics of waveform set while maintaining a high computation efficiency for a large-scale codebook. Through comprehensive simulations, we demonstrate that the proposed joint waveform-filter design improves data rate, along with a significant mitigation in radar detection degradation induced by 2-D modulation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: UAV-Assisted Joint Data Collection and Wireless Power Transfer for Batteryless Sensor Networks.
abstract: The development of wireless power transfer (WPT) and Internet of Things (IoT) offers significant potential but faces challenges such as limited energy supply, dynamic environmental changes, and unstable transmission links. This paper presents an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted data collection and WPT scheme to support batteryless sensor (BLS) networks in remote areas. In this system, BLSs harvest energy from the UAV and utilize the harvested energy to transmit the collected data back to the UAV. The goal is to maximize the collected data volume and fairness index while minimizing the UAV energy consumption. To achieve these objectives, an optimization problem is formulated to jointly optimize the transmit power and UAV trajectory. Due to the non-convexity and dynamic nature of the problem, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based algorithm is proposed to solve the problem. Specifically, this algorithm integrates prioritized experience replay and the performer module to enhance system stability and accelerate convergence. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of collected data volume, fairness, and UAV energy consumption.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Interference Modeling and Performance Analysis of LEO Satellite Networks Based on Beam Hopping.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network with beam hopping (BH) is widely employed to enable global coverage and ubiquitous connectivity in sixth generation (6 G) networks. However, the dynamic beams make the inter-beam interference more complex and intractable. In this paper, an interference model for a LEO satellite downlink communication network based on a polling periodic BH time plan (BHTP) is proposed. Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), outage probability, and ergodic capacity are derived and analyzed to evaluate the impacts of system parameters on inter-beam interference. The analytical results reveal a trade-off between the performance of individual cells and that of the overall satellite communication network. Simulation results highlight the effects of satellite elevation angle, shadowing levels, number of beams, and BHTPs on interference and system performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cooperative Resource Allocation for UAV-assisted IoT with Dynamic Topologies: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: In UAV-assisted Internet of Things (IoT) networks, achieving efficient distributed resource allocation is challenging due to highly dynamic topologies. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches remain limited in handling cooperative relationships under dynamically varying agent populations. To address these challenges, an attention-cooperative multiagent proximal policy optimization (ACMAPPO) framework is proposed, centered on a novel attention-based critic that captures temporal dependencies in each agent's observations via gated recurrent units and dynamically aggregates information across agents using multi-head self-attention, thereby adaptively evaluating and handling time-varying topologies and cooperative relationships. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared with baseline algorithms the proposed ACMAPPO achieves significant improvements in quality-of-service satisfaction, and effective network throughput.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enhancing Physical Layer Security in STAR-RIS Communication Systems Assisted by UAV.
abstract: This paper investigates the physical layer security of a wireless communication system aided by an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS). A multiantenna access point (AP) transmits confidential messages to users in the transmission and reflection regions, respectively, in the presence of eavesdroppers. We formulate an optimization problem to maximize the system sum rate by jointly optimizing the AP's beamforming vectors and the STAR-RIS coefficients matrix. The original non-convex problem is decomposed into two tractable subproblems via an alternating optimization (AO) framework. The non-convexity issues are addressed using successive convex approximation (SCA) and semidefinite relaxation (SDR) techniques, leading to an efficient iterative algorithm that converges to a stationary point of the original problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of sum rate while guaranteeing security. Furthermore, the flexible deployment of the STAR-RIS by the UAV provides additional performance gains.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cooperative Target Detection with AUVs: A Dual-Timescale Hierarchical MADRL Approach.
abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) have shown great potential for cooperative detection and reconnaissance. However, collaborative AUV communications introduce risks of exposure. In adversarial environments, achieving efficient collaboration while ensuring covert operations becomes a key challenge for underwater cooperative missions. In this paper, we propose a novel dual time-scale Hierarchical MultiAgent Proximal Policy Optimization (H-MAPPO) framework. The high-level component determines the individuals participating in the task based on a central AUV, while the low-level component reduces exposure probabilities through power and trajectory control by the participating AUVs. Simulation results show that the proposed framework achieves rapid convergence, outperforms benchmark algorithms, and maximizes long-term cooperative efficiency while ensuring covert operations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Metasource-Based Secret Key Generation via Low-Density Parity-Check Patterns.
abstract: Recently, the concept of metasource-based secret key (MBSK) has been proposed for enhancing physical-layer security. In this paper, we propose a new approach of MBSK generation, via low-density parity-check (LDPC) patterns, where the parity-check matrix is varied and determined by the random channel gain of the legitimate link in each transmission. As there is no information on the legitimate channel gain delivered over the link between the legitimate transmitter and its desired receiver, eavesdroppers are unable to know which parity check matrix is being adopted in the legitimate LDPC encoding and, therefore, they fail to appropriately decode the confidential information protected by the MBSK via LDPC patterns. The security performance of our MBSK approach is evaluated in terms of the error rate difference between legitimate receivers and eavesdroppers. Illustrative simulation results substantiate that, even in the presence of powerful eavesdroppers possessing unlimited computing resources, our MBSK approach via LDPC patterns guarantees the physical-layer security without the aid of upper-layer encryption.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Large-Language-Model Based Beamforming Prediction for Sensing-Aided Communication.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is expected to enable the fifth-generation (5G) networks to provide ubiquitous communication and sensing. However, some highdynamic scenarios hinder applications of conventional ISAC schemes owing to the high overhead. In this paper, we design a novel ISAC architecture and propose a large language model (LLM) based two-stage beamforming prediction scheme. Specifically, in the first stage, we develop an LLM-based approach to predict the future channel state information (CSI) according to the history echoes. In the second stage, according to the predicted/estimated CSI, we formulate a beamforming optimization problem to maximize the achievable sum rate. Then, we propose a Primary-dual network to handle it. Simulation results verify that, compared with the benchmarks, our proposed beamforming prediction scheme not only enjoys a higher channel prediction accuracy but also achieves a better balance between the performance and computational complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Robust Aerial RIS-Aided Secure Transmission in LEO Satellite Systems with Beamforming and Cooperative Jamming.
abstract: This paper investigates the robust aerial reconfigurable intelligent surface (ARIS)-aided secure transmission in a low earth orbit (LEO) satellite system, where the ARIS simultaneously reflects confidential signals and emits cooperative jamming to enhance secrecy performance under imperfect channel state information. We first determine the LEO satellite trajectory and conduct theoretical modeling for the system secrecy rate (SR) under random satellite beamforming, ARIS phase shifts and cooperative jamming settings. By leveraging theories such as mean-square error, Rayleigh quotient, and second-order cone programming, we then propose a hierarchical optimization framework to obtain the optimal settings for SR maximization. Finally, extensive simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in enhancing the SR performance of the considered system.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Secure UAV-PASS Networks: Joint Trajectory and PAs' Positions Optimization.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are highly susceptible to eavesdropping due to the line-of-sight (LoS)-dominated transmission. The emerging pinching antenna system (PASS) is expected to mitigate large-scale path loss with dynamical pinching antenna (PA) position adjustment, thus creating new dimensions for security enhancement. In this paper, we propose a novel secure UAV-PASS framework, where a UAV transmits data to a ground PA-equipped base station, while a malicious eavesdropper attempts to intercept the transmitted information. The goal is to maximize the average secrecy rate by jointly optimizing PAs' positions, transmit power, and UAV trajectory. To solve this non-convex problem, a joint optimization algorithm is proposed, based on the welldesigned constructive phase alignment (CPA) method and the successive convex approximation (SCA) approach. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves a higher average secrecy rate than traditional array antenna system and uniformly distributed fixed array system, and the joint optimization algorithm effectively enhances secure communication by dynamically adjusting PAs' positions to constructively align signals, which yields a substantial performance improvement over the benchmark schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Robust Uplink Multi-User Digital Semantic Communication Under Imperfect Synchronization.
abstract: In multi-user semantic communication systems, synchronization errors caused by hardware imperfections and de-vice-base station (BS) misalignment are inevitable, hindering reliable semantic decoding and degrading overall performance. In this paper, we propose a robust uplink multi-user digital semantic communication method based on model division multiple access (MDMA), specifically designed for scenarios with imperfect synchronization. First, a multi-user digital semantic communication system is established, which jointly considers two types of synchronization errors: inter-user frame misalignment and symbol-level timing offsets. Next, a robust multi-user semantic transmission algorithm against synchronization errors (RMUSTA-SE) is proposed to enhance the robustness of the MDMA system. This algorithm injects the two types of synchronization errors during training to improve robustness, and exploits the correlation properties of embedded synchronization headers to achieve coarse inter-user frame alignment. Finally, extensive experiments on image reconstruction task demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves semantic reconstruction quality under various synchronization errors, providing a practical solution for multi-user semantic transmission with imperfect synchronization.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Lyapunov-Potential Game Driven Online Ecs Instance Orchestration for Low-Altitude 6G Networks.
abstract: In 6G-enabled low-altitude economy networks, Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation (ISCC) networks must jointly orchestrate sensing, air-to-ground transmission, and elastic cloud computing to balance coverage, latency, energy, and cost under highly time-varying conditions. This paper studies multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collaborative sensing and computation offloading with cloud-side Elastic Compute Service (ECS) scaling, and formulates a longterm stochastic optimization that couples sensing-driven task arrivals, link capacity, UAV energy consumption, and ECS rental cost. By introducing multi-dimensional real/virtual queues and applying the Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty (LDPP) framework, we transform the long-term problem into a per-slot deterministic optimization. We further prove the per-slot problem induces an exact potential game and develop a distributed online algorithm, Lyapunov Scheduling via Potential Game (LS-PG), with closedform/threshold best-response updates for sensing and resource scaling. Theoretical results establish strong queue stability and an$O(1/V)$performance gap to the optimum. Extensive simulations show LS-PG preserves sensing coverage under dynamic loads and achieves end-to-end latency, energy consumption, and cloud cost close to a centralized upper bound, significantly outperforming static and heuristic baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Resilience-Driven Topology Reconfiguration via Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning in Low-Altitude UAV Networks.
abstract: In low-altitude wireless networks, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are susceptible to environmental disturbances that may disrupt topology and degrade coverage and backhaul performance. To address this, we propose UR-HDRL (UAV network Reconfiguration based on Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning), a hierarchical framework that decouples safety constraints from communication optimization. By integrating Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), UR-HDRL ensures safety and enhances cooperative decision-making in obstacle-rich environments. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in transmission efficiency, coverage, and collision avoidance over baseline methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Routing Scheme in Networks: Reliability & Energy Efficiency.
abstract: Service networks should meet customer expectations for network construction in the early stage of the planning. Based on a clear and measurable metric system, the degraded network structure can be improved and upgraded, and the longterm sustainable evolution of the network can be gradually achieved. Currently, various network benchmarks, including reliability and energy efficiency, have been studied in both academia and industry. However, single metrics have some limitations. This paper considers the reliability of a network from a game theoretical perspective, network security games as well as energy efficiency based on the dynamic voltage scaling scheduling model. Several formulations have been proposed, and computational experiments have been conducted. Our experiments show that reliability and energy efficiency can be improved significantly.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fine-Tuning and Feature Fusion for Automatic Modulation Classification.
abstract: Robust modulation classification remains challenging under low-SNR and non-ideal channel conditions. Due to the diversity of modulation formats and signal characteristics, a single signal representation often fails to capture the full range of discriminative features needed for accurate classification. In addition, most existing AMC models are trained from scratch, which is often inefficient in terms of training time and data usage. Fine-tuning large-scale models leverages transferable features learned from diverse visual data, enabling more efficient and generalized learning. In this work, we propose CHEST, a dualstrategy framework that combines multi-representation feature fusion with fine-tuning of pre-trained models to improve classification robustness. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms existing baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid Beamforming Design for Finite-Blocklength Covert mmWave ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates the design of hybrid beamforming (HBF) for covert millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication systems under finite blocklength (FBL) constraint. Specifically, a dual-function mmWave transmitter (Alice) aims to sense potential targets and communicate with multiple legitimate users (Bobs) in the presence of a malicious warden (Willie). To this end, we formulate the HBF design problem to maximize the covert sum rate (CSR) with FBL constraint, while ensuring covertness of transmission, maintaining sensing beampattern gain, and satisfying Bobs' minimum covert rate requirements. Then, we reformulate the original challenging problem into more tractable form via the penalty dual decomposition method. Subsequently, we propose a computationally efficient alternating iteration algorithm, incorporating the Riemannian exact penalty optimization, elementwise iteration, and closed-form variable updates. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed HBF design in terms of achievable CSR and computational efficiency compared to benchmark schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Localization and Orientation Assisted by Massive MIMO-OFDM Triple-Beam Fingerprints.
abstract: Wireless communication systems offer strong potential for accurate localization, and deep-learning-based fingerprinting has shown good adaptability in complex propagation environments. However, existing fingerprints are limited to static location features, and current neural network designs do not fully utilize their structural properties. To improve this, we introduce a dynamic triple-beam fingerprint (TBF) for massive multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems and develop a localization and orientation awareness network (LOA-Net) designed to align with its sparse structural characteristics for joint localization and orientation estimation. We analyze the advantages of TBF for localization and orientation awareness through channel modeling. Localization is formulated as a regression task and enhanced with a masking mechanism, while orientation estimation is modeled as a multi-class classification problem using the estimated coordinates as prior information. Simulations in standard 3GPP scenarios demonstrate the high localization accuracy and the potential for effective orientation awareness.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MFM-Enabled ISAC for 6G Networks: General Framework and Predictive Beamforming via BQNet.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is essential for the Low-Altitude Economy (LAE) to support seamless UAV operations. However, conventional ISAC systems struggle with multimodal data processing and semantic understanding in dynamic low-altitude environments. This paper proposes a multimodal fusion model (MFM)-ISAC framework, where a large model is deeply embedded into the closed-loop sensing-communication interaction rather than acting as a backend tool. The framework projects multimodal inputs into a shared latent space and aligns asynchronous streams for realtime decision-making. Building on the resulting unified and temporally aligned representation, we developed the ISAC-beamaware query network (BQNet) for predictive beamforming, which maps sensing sequences directly to optimal beams using temporal harmonization and codebook-informed queries, bypassing explicit channel estimation and beam sweeping. Experiments on a custom low-altitude UAV mmWave dataset showed that ISAC-BQNet achieves$\mathbf{7 9. 9 5 {\%}}$Top-1 and 96.35% Top-3 accuracy, outperforming representative baseline models.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel Ray-Tracing Channel Model with Full-Wave Simulations for THz Communication Systems.
abstract: Accurate characterization of scattering mechanism is essential for terahertz (THz) channel models, but the current methods are not accurate enough for ray tracing (RT).
