In this paper, we propose a novel RT THz channel model with fullwave simulations to accurately characterize scattering mechanism. Full-wave simulations are employed to generate accurate scattering information for rough surfaces, while the directional information and electromagnetic parameters of scattered rays are extracted and stored in a database. When a ray interacts with a rough surface in RT, the directional information and electromagnetic parameters from the database are used in RT process. The simulation results indicate that the scattering results in the THz frequency band obtained through the proposed method match well with those from a commercial RT software.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Massive Beam Scheduling in LEO Systems: Low Complexity via Effective Interference Approximation.
abstract: Multi-beam Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites are poised to play a central role in integrated 6G in space. Existing approaches for beam scheduling, with exact inter-beam interference modeling in every time slot, greatly suffer from prohibitive computational complexity as the number of beams scales up. This paper introduces a tractable interference approximation model that captures inter-beam interference in an aggregated form, completely removing slot-level computations while maintaining high accuracy. The model admits efficient numerical solutions that yield the probabilities of beam activation, enabling nearinstantaneous construction of beam scheduling with minimum computational cost. Simulation results show that our method maintains over 95% accuracy in predicting scheduling performance compared to exact interference modeling, with less than 6% loss relative to the global optimum for capacity-demand ratio optimization. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed model as a foundation for efficient beam scheduling in next-generation large-scale LEO satellite systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Stackelberg-Contract-Based Dependent Task Offloading and Resource Pricing in PVEC Networks.
abstract: Parked Vehicle-assisted Edge Computing (PVEC) utilizes idle parked vehicles (PVs) to offer edge computing services for user vehicles (UVs), effectively reducing latency and energy consumption. Nevertheless, uneven resource distribution and inter-task dependencies in PVEC networks may cause inefficient task offloading and unfair resource pricing. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents a Stackelberg game and Contract theory-based Dependent task Offloading and resource Pricing (SCDOP) framework. In this framework, UVs partially offload their dependent tasks to Roadside Units (RSUs) managed by an SDN controller, while overloaded RSUs will transmit the tasks to nearby PVs. The interactions among RSUs, UVs, and PVs are modeled by Stackelberg game and contract theory, and the economic properties of SCDOP are mathematically proven. A social welfare maximization problem is formulated and a Particle Swarm Optimization Plus Genetic (PSOPG) algorithm is developed to derive near-optimal solutions. Simulation results show that PSOPG achieves higher task completion rates and greater social welfare than benchmark schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Optimized Deployment of HAPS Systems for GNSS Localization Enhancement in Urban Environments.
abstract: While high altitude platform stations (HAPS) have been primarily explored as network infrastructure for communication services, their advantageous characteristics also make them promising candidates for augmenting GNSS localization. This paper proposes a metaheuristic framework to jointly optimize the number and placement of HAPS for GNSS enhancement in dense urban environments, considering practical constraints such as elevation masks, altitude limits, and ray-traced visibility from 3D city models. The problem is highly nonconvex due to the discrete HAPS count and the environment-dependent 3D Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). To address this, we develop a tailored version of the adaptive special-crowding distance nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II (ASDNSGA-II). Simulations show the method successfully identifies the minimum number of HAPS needed to satisfy a CRLB threshold and selects the configuration with the lowest CRLB within that minimum, offering a cost-effective and scalable solution for future HAPSaided positioning systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multimodal Radio and Vision Fusion for Robust Localization in Urban V2I Communications.
abstract: Accurate localization is critical for vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication systems, especially in urban areas where GPS signals are often obstructed by tall buildings, leading to significant positioning errors, necessitating alternative or complementary techniques for reliable and precise positioning in applications like autonomous driving and smart city infrastructure. This paper proposes a multimodal contrastive learning regression based localization framework for V2I scenarios that combines channel state information (CSI) with visual information to achieve improved accuracy and reliability. The approach leverages the complementary strengths of wireless and visual data to overcome the limitations of traditional localization methods, offering a robust solution for V2I applications. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CSI and vision fusion model significantly outperforms traditional methods and single modal models, achieving superior localization accuracy and precision in complex urban environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Clustering-Based User Selection in Federated Learning: Metadata Exploitation for 3GPP Networks.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw user data, but conventional simulations often rely on unrealistic data partitioning and current user selection methods ignore data correlation among users. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a metadatadriven FL framework. We first introduce a novel data partition model based on a homogeneous Poisson point process (HPPP), capturing both heterogeneity in data quantity and natural overlap among user datasets. Building on this model, we develop a clustering-based user selection strategy that leverages metadata, such as user location, to reduce data correlation and enhance label diversity across training rounds. Extensive experiments on FMNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that the proposed framework improves model performance, stability, and convergence in non-IID scenarios, while maintaining comparable performance under IID settings. Furthermore, the method shows pronounced advantages when the number of selected users per round is small. These findings highlight the framework's potential for enhancing FL performance in realistic deployments and guiding future standardization.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy Efficiency Maximization in Hybrid Bit-Semantic Communication Networks.
abstract: Semantic communications (SCs) have revealed significant potential in improving transmission efficiency by conveying semantic information rather than raw bit signals. However, the additional computational overhead introduced at transceivers makes it challenging to achieve high energy efficiency in deep learning (DL)-enabled SC systems. In this paper, we first define a semantic energy efficiency (S-EE) metric by jointly considering the semantic rate, transmission power, computing power, signal processing power, and circuit power at both the transmitter and receiver sides. In contrast, existing studies typically consider only one side of power consumption and thus overlook the effects of the semantic extraction ratio and computational consumption on S-EE. We then formulate an S-EE maximization problem by jointly optimizing the semantic extraction ratio, transmission rate, and bandwidth allocation. An alternating optimizationbased scheme is proposed to solve this non-convex problem. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed SC-based scheme achieves significant improvement in terms of S-EE compared to the conventional communication.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Near-Field XL-MiMO for ISAC: Joint Multi-User Channel Sensing and Predictive Beamforming.
abstract: Near-field (NF) extremely large-scale multiple-input-multiple-output (XL-MIMO) enables new opportunities for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). In this paper, we first propose a generic OFDM-ISAC scheme to sense and communicate with multiple mobile users simultaneously, which includes discovery phase and tracking phase. In the discovery phase, noting that the radar received signal at each antenna suffers from different Doppler shift in the NF scenario, the radar parameter estimation is more challenging than its counterpart in the far-field (FF). To address this problem, we divide the XL antenna array into multiple subarrays by which the channel between each subarray and user can be modeled approximately as the FF condition. Then, the classical FF sensing methods are utilized to estimate the radar parameters of all subarrays. Moreover, the iterative parallel interference cancellation is employed to eliminate the interference among subarrays, and the information fusion is efficiently performed to recover the speed and motion direction. In the tracking phase, based on the estimated velocity, predictive beamforming is designed for mobile users to assist the communication. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed structure is verified by numerical simulations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Channel Estimation and MA Trajectory Design with Time Constraint.
abstract: Movable antenna (MA) has emerged as a promising technology to enhance communication performance. However, since the movement speed of MA is practically constrained by mechanical drivers and the channel coherence time is limited, the time overhead for antenna movement in channel estimation and performance improvement can significantly affect the effective rate of MA systems in practice. To address this issue, we propose in this paper to jointly design the MA's trajectories, including the trajectory for obtaining channel measurements and that for moving to the rate-optimal position, to maximize the average effective rate of an MA-aided receiver subject to the given transmission block duration by a two time-scale optimization approach. Specifically, the number of channel measurements as well as the MA's trajectory for obtaining them are first optimized in the long term based on the known channel distribution, while the number of moving steps as well as the MA's trajectory for moving to the rate-optimal position are adaptively designed in the short term to cater to the instantaneous channel realizations, thus simplifying the design complexity and yet providing high adaptability to channel variations. A key challenge in our short-term design is accurately reconstructing the channel map from measurements at only a subset of antenna positions. By exploiting the spatial channel correlations over positions in the moving region, we propose a kernel-based regression (KBR) method to reconstruct the channel map. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms the fixed-position antenna (FPA) system and other benchmark MA designs that neglect the antenna movement time under various channel setups.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Hybrid Semantic-Bit Networks for Asymmetric Industrial WNCSs: Resource Optimization with Peak Age of Semantic-Enabled Loop.
abstract: Industrial wireless networked control systems (WNCSs) exhibit strong uplink-downlink (UL-DL) asymmetry. UL transmissions produce high-volume sensing data, whereas DL transmissions deliver small yet ultra-reliable control commands. Conventional symmetric frameworks cannot simultaneously satisfy these divergent requirements. This paper proposes a semantic-bit hybrid communication and control co-optimization framework for asymmetric industrial WNCSs. The UL adopts semantic encoding to compress task-relevant information, while the DL preserves bit-level reliability to ensure deterministic actuation. A peak age of semantic-enabled loop (PAoSL) metric is introduced to quantify the timeliness of knowledge and its impact on control performance. To jointly optimize UL-DL operations, a hierarchical solution based on an asynchronous dual-actor reinforcement learning framework is developed, where shared communication resources are dynamically allocated, and control gains are updated via LQR design. Simulation results show that the proposed method significantly reduces average PAoSL while maintaining ultra-high reliability and scalability compared with baseline schemes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Trajectory-Resource Scheduling for UAV-USV Collaborative Perception in Dynamic Maritime Environments.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) are increasingly deployed for wide-area and persistent maritime target perception in applications such as search and rescue, environmental surveillance, and navigation safety. However, such systems face significant challenges due to dynamic ocean conditions, unstable communication links, and stringent on-board energy constraints, which limit their operational endurance and perception integrity. To address these issues, this paper focuses on the cooperative perception of partially submerged maritime targets using a UAV-USV team and tackles the joint problem of trajectory planning and communication resource allocation under realistic ocean current disturbances. We develop a system model that incorporates target and platform mobility influenced by currents and formulate an energy-efficient optimization framework that ensures a minimum perception quality. A Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG)-based solution is designed to enable decentralized coordination and adaptive decision-making. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces total system energy consumption by 15% - 20% compared to a baseline method while maintaining reliable target perception performance in dynamic maritime settings.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cooperative Task Offloading in Multi-UAV Covert Communication Networks.
abstract: Aerial edge computing networks can effectively extend ground sensor systems by improving perception coverage and computation efficiency. However, the openness of wireless links makes data transmission vulnerable to detection and eavesdropping, while most existing aerial edge computing works mainly optimize latency/energy without explicitly considering covert security. Meanwhile, UAV covert communication research typically focuses on physical-layer design or transmission capability, but rarely incorporates multi-UAV collaboration and edge computing efficiency. To bridge this gap, we investigate a multiUAV secure edge computing scenario, in which UAVs cooperate both for self-jamming to thwart the aerial eavesdropper and for distributed edge computing to assist task processing. To tackle the latency minimization problem under covert communication constraints, we propose a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based 3D deployment method whose fitness is evaluated via an inner block coordinate descent (BCD) routine. Extensive analysis and simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, achieving covert task offloading while significantly reducing task processing latency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Environment-Adaptive UAV Trajectory Optimization via Kernel Density Estimation.
abstract: The low-altitude economy is a hot topic in recent years, but the current researches on unmanned aerial vehicles are inefficient to address the critical coupled problem of physical collision risks and limited wireless spectrum. To solve the problem, a dynamic airspace management mechanism is proposed in this paper, which combines the historical channel state information mining and predictive trajectory planning. First, a high-precision system model is constructed, including probabilistic line-of-sight channels dependent on the environment. Then, the kernel density estimation is designed to generate continuous potential congestion fields to avoid active hotspots. Then, a joint optimization problem of three-dimensional trajectory and communication quality is formulated to minimize the weighted sum of energy consumption and congestion costs. Finally, the kernel density estimation enhanced successive convex approximation algorithm is designed to efficiently solve the derived non-convex optimization problem. Simulation results reveal that the proposed algorithm outperforms the particle swarm optimization algorithm and the straight-line benchmark, reducing the peak congestion by 35 % in complex urban scenario while maintaining the stable quality of service.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DAM-SC: Text-Driven Semantic Communication for Ultra-Low Bitrate Video Transmission Using Dynamic Attribute Models.
abstract: The explosive growth of video traffic from mobile and remote sources, such as surveillance cameras and IoT devices, imposes immense strain on communication networks. Conventional video codecs like HEVC falter at ultra-low bitrates, often sacrificing critical semantic information. This paper challenges the traditional pixel-transmission paradigm by introducing DAMSC, a novel semantic communication framework. Instead of transmitting pixel data, our framework deconstructs a video into a compact semantic packet containing a static background, initial object appearances, and a structured textual description of object motion. A key innovation is the pioneering use of a region-aware, descriptive Large Multimodal Model (LMM) as a semantic encoder to generate this description. At the receiver, we design a two-stage hybrid synthesis pipeline that first renders sparse keyframes and then employs a Video Frame Interpolation (VFI) model to generate a temporally coherent final video. Through comprehensive evaluation, we demonstrate that DAM-SC consistently outperforms traditional codecs (H.264, HEVC, VVC), achieving superior semantic fidelity (MOTA) while saving approximately 70–80 % of the bitrate compared to HEVC in bandwidth-constrained scenarios, paving the way for nextgeneration intelligent communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: PBFT-AdaGossip: A Robust Consensus Strategy for Post-Disaster Wireless Collaborative Networks.
abstract: Natural disasters often lead to the destruction of traditional communication infrastructures and the failure of centralized coordination systems, significantly impeding the efficiency of emergency rescue operations. To facilitate rapid recovery and coordination, temporary wirelesscollaborative networks are increasingly deployed in post-disaster scenarios. Blockchain technology, with its inherent decentralization and immutability, ensures the consistency and trustworthiness of information exchanged among stakeholders during disaster relief efforts. However, the instability and interference inherent in wireless channels frequently result in high packet loss rates, severely degrading consensus efficiency. In this paper, we first analyze the impact of packet loss rates on the Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) consensus and find that high packet loss rates lead to a sharp decline in the consensus success rate. On this analysis, we propose a consensus strategy that integrates the adaptive Gossip protocol, termed PBFT-AdaGossip. Then, we analyze and validate the effectiveness using an epidemic model and a discrete-time Markov chain. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly improves the consensus success rate, while keeping communication delay under control, thereby validating its robustness in high packet loss wireless environments.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: UAV-Relay and UAV-SAR Assisted ISAC System for Target Areas Imaging.
abstract: This paper investigates a novel integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system assisted by a UAV-relay and a UAV-SAR for target areas imaging. The system comprises a UAVSAR equipped with an ISAC system for high-resolution imaging of target areas, and a UAV-relay that forwards the collected data to the data center when the direct link is obstructed or insufficient for high-rate SAR data transmission. To minimize the total system energy consumption while ensuring system performance, we formulate a joint optimization problem over the UAV-SAR's trajectory, flight velocity, beamforming design, and the UAV-relay's deployment, explicitly incorporating constraints on SAR image SNR for reliable imaging and communication data rate for timely sensing information transmission. To address the non-convexity of the formulated problem, a penalty-based block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm is developed, which iteratively solves a sequence of convex subproblems. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces energy consumption by 19.74 % compared with the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fundamental Limits of Moving User Localization in Near-Field XL-RIS Assisted OTFS Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of moving user localization in extremely large-scale Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (XL-RIS) assisted Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) systems. We address the critical challenge arising from the interplay between the near-field spherical wavefronts characterized by extremely large apertures and the severe Doppler shifts induced by high mobility. To tackle this, we develop a mixed-field system model that jointly captures the spherical propagation characteristics of the XL-RIS and the plane-wave propagation of the far-field Base Station (BS). Based on this unified model, the exact Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (CRB) for position and velocity estimation is derived using Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) analysis. Simulation results validate the proposed model, demonstrating its capability to accurately characterize the propagation mechanisms of both the near-field RIS and far-field BS, thereby providing a rigorous and efficient benchmark for dynamic near-field sensing.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Semantic-Aware Video Communication: Enhancing Traditional and Deep Video Encoders.
abstract: Video semantic communication (VSC) offers a novel approach to compress videos at aggressive rates. However, existing VSC methods primarily emphasize intra-frame semantic importance while ignoring the inter-frame semantic importance. To address this issue, we propose a semantic-aware video communication (SAVC) scheme, where encoding parameters such as compression rate and key frame interval are adaptively adjusted for each group of pictures (GOP) in the video based on interframe semantic importance. In the proposed scheme, GOPs are adaptively encoded with semantic-aware encoding parameters, followed by reconstruction at the receiver. First, we use a deep neural network to extract semantic features and introduce a semantic importance metric based on semantic similarity between GOPs, where higher similarity indicates lower importance. Then, we formulate an video encoding parameter optimization problem that balances video quality and bitrate, and we design a proximal policy optimization algorithm for parameter selection (PPOPS) to solve the optimization problem. Simulation results show that the proposed SAVC scheme can reduce at most 8.188% and 8.021% Bjøntegaard Delta rate in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index measure over baseline methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Sparse Code and Modulation Design for OTFS-NOMA.
abstract: In the evolving landscape of 6G mobile networks, ensuring reliable massive access in high-mobility environments presents a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel uplink orthogonal time frequency space-modulated low density signature (OTFS-LDS) system specifically designed to address these challenges. We first propose an LDS sparse matrix design that leverages the sparse nature of the OTFS channel matrix in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain and deploys LDS over the entire DD domain to improve bit error rate (BER) performance. We further present a low-complexity improved approximate message passing (IAMP) detection scheme for the uplink receiver that strategically balances performance with computational demands. Both theoretical average BER (ABER) performance bound and simulation results are provided for OTFS-LDS system, demonstrating the superiority of our proposed spreading code design and the IAMP algorithm over the state-of-the-art message passing algorithm-based detectors.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Low-Complexity Precoding Design for Massive MIMO LEO Satellite Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the low-complexity downlink (DL) precoding design for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications (SATCOM). We first formulate a DL beam-based channel model tailored to the unique propagation characteristics of massive MIMO LEO SATCOM. Leveraging this model, we propose a low-complexity precoding method based on average signal-to-leakage-plus-noise ratio (ASLNR) maximization with statistical channel state information (sCSI). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves DL sum-rate performance while substantially reducing computational complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Radio Frequency Fingerprint Recognition for Uav in Low-Altitude Intelligent Networks.
abstract: In low-altitude intelligent networks, reliable identification of individual uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for ensuring airspace security. Radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting offers unique advantages such as passive detection, noncooperative identification, and resilience to encryption or spoofing, making it an effective approach for distinguishing individual UAVs. However, RF fingerprint recognition remains challenging due to multipath fading, interference, and channel variations between line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) conditions. This paper presents a robust UAV identification framework that integrates signal enhancement, supervised contrastive learning, and feature distillation. Specifically, a three-stage signal preprocessing pipeline is developed, which consists of energy-driven segmentation, interference-aware filtering, and spectral shifting with downsampling to extract high-quality UAV control bursts. Then, a supervised contrastive encoder learns discriminative and channel-robust representations. Furthermore, an attentionguided center aggregation and feature distillation module is introduced to align encoder features with aggregated identity centers, improving intra-class compactness and cross-scenario stability. Experiments on the DroneRFb-DIR dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance, with 91.5 % accuracy, 0.882 F1-score, a Silhouette Score of 0.237, and an inter/intra-class ratio (IIR) of 2.69, surpassing existing baselines. These results confirm the method's effectiveness and robustness for UAV RF fingerprint recognition under varying LoS/NLoS channel conditions.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Antenna Coding Optimization for Pixel Antenna Empowered Wireless Communication Using Deep Learning with Heterogeneous Multi-Head Selection.
abstract: Pixel antenna is a promising antenna technology that enables flexible adjustment of radiation characteristics and enhancement of wireless systems through antenna coding. This work proposes a novel deep learning-based antenna coding optimization algorithm. Specifically, the proposed algorithm is supported by a heterogeneous multi-head selection mechanism, whose main idea is to train multiple neural networks based on various coding schemes and select the one that leads to the best system performance. Unlike traditional heuristic searchingbased algorithms that require high computational complexity to achieve satisfactory performance, the proposed data-driven deep learning approach can achieve 98 % of the performance achieved by the searching-based algorithms with significantly reduced computational complexity. Results demonstrate that in pixel antenna empowered single-input single-output systems, the proposed algorithm achieves a computational speed 81 times faster than the searching-based algorithm. For more complex pixel antenna empowered multiple-input multiple-output systems, the computational speed is 297 times faster than the existing searching-based algorithm. Benefiting from the high performance and low computational complexity, this algorithm demonstrates the significant potential of pixel antennas as a novel and practical technology to enhance wireless systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference
